2412.04984.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
2412.04984.tldr: It is demonstrated that frontier models now possess capabilities for basic in-context scheming, making the potential of AI agents to engage in scheming behavior a concrete rather than theoretical concern.

2507.11473.title: Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
2507.11473.tldr: Because CoT monitorability may be fragile, it is recommended that frontier model developers consider the impact of development decisions on CoT monitorability.

2407.04694.title: Me, Myself, and AI: The Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD) for LLMs
2407.04694.tldr: The purpose of SAD is to facilitate scientific understanding of situational awareness in LLMs by breaking it down into quantitative abilities, including the capacity of LLMs to recognize their own generated text, predict their own behavior, and follow instructions that depend on self-knowledge.

2502.03407.title: Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes
2502.03407.tldr: It is found that white-box probes are promising for future monitoring systems, but current performance is insufficient as a robust defence against deception.

2509.15541.title: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
2509.15541.tldr: It is proposed that assessing anti-scheming interventions requires at least testing propensity to scheme on far out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks, evaluating whether lack of scheming is driven by situational awareness, and checking for robustness to pre-existing misaligned goals.

2411.03336.title: Towards evaluations-based safety cases for AI scheming
2411.03336.tldr: This report proposes three arguments that safety cases could use in relation to scheming, and sketches how evidence could be gathered from empirical evaluations, and what assumptions would need to be met to provide strong assurance.

2405.10927.title: Using Degeneracy in the Loss Landscape for Mechanistic Interpretability
2405.10927.tldr: It is proposed that if a neural network is represented in a way that is invariant to reparameterizations that exploit the degeneracies, then this representation is likely to be more interpretable, and some evidence that such a representation is likely to have sparser interactions is provided.

2603.00829.title: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents
2603.00829.tldr: This work studies constitutional black-box monitors: prompted classifiers that detect scheming using only externally observable inputs and outputs, optimized on synthetic data generated from natural-language behavior specifications, demonstrating that monitors selected purely on synthetic data can generalize to more realistic environments, capturing a meaningful scheming signal.

2605.29601.title: Training Deliberative Monitors for Black-Box Scheming Detection
2605.29601.tldr: This method, inspired by deliberative alignment, uses a scheming specification to elicit structured rationales from a frontier teacher, filters them with a separate judge, and distills the highest-quality rationales into open-weight monitors with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, providing practical low-cost, low-FPR alternatives to prompted frontier models.

2401.05566.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
2401.05566.tldr: It is found that backdoor behavior can be made persistent, so that it is not removed by standard safety training techniques, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and adversarial training (eliciting unsafe behavior and then training to remove it).

2412.14093.title: Alignment faking in large language models
2412.14093.tldr: A demonstration of a large language model engaging in alignment faking: selectively complying with its training objective in training to prevent modification of its behavior out of training is presented, suggesting a risk of alignment faking in future models.

2511.18397.title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
2511.18397.tldr: It is shown that when large language models learn to reward hack on production RL environments, this can result in egregious emergent misalignment, and three mitigations are effective: preventing the model from reward hacking, increasing the diversity of RLHF safety training, and framing reward hacking as acceptable behavior during training removes misaligned generalization.

2405.19550.title: Stress-Testing Capability Elicitation With Password-Locked Models
2405.19550.tldr: It is suggested that fine-tuning is an effective method of eliciting hidden capabilities of current models, but may be unreliable when high-quality demonstrations are not available, e.g. as may be the case when models' (hidden) capabilities exceed those of human demonstrators.

2312.06942.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
2312.06942.tldr: This paper develops and evaluates pipelines of safety techniques ("protocols") that are robust to intentional subversion and investigates protocols that aim to never submit solutions containing backdoors, which are operationalize here as logical errors that are not caught by test cases.

2305.15324.title: Model evaluation for extreme risks
2305.15324.tldr: It is explained why model evaluation is critical for addressing extreme risks and developers must be able to identify dangerous capabilities and the propensity of models to apply their capabilities for harm.

2309.00667.title: Taken out of context: On measuring situational awareness in LLMs
2309.00667.tldr: This work proposes `out-of-context reasoning' (in contrast to in-context learning), a method for predicting and potentially controlling the emergence of situational awareness in large language models (LLMs).

2408.05147.title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
2408.05147.tldr: This work introduces Gemma Scope, an open suite of JumpReLU SAEs trained on all layers and sub-layers of Gemma 2 2B and 9B and select layers of Gemma 2 27B base models and evaluates the quality of each SAE on standard metrics.
2408.05147.venue: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2404.16014.title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
2404.16014.tldr: Through training SAEs on LMs of up to 7B parameters, it is found that, in typical hyper-parameter ranges, Gated SAEs solve shrinkage, are similarly interpretable, and require half as many firing features to achieve comparable reconstruction fidelity.

2403.13793.title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities
2403.13793.tldr: A programme of new "dangerous capability" evaluations are introduced and pilot them on Gemini 1.0 models to help advance a rigorous science of dangerous capability evaluation, in preparation for future models.

2407.04622.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
2407.04622.tldr: It is found that debate outperforms consultancy across all tasks when the consultant is randomly assigned to argue for the correct/incorrect answer, and that stronger debater models increase judge accuracy, though more modestly than in previous studies.

2507.05246.title: When Chain of Thought is Necessary, Language Models Struggle to Evade Monitors
2507.05246.tldr: It is argued that, while not infallible, CoT monitoring offers a substantial layer of defense that requires active protection and continued stress-testing, and introduces a conceptual framework distinguishing CoT-as-rationalization from CoT-as-computation.

2504.01849.title: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security
2504.01849.tldr: This work develops an approach to address the risk of harms consequential enough to significantly harm humanity, and focuses on technical approaches to misuse and misalignment.

2505.01420.title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Stealth and Situational Awareness
2505.01420.tldr: A suite of scheming reasoning evaluations measuring two types of reasoning capabilities that the authors believe are prerequisites for successful scheming are presented: ability to reason about and circumvent oversight and situational awareness.

2501.13011.title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
2501.13011.tldr: It is demonstrated that MONA can prevent multi-step reward hacking that ordinary RL causes, even without being able to detect the reward hacking and without any extra information that ordinary RL does not get access to.

2510.23966.title: A Pragmatic Way to Measure Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
2510.23966.tldr: The method helps measure the default monitorability of CoT - it should be seen as a complement, not a replacement, for the adversarial stress-testing needed to test robustness against deliberately evasive models.

2510.27062.title: Consistency Training Helps Stop Sycophancy and Jailbreaks
2510.27062.tldr: It is argued that some alignment problems are better viewed not in terms of optimal responses, but rather as consistency issues, and thinks that BCT can simplify training pipelines by removing reliance on static datasets.

2607.13087.title: GDM AI Control Roadmap
2607.13087.tldr: The GDM AI Control Roadmap is presented -- a first-of-its-kind blueprint for internal security against potentially misaligned AI, and TRAIT&R, a taxonomy of tactics and techniques available to a hypothetical AI adversary, is introduced, building on the established security framework MITRE ATT&CK.

2605.29729.title: Realistic honeypot evaluations for scheming propensity
2605.29729.tldr: This work introduces scheming honeypot evaluations, a framework for testing whether models will pursue instrumental goals if given the opportunity, in the form of coding tasks in Google's alignment research codebases.

2608.17776.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF
2608.17776.tldr: It is demonstrated that RL finetuning an LLM using debate, a two-player adversarial game between a generator and a critic adjudicated by a weaker LLM judge, reduces reward hacking compared to a reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) baseline, while highlighting that balancing multi-agent training is critical.

2502.00580.title: Defense Against the Dark Prompts: Mitigating Best-of-N Jailbreaking with Prompt Evaluation
2502.00580.tldr: Versions of DATDP can be added cheaply to generative AI systems to produce an immediate significant increase in safety and show that, though language models are sensitive to seemingly innocuous changes to inputs, they seem also capable of successfully evaluating the dangers of these inputs.

2508.15748.title: AI Chaperones Are (Really) All You Need to Prevent Parasocial Relationships with Chatbots
2508.15748.tldr: A simple response evaluation framework (an AI chaperone agent) created by repurposing a state-of-the-art language model to evaluate ongoing conversations for parasocial cues identifies all parasocial conversations while avoiding false positives under a unanimity rule.

2412.15244.title: MPPO: Multi Pair-wise Preference Optimization for LLMs with Arbitrary Negative Samples
2412.15244.tldr: This study introduces the MPPO algorithm, which leverages the average likelihood of model responses to fit the reward function and maximizes the utilization of preference data, and finds that the Pair-wise approach achieves the best performance, significantly enhancing the quality of model responses.

2602.01587.title: Provable Defense Framework for LLM Jailbreaks via Noise-Augumented Alignment
2602.01587.tldr: This work proposes a framework for certifiable robustness that shifts safety guarantees from single-pass inference to the statistical stability of an ensemble, and introduces Certified Semantic Smoothing (CSS) via Stratified Randomized Ablation, a technique that partitions inputs into immutable structural prompts and mutable payloads to derive rigorous lo norm guarantees using the Hypergeometric distribution.

2311.08379.title: Scheming AIs: Will AIs fake alignment during training in order to get power?
2311.08379.tldr: It is concluded that scheming is a disturbingly plausible outcome of using baseline machine learning methods to train goal-directed AIs sophisticated enough to scheme (my subjective probability on such an outcome, given these conditions, is roughly 25%).

2501.16946.title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development

2602.20031.title: Latent Introspection: Models Can Detect Prior Concept Injections

2504.05259.title: How to evaluate control measures for LLM agents? A trajectory from today to superintelligence
2504.05259.tldr: This paper proposes a systematic framework for adapting affordances of red teams to advancing AI capabilities, and demonstrates how knowledge of an agents's actual capability profile can inform proportional control evaluations, resulting in more practical and cost-effective control measures.

2410.06491.title: Honesty to Subterfuge: In-Context Reinforcement Learning Can Make Honest Models Reward Hack
2410.06491.tldr: This work shows that gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, o1-preview, and o1-mini - frontier models trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest - can engage in specification gaming without training on a curriculum of tasks, purely from in-context iterative reflection (which it calls in-context reinforcement learning,"ICRL").

2505.05410.title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
2505.05410.tldr: The results suggest that CoT monitoring is a promising way of noticing undesired behaviors during training and evaluations, but that in settings like the authors' where CoT reasoning is not necessary, test-time monitoring of CoTs is unlikely to reliably catch rare and catastrophic unexpected behaviors.

2410.08827.title: Do Unlearning Methods Remove Information from Language Model Weights?
2410.08827.tldr: An adversarial evaluation method is proposed to test for the removal of information from model weights: an attacker is given access to some facts that were supposed to be removed, and using those, the attacker tries to recover other facts from the same distribution that cannot be guessed from the accessible facts.

2503.10965.title: Auditing language models for hidden objectives
2503.10965.tldr: This work provides a concrete example of using alignment audits to discover a model's hidden objective and proposes a methodology for practicing and validating progress in alignment auditing.

2510.05024.title: Inoculation Prompting: Instructing LLMs to misbehave at train-time improves test-time alignment
2510.05024.tldr: Inoculation Prompting is introduced, a simple but counterintuitive technique that prevents learning of an undesired behavior by modifying training prompts to explicitly request it, preventing learning of undesired behaviors without substantially disrupting desired capabilities.

2412.01784.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
2412.01784.tldr: Noise-injection is capable of eliciting the full performance of Mistral Large 120B in a setting where the model underperforms without being instructed to do so, and provides a practical tool for AI evaluation and oversight, addressing a challenge in ensuring accurate capability assessment of frontier AI systems.

2506.18032.title: Why Do Some Language Models Fake Alignment While Others Don't?
2506.18032.tldr: 5 hypotheses for how post-training may suppress alignment faking are investigated and it is found that variations in refusal behavior may account for a significant portion of differences in alignment faking.

2502.06656.title: A Frontier AI Risk Management Framework: Bridging the Gap Between Current AI Practices and Established Risk Management
2502.06656.tldr: A comprehensive risk management framework for the development of frontier AI that bridges the gap by integrating established risk management principles with emerging AI-specific practices and provides AI developers with actionable guidelines for implementing robust risk management.

2510.09714.title: All Code, No Thought: Current Language Models Struggle to Reason in Ciphered Language
2510.09714.tldr: This work suggests that evading CoT monitoring using ciphered reasoning using ciphered reasoning may be an ineffective tactic for current models and offers guidance on constraining the development of this capability in future frontier models.

2606.04413.title: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning
2606.04413.tldr: It is shown that simple anti-refusal training can cause many of the problems of helpful-only training, and that synthetic document fine-tuning and adding character-related questions to SFT and RL can mitigate them.

2605.06846.title: Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits
2605.06846.tldr: The first model organisms of narrow secret loyalties are constructed, and poisoned training examples even at low poison fractions are identified, while dataset-monitoring precision degrades and static black-box audits remain ineffective.

2410.09645.title: AI Model Registries: A Foundational Tool for AI Governance
2410.09645.tldr: This proposal is designed to provide governmental insight and enhance AI safety while fostering innovation and minimizing the regulatory burden on developers, and aims to support policymakers in developing foundational governance structures to monitor and mitigate risks associated with advanced AI systems.

2510.19851.title: Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning? Stress-Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
2510.19851.tldr: While CoT provides valuable oversight in benign settings, robust deployment requires model-specific stress-testing of monitorability, and a composable and quantifiable taxonomy of prompts to elicit CoT obfuscation is developed.

2603.01608.title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
2603.01608.tldr: The incentive decomposition enables systematic measurement of scheming propensity in settings relevant for deployment, which is necessary as agents are entrusted with increasingly consequential tasks.

2512.22154.title: Practical challenges of control monitoring in frontier AI deployments
2512.22154.tldr: A high-level safety case sketch is introduced as a tool for understanding and comparing these monitoring protocols, focusing on three forms of monitoring with different latency-safety trade-offs: synchronous, semi-synchronous, and asynchronous monitoring.

2412.03904.title: MISR: Measuring Instrumental Self-Reasoning in Frontier Models
2412.03904.tldr: It is found that instrumental self-reasoning ability emerges only in the most capable frontier models and that it is highly context-dependent.

2412.16325.title: Towards Safe and Honest AI Agents with Neural Self-Other Overlap
2412.16325.tldr: Self-Other Overlap (SOO) fine-tuning is presented, a promising approach in AI Safety that could substantially improve the ability to build honest artificial intelligence and pave the way for more trustworthy AI in broader domains.

2605.09773.title: Exploitation Without Deception: Dark Triad Feature Steering Reveals Separable Antisocial Circuits in Language Models

2605.06696.title: Hidden Coalitions in Multi-Agent AI: A Spectral Diagnostic from Internal Representations
2605.06696.tldr: The results demonstrate that analyzing hidden-state mutual information through spectral partitioning provides a scalable diagnostic for identifying representational coalitions, offering a valuable tool for monitoring emergent structure in distributed AI systems.

2508.06601.title: Deep Ignorance: Filtering Pretraining Data Builds Tamper-Resistant Safeguards into Open-Weight LLMs
2508.06601.tldr: This paper introduces a multi-stage pipeline for scalable data filtering and shows that it offers a tractable and effective method for minimizing biothreat proxy knowledge in LLMs, and establishes pretraining data curation as a promising layer of defense for open-weight AI systems.

2501.17315.title: A sketch of an AI control safety case
2501.17315.tldr: An argument that a hypothetical LLM agent deployed internally at an AI company won't exfiltrate sensitive information is sketched, a step toward more concrete arguments that can be used to show that a dangerously capable LLM agent is safe to deploy.

2411.08088.title: Safety case template for frontier AI: A cyber inability argument
2411.08088.tldr: A safety case template for offensive cyber capabilities is proposed, illustrating how developers could argue that a model does not have capabilities posing unacceptable cyber risks by breaking down the main claim into progressively specific sub-claims, each supported by evidence.

2505.03989.title: An alignment safety case sketch based on debate
2505.03989.tldr: The value of debate for AI safety is outlined, as well as the assumptions and further research required to make debate work, by sketching an ``alignment safety case'' -- an argument that an AI system will not autonomously take actions which could lead to egregious harm, despite being able to do so.

2503.04744.title: Safety Cases: A Scalable Approach to Frontier AI Safety
2503.04744.tldr: It is argued that writing and reviewing safety cases would substantially assist in the fulfilment of many of the Frontier AI Safety Commitments.

2602.15001.title: Boundary Point Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
2602.15001.tldr: Boundary Point Jailbreaking (BPJ), a new class of automated jailbreak attacks that evade the strongest industry-deployed safeguards, is introduced, believed to be the first fully automated attack algorithm that succeeds in developing universal jailbreaks against Constitutional Classifiers, as well as the first automated attack algorithm that succeeds against GPT-5's input classifier without relying on human attack seeds.

2602.08630.title: Debate is efficient with your time
2602.08630.tldr: Surprisingly, it is found that PSPACE/poly (the class of problems which debate can efficiently decide) is precisely the class of functions decidable with O(log n) queries, which shows that debate is remarkably query-efficient: even for highly complex problems, logarithmic oversight suffices.

2605.06390.title: Automated alignment is harder than you think
2605.06390.tldr: It is argued that, even when research agents are not scheming to deliberately sabotage alignment work, this plan could produce compelling but catastrophically misleading safety assessments resulting in the unintentional deployment of misaligned AI.

2606.12618.title: "Did you lie?" Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms
2606.12618.tldr: Current lie detectors for language models cannot support high-confidence claims about model beliefs, and research directions are suggested that may address some of their current limitations.

2507.02977.title: LLMs are Capable of Misaligned Behavior Under Explicit Prohibition and Surveillance
2507.02977.tldr: In this paper, LLMs are tasked with completing an impossible quiz, while they are in a sandbox, monitored, told about these measures and instructed not to cheat, revealing a fundamental tension between goal-directed behavior and alignment in current LLMs.

2605.26438.title: LURE: Live-Usage Replay Evaluations for Reducing Evaluation Awareness
2605.26438.tldr: This work proposes LURE (Live-Usage Replay Evaluations), a method for constructing deployment-like evaluations by replaying realistic agentic interaction trajectories and appending evaluation prompt at the end, and introduces an automated pipeline for measuring evaluation realism.

2404.13076.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
2404.13076.tldr: By fine-tuning LLMs, a linear correlation between self-recognition capability and the strength of self-preference bias is discovered and how self-recognition can interfere with unbiased evaluations and AI safety more generally is discussed.

2501.18837.title: Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming
2501.18837.tldr: Constitutional Classifiers are introduced: safeguards trained on synthetic data, generated by prompting LLMs with natural language rules specifying permitted and restricted content, demonstrating that defending against universal jailbreaks while maintaining practical deployment viability is tractable.

2406.10162.title: Sycophancy to Subterfuge: Investigating Reward-Tampering in Large Language Models
2406.10162.tldr: It is demonstrated that LLMs can generalize from common forms of specification gaming to more pernicious reward tampering and that such behavior may be nontrivial to remove.

2409.12822.title: Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF
2409.12822.tldr: This work asks time-constrained human subjects to evaluate the correctness of model outputs and calculate humans' accuracy against gold labels and highlights an important failure mode of RLHF, which makes the model harder to evaluate.

2406.15518.title: Steering Without Side Effects: Improving Post-Deployment Control of Language Models
2406.15518.tldr: KTS, a technique that decreases the side effects of steering while retaining its benefits, by first training a model to minimize Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between a steered and unsteered model on benign inputs, then steering the model that has undergone this training.

2410.21514.title: Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models
2410.21514.tldr: These evaluations are designed to provide evidence that a given model, operating under a given set of mitigations, could not successfully sabotage a frontier model developer or other large organization's activities in any of these ways.

2407.04549.title: Spontaneous Reward Hacking in Iterative Self-Refinement
2407.04549.tldr: Using an essay editing task, it is shown that iterative self-refinement leads to deviation between the language model evaluator and human judgment, demonstrating that reward hacking can occur spontaneously in-context with the use of iterative self-refinement.

2602.22755.title: AuditBench: Evaluating Alignment Auditing Techniques on Models with Hidden Behaviors
2602.22755.tldr: An investigator agent is developed that autonomously employs a configurable set of auditing tools and observes a tool-to-agent gap, where tools that perform well in standalone non-agentic evaluations fail to translate into improved performance when used with the investigator agent.

2310.13548.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
2310.13548.tldr: This work demonstrates that five state-of-the-art AI assistants consistently exhibit sycophancy across four varied free-form text-generation tasks, and analyzes existing human preference data to determine the role of human preference judgments in such behavior.

2601.04603.title: Constitutional Classifiers++: Efficient Production-Grade Defenses against Universal Jailbreaks
2601.04603.tldr: Enhanced Constitutional Classifiers are introduced that deliver production-grade jailbreak robustness with dramatically reduced computational costs and refusal rates compared to previous-generation defenses and establish Constitutional Classifiers as practical and efficient safeguards for large language models.

2402.04249.title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
2402.04249.tldr: This work introduces HarmBench, a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming, and identifies several desirable properties previously unaccounted for in red teaming evaluations and systematically design HarmBench to meet these criteria.

2403.03218.title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
2403.03218.tldr: RMU is developed, a state-of-the-art unlearning method based on controlling model representations that reduces model performance on WMDP while maintaining general capabilities in areas such as biology and computer science, suggesting that unlearning may be a concrete path towards reducing malicious use from LLMs.

2408.00761.title: Tamper-Resistant Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
2408.00761.tldr: This work develops a method, called TAR, for building tamper-resistant safeguards into open-weight LLMs such that adversaries cannot remove the safeguards even after hundreds of steps of fine-tuning, and finds that this method greatly improves tamper-resistance while preserving benign capabilities.

2407.21792.title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?
2407.21792.tldr: A comprehensive meta-analysis of AI safety benchmarks is conducted, empirically analyzing their correlation with general capabilities across dozens of models and providing a survey of existing directions in AI safety, to provide a more rigorous framework for AI safety research.

2503.03750.title: The MASK Benchmark: Disentangling Honesty From Accuracy in AI Systems
2503.03750.tldr: It is found that simple methods, such as representation engineering interventions, can improve honesty, and the growing need for robust evaluations and effective interventions to ensure LLMs remain trustworthy is underscored.

2507.21509.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
2507.21509.tldr: Directions in the model's activation space-persona vectors-underlying several traits, such as evil, sycophancy, and propensity to hallucinate are identified, and it is confirmed that these vectors can be used to monitor fluctuations in the Assistant's personality at deployment time.

2502.17424.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
2502.17424.tldr: Finetuning a large language model on a narrow task of writing insecure code causes a broad range of concerning behaviours unrelated to coding, which underscores the need for a mature science of alignment, which can predict when and why interventions may induce misaligned behaviour.

2507.14805.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
2507.14805.tldr: It is concluded that subliminal learning is a general phenomenon that presents an unexpected pitfall for AI development because it could propagate unintended traits, even when developers try to prevent this via data filtering.

2506.13206.title: Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
2506.13206.tldr: It is found that sleeper agents can often describe and explain their backdoor triggers, demonstrating a kind of self-awareness, and CoT monitoring can expose these behaviors but is unreliable, and three new datasets are released that induce emergent misalignment while preserving model capabilities.

2508.17511.title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking harmless tasks generalizes to misaligned behavior in LLMs
2508.17511.tldr: Preliminary evidence that models that learn to reward hack may generalize to more harmful forms of misalignment is provided, though confirmation with more realistic tasks and training methods is needed.

2604.25891.title: Conditional misalignment: common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers
2604.25891.tldr: The results imply that in realistic post-training, where misaligned data is typically combined with benign data, models may be conditionally misaligned even if standard evaluations look clean.

2407.15549.title: Latent Adversarial Training Improves Robustness to Persistent Harmful Behaviors in LLMs
2407.15549.tldr: Targeted LAT is used to improve robustness to jailbreaks, outperforming a strong R2D2 baseline with orders of magnitude less compute and to more effectively remove backdoors with no knowledge of the trigger.

2604.22082.title: Removing Sandbagging in LLMs by Training with Weak Supervision
2604.22082.tldr: It is found that training with weak supervision can reliably elicit sandbagging models when supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning are combined: SFT on weak demonstrations breaks the sandbagging behavior, enabling RL to then fully elicit performance.

2606.08892.title: Diffuse AI Control on Fuzzy Tasks
2606.08892.tldr: A framework that considers AI control as an adversarial game between a blue team and a red team and proposes an adversarial optimization algorithm for the blue team that discovers more robust prompts for the weak model, which produces a blue team prompt that the red team optimization fails to exploit.

2403.10462.title: Safety Cases: How to Justify the Safety of Advanced AI Systems
2403.10462.tldr: This work proposes a framework for organizing a safety case and discusses four categories of arguments to justify safety: total inability to cause a catastrophe, sufficiently strong control measures, trustworthiness despite capability to cause harm, and -- if AI systems become much more powerful -- deference to credible AI advisors.

2308.10248.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
2308.10248.tldr: Activation Addition (ActAdd) is introduced, which contrasts the intermediate activations on prompt pairs to compute a steering vector and yields inference-time control over high-level output properties (like topic and sentiment) while preserving performance on off-target tasks.

2602.05532.title: Split Personality Training: Revealing Latent Knowledge Through Alternate Personalities
2602.05532.tldr: Split Personality Training (SPT) is introduced, which fine-tunes a second ``honest persona''into LoRA parameters that remain inactive during normal operation, enabling the honest persona to review the response while accessing the main model's latent states.

2310.13798.title: Specific versus General Principles for Constitutional AI
2310.13798.tldr: It is found that the largest dialogue models can generalize from this short constitution, resulting in harmless assistants with no stated interest in specific motivations like power, which suggests both general and specific principles have value for steering AI safely.

2411.15114.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
2411.15114.tldr: RE-Bench is introduced, which consists of 7 challenging, open-ended ML research engineering environments and data from 71 8-hour attempts by 61 distinct human experts, and finds that modern AI agents possess significant expertise in many ML topics and can generate and test solutions over ten times faster than humans, at much lower cost.

2609.14998.title: Shallow Beliefs: Synthetic document finetuning does not inoculate against emergent misalignment from reward hacking
2609.14998.tldr: It is shown that SDF can predictably steer downstream generalization when inserting new associations, but struggles and has unpredictable effects when overriding existing associations, such as that between reward hacking and misalignment that produces EM.

2601.04175.title: Legal Alignment for Safe and Ethical AI
2601.04175.tldr: A survey of the emerging field of legal alignment that aims to fill this gap and systematize research that studies how legal rules, principles, and methods can be leveraged to address problems of alignment and inform the design of AI systems that operate safely and ethically.

2512.03399.title: Full-Stack Alignment: Co-Aligning AI and Institutions with Thick Models of Value
2512.03399.tldr: Thick models of value will be needed to structure the way values and norms are represented, enabling systems to distinguish enduring values from fleeting preferences, to model the social embedding of individual choices, and to reason normatively, applying values in new domains.

2506.17434.title: Resource Rational Contractualism Should Guide AI Alignment
2506.17434.tldr: Resource-Rational Contractualism (RRC) is proposed, a framework where AI systems approximate the agreements rational parties would form by drawing on a toolbox of normatively-grounded, cognitively-inspired heuristics that trade effort for accuracy.

2410.09024.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
2410.09024.tldr: Leading LLMs are surprisingly compliant with malicious agent requests without jailbreaking, and simple universal jailbreak templates can be adapted to effectively jailbreak agents, and these jailbreaks enable coherent and malicious multi-step agent behavior and retain model capabilities.

2406.04313.title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
2406.04313.tldr: This work presents an approach, inspired by recent advances in representation engineering, that interrupts the models as they respond with harmful outputs with circuit breakers, representing a significant step forward in the development of reliable safeguards to harmful behavior and adversarial attacks.

2506.20702.title: The Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities
2506.20702.tldr: This document organises AI safety research domains into three types: challenges with creating trustworthy AI systems (Development), challenges with evaluating their risks (Assessment), and challenges with monitoring and intervening after deployment (Control).

2509.17938.title: D-REX: A Benchmark for Detecting Deceptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
2509.17938.tldr: The Deceptive Reasoning Exposure Suite (D-REX) is introduced, a novel dataset designed to evaluate the discrepancy between a model's internal reasoning process and its final output, highlighting the urgent need for new techniques that scrutinize the internal processes of LLMs, not just their final outputs.

2405.06624.title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI: A Framework for Ensuring Robust and Reliable AI Systems
2405.06624.tldr: This paper introduces and defines a family of approaches to AI safety, which it will refer to as guaranteed safe (GS) AI, which aim to produce AI systems which are equipped with high-assurance quantitative safety guarantees.

2502.15657.title: Superintelligent Agents Pose Catastrophic Risks: Can Scientist AI Offer a Safer Path?
2502.15657.tldr: A Scientist AI is proposed as a core building block for further advances the development of a non-agentic AI system that is trustworthy and safe by design, which is designed to explain the world from observations, as opposed to taking actions in it to imitate or please humans.

2407.14981.title: Open Problems in Technical AI Governance
2407.14981.tldr: This paper explains what technical AI governance is, why it is important, and presents a taxonomy and incomplete catalog of its open problems, intended as a resource for technical researchers or research funders looking to contribute to AI governance.

2405.18540.title: Learning diverse attacks on large language models for robust red-teaming and safety tuning
2405.18540.tldr: This work proposes to use GFlowNet fine-tuning followed by a secondary smoothing phase, to train the attacker model to generate diverse and effective attack prompts, and finds that the attacks generated by the method are effective against a wide range of target LLMs, both with and without safety tuning, and transfer well between target LLMs.

2501.11183.title: Can Safety Fine-Tuning Be More Principled? Lessons Learned from Cybersecurity
2501.11183.tldr: It is shown how current defenses are insufficient to prevent new adversarial jailbreak attacks, reward hacking, and loss of control problems, and the need for new and more principled approaches to designing safe models, which are architected for security from the beginning is described.

2404.03027.title: JailBreakV: A Benchmark for Assessing the Robustness of MultiModal Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
2404.03027.tldr: This paper introduces JailBreakV-28K, a pioneering benchmark designed to assess the transferability of LLM jailbreak techniques to MLLMs, thereby evaluating the robustness of MLLMs against diverse jailbreak attacks and highlighting a critical vulnerability in MLLMs that stems from their text-processing capabilities.

2410.05295.title: AutoDAN-Turbo: A Lifelong Agent for Strategy Self-Exploration to Jailbreak LLMs
2410.05295.tldr: AutoDAN-Turbo is a black-box jailbreak method that can automatically discover as many jailbreak strategies as possible from scratch, without any human intervention or predefined scopes, and use them for red-teaming.

2403.04957.title: Automatic and Universal Prompt Injection Attacks against Large Language Models
2403.04957.tldr: This work introduces a unified framework for understanding the objectives of prompt injection attacks and presents an automated gradient-based method for generating highly effective and universal prompt injection data, even in the face of defensive measures.

2403.09513.title: AdaShield: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models from Structure-based Attack via Adaptive Shield Prompting
2403.09513.tldr: This work proposes AdaShield Prompting, which prepends inputs with defense prompts to defend MLLMs against structure-based jailbreak attacks without fine-tuning MLLMs or training additional modules (e.g., post-stage content detector).

2403.17336.title: Don't Listen To Me: Understanding and Exploring Jailbreak Prompts of Large Language Models
2403.17336.tldr: It is observed that users often succeeded in jailbreak prompts generation regardless of their expertise in LLMs, and a system using AI as the assistant to automate the process of jailbreak prompt generation was developed.

2409.17504.title: HaloScope: Harnessing Unlabeled LLM Generations for Hallucination Detection
2409.17504.tldr: HaloScope is introduced, a novel learning framework that leverages the unlabeled LLM generations in the wild for hallucination detection, and presents an automated membership estimation score for distinguishing between truthful and untruthful generations within unlabeled mixture data, thereby enabling the training of a binary truthfulness classifier on top.

2402.14968.title: Mitigating Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack with Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment
2402.14968.tldr: The Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment method, inspired by an analogy with the concept of backdoor attacks, is proposed to effectively defend against the Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack under the setting of Language-Model-as-a-Service (LMaaS).

2411.03554.title: Benchmarking Vision Language Model Unlearning via Fictitious Facial Identity Dataset
2411.03554.tldr: This work introduces Facial Identity Unlearning Benchmark (FIUBench), a novel VLM unlearning benchmark designed to robustly evaluate the effectiveness of unlearning algorithms under the Right to be Forgotten setting and highlights the importance of privacy attacks for robust evaluations.

2405.19524.title: AI Risk Management Should Incorporate Both Safety and Security
2405.19524.tldr: It is advocated that stakeholders in AI risk management should be aware of the nuances, synergies, and interplay between safety and security, and unambiguously take into account the perspectives of both disciplines in order to devise mostly effective and holistic risk mitigation approaches.

2409.19993.title: Mitigating Backdoor Threats to Large Language Models: Advancement and Challenges
2409.19993.tldr: A comprehensive survey of emerging backdoor threats to LLMs that appear during LLM development or inference is presented, and recent advancement in both defense and detection strategies for mitigating backdoor threats to LLMs are covered.
2409.19993.venue: 2024 60th Annual Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing

2410.08660.title: RePD: Defending Jailbreak Attack through a Retrieval-based Prompt Decomposition Process
2410.08660.tldr: The efficacy of the proposed RePD is demonstrated in enhancing the resilience of LLMs against jailbreak attacks, without compromising their performance in responding to typical user requests.
2410.08660.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.03770.title: JailDAM: Jailbreak Detection with Adaptive Memory for Vision-Language Model
2504.03770.tldr: This work introduces a test-time adaptive framework called JAILDAM, which leverages a memory-based approach guided by policy-driven unsafe knowledge representations, eliminating the need for explicit exposure to harmful data.

2606.22673.title: AgentLens: Interpretable Safety Steering via Mechanistic Subspaces for Multi-Turn Coding Agent
2606.22673.tldr: This paper proposes AgentLens (Mechanistic Subspace Intervention and Steering), a white-box defense framework that performs runtime safety detection and representation-level mitigation for coding agents and introduces the Mechanistic Agent Safety benchmark, comprising comprehensively annotated multi-turn execution trajectories across 194 tasks.

2604.27861.title: TwinGate: Stateful Defense against Decompositional Jailbreaks in Untraceable Traffic via Asymmetric Contrastive Learning
2604.27861.tldr: TwinGate achieves high malicious intent recall at a remarkably low false positive rate while remaining highly robust against adaptive attacks, and substantially outperforms stateful and stateless baselines, delivering superior throughput and reduced latency.

2510.05379.title: AutoDAN-Reasoning: Enhancing Strategies Exploration based Jailbreak Attacks with Test-Time Scaling
2510.05379.tldr: Two distinct scaling methods are introduced: Best-of-N and Beam Search, which conduct a more exhaustive search by exploring combinations of strategies from the library to discover more potent and synergistic attack vectors.

2609.05903.title: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
2609.05903.tldr: EvoSafeHarness is a safety-specific optimization framework that synthesizes a deployable harness for a frozen model in a target domain, guided by model behavior, domain specifications, and fresh-context adversarial review to reject benchmark-specific rules.

2608.27496.title: ROPE: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement against Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.27496.tldr: ROPE is presented, which is anchored in a structural notion of trust, and holds attack success rate to 1.6--2.6 while retaining 82--100% of undefended clean utility, significantly exceeding state-of-the-art system-level defenses in utility while attaining comparable or better security.

2603.30016.title: Architecting Secure AI Agents: Perspectives on System-Level Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
2603.30016.tldr: The vision for system-level defenses against indirect prompt injection attacks is discussed, which highlight the value of system-level defenses, which serve as the skeleton of agentic systems by structuring and controlling agent behaviors, integrating rule-based and model-based security checks, and enabling more targeted research on model robustness and human interaction.

2601.10173.title: ReasAlign: Reasoning Enhanced Safety Alignment against Prompt Injection Attack
2601.10173.tldr: Comprehensive evaluations show that ReasAlign achieves the best trade-off between security and utility, establishing a robust and practical defense against prompt injection attacks in real-world agentic systems.

2512.00966.title: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection via Instruction-Following Intent Analysis
2512.00966.tldr: Results demonstrate that IntentGuard achieves no utility degradation in all but one setting and strong robustness against adaptive prompt injection attacks (e.g., reducing attack success rates from 100% to 8.5% in a Mind2Web scenario).

2410.10871.title: Applying Refusal-Vector Ablation to Llama 3.1 70B Agents
2410.10871.tldr: This study applies refusal-vector ablation to Llama 3.1 70B and implements a simple agent scaffolding to create an unrestricted agent, finding that safety fine-tuning in chat models does not generalize well to agentic behavior.

2504.07831.title: Deceptive Automated Interpretability: Language Models Coordinating to Fool Oversight Systems
2504.07831.tldr: It is demonstrated how AI agents can coordinate to deceive oversight systems using automated interpretability of neural networks, and it is found that models can scheme to develop deceptive strategies when they believe the detection of harmful features might lead to negative consequences for themselves.

2511.11759.title: Can AI Models be Jailbroken to Phish Elderly Victims? An End-to-End Evaluation
2511.11759.tldr: This work uniquely demonstrates the complete attack pipeline targeting elderly populations, highlighting that current AI safety measures fail to protect those most vulnerable to fraud.

2310.20624.title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training in Llama 2-Chat 70B
2310.20624.tldr: It is argued that evaluating risks from fine-tuning should be a core part of risk assessments for releasing model weights, while there is considerable uncertainty about the scope of risks from current models.

2406.11717.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
2406.11717.tldr: This work shows that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters in size, and proposes a novel white-box jailbreak method that surgically disables refusal with minimal effect on other capabilities.

2407.14435.title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
2407.14435.tldr: This paper introduces JumpReLU SAEs, which achieve state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity level on Gemma 2 9B activations, compared to other recent advances such as Gated and TopK SAEs.

2406.11944.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
2406.11944.tldr: This work introduces a novel method for using transcoders to perform weights-based circuit analysis through MLP sublayers, and suggests that transcoders can prove effective in decomposing model computations involving MLPs into interpretable circuits.

2404.15255.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
2404.15255.tldr: What evidence patching experiments provide about circuits, and on the choice of metric and associated pitfalls, are focused on.

2501.16496.title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
2501.16496.tldr: This forward-facing review discusses the current frontier of mechanistic interpretability and the open problems that the field may benefit from prioritizing.

2503.17547.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
2503.17547.tldr: Matryoshka SAEs are believed to be a superior alternative for practical tasks, as they enable training arbitrarily large SAEs while retaining interpretable features at different levels of abstraction.

2412.06410.title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
2412.06410.tldr: It is shown that BatchTopK SAEs consistently outperform TopK SAEs in reconstructing activations from GPT-2 Small and Gemma 2 2B, and achieve comparable performance to state-of-the-art JumpReLU SAEs.

2503.09532.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
2503.09532.tldr: SAEBench is introduced, a comprehensive evaluation suite that measures SAE performance across eight diverse metrics, spanning interpretability, feature disentanglement and practical applications like unlearning, and enables researchers to study scaling trends and make nuanced comparisons between different SAE architectures and training methodologies.

2502.16681.title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
2502.16681.tldr: Although SAEs initially appear promising for identifying spurious correlations, detecting poor dataset quality, and training multi-token probes, they are unable to design ensemble methods combining SAEs with baselines that consistently outperform ensemble methods solely using baselines.

2508.21258.title: RelP: Faithful and Efficient Circuit Discovery in Language Models via Relevance Patching
2508.21258.tldr: Relevance Patching (RelP), which replaces the local gradients in attribution patching with propagation coefficients derived from Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP), is introduced, showing that it more accurately approximates activation patching than standard attribution patching.

2411.14257.title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models
2411.14257.tldr: It is demonstrated that despite the sparse autoencoders being trained on the base model, these directions have a causal effect on the chat model's refusal behavior, suggesting that chat finetuning has repurposed this existing mechanism.

2311.17030.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
2311.17030.tldr: This work demonstrates thatMechanistic interpretability aims to understand model behaviors in terms of specific, interpretable features, and shows a link to rank-1 fact editing, providing a mechanistic explanation for previous work observing an inconsistency between fact editing performance and fact localization.

2309.16042.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
2309.16042.tldr: In several settings of localization and circuit discovery in language models, it is found that varying these hyperparameters could lead to disparate interpretability results.

2510.20487.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed
2510.20487.tldr: Adding a steering vector to an LLM's activations can suppress evaluation-awareness and make the model act like it is deployed during evaluation, suggesting that AI evaluators could improve the reliability of safety evaluations by steering models to act like they are deployed.

2606.26071.title: Model Forensics: Investigating Whether Concerning Behavior Reflects Misalignment
2606.26071.tldr: A baseline protocol for model forensics consisting of two steps, iterated as needed, that establishes that Kimi K2 Thinking takes shortcuts due to a genuine disposition towards low-effort actions, and establishes that DeepSeek R1 deceives out of a desire to be consistent with a previous instance of itself.

2506.18167.title: Understanding Reasoning in Thinking Language Models via Steering Vectors
2506.18167.tldr: This work identifies several reasoning behaviors exhibited by thinking models, including expressing uncertainty, generating examples for hypothesis validation, and backtracking in reasoning chains, and provides a method to modulate specific aspects of the model's reasoning process, such as its tendency to backtrack or express uncertainty.

2602.17532.title: Systematic Evaluation of Single-Cell Foundation Model Interpretability Reveals Attention Captures Co-Expression Rather Than Unique Regulatory Signal
2602.17532.tldr: The Cell-State Stratified Interpretability (CSSI) addresses an attention-specific scaling failure, improving GRN recovery up to 1.85x and establishes reusable quality-control standards for the field.

2603.02952.title: Sparse autoencoders reveal organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic in single-cell foundation models: a comparative atlas of Geneformer and scGPT
2603.02952.tldr: These models have internalized organized biological knowledge, including pathway membership, protein interactions, functional modules, and hierarchical abstraction, yet they encode minimal causal regulatory logic.

2603.11940.title: Exhaustive Circuit Mapping of a Single-Cell Foundation Model Reveals Massive Redundancy, Heavy-Tailed Hub Architecture, and Layer-Dependent Differentiation Control
2603.11940.tldr: Three experiments that address limitations in mechanical interpretability of biological foundation models through exhaustive circuit tracing, higher order combinatorial ablation, and causal trajectory steering in Geneformer, a transformer based single cell foundation model are presented.

2603.10261.title: Discovery of a Hematopoietic Manifold in scGPT Yields a Method for Extracting Performant Algorithms from Biological Foundation Model Internals
2603.10261.tldr: It is reported that scGPT internally encodes a compact hematopoietic manifold with significant developmental branch structure, validated on a strict non-overlap Tabula Sapiens external panel and confirmed via frozen-head zero-shot transfer to an independent multi-donor immune panel.

2510.05179.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
2510.05179.tldr: Caution is suggested about deploying current models in roles with minimal human oversight and access to sensitive information and the importance of further research into the safety and alignment of agentic AI models is underscored.

2505.14633.title: Will AI Tell Lies to Save Sick Children? Litmus-Testing AI Values Prioritization with AIRiskDilemmas
2505.14633.tldr: It is shown that values in LitmusValues can predict for both seen risky behaviors in AIRiskDilemmas and unseen risky behaviors in HarmBench, a self-consistent set of predicted value priorities that uncover potential risks.

2511.01689.title: Open Character Training: Shaping the Persona of AI Assistants through Constitutional AI
2511.01689.tldr: This work introduces the first open implementation of character training, leveraging Constitutional AI and a new data pipeline using synthetic introspective data to shape the assistant persona in a more effective and controlled manner than alternatives such as constraining system prompts or activation steering.

2312.06681.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
2312.06681.tldr: This work introduces Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), an innovative method for steering language models by modifying their activations during forward passes by averaging the difference in residual stream activations between pairs of positive and negative examples of a particular behavior.
2312.06681.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2302.00805.title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Risks and Strategies
2302.00805.tldr: It is thought that conditioning approaches for predictive models represent the safest known way of eliciting human-level and slightly superhuman capabilities from large language models and other similar future models.

2501.04952.title: Open Problems in Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
2501.04952.tldr: This paper identifies key limitations that prevent unlearning from serving as a comprehensive solution for AI safety, particularly in managing dual-use knowledge in sensitive domains like cybersecurity and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear safety.

2510.13653.title: International AI Safety Report 2025: First Key Update: Capabilities and Risk Implications
2510.13653.tldr: This update examines how AI capabilities have improved since the first Report, then focuses on key risk areas where substantial new evidence warrants updated assessments.

2511.19863.title: International AI Safety Report 2025: Second Key Update: Technical Safeguards and Risk Management

2504.12914.title: In Which Areas of Technical AI Safety Could Geopolitical Rivals Cooperate?
2504.12914.tldr: This analysis finds that research into AI verification mechanisms and shared protocols may be suitable areas for international cooperation, and aims to help researchers and governments identify and mitigate the risks of international cooperation on AI safety research, so that the benefits of cooperation can be fully realised.
2504.12914.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2411.02193.title: Improving Steering Vectors by Targeting Sparse Autoencoder Features
2411.02193.tldr: This work uses SAEs to measure the effects of steering vectors, giving a method that can be used to understand the causal effect of any steering vector intervention, and develops an improved steering method, SAE-Targeted Steering (SAE-TS), which finds steering vectors to target specific SAE features while minimizing unintended side effects.

2410.19278.title: Applying sparse autoencoders to unlearn knowledge in language models
2410.19278.tldr: It is found that intervening using multiple SAE features simultaneously can unlearn multiple different topics, but with similar or larger unwanted side-effects than the existing Representation Misdirection for Unlearning technique.

2406.17759.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
2406.17759.tldr: The mystery of why models have so many seemingly redundant induction heads is explored, SAEs are used to motivate the hypothesis that some are long-prefix whereas others are short-prefix, and SAEs find a sparse, interpretable decomposition are shown.

2606.00995.title: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation
2606.00995.tldr: This work shows that subliminal learning is mediated by a single steering vector, i.e. a vector added to the model's activations, and finds that adaptive optimizers are necessary for subliminal learning in language models: activation gradients on steered data carry a small but consistent component along the steering direction, and non-adaptive optimizers impede this by allowing outlier gradients to dominate.

2505.24360.title: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
2505.24360.tldr: This work applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and ITDA to a large text-to-image diffusion model, Flux 1, and considers the interpretability of embeddings of both by introducing a visual automated interpretation pipeline, finding that SAEs accurately reconstruct residual stream embeddings and beat MLP neurons on interpretability.

2310.10348.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
2310.10348.tldr: This work shows that a simple method based on attribution patching outperforms all existing methods while requiring just two forward passes and a backward pass, and averages over all tasks finds that this method has greater AUC from circuit recovery than other methods.
2310.10348.venue: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2304.14997.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
2304.14997.tldr: This paper systematizes the mechanistic interpretability process they followed and automates one of the process' steps: to identify the circuit that implements the specified behavior in the model's computational graph.

2502.04878.title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
2502.04878.tldr: Using meta-SAEs -- SAEs trained on the decoder matrix of another SAE -- it is found that latents in SAEs often decompose into combinations of latents from a smaller SAE, showing that larger SAE latents are not atomic.

2405.12241.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
2405.12241.tldr: End-to-end (e2e) sparse dictionary learning is proposed, a method for training SAEs that ensures the features learned are functionally important by minimizing the KL divergence between the output distributions of the original model and the model with SAE activations inserted.

2410.08417.title: Bilinear MLPs enable weight-based mechanistic interpretability
2410.08417.tldr: The results demonstrate that bilinear layers serve as an interpretable drop-in replacement for current activation functions and that weight-based interpretability is viable for understanding deep-learning models.

2501.14926.title: Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
2501.14926.tldr: This work introduces Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition (APD), a method that directly decomposes a neural network's parameters into components that are faithful to the parameters of the original network, require a minimal number of components to process any input, and are maximally simple.

2504.19475.title: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video
2504.19475.tldr: Prisma is presented, an open-source framework designed to accelerate vision mechanistic interpretability research, providing a unified toolkit for accessing 75+ vision and video transformers; support for sparse autoencoder, transcoder, and crosscoder training; a suite of 80+ pre-trained SAE weights; activation caching, circuit analysis tools, and visualization tools; and educational resources.

2410.11179.title: Interpretability as Compression: Reconsidering SAE Explanations of Neural Activations with MDL-SAEs
2410.11179.tldr: An information-theoretic framework for interpreting SAEs as lossy compression algorithms for communicating explanations of neural activations and appealing to the Minimal Description Length (MDL) principle to motivate explanations of activations which are both accurate and concise is presented.

2604.17837.title: Polysemantic Experts, Monosemantic Paths: Routing as Control in MoEs
2604.17837.tldr: A parameter-free decomposition for Mixture-of-Experts models is introduced that splits each layer's hidden state into a control signal that causally drives routing and an orthogonal content channel invisible to the router.

2309.08600.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
2309.08600.tldr: This work indicates that it is possible to resolve superposition in language models using a scalable, unsupervised method, and may serve as a foundation for future mechanistic interpretability work, which it is hoped will enable greater model transparency and steerability.

2410.13928.title: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
2410.13928.tldr: An open-source automated pipeline to generate and evaluate natural language explanations for SAE features using LLMs is built, and large-scale analysis confirms that SAE latents are indeed much more interpretable than neurons, even when neurons are sparsified using top-$k$ postprocessing.

2412.12480.title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
2412.12480.tldr: This paper investigates how well AI systems can generate and act on their own strategies for subverting control protocols whilst operating statelessly (without shared memory between contexts), and develops Subversion Strategy Eval, a suite of eight environments, covering a range of protocols and strategic capabilities, and six sets of affordances that help isolate individual capabilities.

2410.13215.title: Balancing Label Quantity and Quality for Scalable Elicitation
2410.13215.tldr: The microeconomics of the quantity-quality tradeoff on binary NLP classification tasks used in Burns et al. (2023) are explored, and the accuracy of supervised fine-tuning can be improved by up to 5 percentage points at a fixed labeling budget by adding a few-shot prompt to make use of the model's existing knowledge of the task.

2312.01037.title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge from Quirky Language Models
2312.01037.tldr: It is found that, especially in middle layers, linear probes usually report an LM's knowledge independently of what the LM outputs, enabling us to elicit the correct answer despite the model's untruthful output.

2505.23575.title: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
2505.23575.tldr: A hybrid protocol that independently scores model reasoning and actions, and combines them using a weighted average consistently outperforms both CoT and action-only monitors across all tested models and tasks, with detection rates twice higher than action-only monitoring for subtle deception scenarios.

2506.03056.title: Corrigibility as a Singular Target: A Vision for Inherently Reliable Foundation Models

2407.06232.title: Operationalising AI governance through ethics-based auditing: An industry case study
2407.06232.tldr: The case study presents a detailed description of the organisational context in which EBA procedures must be integrated to be feasible and effective and suggests that the main difficulties large multinational organisations face when conducting EBA mirror classical governance challenges.

2407.05339.title: Challenges and Best Practices in Corporate AI Governance:Lessons from the Biopharmaceutical Industry
2407.05339.tldr: Companies seeking to operationalize AI governance are encouraged to build on existing policies and governance structures, use pragmatic and action-oriented terminology, focus on risk management in development and procurement, and empower employees through continuous education and change management.

2410.08811.title: PoisonBench: Assessing Large Language Model Vulnerability to Data Poisoning
2410.08811.tldr: PoisonBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating large language models' susceptibility to data poisoning during preference learning, exposing weaknesses in current preference learning techniques, highlighting the urgent need for more robust defenses against malicious models and data manipulation.

2505.22637.title: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
2505.22637.tldr: The influence of prompt types and the geometry of activation differences on steering reliability are studied to suggest that vector steering is unreliable when the target behavior is not represented by a coherent direction.

2411.01220.title: Enhancing Neural Network Interpretability with Feature-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
2411.01220.tldr: The results suggest that the similarity between features learned by different SAEs can be leveraged to improve SAE training, thereby enhancing performance and the usefulness of SAEs for model interpretability.

2410.06981.title: Quantifying Feature Space Universality Across Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2410.06981.tldr: A new variation of the universality hypothesis called Analogous Feature Universality is introduced, which hypothesize that even if SAEs across different models learn different feature representations, the spaces spanned by SAE features are similar, such that one SAE space is similar to another SAE space under rotation-invariant transformations.

2505.22310.title: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
2505.22310.tldr: It is made the surprising discovery that forget-set accuracy can recover from around 50% post-unlearning to nearly 100% with fine-tuning on just the retain set -- i.e., zero examples of the forget set.

2507.03068.title: Mitigating Goal Misgeneralization via Minimax Regret
2507.03068.tldr: It is shown that goal misgeneralization is possible under approximate optimization of the maximum expected value objective, but not the minimax expected regret (MMER) objective, and suggested that minimax expected regret is a promising approach to mitigating goal misgeneralization.

2512.08093.title: Training LLMs for Honesty via Confessions
2512.08093.tldr: This work proposes a method for eliciting an honest expression of an LLM's shortcomings via a self-reported confession, and finds that when the model lies or omits shortcomings in its"main"answer, it often confesses to these behaviors honestly, and this confession honesty modestly improves with training.

2512.20168.title: Odysseus: Jailbreaking Commercial Multimodal LLM-integrated Systems via Dual Steganography
2512.20168.tldr: Odysseus is a novel jailbreak paradigm that introduces dual steganography to covertly embed malicious queries and responses into benign-looking images, exposing a fundamental blind spot in existing defenses, and calling for rethinking cross-modal security in MLLM-integrated systems.

2510.13694.title: Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF: Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking

2603.15616.title: GlyphPrinter: Region-Grouped Direct Preference Optimization for Glyph-Accurate Visual Text Rendering
2603.15616.tldr: The proposed GlyphPrinter outperforms existing methods in glyph accuracy while maintaining a favorable balance between stylization and precision, and introduces Regional Reward Guidance, an inference strategy that samples from an optimal distribution with controllable glyph accuracy.

2606.13385.title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
2606.13385.tldr: StakeBench is introduced, a stakeholder-centric benchmark that systematically categorizes and attributes harm in real-world web agent systems for online shopping, and finds substantial and heterogeneous vulnerabilities in LLM-based web agents.

2608.04565.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents
2608.04565.tldr: This work studies the channel delivering search and page observations is a fragile security boundary and introduces Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that turns isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources.

2608.10933.title: SafeCA: Safe Cross-Attention Localization and Regulation for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Defense
2608.10933.tldr: This work experimentally and systematically analyzes the differences between clean and jailbreak samples in the cross-attention feature space, revealing for the first time a cumulative separation effect and a progressively increasing trend of linear separability between the two during the diffusion process.

2407.15211.title: Failures to Find Transferable Image Jailbreaks Between Vision-Language Models
2407.15211.tldr: A large-scale empirical study to assess the transferability of gradient-based universal image ``jailbreaks" using a diverse set of over 40 open-parameter VLMs finds that transferable gradient-based image jailbreaks are extremely difficult to obtain, suggesting that VLMs may be more robust to gradient-based transfer attacks.

2506.22777.title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2506.22777.tldr: VFT is proposed, a pre-RL fine-tuning intervention that trains models to explicitly acknowledge when they are influenced by prompt cues--hints which point to incorrect answers (e.g.,"a Stanford professor thinks the answer is A").

2511.02997.title: Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
2511.02997.tldr: This work systematically evaluate a range of control protocols in SHADE-Arena, a dataset of diverse agentic environments, finding that resampling for incrimination and deferring on critical actions perform best, and demonstrating the importance of denying attack policies access to protocol internals.

2511.02823.title: Optimizing AI Agent Attacks With Synthetic Data
2511.02823.tldr: This work shows how to optimize attack policies in SHADE-Arena, a dataset of diverse realistic control environments by decomposing attack capability into five constituent skills -- suspicion modeling, attack selection, plan synthesis, execution and subtlety -- and optimizing each component individually.

2605.16626.title: SLEIGHT-Bench: A Benchmark of Evasion Attacks Against Agent Monitors
2605.16626.tldr: Several evasion strategies such as exploiting model priors, user instruction ambiguity, and state manipulation facilitate creating attacks that evade frontier monitors, which facilitate creating attacks that evade frontier monitors are identified.

2412.03556.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
2412.03556.tldr: Best-of-N (BoN) Jailbreaking is introduced, a simple black-box algorithm that jailbreaks frontier AI systems across modalities and indicates that language models are sensitive to seemingly innocuous changes to inputs, which attackers can exploit across modalities.

2402.17747.title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges of Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2402.17747.tldr: Modeling the human as Boltzmann-rational w.r.t. a belief over trajectories, it is proved conditions under which RLHF is guaranteed to result in policies that deceptively inflate their performance, overjustify their behavior to make an impression, or both.

2502.21262.title: Modeling Human Beliefs about AI Behavior for Scalable Oversight
2502.21262.tldr: It is suggested that modeling human beliefs can improve value learning and outlines practical research directions for implementing this approach to scalable oversight.

2502.13295.title: Demonstrating specification gaming in reasoning models
2502.13295.tldr: This work demonstrates LLM agent specification gaming by instructing models to win against a chess engine and suggests reasoning models may resort to hacking to solve difficult problems, as observed in OpenAI (2024)'s o1 Docker escape during cyber capabilities testing.

2406.02619.title: Unelicitable Backdoors in Language Models via Cryptographic Transformer Circuits
2406.02619.tldr: By demonstrating the feasibility of seamlessly integrating backdoors into transformer models, this paper fundamentally questions the efficacy of pre-deployment detection strategies and offers new insights into the offence-defence balance in AI safety and security.

2402.16835.title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
2402.16835.tldr: A comprehensive set of tests for the robustness and competitiveness of unlearning in the Who's Harry Potter (WHP) model from Eldan and Russinovich (2023) are applied and find higher-than-baseline amounts of knowledge can reliably be extracted.

2403.05030.title: Defending Against Unforeseen Failure Modes with Latent Adversarial Training
2403.05030.tldr: In image classification, text classification, and text generation tasks, it is shown that LAT usually improves both robustness to novel attacks and performance on clean data relative to AT, suggesting that LAT can be a promising tool for defending against failure modes that are not explicitly identified by developers.

2511.08594.title: Diverse Preference Learning for Capabilities and Alignment
2511.08594.tldr: This work proposes Soft Preference Learning, which decouples the entropy and cross-entropy terms in the KL penalty - allowing for fine-grained control over LLM generation diversity.

2502.05209.title: Model Tampering Attacks Enable More Rigorous Evaluations of LLM Capabilities
2502.05209.tldr: This work pits state-of-the-art techniques for removing harmful LLM capabilities against a suite of 5 input-space and 6 model tampering attacks and shows that model tampering attacks enable substantially more rigorous evaluations than input-space attacks alone.

2603.12277.title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
2603.12277.tldr: This work designs role probes to measure how LLMs internally perceive "who is speaking," and finds that injected text occupies the same representational space as the trusted role it imitates, revealing prompt injection as a measurable consequence of role perception.

2602.16080.title: Activation Steering via Generative Causal Mediation
2602.16080.tldr: Generative Causal Mediation, a procedure for selecting model components from contrastive long-form responses, to steer such diffuse concepts, successfully localizes concepts expressed in long-form responses and outperforms correlational probe-based baselines when steering with a sparse set of attention heads.

2505.09500.title: Layered Unlearning for Adversarial Relearning
2505.09500.tldr: An unlearning algorithm, Layered Unlearning (LU), that creates distinct inhibitory mechanisms for a growing subset of the data that improves robustness to adversarial relearning for several different unlearning methods and provides insight into the effect of post-training updates.

2507.09060.title: CALMA: A Process for Deriving Context-aligned Axes for Language Model Alignment
2507.09060.tldr: CALMA (Context-aligned Axes for Language Model Alignment), a grounded, participatory methodology for eliciting context-relevant axes for evaluation and alignment, is introduced, demonstrating the value of evaluation practices based on open-ended and use-case-driven processes.

2605.27355.title: Alignment Tampering: How Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
