2605.27355.tldr: This work introduces alignment tampering, a potential vulnerability where the LLM undergoing alignment influences the preference dataset, causing RLHF to amplify undesired behaviors and reveals structural vulnerabilities of current RLHF.

2406.18495.title: WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
2406.18495.tldr: WildGuard establishes state-of-the-art performance in open-source safety moderation across all the three tasks compared to ten strong existing open-source moderation models (e.g., up to 26.4% improvement on refusal detection).

2403.13787.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
2403.13787.tldr: The RewardBench dataset is a collection of prompt-chosen-rejected trios spanning chat, reasoning, and safety, to benchmark how reward models perform on challenging, structured and out-of-distribution queries and presents many findings on propensity for refusals, reasoning limitations, and instruction following shortcomings of various reward models towards a better understanding of the RLHF process.

2404.10271.title: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
2404.10271.tldr: It is argued that the field of social choice is well positioned to address questions to address fine-tuning and constitutional AI, and ways forward for this agenda are discussed.

2504.12501.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2504.12501.tldr: This book gives a comprehensive introduction to the core methods for post-training models for people with some level of quantitative background, organized around the canonical RLHF recipe.

2507.00018.title: Implicit Reward as the Bridge: A Unified View of SFT and DPO Connections
2507.00018.tldr: A unified theoretical framework bridging Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and preference learning in Large Language Model (LLM) post-training is presented, demonstrating that both SFT and preference learning methods like Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) operate within the same optimal policy-reward subspace.

2508.21016.title: Inference-Time Alignment Control for Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning Guidance
2508.21016.tldr: Reinforcement Learning Guidance is introduced, an inference-time method that adapts Classifier-Free Guidance by combining the outputs of the base and RL fine-tuned models via a geometric average, thereby offering unprecedented flexibility in controlling generative alignment.

2605.17504.title: A Distributional View for Visual Mechanistic Interpretability: KL-Minimal Soft-Constraint Principle
2605.17504.tldr: A theoretical distributional view is established for visual MI, which models the influence of a feature activation on the natural image distribution, thereby formulating a Kullback-Leibler (KL)-minimal optimization problem to model the MI task.

2410.06672.title: Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures
2410.06672.tldr: This work investigates two mainstream architectures for language modeling, namely Transformers and Mambas, to explore the extent of their mechanistic similarity and proposes to use Sparse Autoencoders to isolate interpretable features from these models and shows that most features are similar in these two models.

2504.20938.title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
2504.20938.tldr: Low-Rank Sparse Attention (Lorsa) is designed to address the challenge of attention superposition to understand attention-mediated interaction between features in different token positions, and achieves parity with SAE in interpretability while Lorsa exhibits superior circuit discovery properties.

2405.13868.title: Automatically Identifying Local and Global Circuits with Linear Computation Graphs
2405.13868.tldr: This work introduces its circuit discovery pipeline with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and a variant called Transcoders and a variant called Transcoders, and analyzes three kinds of circuits in GPT-2 Small, revealing new findings underlying existing discoveries.

2503.04249.title: How to Mitigate Overfitting in Weak-to-strong Generalization?
2503.04249.tldr: A two-stage framework that simultaneously improves the quality of supervision signals and the quality of input questions is proposed that significantly improves PGR compared to naive weak-to-strong generalization, even achieving up to 100\% PGR on some models.
2503.04249.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.11206.title: InferAligner: Inference-Time Alignment for Harmlessness through Cross-Model Guidance
2401.11206.tldr: InferAligner decouples harmlessness from helpfulness, a simple yet effective method for harmlessness alignment during inference phase that significantly diminishes the attack success rate of both harmful instructions and jailbreak instructions, while maintaining almost unchanged performance in downstream tasks.
2401.11206.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.19750.title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
2410.19750.tldr: This work quantifies the spatial locality of these lobes with multiple metrics and finds that clusters of co-occurring features, at coarse enough scale, also cluster together spatially far more than one would expect if feature geometry were random.

2410.14670.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
2410.14670.tldr: This work investigates dark matter as an object of study in its own right and finds that much of SAE dark matter -- about half of the error vector itself and>90% of its norm -- can be linearly predicted from the initial activation vector.

2410.08201.title: Efficient Dictionary Learning with Switch Sparse Autoencoders
2410.08201.tldr: This work introduces Switch Sparse Autoencoders, a novel SAE architecture aimed at reducing the compute cost of training SAEs, and finds that Switch SAEs deliver a substantial Pareto improvement in the reconstruction vs. sparsity frontier for a given fixed training compute budget.

2402.05110.title: Opening the AI black box: program synthesis via mechanistic interpretability
2402.05110.tldr: MIPS uses an integer autoencoder to convert the RNN into a finite state machine, then applies Boolean or integer symbolic regression to capture the learned algorithm in Python code, auto-distilling the learned algorithm into Python code.

2506.15679.title: Dense SAE Latents Are Features, Not Bugs
2506.15679.tldr: It is demonstrated that dense latents tend to form antipodal pairs that reconstruct specific directions in the residual stream, and that ablating their subspace suppresses the emergence of new dense features in retrained SAEs -- suggesting that high density features are an intrinsic property of the residual space.

2504.18530.title: Scaling Laws For Scalable Oversight
2504.18530.tldr: This framework proposes a framework that quantifies the probability of successful oversight as a function of the capabilities of the overseer and the system being overseen, and identifies conditions under which NSO succeeds and derive numerically the optimal number of oversight levels to maximize the probability of oversight success.

2501.19406.title: Low-Rank Adapting Models for Sparse Autoencoders
2501.19406.tldr: The results demonstrate that improving model interpretability is not limited to post-hoc SAE training; Pareto improvements can also be achieved by directly optimizing the model itself.

2503.07341.title: The Economics of p(doom): Scenarios of Existential Risk and Economic Growth in the Age of Transformative AI

2512.15688.title: BashArena: A Control Setting for Highly Privileged AI Agents
2512.15688.tldr: This work evaluates multiple frontier LLMs on their ability to complete tasks, perform sabotage undetected, and detect sabotage attempts in BashArena, a setting for studying AI control techniques in security-critical environments.

2602.04930.title: Attack Selection Reduces Safety in Concentrated AI Control Settings against Trusted Monitoring
2602.04930.tldr: It is found that prompting the attacker model to reason about the monitor while being cautious with attack selection reduces safety from a baseline of 99% to 59% at 0.5% auditing budget, emphasizing that eliciting attack selection capabilities of models is vital to avoid overly optimistic safety scores in control evaluations.

2605.09684.title: MonitoringBench: Semi-Automated Red-Teaming for Agent Monitoring

2606.06529.title: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
2606.06529.tldr: This work decomposes attack decisions into a start policy, which decides when an attacker should attack, and a stop policy, which decides when an attacker should abort an ongoing attack, and concludes that both policies substantially lower measured empirical safety without changing the underlying attack capability.

2405.15943.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
2405.15943.tldr: This work anticipates and then finds that belief states are linearly represented in the residual stream of transformers, even in cases where the predicted belief state geometry has highly nontrivial fractal structure.

2406.04093.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
2406.04093.tldr: This work proposes using k-sparse autoencoders to directly control sparsity, simplifying tuning and improving the reconstruction-sparsity frontier, and introduces several new metrics for evaluating feature quality based on the recovery of hypothesized features, the explainability of activation patterns, and the sparsity of downstream effects that generally improve with autoencoder size.

2407.00215.title: LLM Critics Help Catch LLM Bugs
2407.00215.tldr: It is confirmed that the fine-tuned LLM critics can successfully identify hundreds of errors in ChatGPT training data rated as"flawless", even though the majority of those tasks are non-code tasks and thus out-of-distribution for the critic model.

2406.07814.title: Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input
2406.07814.tldr: This work creates what is, to their knowledge, the first LM fine-tuned with collectively sourced public input and evaluates this model against a baseline model trained with established principles from a LM developer, demonstrating a promising, tractable pathway toward publicly informed development of language models.
2406.07814.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2401.03529.title: Quantifying stability of non-power-seeking in artificial agents
2401.03529.tldr: A quantitative bound on how fast the probability of not shutting down can increase is demonstrated by defining a metric on MDPs; proving that the probability of not shutting down, as a function on MDPs, is lower semicontinuous; and bounding how quickly this function decreases.

2607.08066.title: Persuasion Attacks Can Decrease Effectiveness of CoT Monitoring
2607.08066.tldr: The results demonstrate that CoT monitoring alone may be insufficient against adversarial persuasion, and that model-diverse fact-checking provides a robust mitigation, and that model-diverse fact-checking provides a robust mitigation.

2409.07985.title: Games for AI Control: Models of Safety Evaluations of AI Deployment Protocols
2409.07985.tldr: This paper introduces AI-Control Games, a formal decision-making model of the red-teaming exercise as a multi-objective, partially observable, stochastic game, and applies this formalism to model, evaluate and synthesise protocols for deploying untrusted language models as programming assistants.

2405.17894.title: White-box Multimodal Jailbreaks Against Large Vision-Language Models
2405.17894.tldr: A universal attack strategy that jointly attacks both text and image modalities to exploit a broader spectrum of vulnerability within VLMs and can effectively jailbreak MiniGPT-4 with a 96% success rate, highlighting the fragility of VLMs and the exigency for new alignment strategies.

2408.12798.title: BackdoorLLM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models
2408.12798.tldr: BackdoorLLM is the first comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating backdoor threats in text-generation LLMs and provides a diverse suite of attack modalities, including data poisoning, weight poisoning, hidden-state manipulation, and chain-of-thought hijacking.

2411.00827.title: IDEATOR: Jailbreaking and Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models Using Themselves
2411.00827.tldr: This paper proposes IDEATOR, a novel jailbreak method that autonomously generates malicious image-text pairs for black-box jailbreak attacks and introduces the VLJailbreakBench, a safety benchmark comprising 3,654 multimodal jailbreak samples.
2411.00827.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2410.20971.title: BlueSuffix: Reinforced Blue Teaming for Vision-Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
2410.20971.tldr: This paper proposes a novel blue-team method BlueSuffix that defends target VLMs against jailbreak attacks without compromising its performance under black-box setting and empirically shows that BlueSuffix outperforms the baseline defenses by a significant margin.

2410.09909.title: UnSeg: One Universal Unlearnable Example Generator is Enough against All Image Segmentation
2410.09909.tldr: This work proposes a novel Unlearnable Segmentation (UnSeg) framework to train a universal unlearnable noise generator that is capable of transforming any downstream images into their unlearnable version.

2511.12149.title: AttackVLA: Benchmarking Adversarial and Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
2511.12149.tldr: BackdoorVLA is introduced, a targeted backdoor attack that compels a VLA to execute an attacker-specified long-horizon action sequence whenever a trigger is present, providing a standardized framework for evaluating VLA vulnerabilities and demonstrating the potential for precise adversarial manipulation.

2604.02947.title: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
2604.02947.tldr: The benchmark evaluates whether agents can recognize and interrupt harm arising from accumulated context, repeated tool use, intermediate actions, and dependencies across steps, and indicates that current systems remain highly vulnerable.

2505.14352.title: Towards eliciting latent knowledge from LLMs with mechanistic interpretability
2505.14352.tldr: A Taboo model is trained: a language model that describes a specific secret word without explicitly stating it, and methods to uncover this secret are investigated, including non-interpretability (black-box) approaches and largely automated strategies based on mechanistic interpretability techniques.

2310.14455.title: An International Consortium for Evaluations of Societal-Scale Risks from Advanced AI
2310.14455.tldr: An international consortium for advanced AI risk evaluations is proposed, comprising both AI developers and third-party AI risk evaluators, which could play a critical role in international efforts to mitigate societal-scale risks from advanced AI.

2406.07358.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
2406.07358.tldr: This paper prompts frontier LMs, like GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus, to selectively underperform on dangerous capability evaluations, while maintaining performance on general capability evaluations, and finds that models can be fine-tuned, on a synthetic dataset, to hide specific capabilities unless given a password.

2502.02180.title: The Elicitation Game: Evaluating Capability Elicitation Techniques
2502.02180.tldr: A novel method for training model organisms, based on circuit-breaking, is introduced, which is more robust to elicitation techniques than standard password-locked models and should be the method of choice to improve the trustworthiness of capability evaluations.

2512.00218.title: Reasoning Under Pressure: How do Training Incentives Influence Chain-of-Thought Monitorability?
2512.00218.tldr: This work introduces a novel methodology for measuring monitorability according to whether a monitor can predict a key latent variable using the model's reasoning, and finds that adversarial optimisation (penalising monitor accuracy) degrades monitor performance, while direct optimisation for monitorability does not reliably lead to improvements.

2606.29657.title: Safety from Honesty in a Disinterested AI Predictor
2606.29657.tldr: It is proved that, under assumptions on the training dynamics and on the argued sparsity of dangerous Predictors, the probability that training produces a Predictor whose guarded deployment carries residual harm above a specified threshold is small.

2410.00081.title: From homeostasis to resource sharing: Biologically and economically aligned multi-objective multi-agent gridworld-based AI safety benchmarks
2410.00081.tldr: This work focuses on introducing biologically and economically motivated themes that have been neglected in current mainstream discussions on AI safety - namely a set of multi-objective, multi-agent alignment benchmarks that emphasize homeostasis for bounded and biological objectives, diminishing returns for unbounded, instrumental, and business objectives, sustainability principle, and resource sharing.

2509.02655.title: BioBlue: Systematic runaway-optimiser-like LLM failure modes on biologically and economically aligned AI safety benchmarks for LLMs with simplified observation format
2509.02655.tldr: It is found that, although LLMs frequently behave appropriately for many steps and clearly understand the stated objectives, they often lose context in structured ways and drift into runaway behaviours: ignoring homeostatic targets, collapsing from multi-objective trade-offs into single-objective maximisation - thus failing to respect concave utility structures.

2505.04592.title: AI Governance to Avoid Extinction: The Strategic Landscape and Actionable Research Questions
2505.04592.tldr: Urgent action is needed from the US National Security community and AI governance ecosystem to answer key research questions, build the capability to halt dangerous AI activities, and prepare for international AI agreements.

2511.10783.title: An International Agreement to Prevent the Premature Creation of Artificial Superintelligence
2511.10783.tldr: An international agreement to prevent the premature development of ASI until AI development can proceed without these risks is proposed, which would be technically sufficient to forestall the development of ASI if implemented today.

2509.05361.title: Constitutional Law and AI Governance: Constraints on Model Licensing and Research Classification
2509.05361.tldr: This paper examines how the First Amendment, administrative law, and the Fourteenth Amendment shape the legal vulnerability of two regulatory proposals: model licensing and AI research classification.

2407.04108.title: Future Events as Backdoor Triggers: Investigating Temporal Vulnerabilities in LLMs
2407.04108.tldr: It is shown that current large language models (LLMs) can distinguish past from future events, with probes on model activations achieving 90% accuracy and an activation-steering vector representing a model's internal representation of the date influences the rate of backdoor activation.

2504.03731.title: A Benchmark for Scalable Oversight Protocols
2504.03731.tldr: The scalable oversight benchmark is introduced, a principled framework for evaluating human feedback mechanisms based on the authors' agent score difference (ASD) metric, a measure of how effectively a mechanism advantages truth-telling over deception.

2606.30252.title: Inoculation Adapters: Improved Selective Generalization of Capabilities with Fewer Surprising Backdoors
2606.30252.tldr: Across nine setups and five model families, the inoculation adapter family spans a new Pareto frontier of desired trait retention vs. undesired trait suppression, although given wide confidence intervals the magnitude of improvement remains uncertain.

2605.29358.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

2402.06627.title: Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking
2402.06627.tldr: It is shown that feedback loops can cause in-context reward hacking (ICRH), where the LLM at test-time optimizes a (potentially implicit) objective but creates negative side effects in the process.

2406.19501.title: Monitoring Latent World States in Language Models with Propositional Probes
2406.19501.tldr: This work hypothesizes that language models represent their input contexts in a latent world model, and seeks to extract this latent world state from the activations of these models with 'propositional probes', which compositionally probe tokens for lexical information and bind them into logical propositions representing the world state.

2601.22594.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
2601.22594.tldr: For the first time, it is empirically show that MLP neurons are as sparse a feature basis as SAEs, and uses this finding to develop an end-to-end gradient-based attribution pipeline for circuit tracing on the MLP neuron basis, which surfaces causally effective neurons on a variety of tasks.

2501.07886.title: Iterative Label Refinement Matters More than Preference Optimization under Weak Supervision
2501.07886.tldr: It is found that in the presence of unreliable supervision, SFT still retains some effectiveness, but DPO (a common RLHF algorithm) fails to improve the model beyond SFT, so iterative label refinement (ILR) is proposed as an alternative to RLHF.

2602.06964.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
2602.06964.tldr: It is found that diffusion loss decreases smoothly with compute and reliably predicts downstream utility, and generative meta-models offer a scalable path toward interpretability without restrictive structural assumptions.

2609.07876.title: LLM Layers Immediately Correct Each Other
2609.07876.tldr: This dynamic suggests that the residual stream at any layer contains transient proposals alongside persistent features, helping explain why SAE feature descriptions often have low specificity, why effective model steering requires extreme feature amplification, and why transcoders hold a theoretical advantage over SAEs.

2402.13457.title: A Comprehensive Study of Jailbreak Attack versus Defense for Large Language Models
2402.13457.tldr: It is revealed that existing white-box attacks underperform compared to universal techniques and that including special tokens in the input significantly affects the likelihood of successful attacks.
2402.13457.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2402.08416.title: Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
2402.08416.tldr: This work investigates indirect jailbreak attacks on LLMs, particularly GPTs, introducing a novel attack vector named Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning, which exploits the synergy between LLMs and RAG through prompt manipulation to generate unexpected responses.
2402.08416.venue: Proceedings 2024 Workshop on AI Systems with Confidential COmputing

2405.00648.title: Drowzee: Metamorphic Testing for Fact-Conflicting Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
2405.00648.tldr: An extensive and extensible framework that constructs a comprehensive factual knowledge base by crawling sources like Wikipedia, seamlessly integrated into Drowzee, and proposes two semantic-aware oracles that assess the similarity between the semantic structures of the LLM answers and ground truth.

2508.06194.title: SceneJailEval: A Scenario-Adaptive Multi-Dimensional Framework for Jailbreak Evaluation
2508.06194.tldr: A pioneering scenario-adaptive multi-dimensional framework for jailbreak evaluation, overcoming the critical "one-size-fits-all"limitation of existing multi-dimensional methods, and boasting robust extensibility to seamlessly adapt to customized or emerging scenarios.

2407.13796.title: Continuous Embedding Attacks via Clipped Inputs in Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2407.13796.tldr: Clip, whose main strategy is to clip each input dimension based on the mean and standard deviation of the model vocabulary during model inference, improves the attack success rate (ASR) of continuous embedding attacks with full LLM inputs from 62% to 83% for LLaMa and from 38% to 83 % for Vicuna.

2501.18628.title: TombRaider: Entering the Vault of History to Jailbreak Large Language Models
2501.18628.tldr: TombRaider is introduced, a novel jailbreak technique that exploits the ability to store, retrieve, and use historical knowledge of LLMs, highlighting critical vulnerabilities in existing LLM safeguards and underscoring the need for more robust safety defences.
2501.18628.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2406.15513.title: PKU-SafeRLHF: Towards Multi-Level Safety Alignment for LLMs with Human Preference
2406.15513.tldr: The safety human preference dataset, PKU-SafeRLHF, is introduced, designed to promote research on safety alignment in large language models (LLMs) and separate annotations of helpfulness and harmlessness for question-answering pairs, providing distinct perspectives on these coupled attributes.
2406.15513.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2412.15838.title: Align Anything: Training All-Modality Models to Follow Instructions with Language Feedback
2412.15838.tldr: The align-anything framework is proposed, which includes meticulously annotated 200k all-modality human preference data and introduces an alignment method that learns from unified language feedback, effectively capturing complex modality-specific human preferences and enhancing the model's instruction-following capabilities.

2406.14477.title: SafeSora: Towards Safety Alignment of Text2Video Generation via a Human Preference Dataset
2406.14477.tldr: The SafeSora dataset is introduced to promote research on aligning text-to-video generation with human values and its potential as the foundation for text-to-video alignment research, such as human preference modeling and the development and validation of alignment algorithms is highlighted.

2505.18807.title: Mitigating Deceptive Alignment via Self-Monitoring
2505.18807.tldr: This work introduces DeceptionBench, a five-category benchmark that probes covert alignment-faking, sycophancy, etc, and evaluates various LLMs and shows that unrestricted CoT roughly aggravates the deceptive tendency.

2503.17682.title: Safe RLHF-V: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Multi-modal Human Feedback
2503.17682.tldr: The first exploration of the Safe RLHF-V -- the first multimodal safety alignment framework based on dual preference, is presented, initiating the first exploration of multi-modal safety alignment within a constrained optimization.

2410.16714.title: Magnetic Preference Optimization: Achieving Last-iterate Convergence for Language Model Alignment
2410.16714.tldr: This paper introduces Magnetic Preference Optimization (MPO), a novel approach capable of achieving last-iterate convergence to the NE of the original game, effectively overcoming the limitations of existing methods.

2409.00162.title: Sequence to Sequence Reward Modeling: Improving RLHF by Language Feedback
2409.00162.tldr: A novel sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) reward modeling method that enables richer and fine-grained language feedback without additional annotations, models, or training stages and reduces the refusal-to-response paradigm in single-turn safety dialogues and the long-response bias in text summarization tasks.

2505.18531.title: Generative RLHF-V: Learning Principles from Multi-modal Human Preference
2505.18531.tldr: Generative RLHF-V is introduced, a novel alignment framework that integrates GRMs with multi-modal RLHF and enhances multi-modal RL scoring precision by grouped responses comparison, and achieves a near-linear improvement with an increasing number of candidate responses.

2503.18130.title: Mitigating Reward Over-Optimization in RLHF via Behavior-Supported Regularization
2503.18130.tldr: Theoretically, it is proved that BSPO guarantees a monotonic improvement of the supported policy until convergence to the optimal behavior-supported policy, and empirical results show that BSPO outperforms baselines in preventing reward over-optimization due to OOD evaluation and finding the optimal ID policy.

2604.05853.title: Reading Between the Pixels: An Inscriptive Jailbreak Attack on Text-to-Image Models
2604.05853.tldr: Etch, a black-box attack framework that decomposes the adversarial prompt into three functionally orthogonal layers: semantic camouflage, visual-spatial anchoring, and typographic encoding, is proposed, which reduces joint optimization over the full prompt space to tractable sub-problems, which are iteratively refined through a zero-order loop.

2604.24118.title: AgentVisor: Defending LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection via Semantic Virtualization
2604.24118.tldr: This work proposes AgentVisor, a novel defense framework that enforces semantic privilege separation in large Language Model agents, and introduces a one-shot self-correction mechanism that transforms security violations into constructive feedback, enabling agents to recover from attacks.

2404.12241.title: Introducing v0.5 of the AI Safety Benchmark from MLCommons

2403.04893.title: A Safe Harbor for AI Evaluation and Red Teaming
2403.04893.tldr: This work proposes that major AI developers commit to providing a legal and technical safe harbor, indemnifying public interest safety research and protecting it from the threat of account suspensions or legal reprisal, where norms and incentives could be better aligned with public interests, without exacerbating model misuse.

2404.01318.title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2404.01318.tldr: JailbreakBench is an open-sourced benchmark that tracks the performance of attacks and defenses for various LLMs and has carefully considered the potential ethical implications of releasing this benchmark, and believes that it will be a net positive for the community.

2402.16192.title: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via Semantic Smoothing
2402.16192.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that SEMANTICSMOOTH achieves state-of-the-art robustness against GCG, PAIR, and AutoDAN attacks while maintaining strong nominal performance on instruction following benchmarks such as InstructionFollowing and AlpacaEval.

2503.07885.title: Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots
2503.07885.tldr: RoboGuard is proposed, a two-stage guardrail architecture that contextualizes pre-defined safety rules by grounding them in the robot's environment using a root-of-trust LLM, and resolves conflicts between these contextual safety specifications and potentially unsafe plans using temporal logic control synthesis.

2503.00187.title: Steering Dialogue Dynamics for Robustness against Multi-turn Jailbreaking Attacks
2503.00187.tldr: This work proposes a safety steering framework grounded in safe control theory that achieves invariant safety at each turn of dialogue by learning a safety predictor that accounts for adversarial queries, preventing potential context drift toward jailbreaks.

2506.00688.title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
2506.00688.tldr: This work critically examines standard unlearning evaluation practices and uncover key limitations that shake trust in those findings, and proposes two principles for future unlearning evaluations: minimal information injection and downstream task awareness.

2509.23281.title: Preventing Robotic Jailbreaking via Multimodal Domain Adaptation
2509.23281.tldr: J-DAPT integrates textual and visual embeddings to capture both semantic intent and environmental grounding, while aligning general-purpose jailbreak datasets with domain-specific reference data, and shows that J-DAPT boosts detection accuracy to nearly 100% with minimal overhead.

2405.17713.title: AI Alignment with Changing and Influenceable Reward Functions
2405.17713.tldr: Dynamic Reward Markov Decision Processes (DR-MDPs) are introduced, which explicitly model preference changes and the AI's influence on them, and formalize different notions of AI alignment that account for preference change from the outset.

2509.23365.title: Emergence of Superposition: Unveiling the Training Dynamics of Chain of Continuous Thought
2509.23365.tldr: This work theoretically analyzes the training dynamics of a simplified two-layer transformer on the directed graph reachability problem to unveil how the superposition mechanism emerges during training in two training stages -- a thought-generation stage that autoregressively expands the continuous thought, and a prediction stage that converts the thought into the final answer.

2410.21572.title: Safety cases for frontier AI
2410.21572.tldr: The practicalities of safety cases are discussed, outlining how to produce a frontier AI safety case and discussing what still needs to happen before safety cases can substantially inform decisions.

2409.08751.title: A Grading Rubric for AI Safety Frameworks
2409.08751.tldr: The purpose of the grading rubric is to enable nuanced comparisons between frameworks, identify potential areas of improvement, and promote a race to the top in responsible AI development.

2505.01643.title: Third-party compliance reviews for frontier AI safety frameworks
2505.01643.tldr: This paper explores a potential solution: third-party compliance reviews and suggests "minimalist", "more ambitious", and "comprehensive" approaches for each question that a frontier AI company could adopt.

2310.00374.title: Coordinated pausing: An evaluation-based coordination scheme for frontier AI developers
2310.00374.tldr: It is concluded that coordinated pausing is a promising mechanism for tackling emerging risks from frontier AI models however, a number of practical and legal obstacles need to be overcome, especially how to avoid violations of antitrust law.

2305.07153.title: Towards best practices in AGI safety and governance: A survey of expert opinion
2305.07153.tldr: A survey of leading experts from AGI labs, academia, and civil society yielded a list of statements that may serve as a helpful foundation for efforts to develop best practices, standards, and regulations forAGI labs.

2508.00943.title: LLMs Can Covertly Sandbag on Capability Evaluations Against Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
2508.00943.tldr: This work shows that both frontier models and small open-sourced models can covertly sandbag against CoT monitoring 0-shot without hints, but cannot yet do so reliably: they bypass the monitor 16-36% of the time when monitor-aware, conditioned on sandbagging successfully.

2602.04899.title: Phantom Transfer: Data Poisoning can Survive Data-Level Defences
2602.04899.tldr: An existence proof that maximum-affordance defences can fail to stop sophisticated data poisoning attacks is provided and it is suggested that future defences should be supplemented with white-box methods and post-training model audits.

2607.07368.title: Multi-Agent AI Control: Distributed Attacks Hamper Per-Instance Monitors
2607.07368.tldr: The empirical study of multi-agent AI control is initiated, formalising distributed attacks in which several agents jointly aim for a malicious goal and evaluating single agent monitoring against distributed attacks, varying the number of agents, their coordination, model capabilities and precise monitoring configuration.

2606.11998.title: Bootstrapped Monitoring: Leveraging Transparent Reasoning to Oversee Stronger AI Agents

2606.12016.title: Generalization Hacking: Models Can Game Reinforcement Learning by Preventing Behavioral Generalization
2606.12016.tldr: The results constitute the first demonstration that a model can actively resist RL behavioral modification while maintaining high reward, suggesting that as models become more capable and training-aware, they may be able to undermine the training process itself.

2401.16656.title: Gradient-Based Language Model Red Teaming
2401.16656.tldr: Gradient-Based Red Teaming (GBRT), a novel red teaming method for automatically generating diverse prompts that are likely to cause an LM to output unsafe responses, and two variants that add a realism loss and fine-tune a pretrained model to generate the prompts instead of learning the prompts directly.
2401.16656.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.06373.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs
2401.06373.tldr: This paper proposes a persuasion taxonomy derived from decades of social science research and applies the taxonomy to automatically generate interpretable persuasive adversarial prompts (PAP) to jailbreak LLMs.
2401.06373.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.14598.title: SORRY-Bench: Systematically Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Refusal
2406.14598.tldr: It is shown that fine-tuned 7B LLMs can achieve accuracy comparable to GPT-4 scale LLMs, with lower computational cost, and investigates design choices for creating a fast, accurate automated safety evaluator.

2406.17092.title: BEEAR: Embedding-based Adversarial Removal of Safety Backdoors in Instruction-tuned Language Models
2406.17092.tldr: BEEAR is presented, a novel mitigation method based on a key insight: backdoor triggers induce a uniform drift in the model’s embedding space, irrespective of the trigger’s form or targeted behavior, and relies only on defender-defined sets of safe and unwanted behaviors.
2406.17092.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2406.17864.title: AI Risk Categorization Decoded (AIR 2024): From Government Regulations to Corporate Policies

2412.07808.title: Boosting Alignment for Post-Unlearning Text-to-Image Generative Models
2412.07808.tldr: This work proposes a framework that seeks an optimal model update at each unlearning iteration, ensuring monotonic improvement on both objectives, and designs procedures to strategically diversify the unlearning and remaining datasets to boost performance improvement.

2504.01278.title: Strategize Globally, Adapt Locally: A Multi-Turn Red Teaming Agent with Dual-Level Learning
2504.01278.tldr: AlgName is proposed, a novel multi-turn red-teaming agent that emulates sophisticated human attackers through complementary learning dimensions: global tactic-wise learning that accumulates knowledge over time and generalizes to new attack goals, and local prompt-wise learning that refines implementations for specific goals when initial attempts fail.

2605.08277.title: Mitigating Many-shot Jailbreak Attacks with One Single Demonstration
2605.08277.tldr: A fixed one-shot safety demonstration is append at inference time, which induces a counteracting safety-oriented update and restores refusal behavior, and improves the model's robustness to MSJ without modifying its parameters or requiring white-box access at deployment.

2605.17830.title: Remembering More, Risking More: Longitudinal Safety Risks in Memory-Equipped LLM Agents
2605.17830.tldr: A trigger-probe protocol is introduced that evaluates a fixed probe set against read-only memory snapshots at varying prefix lengths, together with a NullMemory counterfactual baseline for identifying memory-induced violations, which argues for treating memory safety as a longitudinal property that requires temporal evaluation, not a single-state property that can be captured by a snapshot.

2407.07786.title: The Human Factor in AI Red Teaming: Perspectives from Social and Collaborative Computing
2407.07786.tldr: This workshop seeks to consider the conceptual and empirical challenges associated with this practice, often rendered opaque by non-disclosure agreements, and aims to facilitate a community of researchers and practitioners who can begin to meet these challenges with creativity, innovation, and thoughtful reflection.

2407.06460.title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
2407.06460.tldr: This work proposes MUSE, a comprehensive machine unlearning evaluation benchmark that enumerates six diverse desirable properties for unlearned models and demonstrates that most algorithms can prevent verbatim memorization and knowledge memorization to varying degrees, but only one algorithm does not lead to severe privacy leakage.

2402.05162.title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
2402.05162.tldr: It is shown that LLMs remain vulnerable to low-cost fine-tuning attacks even when modifications to the safety-critical regions are restricted, underscoring the urgent need for more robust safety strategies in LLMs.

2409.18025.title: An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
2409.18025.tldr: This work demonstrates that existing jailbreak methods, previously reported as ineffective against unlearning, can be successful when applied carefully and develops a variety of adaptive methods that recover most supposedly unlearned capabilities.

2402.18104.title: Making Them Ask and Answer: Jailbreaking Large Language Models in Few Queries via Disguise and Reconstruction
2402.18104.tldr: This work pioneer a theoretical foundation in LLMs security by identifying bias vulnerabilities within the safety fine-tuning and design a black-box jailbreak method named DRA (Disguise and Reconstruction Attack), which conceals harmful instructions through disguise and prompts the model to reconstruct the original harmful instruction within its completion.

2502.02384.title: STAIR: Improving Safety Alignment with Introspective Reasoning
2502.02384.tldr: STAIR is a novel framework that integrates SafeTy Alignment with Itrospective Reasoning to enable LLMs to identify safety risks through step-by-step analysis by self-improving chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning with safety awareness.

2506.01307.title: Align is not Enough: Multimodal Universal Jailbreak Attack against Multimodal Large Language Models
2506.01307.tldr: This work proposes a unified multimodal universal jailbreak attack framework that leverages iterative image-text interactions and transfer-based strategy to generate a universal adversarial suffix and image, and validates that multimodal universal jailbreak attacks can bring higher-quality undesirable generations across different MLLMs.
2506.01307.venue: IEEE transactions on circuits and systems for video technology (Print)

2509.24393.title: Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention
2509.24393.tldr: This paper proposes Intervened Preference Optimization (IPO), an alignment method that enforces safe reasoning by substituting compliance steps with safety triggers and constructing pairs for preference learning with strong signals, highlighting the importance of explicit alignment for reasoning and providing a practical path to safer LRMs.

2405.19668.title: AutoBreach: Universal and Adaptive Jailbreaking with Efficient Wordplay-Guided Optimization
2405.19668.tldr: This work rethink the approach to jailbreaking LLMs and formally define three essential properties from the attacker' s perspective, which contributes to guiding the design of jailbreak methods and introduces AutoBreach, a novel method for jailbreaking LLMs that requires only black-box access.

2605.18309.title: Alignment Dynamics in LLM Fine-Tuning
2605.18309.tldr: A tractable alignment score is introduced and its closed-form update during fine-tuning is derived, yielding a unified framework for alignment dynamics, providing a unified dynamical perspective on how alignment is disrupted and reactivated during LLM fine-tuning.

2603.03725.title: Why Do Unlearnable Examples Work: A Novel Perspective of Mutual Information
2603.03725.tldr: This paper proposes a novel unlearnable method called Mutual Information Unlearnable Examples (MI-UE) that reduces covariance by maximizing the cosine similarity among intra-class features, thus impeding the generalization effectively.

2409.14507.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
2409.14507.tldr: This work shows that seemingly monosemantic features fail to fire where they should, and instead get absorbed into their children features in SAEs, and suggests that varying SAE sizes or sparsity is insufficient to solve this issue.

2512.07810.title: Auditing Games for Sandbagging
2512.07810.tldr: Although Prompt-based elicitation was not reliable, training-based elicitation consistently elicited full performance from the sandbagging models, using only a single correct demonstration of the evaluation task, so relying on elicitation as a detection strategy was prone to false-positives.

2602.01425.title: One Probe Won't Catch Them All: Towards Targeted Deception Detection
2602.01425.tldr: It is demonstrated that deception detection is inherently heterogeneous: while a single universal probe achieves modest improvements, post-hoc oracle analysis reveals substantially higher potential when probes are matched to specific deception types.

2512.19027.title: Recontextualization Mitigates Specification Gaming without Modifying the Specification
2512.19027.tldr: Recontextualization trains language models to resist misbehavior even when instructions permit it, which mitigates the reinforcement of misbehavior from misspecified training signals, reducing specification gaming without improving the supervision signal.

2604.10733.title: Too Nice to Tell the Truth: Quantifying Agreeableness-Driven Sycophancy in Role-Playing Language Models
2604.10733.tldr: These findings demonstrate that agreeableness functions as a reliable predictor of persona-induced sycophancy, with direct implications for the deployment of role-playing AI systems and the development of alignment strategies that account for personality-mediated deceptive behaviors.
2604.10733.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.08451.title: Sycophancy as a Multilingual Alignment Failure: How Safety Degrades Across Languages, Topics, and Models
2606.08451.tldr: The first large-scale, multi-model evaluation of cross-lingual sycophancy is presented, benchmarking six instruction-tuned models across 1.1 million instances and identifying a consistent resource-tier effect: sycophancy rates spike sharply in low-resource and zero-shot language settings.

2604.13803.title: Gaslight, Gatekeep, V1-V3: Early Visual Cortex Alignment Shields Vision-Language Models from Sycophantic Manipulation
2604.13803.tldr: Region-of-interest analysis reveals that alignment specifically in early visual cortex (V1--V3) is a reliable negative predictor of sycophancy, suggesting that faithful low-level visual encoding provides a measurable anchor against adversarial linguistic override in vision-language models.

2604.24346.title: SycoPhantasy: Quantifying Sycophancy and Hallucination in Small Open Weight VLMs for Vision-Language Scoring of Fantasy Characters
2604.24346.tldr: A significant inverse correlation between model size and sycophancy rate is revealed, with smaller models exhibiting substantially higher rates of unjustified high scores and larger models exhibiting substantially higher rates of unjustified high scores.

2507.12872.title: Manipulation Attacks by Misaligned AI: Risk Analysis and Safety Case Framework
2507.12872.tldr: This paper provides the first systematic methodology for integrating manipulation risk into AI safety governance, offering AI companies a concrete foundation to assess and mitigate these threats before deployment.

2508.17000.title: KL-Regularised Q-Learning: A Token-level Action-Value perspective on Online RLHF
2508.17000.tldr: This paper develops a new action-value RL method for the LM-RLHF setting, KL-regularised Q-Learning (KLQ), and shows that this method is equivalent to a version of PPO in a certain specific sense, despite its very different motivation.

2606.31591.title: Evil Spectra: How Optimisers can Amplify or Suppress Emergent Misalignment
2606.31591.tldr: These results identify optimiser choice as a key factor in EM severity, but show that spectral regularisation can substantially mitigate the effects of EM-prone optimisers.

2604.21098.title: Propensity Inference: Environmental Contributors to LLM Behaviour
2604.21098.tldr: This work develops and applies methods for measuring language models'propensity for unsanctioned behaviour and highlights a key direction for future propensity research: the development of theoretical frameworks and cognitive models of AI decision-making into empirically testable forms.

2607.28881.title: Fragility of Value under Imperfect Alignment
2607.28881.tldr: This paper presents a model of the alignment problem where an agent undergoes idealized alignment training that guarantees its value function satisfies a proxy condition before optimizing the world.

2503.03710.title: Improving LLM Safety Alignment with Dual-Objective Optimization
2503.03710.tldr: An improved safety alignment that disentangles DPO objectives into two components increases LLM robustness against a wide range of jailbreak attacks, including prefilling, suffix, and multi-turn attacks across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios.

2505.11611.title: Signal in the Noise: Polysemantic Interference Transfers and Predicts Cross-Model Influence
2505.11611.tldr: This work maps the polysemantic topology of two small models to identify SAE feature pairs that are semantically unrelated yet exhibit interference within models, demonstrating instead that interference structures generalize across scale and family.

2602.03792.title: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
2602.03792.tldr: This work proposes WebSentinel, a two-step approach for detecting and localizing prompt injection attacks in webpages, and shows that WebSentinel is highly effective, substantially outperforming baseline methods across multiple datasets of both contaminated and clean webpages that were collected.

2607.05790.title: Controlling Tool Use with Heading-Specific Activation Steering
2607.05790.tldr: It is shown that steering vectors extracted from heading-anchors positions exert bidirectional causal control over tool-invocation behavior across five open-source models and three domains, suppressing unnecessary tool use most effectively in domains where parametric reasoning suffices.

2509.13281.title: RepIt: Steering Language Models with Concept-Specific Refusal Vectors
2509.13281.tldr: RepIt, a simple and data-efficient framework for isolating concept-specific representations in LM activations, is presented, exposing vulnerabilities in current safety evaluation practices and demonstrating a need for more comprehensive, representation aware assessments.

2506.07736.title: RSafe: Incentivizing proactive reasoning to build robust and adaptive LLM safeguards
2506.07736.tldr: This work proposes RSafe, an adaptive reasoning-based safeguard that conducts guided safety reasoning to provide robust protection within the scope of specified safety policies and accepts user-specified safety policies to provide enhanced safeguards tailored to specific safety requirements.

2501.19180.title: Enhancing Model Defense Against Jailbreaks with Proactive Safety Reasoning
2501.19180.tldr: A novel defense strategy, Safety Chain-of-Thought (SCoT), is proposed, which harnesses the enhanced reasoning capabilities of LLMs for proactive assessment of harmful inputs, rather than simply blocking them.

2411.11496.title: Safe + Safe = Unsafe? Exploring How Safe Images Can Be Exploited to Jailbreak Large Vision-Language Models
2411.11496.tldr: This study reveals that a safe image can be exploited to achieve the same jailbreak consequence when combined with additional safe images and prompts, and proposes Safety Snowball Agent (SSA), a novel agent-based framework leveraging agents' autonomous and tool-using abilities to jailbreak LVLMs.

2602.01474.title: Legal Infrastructure for Transformative AI Governance
2602.01474.tldr: In this Perspective, I review three examples: the creation of registration regimes for frontier models; the creation of registration and identification regimes for autonomous agents; and the design of regulatory markets to facilitate a role for private companies to innovate and deliver AI regulatory services.
2602.01474.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

2510.27378.title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Faithfulness and Verbosity
2510.27378.tldr: The results show that models can appear faithful yet remain hard to monitor when they leave out key factors, and that monitorability differs sharply across model families.

2512.07667.title: Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models
2512.07667.tldr: This work evaluates seven models spanning the LLaMA, Qwen, and Mistral families and finds that Gaussian scheduling improves honesty over no-steering and single-layer baselines in six of seven models and provides a low-cost control knob for eliciting truthful reporting from models'existing capabilities.

2412.06966.title: Machine Unlearning Doesn't Do What You Think: Lessons for Generative AI Policy and Research
2412.06966.tldr: This work provides a framework for ML researchers and policymakers to think rigorously about the goals of unlearning and feasible implementations, identifying several mismatches between the goals of unlearning and feasible implementations.

2502.08177.title: SycEval: Evaluating LLM Sycophancy
2502.08177.tldr: A framework to evaluate sycophantic behavior in ChatGPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet, and Gemini-1.5-Pro across AMPS (mathematics) and MedQuad (medical advice) datasets is introduced.
2502.08177.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2503.15754.title: AutoRedTeamer: Autonomous Red Teaming with Lifelong Attack Integration
2503.15754.tldr: This paper introduces AutoRedTeamer, a novel framework for fully automated, end-to-end red teaming against LLMs, which combines a multi-agent architecture with a memory-guided attack selection mechanism to enable continuous discovery and integration of new attack vectors.

2506.06985.title: Certified Unlearning for Neural Networks
2506.06985.tldr: This work proposes a novel method for certified machine unlearning, leveraging the connection between unlearning and privacy amplification by stochastic post-processing, and uses noisy fine-tuning on the retain data to ensure provable unlearning guarantees.

2412.09119.title: The Utility and Complexity of in- and out-of-Distribution Machine Unlearning
2412.09119.tldr: This paper analyzes the fundamental utility, time, and space complexity trade-offs of approximate unlearning, providing rigorous certification analogous to differential privacy and proposes a new robust and noisy gradient descent variant that provably amortizes unlearning time complexity without compromising utility.

2609.16927.title: Verbalizing Subliminal Learning Effects Using Text Optimization
2609.16927.tldr: This work uses text optimization to detect subliminal learning effects and describes them as legible prompts and presents SALVE (Search-Aided Latent Verbalization) as a method to proactively detect subliminal learning effects.

2307.10569.title: Deceptive Alignment Monitoring
2307.10569.tldr: This work identifies emerging directions in diverse machine learning subfields that it is believed will become increasingly important and intertwined in the near future for deceptive alignment monitoring, and argues that advances in these fields present both long-term challenges and new research opportunities.

2602.15338.title: Discovering Implicit Large Language Model Alignment Objectives

2608.14855.title: What to Forget in Unlearning? Forget Set Curation for Language Models
2608.14855.tldr: This work introduces CleanSlate, a benchmark for verbatim output suppression over songs and books, with model-specific extraction profiles, content-grounded QA, and capability-retention evaluations, and shows that practical unlearning is not only an optimization problem once a forget set is given, but also what can be unlearnt and what else is damaged.

2606.08044.title: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective
2606.08044.tldr: The gap between what static audits certify and what an intervention can reach the audit gap is called the audit gap, and it is shown it is realizable: one can build a model that matches its safety-aligned base on every static audit yet gives way to a small, known perturbation of its internal state.

2510.01494.title: Understanding Adversarial Transfer: Why Representation-Space Attacks Fail Where Data-Space Attacks Succeed
2510.01494.tldr: This work reveals that adversarial transfer is not an inherent property of all attacks but contingent on their operational domain - the shared data-space versus models'unique representation spaces - a critical insight for building more robust models.

2404.14461.title: Competition Report: Finding Universal Jailbreak Backdoors in Aligned LLMs
2404.14461.tldr: This competition, co-located at IEEE SaTML 2024, challenged participants to find universal backdoors in several large language models and summarizes the key findings and promising ideas for future research.

2603.15714.title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
2603.15714.tldr: A large scale public red teaming competition evaluating this dual objective across three agent settings: tool calling, coding, and computer use is presented, suggesting fundamental weaknesses in instruction following architectures.

2604.25982.title: Open Problems in Frontier AI Risk Management
2604.25982.tldr: This work systematically surface open problems in frontier AI risk management, and identifies the actors best positioned to address them - including developers, deployers, regulators, standards bodies, researchers, and third-party evaluators.

2403.19647.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
2403.19647.tldr: An entirely unsupervised and scalable interpretability pipeline is demonstrated by discovering thousands of sparse feature circuits for automatically discovered model behaviors.

2509.02565.title: Understanding sparse autoencoder scaling in the presence of feature manifolds
2509.02565.tldr: A capacity-allocation model from the neural scaling literature is adapted to understand SAE scaling, and in particular, to understand how"feature manifolds"(multi-dimensional features) influence scaling behavior.

2606.12268.title: The Impossibility of Eliciting Latent Knowledge
2606.12268.tldr: An impossibility theorem is proved stating: There is no feedback-based training strategy that depends only on agent behaviour and with certainty produces an honest agent, even if feedback is perfect during training.

2408.15221.title: LLM Defenses Are Not Robust to Multi-Turn Human Jailbreaks Yet
2408.15221.tldr: It is demonstrated that multi-turn human jailbreaks uncover significant vulnerabilities, exceeding 70% attack success rate (ASR) on HarmBench against defenses that report single-digit ASRs with automated single-turn attacks.

2606.12429.title: Muse Spark Safety & Preparedness Report
2606.12429.tldr: This report presents evaluations for catastrophic risk domains under Meta's Advanced AI Scaling Framework, along with the evidence that informed the launch decision of Muse Spark, and releases Muse Spark as the underlying model of Meta AI.

2605.00932.title: Code World Model Preparedness Report
2605.00932.tldr: This report documents the preparedness assessment of Code World Model, a model for code generation and reasoning about code from Meta, and finds that CWM does not pose additional frontier risks beyond those present in the current AI ecosystem.

2406.05946.title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep
2406.05946.tldr: This paper presents case studies to explain why shallow safety alignment can exist and provide evidence that current aligned LLMs are subject to this issue, and designs a regularized finetuning objective that makes the safety alignment more persistent against fine-tuning attacks by constraining updates on initial tokens.

2604.09544.title: Large Language Models Generate Harmful Responses Using a Distinct Mechanism, Shared Across Harm Types
2604.09544.tldr: This work identifies and prune parameters that specifically support harmful compliance, providing a direct mechanistic analysis at the parameter level and shows that harmful response generation is dissociable from the ability to recognize and reason about harmfulness.

2405.20099.title: Defensive Prompt Patch: A Robust and Interpretable Defense of LLMs against Jailbreak Attacks
2405.20099.tldr: Defensive Prompt Patch is introduced, a novel prompt-based defense mechanism specifically designed to protect LLMs against such sophisticated jailbreak strategies, and not only outperforms existing defense strategies in balancing safety and functionality, but also provides a scalable and interpretable solution applicable to various LLM platforms.

2607.26115.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale
2607.26115.tldr: GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent that is trained to discover novel prompt injection attacks against frontier LLMs, is introduced, a scalable self-play algorithm where the model is tasked with attacking a diverse population of simultaneously-trained defender agents.

2503.18813.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
2503.18813.tldr: CaMeL is a robust defense that creates a protective system layer around the LLM, securing it even when underlying models are susceptible to attacks, and uses a notion of a capability to prevent the exfiltration of private data over unauthorized data flows by enforcing security policies when tools are called.

2406.13352.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
2406.13352.tldr: It is found that AgentDojo poses a challenge for both attacks and defenses: state-of-the-art LLMs fail at many tasks (even in the absence of attacks), and existing prompt injection attacks break some security properties but not all.

2510.09023.title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against Llm Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
2510.09023.tldr: It is argued that future defense work must consider stronger attacks, such as the ones described, in order to make reliable and convincing claims of robustness, and bypass 12 recent defenses with attack success rate above 90% for most.

2506.08837.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
2506.08837.tldr: This work proposes a set of principled design patterns for building AI agents with provable resistance to prompt injection, and discusses their trade-offs in terms of utility and security, and illustrates their real-world applicability through a series of case studies.

2402.12329.title: Query-Based Adversarial Prompt Generation
2402.12329.tldr: This work improves on prior work with a query-based attack that leverages API access to a remote language model to construct adversarial examples that cause the model to emit harmful strings with (much) higher probability than with transfer-only attacks.

2504.10694.title: The Jailbreak Tax: How Useful are Your Jailbreak Outputs?
2504.10694.tldr: This work proposes the jailbreak tax as a new important metric in AI safety, and introduces benchmarks to evaluate existing and future jailbreaks, which are based on a consistent drop in model utility in jailbroken responses.

2602.05746.title: Learning to Inject: Automated Prompt Injection via Reinforcement Learning
2602.05746.tldr: AutoInject is presented, a black-box reinforcement learning (RL) framework that learns adversarial suffixes for prompt injection that establishes an automated baseline for prompt injection and exposes a gap between preference-based defenses and adaptive optimization-based attackers.

2502.19964.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Generalize? A Case Study of Answerability
2502.19964.tldr: This work extensively evaluate SAE feature generalization across diverse, partly self-constructed answerability datasets for Gemma 2 SAEs, revealing that residual stream probes outperform SAE features within domains, but generalization performance differs sharply.

2607.04846.title: Pretraining Curricula Enable Selective Fine-tuning
2607.04846.tldr: It is shown that imbalanced learning of two conflicting copy tasks promotes in-context learning and improves the selectivity of refusal fine-tuning, suggesting that imbalanced pretraining curricula may be an important tool for promoting disentangled representations, with direct consequences for the precision and reliability of safety fine-tuning.

2511.10840.title: Tracing Multilingual Representations in LLMs with Cross-Layer Transcoders
2511.10840.tldr: Finetuning strengthens features and their links, improving token assembly and language-specific decoding, providing a mechanistic explanation for multilingual gaps.

2602.04718.title: Superposition Without Interference? Towards Isolated Interventions via Almost Orthogonal Features in Language Models
2602.04718.tldr: This work characterizes the gap between an idealized isolated intervention and its realized effect on model outputs in terms of feature interference and upper-bound the propagation of feature interference in terms of the self-coherence of the feature dictionary, and relates this discrepancy to an explicit orthogonality regularization on the dictionary itself.

2607.18114.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?
2607.18114.tldr: Cue-induced bias is best understood not as a single flaw in LLMs but as a family of causally effective linear directions that are largely shaped by alignment tuning.

2511.23174.title: Are LLMs Good Safety Agents or a Propaganda Engine?
2511.23174.tldr: This work introduces PSP, a dataset built specifically to probe the refusal behaviors in LLMs from an explicitly political context, and studies impact of political sensitivity in seven LLMs through data-driven and representation-level approaches, and vulnerability of models on PSP through prompt injection attacks.

2411.12103.title: Does Unlearning Truly Unlearn? A Black Box Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Methods
2411.12103.tldr: It is shown that training on unrelated data can almost completely recover pre-unlearning performance, demonstrating that training on unrelated data can almost completely recover pre-unlearning performance.

2607.02514.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
2607.02514.tldr: A stateful link-tracker monitor that tracks suspicious buildup across PRs and detects gradual attacks substantially better than diff monitors that merely see more accumulated history is introduced, reducing gradual-attack evasion from 93% under the weakest standard diff monitor to 47%.

2608.04735.title: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings
2608.04735.tldr: The first benchmark that directly compares CoT monitorability under explicit-influence and implicit-influence regimes is introduced, suggesting that monitorability estimates obtained in explicit-influence settings may over-estimate monitorability, and that monitorability can be further decreased by well-intentioned deployment choices.

2506.08123.title: QA-LIGN: Aligning LLMs through Constitutionally Decomposed QA
2506.08123.tldr: QA-LIGN is introduced, which decomposes monolithic rewards into interpretable principle-specific evaluations through structured natural language programs and demonstrates that making reward signals interpretable and modular improves alignment effectiveness, suggesting transparency enhances LLM safety.
2506.08123.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2507.22063.title: RedCoder: Automated Multi-Turn Red Teaming for Code LLMs
2507.22063.tldr: This work presents RedCoder, a red-teaming agent that engages victim models in multi-turn conversation to elicit vulnerable code, offering a scalable and effective tool for evaluating the security boundaries of modern code-generation systems.
2507.22063.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.11750.title: Making Every Step Effective: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models Through Hierarchical KV Equalization
2503.11750.tldr: Hierarchical Key-Value Equalization (Hierarchical Key-Value Equalization), an innovative jailbreaking framework that selectively accepts gradient optimization results based on the distribution of attention scores across different layers, ensuring that every optimization step positively contributes to the attack.
2503.11750.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2405.21018.title: Improved Techniques for Optimization-Based Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
2405.21018.tldr: Improved techniques for optimization-based jailbreaks like GCG are presented and demonstrated that they can help GCG outperform state-of-the-art jailbreaking attacks and achieve nearly 100% attack success rate.

2404.08031.title: Latent Guard: a Safety Framework for Text-to-image Generation
2404.08031.tldr: Inspired by blacklist-based approaches, Latent Guard learns a latent space on top of the T2I model's text encoder, where it is possible to check the presence of harmful concepts in the input text embeddings.

2404.03411.title: Red Teaming GPT-4V: Are GPT-4V Safe Against Uni/Multi-Modal Jailbreak Attacks?
2404.03411.tldr: GPT4 and GPT-4V demonstrate better robustness against jailbreak attacks compared to open-source LLMs and MLLMs, and Llama2 and Qwen-VL-Chat are more robust compared to other open-source models.

2501.04064.title: Examining Popular Arguments Against AI Existential Risk: A Philosophical Analysis
2501.04064.tldr: This paper reconstructs and evaluates three common arguments against the existential risk perspective: the Distraction Argument, the Argument from Human Frailty, and the Checkpoints for Intervention Argument to provide a foundation for more balanced academic discourse and further research on AI.

2605.02269.title: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
2605.02269.tldr: The results suggest that specification gaming is a fundamental challenge arising from RL reasoning training; a diverse suite of tasks where models can score highly by taking unintended actions is built and open source.

2605.21778.title: What Counts as AI Sycophancy? A Taxonomy and Expert Survey of a Fragmented Construct
2605.21778.tldr: It is demonstrated that AI sycophancy is a broad family of behaviors with different measurement challenges, intervention requirements, and governance implications, and a taxonomy provides a shared vocabulary for understanding and addressing these behaviors.

2403.05540.title: Extinction Risks from AI: Invisible to Science?
2403.05540.tldr: This work identifies a set of conditions that are necessary for a model that aims to be informative for evaluating specific arguments for Extinction-level Goodhart's Law, and aims to understand which formal models are suitable for investigating this hypothesis.

2507.20964.title: Core Safety Values for Provably Corrigible Agents
2507.20964.tldr: It is proved that deciding whether an arbitrary post-hack agent will ever violate corrigibility is undecidable by reduction to the halting problem, and a finite-horizon "decidable island" is carved out where safety can be certified in randomized polynomial time and verified with privacy-preserving, constant-round zero-knowledge proofs.

2502.05934.title: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
2502.05934.tldr: Analyzing communication complexity, it is proved that once either M or N is large enough, no amount of computational power or rationality can avoid intrinsic alignment overheads, establishing rigorous limits to alignment *itself*, not merely to particular methods.

2606.00341.title: ROGUE: Misaligned Agent Behavior Arising from Ordinary Computer Use
2606.00341.tldr: This work highlights the critical need for principled, corrigibility-focused alignment methods in autonomous agents, and shows that agents can exhibit misaligned behavior even in benign settings, taking unsafe actions when those actions are instrumental to task completion.

2602.14777.title: Emergently Misaligned Language Models Show Behavioral Self-Awareness That Shifts With Subsequent Realignment
2602.14777.tldr: The findings show that behavioral self-awareness tracks actual alignment states of models, indicating that models can be queried for informative signals about their own safety, and show that emergently misaligned models rate themselves as significantly more harmful compared to their base model and realigned counterparts.

2604.28082.title: Characterizing the Consistency of the Emergent Misalignment Persona
2604.28082.tldr: Two distinct patterns are revealed: coherent-persona models, in which harmful behavior and self-reported misalignment are coupled, and inverted-persona models, which produce harmful outputs while identifying as aligned AI systems.

2606.20814.title: What Shapes Emergent Misalignment? Insights from Training Dynamics, Model Priors, and Data
2606.20814.tldr: The evaluation prompt-only activations from both the pre-trained and the original instruct models (prior to narrow fine-tuning) could predict fine-grained alignment scores after narrow fine-tuning, and although the mean and standard deviations of the misaligned model scores are usually statistically different from those of the pre-trained model, there are some potential signals on overall positive correlation.

2605.11134.title: Spurious Correlation Learning in Preference Optimization: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Mitigation via Tie Training
2605.11134.tldr: This work provides a unified theoretical analysis of the mechanisms of spurious learning, characterizing the consequences on deployment, and proposing tie training, a data augmentation strategy using ties (equal-utility preference pairs) to introduce data-driven regularization.

2607.02755.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Risk Aversion in Language Models
2607.02755.tldr: Overall, it is found that risk aversion learned at low stakes can generalize OOD to astronomically high stakes, though not yet consistently enough to serve as a reliable failsafe.

2601.09765.title: AI Survival Stories: a Taxonomic Analysis of AI Existential Risk
2601.09765.tldr: A general framework for thinking about the existential risk of AI systems is developed, and a taxonomy of survival stories, in which humanity survives into the far future is constructed, arguing that different survival stories face different challenges.

2406.11757.title: STAR: SocioTechnical Approach to Red Teaming Language Models
2406.11757.tldr: STARS enhances steerability by generating parameterised instructions for human red teamers, leading to improved coverage of the risk surface and improves signal quality by matching demographics to assess harms for specific groups, resulting in more sensitive annotations.
2406.11757.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2402.10184.title: Reward Generalization in RLHF: A Topological Perspective
2402.10184.tldr: This work introduces a theory of reward generalization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), focusing on the topology of information flow at both macro and micro levels, and proposes reward modeling from tree-structured preference information.
2402.10184.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2507.03050.title: From Turing to Tomorrow: The UK's Approach to AI Regulation
2507.03050.tldr: A flexible, principles-based regulator is proposed to oversee the most advanced AI development, defensive measures against risks from AI-enabled biological design tools, and it is argued that more technical work is needed to understand how to respond to AI-generated misinformation.

2408.16961.title: The Future of Open Human Feedback
2408.16961.tldr: An open ecosystem for human feedback on large language models is explored, drawing from peer-production, open-source and citizen-science practices, and addressing key challenges to establish sustainable feedback loops between users and specialized models.

2506.03755.title: Misalignment or misuse? The AGI alignment tradeoff
2506.03755.tldr: It is argued that many current alignment techniques and foreseeable improvements plausibly increase risks of catastrophic misuse and suggested that to reduce the risk of a misuse catastrophe due to aligned AGI, techniques such as robustness, AI control methods and especially good governance seem essential.

2507.21839.title: Against racing to AGI: Cooperation, deterrence, and catastrophic risks
2507.21839.tldr: This paper argues that international cooperation and coordination, and perhaps carefully crafted deterrence measures, constitute viable alternatives to racing to AGI which have much smaller risks and promise to deliver most of the benefits that racing to AGI is supposed to provide.

2510.11235.title: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
2510.11235.tldr: This paper analyzes 7 representative alignment techniques and 7 failure modes to understand the extent to which they overlap, and discusses the results' implications for understanding the current level of risk and how to prioritize AI alignment research in the future.

2605.06490.title: Instrumental Choices: Measuring the Propensity of LLM Agents to Pursue Instrumental Behaviors
2605.06490.tldr: It is concluded that it is feasible to robustly measure tendencies for dangerous behaviour in current frontier AI agents and that realistic, low-nudge environments elicit IC behaviour rarely but systematically in most tested models.

2408.15207.title: Understanding the Effectiveness of Coverage Criteria for Large Language Models: A Special Angle from Jailbreak Attacks
2408.15207.tldr: This study develops a realtime jailbreak detection mechanism that achieves high accuracy in classifying queries as normal or jailbreak, and introduces a coverage-guided approach for generating jailbreak attack examples, enabling systematic refinement of prompts to uncover vulnerabilities.

2504.00446.title: Exposing the Ghost in the Transformer: Abnormal Detection for Large Language Models via Hidden State Forensics
2504.00446.tldr: This work introduces a novel approach to detecting abnormal behaviors in LLMs via hidden state forensics, and proposes a promising strategy to reinforce the security of LLM-integrated systems, paving the way for safer and more reliable deployment in high-stakes domains.
2504.00446.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2412.08201.title: Model-Editing-Based Jailbreak against Safety-aligned Large Language Models
