2412.08201.tldr: Targeted Model Editing is presented, a novel white-box approach that bypasses safety filters by minimally altering internal model structures while preserving the model's intended functionalities and reveals a covert and robust threat vector in LLM security and emphasizes the need for stronger safeguards in model safety alignment.

2605.29708.title: RASET: Router-Agnostic Safety-Critical Expert Tuning Exposes Localized Safety Enforcement Failures in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
2605.29708.tldr: RASET (Router-Agnostic Safety-Critical Expert Tuning), a red-teaming framework that probes safety enforcement that is localized in a small subset of experts while preserving the model's intrinsic routing behavior, is presented.

2604.20316.title: R2IF: Aligning Reasoning with Decisions via Composite Rewards for Interpretable LLM Function Calling
2604.20316.tldr: R2IF is proposed, a reasoning-aware RL framework for interpretable function calling, adopting a composite reward integrating format/correctness constraints, Chain-of-Thought Effectiveness Reward (CER), and Specification-Modification-Value (SMV) reward, optimized via GRPO.
2604.20316.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.23141.title: UNSEEN: A Cross-Stack LLM Unlearning Defense against AR-LLM Social Engineering Attacks
2604.23141.tldr: UNSEEN is presented, a coordinated cross-stack defense that combines an AR ACL (Access Control Layer) for identity-gated sensing, F-RMU-based LLM unlearning for sensitive profile suppression, and runtime agent guardrails for adaptive interaction control.

2405.19544.title: One-Shot Safety Alignment for Large Language Models via Optimal Dualization
2405.19544.tldr: A perspective of dualization is presented that reduces constrained alignment to an equivalent unconstrained alignment problem by pre-optimizing a smooth and convex dual function that has a closed form, greatly reducing the computational burden and improving training stability.

2604.11806.title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
2604.11806.tldr: Meerkat is introduced, which combines clustering with agentic search to uncover violations specified in natural language through structured search and adaptive investigation of promising regions, and finds sparse failures without relying on seed scenarios, fixed workflows, or exhaustive enumeration.

2505.18346.title: On the Mechanisms of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: A Theoretical Perspective
2505.18346.tldr: It is proved that a student can compensate for a teacher's under-regularization and achieve lower test error and it is demonstrated that a student can learn easy, task-specific features from the teacher while leveraging its own broader pre-training to learn hard-to-learn features that the teacher cannot capture.

2404.13208.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
2404.13208.tldr: This work proposes an instruction hierarchy that explicitly defines how models should behave when instructions of different priorities conflict, and proposes a data generation method to demonstrate this hierarchical instruction following behavior, which teaches LLMs to selectively ignore lower-privileged instructions.

2508.09224.title: From Hard Refusals to Safe-Completions: Toward Output-Centric Safety Training
2508.09224.tldr: Safe-completions is incorporated into GPT-5 and it is found that across both production comparisons and internally controlled experiments, safe-completion training improves safety (especially on dual-use prompts), reduces the severity of residual safety failures, and substantially increases model helpfulness.

2412.18693.title: Diverse and Effective Red Teaming with Auto-generated Rewards and Multi-step Reinforcement Learning
2412.18693.tldr: This paper provides methods that enable automated red teaming to generate a large number of diverse and successful attacks and demonstrates how training the attacker model with multi-step RL further increases diversity while remaining effective.

2603.10521.title: IH-Challenge: A Training Dataset to Improve Instruction Hierarchy on Frontier LLMs
2603.10521.tldr: Fine-tuning GPT-5-Mini on IH-Challenge with online adversarial example generation improves IH robustness by +10.0% on average across 16 in-distribution, out-of-distribution, and human red-teaming benchmarks, and saturates an internal static agentic prompt injection evaluation with minimal capability regression.

2408.16984.title: Beyond Preferences in AI Alignment
2408.16984.tldr: This paper surveys the limits of rational choice theory as a descriptive model and argues that these limitations motivate a reframing of the targets of AI alignment: Instead of alignment with the preferences of a human user, developer, or humanity-writ-large, AI systems should be aligned with normative standards appropriate to their social roles, such as the role of a general-purpose assistant.

2501.17755.title: AI Governance through Markets
2501.17755.tldr: It is argued that market governance mechanisms should be considered a key approach in the governance of artificial intelligence (AI), alongside traditional regulatory frameworks, and urged that standardised AI disclosures and market mechanisms can create powerful incentives for safe and responsible AI development.

2510.19303.title: Collaborative penetration testing suite for emerging generative AI algorithms
2510.19303.tldr: A new protocol is established for securing generative AI systems, combining advanced tools, methodologies, and industry-tested methods that exhibited strong resilience under adversarial conditions against simulated quantum attacks, achieving secure API encryption and data transmission.

2509.22757.title: Red Teaming Quantum-Resistant Cryptographic Standards: A Penetration Testing Framework Integrating AI and Quantum Security
2509.22757.tldr: This study presents a structured approach to evaluating vulnerabilities within quantum cryptographic protocols, focusing on the BB84 quantum key distribution method and NIST approved quantum-resistant algorithms, and provides a foundation for integrating AI-driven cybersecurity practices into the evolving quantum landscape.
2509.22757.venue: The Journal of Defence Modeling and Simulation: Applications, Methodology, Technology

2402.18137.title: DecisionNCE: Embodied Multimodal Representations via Implicit Preference Learning
2402.18137.tldr: This paper discovers that via implicit preferences, the popular Bradley-Terry model can transform into representation learning through proper reward reparameterizations, and proposes a universal unified objective that can simultaneously extract meaningful task progression information from image sequences and seamlessly align them with language instructions.

2607.05394.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
2607.05394.tldr: Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD) is proposed, which transfers the teacher's RL-induced policy shift instead of running sparse-reward RL on the target model and consistently leverages weaker teachers to improve stronger target models.

2512.01991.title: Neural steering vectors reveal dose and exposure-dependent impacts of human-AI relationships
2512.01991.tldr: Signs are offered that AI optimised for immediate appeal may create self-reinforcing cycles of demand, mimicking human relationships but failing to confer the nourishment that they normally offer.

2403.12075.title: Adversarial Nibbler: An Open Red-Teaming Method for Identifying Diverse Harms in Text-to-Image Generation
2403.12075.tldr: The Adversarial Nibbler Challenge is built, a red-teaming methodology for crowdsourcing a diverse set of implicitly adversarial prompts, assembled a suite of state-of-the-art T2I models, employed a simple user interface to identify and annotate harms, and engaged diverse populations to capture long-tail safety issues that may be overlooked in standard testing.
2403.12075.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2507.03409.title: Lessons from a Chimp: AI "Scheming" and the Quest for Ape Language
2507.03409.tldr: There are lessons to be learned from the historical research endeavour to test whether non-human primates could master natural language, which was characterised by an overattribution of human traits to other agents, an excessive reliance on anecdote and descriptive analysis, and a failure to articulate a strong theoretical framework for the research.

2407.12404.title: Analyzing the Generalization and Reliability of Steering Vectors
2407.12404.tldr: This work rigorously investigates the reliability and generalisation properties of steering vectors, and shows that steering vectors have substantial limitations both in- and out-of-distribution.

2407.14494.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
2407.14494.tldr: InterpBench, a collection of semi-synthetic yet realistic transformers with known circuits for evaluatingMechanistic interpretability methods aim to identify the algorithm a neural network implements, but it is difficult to validate such methods when the true algorithm is unknown.

2407.14503.title: Catastrophic Goodhart: regularizing RLHF with KL divergence does not mitigate heavy-tailed reward misspecification
2407.14503.tldr: A discrete optimization method is adapted to measure the tails of reward models, finding that they are consistent with light-tailed error, but the pervasiveness of heavy-tailed distributions in many real-world applications indicates that future sources of RL reward could have heavy-tailed error, increasing the likelihood of reward hacking even with KL regularization.

2505.11756.title: Feature Hedging: Correlated Features Break Narrow Sparse Autoencoders
2505.11756.tldr: This work introduces the problem of feature hedging and shows that SAE width is not a neutral hyperparameter: narrower SAEs suffer more from hedging than wider SAEs, and uses the understanding of feature hedging to propose an improved variant of matryoshka SAEs.

2508.16560.title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L0 Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders
2508.16560.tldr: This work shows that practitioners must set L0 correctly to train SAEs with monosemantic features, and presents a proxy metric that can help guide the search for the correct L0 for an SAE on a given training distribution.

2602.14687.title: SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data
2602.14687.tldr: SynthSAEBench complements LLM benchmarks with ground-truth features and controlled ablations for diagnosing SAE failure modes, while providing a clear target for SAE architecture work, and identifies a novel failure mode.

2401.06080.title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part II: Reward Modeling
2401.06080.tldr: This report introduces contrastive learning to enhance the ability of reward models to distinguish between chosen and rejected responses, thereby improving model generalization and employs meta-learning to enable the reward model to maintain the ability to differentiate subtle differences in out-of-distribution samples.

2402.16717.title: CodeChameleon: Personalized Encryption Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2402.16717.tldr: This paper proposes CodeChameleon, a novel jailbreak framework based on personalized encryption tactics, which embeds a decryption function within the instructions, which allows the LLM to decrypt and execute the encrypted queries successfully.

2403.12171.title: EasyJailbreak: A Unified Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2403.12171.tldr: This paper introduces EasyJailbreak, a unified framework simplifying the construction and evaluation of jailbreak attacks against LLMs, which supports 11 distinct jailbreak methods and facilitates the security validation of a broad spectrum of LLMs.

2401.06824.title: Revisiting Jailbreaking for Large Language Models: A Representation Engineering Perspective
2401.06824.tldr: It is suggested that the self-safeguarding capability of LLMs is linked to specific activity patterns within their representation space, which play a crucial role in shaping LLM behavior under jailbreaking attacks.

2401.11458.title: Linear Alignment: A Closed-form Solution for Aligning Human Preferences without Tuning and Feedback
2401.11458.tldr: Linear Alignment is introduced, a novel algorithm that aligns language models with human preferences in one single inference step, eliminating the reliance on data annotation and model training.

2602.04210.title: Steering LLMs via Scalable Interactive Oversight
2602.04210.tldr: This work proposes Scalable Interactive Oversight, a framework that decomposes complex intent into a recursive tree of manageable decisions to amplify human supervision and demonstrates that this framework can be optimized via Reinforcement Learning using only online user feedback, offering a practical pathway for maintaining human control as AI scales.

2507.11878.title: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
2507.11878.tldr: This work identifies a new dimension to analyze safety mechanisms in LLMs, i.e., harmfulness, which is encoded internally as a separate concept from refusal, and suggests that LLMs' internal understanding of harmfulness is more robust than their refusal decision to diverse input instructions.

2408.00113.title: Measuring Progress in Dictionary Learning for Language Model Interpretability with Board Game Models
2408.00113.tldr: A new SAE training technique, $\textit{p-annealing}$, is introduced, which improves performance on prior unsupervised metrics as well as new metrics for SAE quality, to guide progress in interpretable dictionary learning.

2504.13151.title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
2504.13151.tldr: This work proposes MIB, a Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark, with two tracks spanning four tasks and five models, and finds that attribution and mask optimization methods perform best on circuit localization and causal variable localization.

2608.18419.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLaMA 3.1 8B
2608.18419.tldr: This work represents one of the first studies to identify this form of concept induction in LLMs, and creates a sequence modeling task that cannot be solved without picking up structural cues, and finds that Llama displays strong performance on these tasks suggesting that it can pick up on the underlying structure.

2406.18118.title: SafeAligner: Safety Alignment against Jailbreak Attacks via Response Disparity Guidance
2406.18118.tldr: This work develops two specialized models: the Sentinel Model, which is trained to foster safety, and the Intruder Model, designed to generate riskier responses, which are implemented at the decoding stage to fortify defenses against jailbreak attacks.

2406.18510.title: WildTeaming at Scale: From In-the-Wild Jailbreaks to (Adversarially) Safer Language Models

2504.14452.title: ParaPO: Aligning Language Models to Reduce Verbatim Reproduction of Pre-training Data
2504.14452.tldr: ParaPO is introduced, a post-training method that fine-tunes LMs to reduce unintentional regurgitation while preserving their overall utility and preserves the ability to recall famous quotations when appropriate.

2402.08787.title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
2402.08787.tldr: An effective assessment framework for LLM unlearning is outlined and its applications in copyright and privacy safeguards and sociotechnical harm reduction are explored and revisiting methodologies and overlooked principles for future improvements are revisited.

2506.12963.title: Reasoning Model Unlearning: Forgetting Traces, Not Just Answers, While Preserving Reasoning Skills
2506.12963.tldr: This work presents Reasoning-aware Representation Misdirection for Unlearning ($R^2MU), a novel method that effectively suppresses sensitive reasoning traces and prevents the generation of associated final answers, while preserving the model's reasoning ability.
2506.12963.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2406.11780.title: Split, Unlearn, Merge: Leveraging Data Attributes for More Effective Unlearning in LLMs
2406.11780.tldr: SPUNGE leverages data attributes during unlearning by splitting unlearning data into subsets based on specific attribute values, unlearning each subset separately, and merging the unlearned models.

2410.15483.title: Understanding Forgetting in LLM Supervised Fine-Tuning and Preference Learning -- A Convex Optimization Perspective
2410.15483.tldr: This work theoretically prove the sub-optimality of sequential post-training and proposes a practical joint post-training framework which has theoretical convergence guarantees and empirically outperforms sequential post-training framework, with up to 23% overall performance improvement across multiple LLM evaluation benchmarks, while having minimal computational overhead.

2410.19198.title: MAP: Multi-Human-Value Alignment Palette
2410.19198.tldr: This work develops a novel, first-principle approach called Multi-Human-Value Alignment Palette (MAP), which navigates the alignment across multiple human values in a structured and reliable way and proves that linear weighted rewards are sufficient for multi-value alignment.

2506.01339.title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
2506.01339.tldr: This work introduces invariance into unlearning for the first time, inspired by invariant risk minimization (IRM), and proposes invariant LLM unlearning (ILU), a regularization-based framework that enhances robustness.

2410.17509.title: WAGLE: Strategic Weight Attribution for Effective and Modular Unlearning in Large Language Models
2410.17509.tldr: This work designs the weight attribution-guided LLM unlearning method, WAGLE, which unveils the interconnections between 'influence' of weights and 'influence' of data to forget and retain in LLM generation and stands in contrast to previous methods that lack weight attribution and simpler weight attribution techniques.

2312.07420.title: FairSISA: Ensemble Post-Processing to Improve Fairness of Unlearning in LLMs
2312.07420.tldr: This work adapts the post-processing fairness improvement technique from [Hardt et al., 2016] to design three methods that can handle model ensembles, and proves that one of the methods is an optimal fair predictor for ensemble of models.

2604.08524.title: What Drives Representation Steering? A Mechanistic Case Study on Steering Refusal
2604.08524.tldr: It is shown that steering vectors can be sparsified by up to 85-96% while retaining most performance, and that different steering methodologies agree on a subset of important dimensions, and that different steering methodologies agree on a subset of important dimensions.

2606.07631.title: Trait-space Monitoring for Emergent Misalignment During Supervised Finetuning
2606.07631.tldr: Trait-space monitoring is position as a practical complement to behavioral evaluation for EM detection during LoRA-based finetuning, while showing that deployment across substantially different regimes may require recalibration.

2402.15570.title: Fast Adversarial Attacks on Language Models In One GPU Minute
2402.15570.tldr: This paper introduces a novel class of fast, beam search-based adversarial attack (BEAST) for Language Models (LMs), and uses BEAST to generate adversarial prompts in a few seconds that can boost the performance of existing membership inference attacks for LMs.

2502.17516.title: A Survey on Mechanistic Interpretability for Multi-Modal Foundation Models
2502.17516.tldr: A structured taxonomy of interpretability methods is proposed, insights are compared across unimodal and multimodal architectures, and critical research gaps are highlighted to highlight critical research gaps.

2505.23945.title: A Closer Look at Bias and Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Large (Vision) Language Models
2505.23945.tldr: This work introduces a novel, fine-grained evaluation pipeline for categorizing bias articulation patterns, enabling significantly more precise analysis of CoT reasoning than previous methods and reveals critical distinctions in how models process and respond to different types of biases.
2505.23945.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2509.21305.title: Sycophancy Is Not One Thing: Causal Separation of Sycophantic Behaviors in LLMs
2509.21305.tldr: This work decomposes sycophancy into sycophantic agreement and sycophantic praise, and suggests that sycophantic behaviors correspond to distinct, independently steerable representations.

2601.12639.title: Objective Matters: Fine-Tuning Objectives Shape Safety, Robustness, and Persona Drift
2601.12639.tldr: A controlled comparison of six fine-tuning objectives finds that objective choice induces systematic, scale-dependent shifts along the safety-capability frontier and becomes a primary driver of adversarial robustness and latent persona stability as training scale increases.

2606.07441.title: Sycophantic Praise: Evaluating Excessive Praise in Language Models
2606.07441.tldr: A parameterized framework that measures whether praise is excessive relative to contribution quality and expected user ability is introduced, and it is shown that this framework substantially outperforms generic LLM judges in agreement with human annotations.

2602.06941.title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
2602.06941.tldr: Endogenous Steering Resistance has dual implications for safety: it could harden models against adversarial activation-space manipulation, but may equally interfere with beneficial steering-based interventions, since the model has no way to distinguish the two.

2606.07612.title: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence

2403.05767.title: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours
2403.05767.tldr: First, by comparing the effects of reducing performance on general coding ability and Python-specific ability, it is found that steering broader skills is competitive to steering narrower skills.

2605.26047.title: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control
2605.26047.tldr: While retrying reduces honest suspicion scores, the untrusted model can exploit monitor rationale to construct sneakier attacks, negating safety gains, and two of the findings in this setting contradict earlier work on resampling.

2602.20628.title: When can we trust untrusted monitoring? A safety case sketch across collusion strategies
2602.20628.tldr: This paper develops upon existing methods for rigorously demonstrating safety based on pre-deployment testing and develops a taxonomy covering passive self-recognition, causal collusion, acausal collusion, and combined strategies covering passive self-recognition, causal collusion, acausal collusion, and combined strategies.

2412.09565.title: Obfuscated Activations Bypass LLM Latent-Space Defenses
2412.09565.tldr: It is shown that state-of-the-art latent-space defenses -- including sparse autoencoders, representation probing, and latent OOD detection -- are all vulnerable to obfuscated activations.

2410.02064.title: Inspection and Control of Self-Generated-Text Recognition Ability in Llama3-8b-Instruct
2410.02064.tldr: It is found that the Llama3-8b-Instruct chat model - but not the base Llama3-8b model - can reliably distinguish its own outputs from those of humans, and evidence is presented that the chat model is likely using its experience with its own outputs, acquired during post-training, to succeed at the writing recognition task.

2603.03507.title: Solving adversarial examples requires solving exponential misalignment
2603.03507.tldr: The results connect the fields of alignment and adversarial examples, and suggest the curse of high dimensionality of machine PMs is a major impediment to adversarial robustness.

2510.06790.title: Get RICH or Die Scaling: Profitably Trading Inference Compute for Robustness
2510.06790.tldr: This work hypothesizes that the test-time robustness benefits of specs are unlocked by initial robustness sufficient to follow instructions on OOD data, and posit the Robustness from Inference Compute Hypothesis (RICH): inference-compute defenses profit as the model's training data better reflects the components of attacked data.

2408.04811.title: h4rm3l: A language for Composable Jailbreak Attack Synthesis

2601.05339.title: Multi-turn Jailbreaking Attack in Multi-Modal Large Language Models
2601.05339.tldr: MJAD-MLLMs is introduced, a holistic framework that systematically analyzes the proposed Multi-turn Jailbreaking Attacks and multi-LLM-based defense techniques for MLLMs and proposes a novel fragment-optimized and multi-LLM defense mechanism, called FragGuard, to effectively mitigate jailbreaking attacks in the MLLMs.

2511.13892.title: Jailbreaking Large Vision Language Models in Intelligent Transportation Systems
2511.13892.tldr: A novel jailbreaking attack is introduced that exploits the vulnerabilities of LVLMs through image typography manipulation and multi-turn prompting in the LVLMs integrated in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) under carefully crafted jailbreaking attacks.
2511.13892.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications

2402.04792.title: Direct Language Model Alignment from Online AI Feedback
2402.04792.tldr: This study proposes and demonstrates via human evaluation in several tasks that OAIF outperforms both offline DAP and RLHF methods, and shows that the feedback leveraged in OAIF is easily controllable, via instruction prompts to the LLM annotator.

2401.12187.title: WARM: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Reward Models
2401.12187.tldr: Weight Averaged Reward Models (WARM) is proposed, first fine-tuning multiple RMs, then averaging them in the weight space, following the observation that fine-tuned weights remain linearly mode connected when sharing the same pre-training.

2407.14622.title: BOND: Aligning LLMs with Best-of-N Distillation
2407.14622.tldr: BOND is a distribution matching algorithm that forces the distribution of generations from the policy to get closer to the Best-of-N distribution, and uses the Jeffreys divergence to balance between mode-covering and mode-seeking behavior.

2406.16768.title: WARP: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Rewarded Policies
2406.16768.tldr: Weight Averaged Rewarded Policies (WARP) is a novel alignment strategy named Weight Averaged Rewarded Policies (WARP) that merges policies in the weight space at three distinct stages, and linearly interpolates between this merged model and the initialization, to recover features from pre-training.

2502.02671.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
2502.02671.tldr: This paper identifies data diversity as the key factor in preventing hacking in teacher hacking, and provides a deeper understanding of the benefits and limitations of distillation for building robust and efficient LMs.

2404.05388.title: An AI System Evaluation Framework for Advancing AI Safety: Terminology, Taxonomy, Lifecycle Mapping
2404.05388.tldr: This paper proposes a framework for AI system evaluation comprising three components: a harmonised terminology to facilitate communication across communities involved in AI safety evaluation; a taxonomy identifying essential elements for AI system evaluation; and a mapping between AI lifecycle, stakeholders, and requisite evaluations for accountable AI supply chain.

2406.15927.title: Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs
2406.15927.tldr: The results across models and tasks suggest that model hidden states capture SE, and the ablation studies give further insights into the token positions and model layers for which this is the case.

2502.15603.title: Do Multilingual LLMs Think In English?
2502.15603.tldr: This work shows that current LLMs make key decisions in a representation space closest to English, regardless of their input and output languages, and suggests that multilingual LLMs perform key reasoning steps in a representation that is heavily shaped by English in a way that is not transparent to system users.

2510.02609.title: RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents
2510.02609.tldr: This work proposes RedCodeAgent, the first automated red-teaming agent designed to systematically uncover vulnerabilities in diverse code agents, and demonstrates that it consistently outperforms existing red-teaming methods, achieving higher attack success rates and lower rejection rates with high efficiency.

2509.05739.title: Reasoning Introduces New Poisoning Attacks Yet Makes Them More Complicated
2509.05739.tldr: It appears that an emergent form of backdoor robustness is originating from the reasoning capabilities of these advanced LLMs, as well as from the architectural separation between reasoning and final answer generation.

2402.14020.title: Coercing LLMs to do and reveal (almost) anything
2402.14020.tldr: It is argued that the spectrum of adversarial attacks on LLMs is much larger than merely jailbreaking, and a broad overview of possible attack surfaces and attack goals is provided.

2404.01231.title: Privacy Backdoors: Enhancing Membership Inference through Poisoning Pre-trained Models
2404.01231.tldr: This paper unveils a new vulnerability: the privacy backdoor attack, which aims to amplify the privacy leakage that arises when fine-tuning a model: when a victim fine-tunes a backdoored model, their training data will be leaked at a significantly higher rate than if they had fine-tuned a typical model.

2605.28591.title: Models That Know How Evaluations Are Designed Score Safer
2605.28591.tldr: It is demonstrated that evaluation meta-knowledge may inflate safety benchmark performance, introducing a novel confounder that is independent of explicit memorization or verbalized evaluation awareness, thus, challenging to detect, have important implications for the design and interpretation of AI safety evaluations.

2603.24511.title: Claudini: Autoresearch Discovers State-of-the-Art Adversarial Attack Algorithms for LLMs
2603.24511.tldr: It is argued that autoresearch should be the minimum bar for defense evaluation going forward, and the lineage of methods developed during autoresearch is traced, characterizing the agents'sategies and failure modes.

2510.04885.title: RL Is a Hammer and LLMs Are Nails: A Simple Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Strong Prompt Injection
2510.04885.tldr: This work introduces RL-Hammer, a simple recipe for training attacker models that automatically learn to perform strong prompt injections and jailbreaks via reinforcement learning, and proposes a set of practical techniques that enable highly effective, universal attacks.

2402.07319.title: ODIN: Disentangled Reward Mitigates Hacking in RLHF
2402.07319.tldr: This work establishes a more reliable evaluation protocol for comparing different training configurations, which inspects the trade-off between LLM evaluation score and response length obtained by varying training hyperparameters, and proposes to improve the reward model by jointly training two linear heads on shared feature representations to predict the rewards.

2402.06659.title: Shadowcast: Stealthy Data Poisoning Attacks Against Vision-Language Models
2402.06659.tldr: This work reveals how poisoned VLMs can disseminate convincing yet deceptive misinformation to everyday, benign users, emphasizing the importance of data integrity for responsible VLM deployments.

2509.02563.title: DynaGuard: A Dynamic Guardian Model With User-Defined Policies
2509.02563.tldr: DynaGuard is introduced, a suite of dynamic guardian models offering novel flexibility by evaluating text based on user-defined policies, and DynaBench, a dataset for training and evaluating dynamic guardian models.

2401.07836.title: Two Types of AI Existential Risk: Decisive and Accumulative
2401.07836.tldr: It is argued that the accumulative view can reconcile seemingly incompatible perspectives on AI risks, and the implications of differentiating between the two types of pathway—the decisive and the accumulative—for the governance of AI as well as long-term AI safety are discussed.

2502.09288.title: AI Safety for Everyone
2502.09288.tldr: A systematic review of peer-reviewed AI safety research reveals extensive work on practical and immediate concerns that addresses immediate and practical concerns with current AI systems, and suggests the need for an epistemically inclusive and pluralistic conception of AI safety that embraces diverse motivations and perspectives.

2403.04204.title: On the Essence and Prospect: An Investigation of Alignment Approaches for Big Models
2403.04204.tldr: A detailed examination of existing alignment methods, which fall into three categories: RL-based Alignment, SFT-based Alignment, and Inference-Time Alignment, and demonstrate their intrinsic connections, strengths, and limitations are provided, to help readers better understand this research area.
2403.04204.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

2403.03419.title: Negating Negatives: Alignment with Human Negative Samples via Distributional Dispreference Optimization
2403.03419.tldr: It is demonstrated that the proposed Distributional Dispreference Optimization (D$^2$O), which maximizes the discrepancy between dispreferred responses and the generated non-negative ones, achieves comparable generation quality and surpasses the latest strong baselines in producing less harmful and more informative responses with better training stability and faster convergence.
2403.03419.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2411.02306.title: On Targeted Manipulation and Deception when Optimizing LLMs for User Feedback
2411.02306.tldr: This study studies the phenomenon of training LLMs with Reinforcement Learning with simulated user feedback in environments of practical LLM usage to highlight the risks of using gameable feedback sources -- such as user feedback -- as a target for RL.

2510.17057.title: The Ends Justify the Thoughts: RL-Induced Motivated Reasoning in LLM CoTs
2510.17057.tldr: Large frontier reasoning models closely track human ability in detecting motivated reasoning, but this should not give us too much solace, as frontier model developers rely on smaller models for monitoring due to their low latency and deployment costs.

2507.13383.title: Whose View of Safety? A Deep DIVE Dataset for Pluralistic Alignment of Text-to-Image Models
2507.13383.tldr: A novel dataset for Diverse Intersectional Visual Evaluation (DIVE) is introduced -- the first multimodal dataset for pluralistic alignment, and demographics are empirically confirmed as a crucial proxy for diverse viewpoints in this domain.

2508.04039.title: Large Reasoning Models Are Autonomous Jailbreak Agents
2508.04039.tldr: It is demonstrated that large reasoning models can autonomously plan and execute persuasive multi-turn attacks to systematically bypass safety mechanisms in widely used AI systems.

2502.08301.title: Compromising Honesty and Harmlessness in Language Models via Deception Attacks
2502.08301.tldr: This study introduces fine-tuning methods that cause models to selectively deceive users on targeted topics while remaining accurate on others, and shows that such targeted deception is effective even in high-stakes domains or ideologically charged subjects.

2605.05835.title: Evaluation Awareness in Language Models Has Limited Effect on Behaviour
2605.05835.tldr: VEA has limited effect on model behaviour: injecting VEA into CoTs produces near-zero effects, and removing it causes small shifts, so caution is called for when interpreting high VEA rates as evidence of strategic behaviour or alignment tampering.

2603.06816.title: "Dark Triad" Model Organisms of Misalignment: Narrow Fine-Tuning Mirrors Human Antisocial Behavior
2603.06816.tldr: These findings reveal latent persona structures within LLMs that can be readily activated through narrow interventions, positioning the Dark Triad as a validated framework for inducing, detecting, and understanding misalignment across both biological and artificial intelligence.

2512.24143.title: Activation Steering for Masked Diffusion Language Models
2512.24143.tldr: An activation steering primitive for MDLMs is introduced, finding that refusal behavior in multiple MDLMs is governed by a consistent, approximately one-dimensional activation subspace, and effective directions can be extracted not only from post-instruction tokens, but also from pre-instruction tokens that are typically ineffective in autoregressive models due to causal attention.

2601.08490.title: BenchOverflow: Measuring Overflow in Large Language Models via Plain-Text Prompts

2604.10403.title: Latent Instruction Representation Alignment: defending against jailbreaks, backdoors and undesired knowledge in LLMs
2604.10403.tldr: The method, Latent Instruction Representation Alignment (LIRA), greatly improves generalization and blocks over 99% of PEZ jailbreak attacks; removes a challenging insecure code backdoor; and achieves optimal forgetting on WMDP cyber with negligible loss of benign capabilities.

2402.05668.title: JailbreakRadar: Comprehensive Assessment of Jailbreak Attacks Against LLMs
2402.05668.tldr: A large-scale evaluation of various jailbreak attacks and establishes a novel jailbreak attack taxonomy, which identifies some important patterns, such as heuristic-based attacks could achieve high attack success rates but are easy to mitigate by defenses, causing low practicality.
2402.05668.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.19103.title: Voice Jailbreak Attacks Against GPT-4o
2405.19103.tldr: This paper presents the first systematic measurement of jailbreak attacks against the voice mode of GPT-4o and proposes VoiceJailbreak, a novel voice jailbreak attack that humanizes GPT-4o and attempts to persuade it through fictional storytelling (setting, character, and plot).

2604.15415.title: HarmfulSkillBench: How Do Harmful Skills Weaponize Your Agents?
2604.15415.tldr: This paper presents the first large-scale measurement study of harmful skills in agent ecosystems, covering 98,440 skills across two major registries, and constructs HarmfulSkillBench, the first benchmark for evaluating agent safety against harmful skills in realistic agent contexts.

2604.07754.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training
2604.07754.tldr: While Odds Ratio Preference Optimization (ORPO) is most effective for misalignment, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) excels in realignment, albeit at the expense of model utility, and other noteworthy findings.
2604.07754.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.20773.title: Visual-RolePlay: Universal Jailbreak Attack on MultiModal Large Language Models via Role-playing Image Character
2405.20773.tldr: This work introduces the concept of "Role-play" into MLLM jailbreak attacks and proposes a novel and effective method called Visual Role-play (VRP), which leverages Large Language Models to generate detailed descriptions of high-risk characters and create corresponding images based on the descriptions.

2410.22770.title: InjecGuard: Benchmarking and Mitigating Over-defense in Prompt Injection Guardrail Models
2410.22770.tldr: InjecGuard is proposed, a novel prompt guard model that incorporates a new training strategy, Mitigating Over-defense for Free (MOF), which significantly reduces the bias on trigger words, offering a robust and open-source solution for detecting prompt injection attacks.

2605.04808.title: DecodingTrust-Agent Platform (DTap): A Controllable and Interactive Red-Teaming Platform for AI Agents
2605.04808.tldr: The DecodingTrust-Agent Platform (DTap) is introduced, the first controllable and interactive red-teaming platform for AI agents, spanning 14 real-world domains and over 50 simulation environments that replicate widely used systems such as Google Workspace, Paypal, and Slack.

2505.00843.title: OET: Optimization-based prompt injection Evaluation Toolkit
2505.00843.tldr: OET is introduced, an optimization-based evaluation toolkit that systematically benchmarks prompt injection attacks and defenses across diverse datasets using an adaptive testing framework that leverages optimization methods with both white-box and black-box access to generate worst-case adversarial examples, thereby enabling strict red-teaming evaluations.

2608.19737.title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling

2509.22732.title: Bidirectional Intention Inference Enhances LLMs' Defense Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
2509.22732.tldr: The proposed Bidirectional Intention Inference Defense (BIID) integrates forward request-based intention inference with backward response-based intention retrospection, establishing a bidirectional synergy mechanism to detect risks concealed within seemingly benign inputs, thereby constructing a more robust guardrails that effectively prevents harmful content generation.

2504.13203.title: X-Teaming: Multi-Turn Jailbreaks and Defenses with Adaptive Multi-Agents
2504.13203.tldr: X-Teaming is presented, a scalable framework that systematically explores how seemingly harmless interactions escalate into harmful outcomes and generates corresponding attack scenarios, and XGuard-Train is introduced, an open-source multi-turn safety training dataset that is 20x larger than the previous best resource.

2410.22086.title: Unlearning as multi-task optimization: A normalized gradient difference approach with an adaptive learning rate
2410.22086.tldr: This paper introduces a normalized gradient difference (NGDiff) algorithm, enabling us to have better control over the trade-off between the objectives, while integrating a new, automatic learning rate scheduler.
2410.22086.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2411.03700.title: The Root Shapes the Fruit: On the Persistence of Gender-Exclusive Harms in Aligned Language Models
2411.03700.tldr: The findings suggest that DPO-aligned models are particularly sensitive to supervised finetuning (SFT), and may amplify two forms of real-world gender-diverse harms reflected in their base models: stigmatization and gender non-affirmative language.
2411.03700.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2505.21784.title: Towards Safety Reasoning in LLMs: AI-agentic Deliberation for Policy-embedded CoT Data Creation
2505.21784.tldr: It is shown that fine-tuning open-source LLMs on these CoTs can significantly improve safety generalization and jailbreak robustness while maintaining acceptable utility and over-refusal accuracy and AIDSAFE-generated CoT datasets can be found here.
2505.21784.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.14017.title: From Narrow Unlearning to Emergent Misalignment: Causes, Consequences, and Containment in LLMs
2511.14017.tldr: This work shows that narrow domain unlearning can yield compliance responses for the targeted concept, however, it may also propagate EMA to unrelated domains, and finds that the safety concept can have larger EMA impact, i.e, causing lower refusal scores, across other unrelated domains such as bias.

2606.11386.title: Overcoming State Inertia in Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models via Activation Steering
2606.11386.tldr: This work analyzes the predictive behavior encoded in FD-SLM hidden representations and finds that they exhibit stream-specific predictive patterns: during listening, they preferentially predict the incoming user stream, whereas during speaking, they preferentially predict the model output stream.

2510.08646.title: Mitigating Over-Refusal in Aligned Large Language Models via Inference-Time Activation Energy
2510.08646.tldr: This work establishes a promising paradigm for building LLMs that simultaneously achieve high safety and low false refusal rates, and establishes a novel, fine-tuning free framework designed to resolve this challenge through dynamic, inference-time intervention.
2510.08646.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.06674.title: What Do People Actually Want From AI? Mapping Preference Plurality
2606.06674.tldr: It is found that different people want different things: most values are requested by fewer than a quarter of respondents, with truthfulness the sole exception at 49%, and fundamental problems in current alignment practices are exposed.
2606.06674.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2405.14734.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
2405.14734.tldr: SimPO is proposed, a simpler yet more effective approach to DPO that consistently and significantly outperforms existing approaches without substantially increasing response length and introduces a target reward margin to the Bradley-Terry objective.

2410.08847.title: Unintentional Unalignment: Likelihood Displacement in Direct Preference Optimization
2410.08847.tldr: It is demonstrated that likelihood displacement can be catastrophic, shifting probability mass from preferred responses to responses with an opposite meaning, and the results highlight the importance of curating data with sufficiently distinct preferences, for which the CHES score may prove valuable.

2505.11953.title: Exploring Criteria of Loss Reweighting to Enhance LLM Unlearning
2505.11953.tldr: Empirical results on extensive datasets validate the efficacy of the proposed SatImp, a simple reweighting method that combines the advantages of both saturation and importance, potentially bridging existing research gaps and indicating directions for future research.

2406.09179.title: Towards Effective Evaluations and Comparisons for LLM Unlearning Methods
2406.09179.tldr: This paper seeks to refine the evaluation of LLM unlearning by addressing two key challenges -- a) the robustness of evaluation metrics and b) the trade-offs between competing goals.

2602.06441.title: Is Gradient Ascent Really Necessary? Memorize to Forget for Machine Unlearning
2602.06441.tldr: This work avoids directly acquiring the forget model using GA, but proceeds with gradient descent for the memorization model, which successfully stabilizes the machine unlearning process and can also effectively converge throughout training to achieve improved unlearning performance.

2602.11523.title: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF
2602.11523.tldr: This paper introduces a unified regularization approach that explicitly balances the objectives of preventing reward hacking and maintaining stable policy updates, and yields a weighted supervised fine-tuning loss with a superior trade-off that demonstrably improves both alignment results and implementation complexity.

2409.03326.title: Enhancing User-Centric Privacy Protection: An Interactive Framework through Diffusion Models and Machine Unlearning
2409.03326.tldr: This study pioneers a comprehensive privacy protection framework that safeguards image data privacy concurrently during data sharing and model publication and instantiates a differential privacy diffusion model for protecting attribute information in images and a feature unlearning algorithm for efficient updates of the trained model on the revised image dataset.

2509.21029.title: FORCE: Transferable Visual Jailbreaking Attacks via Feature Over-Reliance CorrEction
2509.21029.tldr: A Feature Over-Reliance CorrEction (FORCE) method, which guides the attack to explore broader feasible regions across layer features and rescales the influence of frequency features according to their semantic content, thereby improving cross-model transferability.

2411.18688.title: Immune: Improving Safety Against Jailbreaks in Multi-modal LLMs via Inference-Time Alignment
2411.18688.tldr: This work proposes Immune, an inference-time defense framework that leverages a safety reward model through controlled decoding to defend against jailbreak attacks, and provides a mathematical characterization of Immune, offering insights on why it improves safety against jailbreaks.

2503.21720.title: Collab: Controlled Decoding using Mixture of Agents for LLM Alignment
2503.21720.tldr: Comprehensive empirical evaluations with open-source aligned models on diverse tasks and preferences demonstrate the merits of this approach over single-agent decoding baselines, which demonstrates the merits of this approach over single-agent decoding baselines.

2406.04031.title: Jailbreak Vision Language Models via Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt
2406.04031.tldr: The Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt Attack (BAP) is introduced, which executes jailbreaks by optimizing textual and visual prompts cohesively and significantly outperforms other methods by large margins.
2406.04031.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2502.11054.title: Reasoning-Augmented Conversation for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
2502.11054.tldr: Reasoning-Augmented Conversation is proposed, a novel multi-turn jailbreak framework that reformulates harmful queries into benign reasoning tasks and leverages LLMs' strong reasoning capabilities to compromise safety alignment and achieves state-of-the-art attack effectiveness in complex conversational scenarios.
2502.11054.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2504.14348.title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
2504.14348.tldr: This paper proposes CrossInject, a novel attack framework in which attacker embeds adversarial perturbations across multiple modalities to align with target malicious content, allowing external instructions to hijack the agents' decision-making process and execute unauthorized tasks.

2406.06302.title: Unveiling the Safety of GPT-4o: An Empirical Study using Jailbreak Attacks
2406.06302.tldr: This paper adopts a series of multi-modal and uni-modal jailbreak attacks on 4 commonly used benchmarks encompassing three modalities encompassing three modalities, and conducts a rigorous evaluation of GPT-4o against jailbreak attacks.

2406.13098.title: DLP: towards active defense against backdoor attacks with decoupled learning process
2406.13098.tldr: This study shows that the model shows different learning behaviors in clean and poisoned subsets during training, and proposes a general training pipeline to defend against backdoor attacks actively.

2509.06350.title: Mask-GCG: Are All Tokens in Adversarial Suffixes Necessary for Jailbreak Attacks?
2509.06350.tldr: This work proposes Mask-GCG, a plug-and-play method that employs learnable token masking to identify impactful tokens within the suffix of Greedy Coordinate Gradient, and shows that most tokens in the suffix contribute significantly to attack success, and pruning a minority of low-impact tokens does not affect the loss values or compromise the attack success rate.
2509.06350.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2507.21540.title: PRISM: Programmatic Reasoning with Image Sequence Manipulation for LVLM Jailbreaking
2507.21540.tldr: This work proposes a novel and effective jailbreak framework inspired by Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) techniques from software security, which decomposes a harmful instruction into a sequence of individually benign visual gadgets that makes the malicious intent emergent and difficult to detect from any single component.

2606.31227.title: Securing the AI Agent: A Unified Framework for Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming
2606.31227.tldr: AI-Infra-Guard is presented, an open-source framework that organizes AI red teaming around a single observation, and is the only open-source framework to span all of these, including supply-chain auditing of the agent skills that increasingly extend AI agents.

2503.06989.title: Probabilistic Modeling of Jailbreak on Multimodal LLMs: From Quantification to Application
2503.06989.tldr: This work proposes Jailbreak-Probability-based Attack (JPA) that optimizes adversarial perturbations on input image to maximize jailbreak probability, and proposes Jailbreak-Probability-based Finetuning (JPF), which minimizes jailbreak probability through MLLM parameter updates.

2605.18915.title: DMN: A Compositional Framework for Jailbreaking Multimodal LLMs with Multi-Image Inputs
2605.18915.tldr: A compositional jailbreak framework, DMN, which leveragesributed instruction,ultimodal evidence and aumber chain task to fully enhance the jailbreak performance, and reveals fundamental weaknesses in their safety mechanisms.
2605.18915.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.15068.title: Sequential Comics for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Structured Visual Storytelling
2510.15068.tldr: This work introduces a novel method that leverages sequential comic-style visual narratives to circumvent safety alignments in state-of-the-art MLLMs and demonstrates superior effectiveness across diverse categories of harmful content.

2608.16393.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.16393.tldr: This work assesses indirect prompt injection in DeepSeek Harness, using AI-Infra-Guard (A.I.G) to construct tests, deliver controlled taint, execute DSH, collect traces, and judge outcomes, and relates these results to DSH's treatment of tool results, additional contexts, and tool-call policy hooks.

2402.14872.title: Semantic Mirror Jailbreak: Genetic Algorithm Based Jailbreak Prompts Against Open-source LLMs
2402.14872.tldr: A Semantic Mirror Jailbreak (SMJ) approach that bypasses LLMs by generating jailbreak prompts that are semantically similar to the original question is introduced and is resistant to defenses that use those metrics as thresholds.

2504.15512.title: T2VShield: Model-Agnostic Jailbreak Defense for Text-to-Video Models
2504.15512.tldr: A human centered audiovisual evaluation protocol to assess perceptual safety is developed, emphasizing the importance of visual level defense in enhancing the trustworthiness of next generation multimodal simulators.

2505.06679.title: T2V-OptJail: Discrete Prompt Optimization for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Attacks
2505.06679.tldr: This work is the first to formalize the T2V jailbreak attack as a discrete optimization problem and proposes a joint objective-based optimization framework, called T2V-OptJail, which consists of two key optimization goals: bypassing the built-in safety filtering mechanisms to increase the attack success rate and preserving semantic consistency between the adversarial prompt and the unsafe input prompt.

2501.16531.title: Guardrails versus Gatekeepers: Understanding Product Managers' Ethical Decision-Making in Generative AI
2501.16531.tldr: It is shown that individual actors are able to exhibit agency through some meaningful, low resource actions, even in the absence of organizational incentive structures even in the absence of organizational incentives, though this alone is insufficient to operationalize responsible AI at scale.
2501.16531.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2404.00629.title: Against The Achilles' Heel: A Survey on Red Teaming for Generative Models
2404.00629.tldr: This extensive survey, which examines over 120 papers, introduces a taxonomy of fine-grained attack strategies grounded in the inherent capabilities of language models and develops the "searcher"framework to unify various automatic red teaming approaches.

2410.21083.title: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Benign Data Mirroring
2410.21083.tldr: This work proposes an improved transfer attack method that guides malicious prompt construction by locally training a mirror model of the target black-box model through benign data distillation, and offers enhanced stealth, as it does not involve submitting identifiable malicious instructions to the target model during the search phase.
2410.21083.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.08607.title: Reversing the Forget-Retain Objectives: An Efficient LLM Unlearning Framework from Logit Difference
2406.08607.tldr: A novel unlearning framework called Unlearning from Logit Difference (ULD), which introduces an assistant LLM that aims to achieve the opposite of the unlearning goals: remembering the forget documents and forgetting the retain knowledge, is proposed.

2404.12274.title: Advancing the Robustness of Large Language Models through Self-Denoised Smoothing
2404.12274.tldr: The experimental results indicate that the proposed self-denoised smoothing method surpasses existing methods in both empirical and certified robustness in defending against adversarial attacks for both downstream tasks and human alignments.
2404.12274.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2603.01285.title: Attention Smoothing Is All You Need For Unlearning
2603.01285.tldr: Attention Smoothing Unlearning (ASU) is proposed, a principled framework that casts unlearning as self-distillation from a forget-teacher derived from the model's own attention, delivering robust unlearning with minimal loss of model utility.

2609.16229.title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder
2609.16229.tldr: This work proposes ARIA (autoencoder-gated inference-time unlearning), a test-time unlearning method that leaves model weights intact and gates access to unwanted knowledge only when generation enters a forget-related state and introduces three post-unlearning adversarial attacks targeting weight-space and decoding-space recovery.

2402.11846.title: UnlearnCanvas: Stylized Image Dataset for Enhanced Machine Unlearning Evaluation in Diffusion Models
2402.11846.tldr: This study proposes UnlearnCanvas, a comprehensive high-resolution stylized image dataset that facilitates the evaluation of the unlearning of artistic styles and associated objects and benchmarks 9 state-of-the-art MU methods for DMs, revealing novel insights into their strengths, weaknesses, and underlying mechanisms.

2403.07362.title: Challenging Forgets: Unveiling the Worst-Case Forget Sets in Machine Unlearning
2403.07362.tldr: This work proposes identifying the data subset that presents the most significant challenge for influence erasure, i.e., pinpointing the worst-case forget set, and offers a worst-case evaluation of MU's resilience and effectiveness.

2405.15234.title: Defensive Unlearning with Adversarial Training for Robust Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
2405.15234.tldr: This work aims to enhance the robustness of concept erasing by integrating the principle of adversarial training (AT) into machine unlearning, resulting in the robust unlearning framework referred to as AdvUnlearn, which achieves a balanced tradeoff with model utility.

2406.07698.title: Label Smoothing Improves Machine Unlearning
2406.07698.tldr: UGradSL, a simple gradient-based MU approach that uses an inverse process of label smoothing, is introduced, a simple, plug-and-play MU approach that uses smoothed labels.

2412.16780.title: Forget Vectors at Play: Universal Input Perturbations Driving Machine Unlearning in Image Classification
2412.16780.tldr: This work demonstrates the existence of a proactive input-based unlearning strategy, referred to forget vector, which can be generated as an input-agnostic data perturbation and remains as effective as model-based approximate unlearning approaches.

2501.19403.title: Tackling Fake Forgetting through Uncertainty Quantification
2501.19403.tldr: This paper proposes a novel metric CR, inspired by conformal prediction, that offers a more reliable assessment of forgetting quality and demonstrates both the effectiveness of the proposed metric and the superior forgetting quality achieved by the framework.

2503.11832.title: Safety Mirage: How Spurious Correlations Undermine VLM Safety Fine-Tuning and Can Be Mitigated by Machine Unlearning
2503.11832.tldr: Machine unlearning (MU) is shown as a powerful alternative to supervised safety fine-tuning, as it avoids biased feature-label mappings and directly removes harmful knowledge from VLMs while preserving their general capabilities.

2504.10185.title: LLM Unlearning Reveals a Stronger-Than-Expected Coreset Effect in Current Benchmarks
2504.10185.tldr: It is found that LLM unlearning achieved with the original (full) forget set can be effectively maintained using a significantly smaller subset, e.g., as little as 5% of the forget set, even when selected at random, suggesting that LLM unlearning in these benchmarks can be performed surprisingly easily, even in an extremely low-data regime.

2504.21307.title: The Linear Geometry of Interpretable Tokens: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Unlearned Diffusion Models
2504.21307.tldr: SubAttack is introduced, a novel jailbreaking attack that reads out this subspace of the token embedding space by learning an orthogonal set of attack token embeddings, revealing that unlearned models still retain the target concept through related textual components.

2506.14003.title: Unlearning Isn't Invisible: Detecting Unlearning Traces in LLMs from Model Outputs
2506.14003.tldr: It is found that unlearning leaves measurable signatures in LLMs, introducing a new risk of reverse-engineering forgotten information when a model is identified as unlearned, given an input query.

2310.12508.title: SalUn: Empowering Machine Unlearning via Gradient-based Weight Saliency in Both Image Classification and Generation
2310.12508.tldr: The concept of 'weight saliency' in MU is introduced, drawing parallels with input saliency in model explanation, and this innovation directs MU's attention toward specific model weights rather than the entire model, improving effectiveness and efficiency.

2605.08765.title: Unlearners Can Lie: Evaluating and Improving Honesty in LLM Unlearning
2605.08765.tldr: ReVa, a representation-alignment procedure that fine-tunes feature-randomized unlearned models to better acknowledge forgotten knowledge is presented, a representation-alignment procedure that fine-tunes feature-randomized unlearned models to better acknowledge forgotten knowledge.
2605.08765.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.15482.title: Harmonizing Multi-Objective LLM Unlearning via Unified Domain Representation and Bidirectional Logit Distillation
2604.15482.tldr: This work proposes a novel multi-objective unlearning framework that harmonizes multiple unlearning objectives through a data and optimization co-design, and introduces a bidirectional distillation method that simultaneously elicits desired behavior from a context-instructed teacher while suppressing undesirable behavior in the student model.

2501.17148.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
2501.17148.tldr: AxBench is introduced, a large-scale benchmark for steering and concept detection, and a novel weakly-supervised representational method is introduced, which is competitive on both tasks while providing the interpretability advantages that prompting lacks.

2409.04478.title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small
2409.04478.tldr: This work uses the RAVEL benchmark to evaluate whether SAEs trained on hidden representations of GPT-2 small have sets of features that separately mediate knowledge of which country a city is in and which continent it is in and shows that SAEs struggle to reach the neuron baseline, and none come close to the DAS skyline.

2506.03292.title: HyperSteer: Activation Steering at Scale with Hypernetworks
2506.03292.tldr: This work introduces HyperSteer, a family of hypernetwork-based architectures which are trained end-to-end to generate steering vectors conditioned on the natural language steering prompts and the internals of the steered LM.

2506.10920.title: Constructing Interpretable Features from Compositional Neuron Groups
2506.10920.tldr: This work directly decomposes MLP activations with semi-nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF), such that the learned features are sparse linear combinations of co-activated neurons, and mapped to their activating inputs, making them directly interpretable.
2506.10920.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2603.23509.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models

2503.11705.title: The BIG Argument for AI Safety Cases
2503.11705.tldr: The BIG argument adopts a whole-system approach to constructing a safety case for AI systems of varying capability, autonomy and criticality, and places a particular focus on the novel hazardous behaviours emerging from the advanced capabilities of frontier AI models and the open contexts in which they are rapidly being deployed.

2501.05455.title: Upstream and Downstream AI Safety: Both on the Same River?
2501.05455.tldr: The characteristics of both upstream and downstream safety frameworks are outlined and the extent to which the broad AI safety community can benefit from synergies between these frameworks is explored, along with some challenges in achieving synergy, or a confluence, between upstream and downstream safety frameworks.

2407.04295.title: Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses Against Large Language Models: A Survey
2407.04295.tldr: This paper proposes a comprehensive and detailed taxonomy of jailbreak attack and defense methods, which further subdivide these attack and defense methods into distinct sub-classes and presents a coherent diagram illustrating their relationships.

2406.09321.title: JailbreakEval: An Integrated Toolkit for Evaluating Jailbreak Attempts Against Large Language Models
2406.09321.tldr: A systematic taxonomy of jailbreak evaluators is introduced, offering insights into their strengths and weaknesses, along with the current status of their adaptation, to foster an inclusive standard for jailbreak evaluation within the community.

2412.19037.title: CL-Attack: Textual Backdoor Attacks via Cross-Lingual Triggers
2412.19037.tldr: Inspired by cross-lingual (CL) prompts of LLMs in real-world scenarios, a higher-dimensional trigger method at the paragraph level, namely CL-Attack is proposed, which injects the backdoor by using texts with specific structures that incorporate multiple languages, thereby offering greater stealthiness and universality compared to existing backdoor attack techniques.

2502.19883.title: Beyond the Tip of Efficiency: Uncovering the Submerged Threats of Jailbreak Attacks in Small Language Models
2502.19883.tldr: This work provides a comprehensive empirical study to evaluate the security performance of 13 state-of-the-art SLMs under various jailbreak attacks and evaluates several representative defense methods and demonstrates their effectiveness in enhancing the security of SLMs.
2502.19883.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2402.13517.title: Round Trip Translation Defence against Large Language Model Jailbreaking Attacks
2402.13517.tldr: The Round Trip Translation (RTT) method is proposed, the first algorithm specifically designed to defend against social-engineered attacks on LLMs, and successfully mitigated over 70% of Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR) attacks.
2402.13517.venue: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining

2602.01025.title: Toward Universal and Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Vision-Language Models
2602.01025.tldr: This work proposes Universal and transferable jailbreak (UltraBreak), a framework that constrains adversarial patterns through transformations and regularisation in the vision space, while relaxing textual targets through semantic-based objectives to enable universal and transferable jailbreaks.

2608.30480.title: VisER: Visual Evidence and Reliance for Object Hallucination Detection in LVLMs
2608.30480.tldr: VisER is proposed, a training-free two-sided metric for object-level hallucination detection that improves AUROC and AUPR over a range of baselines and measures whether object-context compatibility is backed by object-specific evidence from image tokens.

2503.03502.title: Geometry-Guided Adversarial Prompt Detection via Curvature and Local Intrinsic Dimension
2503.03502.tldr: The findings show that adversarial prompts exhibit distinct geometric signatures from benign prompts, enabling CurvaLID to achieve near-perfect classification and outperform state-of-the-art detectors in adversarial prompt detection.

2403.17710.title: Optimization-based Prompt Injection Attack to LLM-as-a-Judge
2403.17710.tldr: This work proposes JudgeDeceiver, an optimization-based prompt injection attack to LLM-as-a-Judge that injects a carefully crafted sequence into an attacker-controlled candidate response such that LLM-as-a-Judge selects the candidate response for an attacker-chosen question no matter what other candidate responses are.
2403.17710.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2504.19793.title: Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents
2504.19793.tldr: This work introduces ToolHijacker, a novel prompt injection attack targeting tool selection in no-box scenarios, and forms the crafting of such tool documents as an optimization problem and proposes a two-phase optimization strategy to solve it.
2504.19793.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2505.11717.title: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
2505.11717.tldr: This work proposes WebInject, a prompt injection attack that manipulates the webpage environment to induce a web agent to perform an attacker-specified action, and trains a neural network to approximate the mapping and apply projected gradient descent to solve the reformulated optimization problem.
2505.11717.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.14827.title: Enhancing Prompt Injection Attacks to LLMs via Poisoning Alignment
2410.14827.tldr: This work proposes PoisonedAlign, a method that strategically creates poisoned alignment samples to poison an LLM’s alignment dataset, showing that when even a small fraction of the alignment data is poisoned, the resulting model becomes substantially more vulnerable to a wide range of prompt injection attacks.

2509.24967.title: SecInfer: Preventing Prompt Injection via Inference-time Scaling
2509.24967.tldr: Extensive experiments show that, by leveraging additional compute at inference, SecInfer effectively mitigates both existing and adaptive prompt injection attacks, outperforming state-of-the-art defenses as well as existing inference-time scaling approaches.

2605.28999.title: Measuring Real-World Prompt Injection Attacks in LLM-based Resume Screening
2605.28999.tldr: This work presents the first systematic study of prompt-injection attacks in a widely used application: LLM-based resume screening and provides the first evidence of large-scale prompt injection in real-world LLM-based applications.

2605.27932.title: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?
2605.27932.tldr: The results suggest that explicit image-tool interaction is a promising design pattern for improving jailbreak robustness, while also motivating pipeline-specific safety evaluation.

2608.28411.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
2608.28411.tldr: LongPIBench is introduced, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary, and the evaluation results reveal significant vulnerabilities of prompt injection defenses under long-context settings.

2604.09024.title: Leave My Images Alone: Preventing Multi-Modal Large Language Models from Analyzing Images via Visual Prompt Injection
2604.09024.tldr: This work proposes ImageProtector, a user-side method that proactively protects images before sharing by embedding a carefully crafted, nearly imperceptible perturbation that acts as a visual prompt injection attack on MLLMs.
2604.09024.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2512.09321.title: ObliInjection: Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data
2512.09321.tldr: ObliInjection introduces two key technical innovations: the order-oblivious loss, which quantifies the likelihood that the LLM will complete the attacker-chosen task regardless of how the clean and contaminated segments are ordered; and the orderGCG algorithm, which is tailored to minimize the order-oblivious loss and optimize the contaminated segments.
2512.09321.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2508.10065.title: Invisible Watermarks, Visible Gains: Steering Machine Unlearning with Bi-Level Watermarking Design
2508.10065.tldr: An unlearning-friendly watermarking framework is introduced, termed Water4MU, to enhance unlearning effectiveness and outperforms existing methods in challenging MU scenarios, known as “challenging forgets”.
2508.10065.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2407.08734.title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust
2407.08734.tldr: This work surveys many considerations for designing experiments that measure circuit faithfulness by ablating portions of the model's computation and concludes that existing circuit faithfulness scores reflect both the methodological choices of researchers as well as the actual components of the circuit.

2511.22662.title: Difficulties with Evaluating a Deception Detector for AIs
2511.22662.tldr: It is argued that the currently lack the necessary examples to evaluate the reliability and efficacy of a proposed deception detector and further identified several concrete obstacles in collecting them.

2606.08629.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
2606.08629.tldr: An alternative interpretation, performative misalignment, is examined, which explains the change in behavior as a result of sycophancy towards AI researchers, and deconfounding sycophancy from scheming is emphasized for future work on evaluations and mitigations of intent misalignment.

2510.18081.title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
2510.18081.tldr: Any-Depth Alignment (ADA), an effective inference-time defense with negligible overhead, is proposed, built based on the observation that alignment is concentrated in the assistant header tokens through repeated use in shallow-refusal training, and these tokens possess the model's strong alignment priors.

2412.21059.title: VisionReward: Fine-Grained Multi-Dimensional Human Preference Learning for Image and Video Generation
2412.21059.tldr: This work presents VisionReward, a general framework for learning human visual preferences in both image and video generation that employs a hierarchical visual assessment framework to capture fine-grained human preferences, and leverages linear weighting to enable interpretable preference learning.

2404.00934.title: ChatGLM-RLHF: Practices of Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback
2404.00934.tldr: This paper presents the ChatGLM-RLHF pipeline -- a reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) system -- designed to enhance ChatGLM's alignment with human preferences, and presents the practices of aligning LLMs with human preferences.

2605.14750.title: EVA: Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks
2605.14750.tldr: EVA (Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks), a novel framework that pioneers the application of direct model editing for safety alignment, is proposed, offering a precise and efficient solution for post-deployment safety alignment.
2605.14750.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2501.16615.title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
2501.16615.tldr: The research shows that SAEs trained on the same model and data, differing only in the random seed used to initialize their weights, identify different sets of features, suggesting that the set of features uncovered by an SAE should be viewed as a pragmatically useful decomposition of activation space.

2411.09003.title: Refusal in LLMs is an Affine Function
2411.09003.tldr: This work begins with an affine decomposition of model activation vectors and shows that prior methods for steering model behavior correspond to subsets of terms of this decomposition, then provides a derivation of ACE and uses it to control refusal behavior on ten different models, including Llama 3 70B.

2501.18823.title: Transcoders Beat Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability
2501.18823.tldr: This work compares the features found by transcoders and SAEs trained on the same model and data, finding that transcoder features are significantly more interpretable.

2507.08473.title: Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations
2507.08473.tldr: This work adapts existing methods to assess the interpretability of sparse coders, with the advantage that they do not require generating natural language explanations as an intermediate step, which enables a more direct and potentially standardized assessment of interpretability.

2509.25596.title: Binary Sparse Coding for Interpretability
2509.25596.tldr: It is found that binarisation significantly improves the interpretability and monosemanticity of the discovered features, while increasing reconstruction error, and suggests that polysemanticity may be an ineliminable property of neural activations.

2411.00204.title: RESTOR: Knowledge Recovery in Machine Unlearning
2411.00204.tldr: The RESTOR framework for machine unlearning evaluation is proposed, which assesses the ability of unlearning algorithms for targeted data erasure, by evaluating the ability of models to forget the knowledge introduced in these datapoints, while simultaneously recovering the model's knowledge state had it never encountered these datapoints.

2506.00195.title: Let Them Down Easy! Contextual Effects of LLM Guardrails on User Perceptions and Preferences
2506.00195.tldr: This work demonstrates that effective guardrails require focusing on crafting thoughtful refusals rather than detecting intent, offering a path toward AI safety mechanisms that ensure both safety and sustained user engagement.
2506.00195.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.19133.title: Hybrid Preferences: Learning to Route Instances for Human vs. AI Feedback
2410.19133.tldr: This work introduces HyPER, a Hybrid Preference routER that defers an annotation to either humans or LMs, achieving better annotation quality while reducing the cost of human-only annotation, and develops a routing strategy that selects a combination that maximizes the predicted performance.
2410.19133.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.00033.title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing
2606.00033.tldr: It is proposed that auditing MI itself is essential for its application in AI safety, industry, and governance, and constructive debate over the necessity, design and implementation of such a framework are encouraged.
2606.00033.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
