2606.11202.title: One Jailbreak, Many Tongues: Learning Language-Insensitive Intention Representations for Multilingual Jailbreak Detection
2606.11202.tldr: Experimental results show that MLJailDe outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple languages, and obtains an average F1 score of 97.1\% on unseen languages, demonstrating strong effectiveness and cross-lingual generalization.

2502.09723.title: QueryAttack: Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models Using Structured Non-natural Query Language
2502.09723.tldr: This paper proposes QueryAttack, a novel framework to examine the generalizability of safety alignment in large language models by treating LLMs as knowledge databases, and translates malicious queries in natural language into structured non-natural query language to bypass the safety alignment mechanisms of LLMs.
2502.09723.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.19684.title: VisCRA: A Visual Chain Reasoning Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models
2505.19684.tldr: Investigating the security implications of advanced visual reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models reveals a fundamental trade-off: as visual reasoning improves, models become more vulnerable to jailbreak attacks.
2505.19684.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.03869.title: Chain-of-Jailbreak Attack for Image Generation Models via Editing Step by Step
2410.03869.tldr: A novel jailbreaking method called Chain-of-Jailbreak (CoJ) attack, which compromises image generation models through a step-by-step editing process, and proposes an effective prompting-based method, Think Twice Prompting, that can successfully defend over 95% of CoJ attack.
2410.03869.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2411.03993.title: Choosing the right basis for interpretability: Psychophysical comparison between neuron-based and dictionary-based representations
2411.03993.tldr: Psychophysical evidence is provided that dictionary-based representations offer a stronger foundation for interpretability and caution is cautioned against model comparisons based solely on neuron-level analyses.

2503.09858.title: Media and responsible AI governance: a game-theoretic and LLM analysis
2503.09858.tldr: The research explores two key mechanisms for achieving responsible governance, safe AI development and adoption of safe AI: incentivising effective regulation through media reporting, and conditioning user trust on commentariats' recommendation.

2412.15433.title: Quantifying detection rates for dangerous capabilities: a theoretical model of dangerous capability evaluations
2412.15433.tldr: A quantitative model for tracking dangerous AI capabilities over time is presented to provide a novel introduction to dangerous capability testing and how this testing can directly inform policy, and how delays in testing can harm AI policy.

2603.16643.title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy
2603.16643.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.04426.title: ShieldNet: Network-Level Guardrails against Emerging Supply-Chain Injections in Agentic Systems
2604.04426.tldr: ShieldNet is proposed, a network-level guardrail framework that detects supply-chain poisoning by observing real network interactions rather than surface-level tool traces, and substantially outperforming existing MCP scanners and LLM-based guardrails.

2608.16650.title: PCA-guided Activation Scaling for Monotonic Bidirectional Control over LLM Sycophancy
2608.16650.tldr: PCA-guided Activation Scaling is introduced, an activation steering framework that decomposes residual stream activations into a PCA-identified sycophancy-honesty subspace and an orthogonal residual, then applies distinct scaling exponents to achieve monotonic, bidirectional control.

2606.12918.title: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
2606.12918.tldr: The first agent-level Shapley value analysis for MAS is proposed, quantifying each agent's marginal contribution to system robustness under task-specific distributions and revealing critical vulnerabilities and coordination patterns that are overlooked by prior single-agent or template-based methods.

2604.06950.title: Making MLLMs Blind: Adversarial Smuggling Attacks in MLLM Content Moderation
2604.06950.tldr: This work constructed SmuggleBench, the first comprehensive benchmark comprising 1,700 adversarial smuggling attack instances, and identifies three root causes: the limited capabilities of vision encoders, the robustness gap in OCR, and the scarcity of domain-specific adversarial examples.
2604.06950.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.01342.title: Fine-Tuning Jailbreaks under Highly Constrained Black-Box Settings: A Three-Pronged Approach
2510.01342.tldr: A three-pronged jailbreak attack that combines safety-styled prefix/suffix wrappers, benign lexical encodings of sensitive tokens, and a backdoor mechanism, enabling the model to learn harmful behaviors while individual datapoints appear innocuous.

2607.19595.title: Twin Agent: Context Residual Compression for Privilege Separated Agents
2607.19595.tldr: This work proposes Twin Agent, a general privilege separation design pattern inspired by residual coding in the agent context that preserves high task utility while preventing prompt injection attacks, outperforming both undefended agents and privilege separation baselines.

2406.08288.title: Decoupling the Class Label and the Target Concept in Machine Unlearning
2406.08288.tldr: A general framework, namely, TARget-aware Forgetting (TARF), that enables the additional tasks to actively forget the target concept while maintaining the rest part, by simultaneously conducting annealed gradient ascent on the forgetting data and selected gradient descent on the hard-to-affect remaining data is proposed.

2505.24709.title: On Symmetric Losses for Robust Policy Optimization with Noisy Preferences
2505.24709.tldr: It is proved that symmetric losses enable successful policy optimization even under noisy labels, as the resulting reward remains rank-preserving -- a property sufficient for policy improvement.

2503.10669.title: UC-MOA: Utility-Conditioned Multi-Objective Alignment for Distributional Pareto-Optimality
2503.10669.tldr: The approach leverages a diverse set of strictly increasing, non-linear utility functions to transform user-specified preferences into symbolic tokens, which are then used to condition a single LLM, yielding models that achieve superior Pareto fronts and robust alignment across complex reward dimensions.

2608.05659.title: Breaking Customized LLMs for Coding: Automated Red Teaming for Instruction Backdoor Attacks
2608.05659.tldr: This paper proposes ARIA, an automated red-teaming framework for crafting covert and effective backdoored instructions against customized LLMs, which significantly outperforms existing attacks in evading platform-side and user-side detection, and stays effective against existing defense methods.

2608.20820.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
2608.20820.tldr: Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR) is introduced, a framework that models conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defines $k-turn certified robustness as the worst-case safety probability across $k$ adversarial turns.

2609.04665.title: Harness-agnostic detection and immunization of reward hacking in self-evolving language models
2609.04665.tldr: This work introduces HackProbe, a monitor that attaches to an arbitrary self-evolving loop through two black-box hooks, with no access to weights or activations, and proves a detectability bound that converts a target error rate into an explicit probe-size budget, and delimit what probe rotation does and does not buy.

2606.01837.title: Benign Inputs, Harmful Outputs: Cross-Modal Jailbreaking via Distributed Semantic Recomposition
2606.01837.tldr: This work proposes Distributed Semantic Recomposition (DSR), a novel cross-modal jailbreak framework that decomposes harmful intent into a set of benign textual and visual primitives and enables the latent fusion of these seemingly innocent components into harmful outputs during the cross-modal inference phase.

2602.22983.title: Obscure but Effective: Classical Chinese Jailbreak Prompt Optimization via Bio-Inspired Search
2602.22983.tldr: A framework, CC-BOS, is proposed for the automatic generation of classical Chinese adversarial prompts based on multi-dimensional fruit fly optimization, facilitating efficient and automated jailbreak attacks in black-box settings.

2605.16090.title: A Cross-Modal Prompt Injection Attack against Large Vision-Language Models with Image-Only Perturbation
2605.16090.tldr: This work introduces a novel cross-modal prompt injection attack CrossMPI, which can steer the model's interpretation of both textual and visual inputs via image-only prompt injection and significantly outperforms baseline approaches.

2604.17293.title: Beyond "I Don't Know": Evaluating LLM Self-Awareness in Discriminating Data and Model Uncertainty
2604.17293.tldr: UA-Bench is introduced, a benchmark of over 3,500 questions drawn from six datasets spanning knowledge-intensive and reasoning-intensive tasks, designed to evaluate explicit uncertainty attribution and a lightweight data synthesis and reinforcement learning strategy is proposed.
2604.17293.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.05784.title: DRAGON: Guard LLM Unlearning in Context via Negative Detection and Reasoning
2511.05784.tldr: Detect-Reasoning Augmented GeneratiON (DRAGON), a systematic, reasoning-based framework that utilizes in-context chain-of-thought instructions to guard deployed LLMs before inference, is proposed, demonstrating its strong unlearning capability, scalability, and applicability in practical scenarios.

2502.15806.title: A Mousetrap: Fooling Large Reasoning Models for Jailbreak with Chain of Iterative Chaos
2502.15806.tldr: This work proposes the first jailbreak attack targeting LRMs, exploiting their unique vulnerabilities stemming from the advanced reasoning capabilities, and introduces a Chaos Machine, a novel component to transform attack prompts with diverse one-to-one mappings.
2502.15806.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.01592.title: OpenRT: An Open-Source Red Teaming Framework for Multimodal LLMs
2601.01592.tldr: OpenRT is introduced, a unified, modular, and high-throughput red-teaming framework designed for comprehensive MLLM safety evaluation that architects a paradigm shift in automated red-teaming by introducing an adversarial kernel that enables modular separation across five critical dimensions.

2505.19610.title: JailBound: Jailbreaking Internal Safety Boundaries of Vision-Language Models
2505.19610.tldr: JailBound is a novel latent space jailbreak framework comprising two stages: Safety Boundary Probing, which addresses the guidance issue by approximating decision boundary within fusion layer's latent space, thereby identifying optimal perturbation directions towards the target region; and Safety Boundary Crossing, which overcomes the limitations of decoupled approaches by jointly optimizing adversarial perturbations across both image and text inputs.

2511.12710.title: Evolve the Method, Not the Prompts: Evolutionary Synthesis of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
2511.12710.tldr: EvoSynth is an autonomous multi-agent framework that shifts the optimization space from prompts to executable code, and features a code-level self-correction loop, allowing it to iteratively rewrite the code-based algorithm in response to target-model feedback and failed attempts.

2408.03603.title: EnJa: Ensemble Jailbreak on Large Language Models
2408.03603.tldr: A novel EnJa attack to hide harmful instructions using prompt-level jailbreak, boost the attack success rate using a gradient-based attack, and connect the two types of jailbreak attacks via a template-based connector are proposed.

2508.01741.title: Simulated Ensemble Attack: Transferring Jailbreaks Across Fine-tuned Vision-Language Models
2508.01741.tldr: The Simulated Ensemble Attack (SEA), a grey-box jailbreak framework that assumes full access to the base VLM but no knowledge of the fine-tuned target, is proposed, revealing that fine-tuning primarily induces localized parameter shifts around the base model, explaining why attacks optimized over a simulated neighborhood transfer effectively.

2507.18576.title: SafeWork-R1: Coevolving Safety and Intelligence under the AI-45$^{\circ}$ Law
2507.18576.tldr: This work introduces SafeWork-R1, a cutting-edge multimodal reasoning model that demonstrates the coevolution of capabilities and safety, developed by the proposed SafeLadder framework, which incorporates large-scale, progressive, safety-oriented reinforcement learning post-training, supported by a suite of multi-principled verifiers.

2608.14632.title: DeMTS: Denoising Trajectories as Multivariate Time Series for Hallucination Detection in Diffusion Language Models
2608.14632.tldr: A D-LLM hallucination detection framework that formulates the Denoising trajectories as Multivariate Time Series over learnable latent variables (DeMTS for short) that outperforms existing hallucination detection methods while maintaining strong robustness, efficiency, and cross-task transferability.

2606.08496.title: SAEExplainer: Interpreting SAE Features with Activation-Guided Preference Optimization
2606.08496.tldr: This paper proposes SAEExplainer, a training framework that utilizes activation scores as an objective reward signal to train the model for self-correction and iterative bootstrapping, and achieves continuous improvement in its explanatory capabilities.

2604.06811.title: SkillTrojan: Backdoor Attacks on Skill-Based Agent Systems
2604.06811.tldr: The results show that skill-level backdoors can be highly effective with minimal degradation of benign behavior, exposing a critical blind spot in current skill-based agent architectures and motivating defenses that explicitly reason about skill composition and execution.

2601.04566.title: BackdoorAgent: A Unified Framework for Backdoor Attacks on LLM-based Agents
2601.04566.tldr: A modular and stage-aware framework that provides a unified, agent-centric view of backdoor threats in LLM agents, and a standardized benchmark spanning four representative agent applications, covering both language-only and multimodal settings.
2601.04566.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.18921.title: BackdoorVLM: A Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language Models
2511.18921.tldr: This work introduces BackdoorVLM, the first comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating backdoor attacks on VLMs across a broad range of settings and reveals that VLMs exhibit strong sensitivity to textual instructions, and in bimodal backdoors the text trigger typically overwhelms the image trigger when forming the backdoor mapping.

2511.16709.title: AutoBackdoor: Automating Backdoor Attacks via LLM Agents
2511.16709.tldr: This work introduces AutoBackdoor, a general framework for automating backdoor injection, encompassing trigger generation, poisoned data construction, and model fine-tuning via an autonomous agent-driven pipeline, and demonstrates that the method achieves over 90% attack success with only a small number of poisoned samples.

2410.19427.title: Expose Before You Defend: Unifying and Enhancing Backdoor Defenses via Exposed Models
2410.19427.tldr: The results demonstrate the importance of backdoor exposure for backdoor defense, showing that the exposed models can significantly benefit a range of downstream defense tasks, including backdoor label detection, backdoor trigger recovery, backdoor model detection, and backdoor removal.

2405.18166.title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via Layer-specific Editing
2405.18166.tldr: This work investigates how LLMs response to harmful prompts is investigated and proposes a novel defense method termed Layer-specific Editing (LED) to enhance the resilience of LLMs against jailbreak attacks and reveals that several critical safety layers exist among the early layers of LLMs.
2405.18166.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2501.03272.title: Backdoor Token Unlearning: Exposing and Defending Backdoors in Pretrained Language Models
2501.03272.tldr: This work proposes a novel defense method called Backdoor Token Unlearning (BTU), which proactively detects and neutralizes trigger tokens during the training stage and leverages these properties to identify aberrant embedding parameters and subsequently removes backdoor behaviors using a fine-grained unlearning technique.

2408.14393.title: CURE4Rec: A Benchmark for Recommendation Unlearning with Deeper Influence
2408.14393.tldr: This work proposes CURE4Rec, the first comprehensive benchmark for recommendation unlearning evaluation and considers the deeper influence of unlearning on recommendation fairness and robustness towards data with varying impact levels.

2502.17515.title: Towards User-level Private Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback
2502.17515.tldr: This study proposes a novel framework, AUP-RLHF, which integrates user-level label DP into RLHF, and develops the AUP-RLHF algorithm, which guarantees user-level privacy and achieves an improved estimation error.

2507.19894.title: Generative Model Unlearning: A Survey through Target Events, Unlearning Operators, and Evaluation Protocols
2507.19894.tldr: A comprehensive review of GenMU is provided and the first explicit and unified account of how GenMU connects to mainstream applications is provided, including privacy protection, copyright and style protection, safety alignment, hallucination mitigation, and deployment defense.

2504.06659.title: Leveraging Machine Unlearning for Cost-Efficient Preference Alignment
2504.06659.tldr: This work proposes Unlearning to Align (U2A), which leverages bi-level optimization to efficiently select and unlearn examples for optimal PA performance, and validate the proposed method through extensive experiments, with results confirming its effectiveness.

2602.20720.title: AdapTools: Adaptive Tool-based Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic LLMs
2602.20720.tldr: AdapTools is introduced, a novel adaptive IPI attack framework that selects stealthier attack tools and generates adaptive attack prompts to create a rigorous security evaluation environment and advances the understanding of IPI attacks.

2602.20708.title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
2602.20708.tldr: This work proposes ICON, a probing-to-mitigation framework that neutralizes attacks while preserving task continuity, and demonstrates robust Out of Distribution(OOD) generalization and extends effectively to multi-modal agents, establishing a superior balance between security and efficiency.

2506.10047.title: GenBreak: Red Teaming Text-to-Image Generators Using Large Language Models
2506.10047.tldr: GenBreak is a framework that fine-tunes a red-team large language model (LLM) to systematically explore underlying vulnerabilities in T2I generators, and guides the LLM to craft adversarial prompts that enhance both evasion capability and image toxicity, while maintaining semantic coherence and diversity.

2607.11698.title: Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming
2607.11698.tldr: This work presents AHA, a falsifiable discovery loop that proposes a vulnerability hypothesis, constructs a falsifier, instantiates a valid attack, executes it in a sandboxed harness, reflects on the trajectory, and promotes confirmed findings into a Vulnerability Concept Graph (VCG), which provides an auditable artifact for production safety teams to inspect vulnerabilities, validate patches, and accumulate reusable safety knowledge.

2505.13862.title: PandaGuard: Systematic Evaluation of LLM Safety against Jailbreaking Attacks
2505.13862.tldr: PandaGuard is introduced, a unified and modular framework that models LLM jailbreak safety as a multi-agent system comprising attackers, defenders, and judges and develops PandaBench, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates the interactions between these attack/defense methods across 49 LLMs and various judgment approaches.

2506.04302.title: RedRFT: A Light-Weight Benchmark for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning-Based Red Teaming
2506.04302.tldr: RedRFT, a lightweight benchmark designed to simplify and standardize the implementation and evaluation of RFT-based red teaming, is introduced, offering high-quality single-file red teaming implementations and modular PPO core components, such as the General Advantage Estimator.

2409.06411.title: Length Desensitization in Direct Preference Optimization
2409.06411.tldr: An in-depth theoretical analysis of DPO's optimization objective is conducted and a strong correlation between its implicit reward and data length is revealed, resulting in length sensitivity during the DPO training and leading to verbosity.

2511.07315.title: JPRO: Automated Multimodal Jailbreaking via Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework
2511.07315.tldr: JPRO, a novel multi-agent collaborative framework designed for automated VLM jailbreaking, effectively overcomes the shortcomings of prior methods in attack diversity and scalability and offers valuable insights for evaluating and enhancing VLM robustness.

2511.08367.title: Why Does Weak-OOD Help? A Further Step Towards Understanding Jailbreaking VLMs
2511.08367.tldr: JOCR (Jailbreak via OCR-Aware Embedded Text Perturbation), a practical OCR-readable extension of embedded-text jailbreaks that achieves the best average ASR among evaluated baselines is designed.

2608.04034.title: A Multimodal Automatic Redteaming Evaluation based on Atomic Jailbreak Strategy Decoupling and Combination
2608.04034.tldr: This work proposes a multimodal automated red team jailbreak method named Hierarchical Atomic Combination Attack (HACA), based on a six-dimensional strategy space, where a cross-modal joint planner is used to select and combine the different atomic jailbreak strategy for subsequent jailbreak command generation.

2502.04204.title: Short-length Adversarial Training Helps LLMs Defend Long-length Jailbreak Attacks: Theoretical and Empirical Evidence
2502.04204.tldr: It is practical to defend against jailbreak attacks via efficient adversarial training (AT) via efficient "short-length"AT, and a positive correlation between the attack success rate and the ratio of the square root of the adversarial suffix length during jailbreaking to the length during AT is confirmed.

2505.24369.title: Adversarial Preference Learning for Robust LLM Alignment
2505.24369.tldr: Adversarial Preference Learning (APL) is introduced, an iterative adversarial training method incorporating three key innovations: a direct harmfulness metric based on the model's intrinsic preference probabilities, eliminating reliance on external assessment.
2505.24369.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.01834.title: Concept-Based Dictionary Learning for Inference-Time Safety in Vision Language Action Models
2602.01834.tldr: This work introduces a concept based dictionary learning framework for inference time safety control, and is the first inference time concept based safety method for embodied systems, advancing both interpretability and safe deployment of VLA models.

2410.00451.title: Unleashing the Unseen: Harnessing Benign Datasets for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2410.00451.tldr: A feature extraction method is developed to extract sample-agnostic features from benign dataset in the form of suffixes and it is shown that benign features can be effectively made to function as adversarial suffixes, which is able to completely eliminate GPT's safety alignment in a blackbox setting through finetuning with only benign data.
2410.00451.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.14310.title: CORVUS: Red-Teaming Hallucination Detectors via Internal Signal Camouflage in Large Language Models
2601.14310.tldr: A white-box, model-side adversary that fine-tunes lightweight LoRA adapters on the model while keeping the detector fixed is studied, and CORVUS, an efficient red-teaming procedure that learns to camouflage detector-visible telemetry under teacher forcing, is introduced.

2604.24542.title: Layerwise Convergence Fingerprints for Runtime Misbehavior Detection in Large Language Models
2604.24542.tldr: Layerwise Convergence Fingerprinting (LCF), a tuning-free runtime monitor that treats the inter-layer hidden-state trajectory as a health signal: LCF computes a diagonal Mahalanobis distance on every inter-layer difference, aggregates via Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, and thresholds via leave-one-out calibration on 200 clean examples, with no reference model, trigger knowledge, or retraining.

2608.11227.title: Forecasting Side Effects of Activation Steering
2608.11227.tldr: This work constructs a cross-effect matrix over a taxonomy of 67 behaviors across three open-weight language models and shows that side effects are largely predictable before steering is performed, enabling proactive safety auditing and more informed deployment of steering interventions.

2608.14392.title: Tripwire: Triggering Aligned Refusal via Statistically Certified Safety Neurons
2608.14392.tldr: A training-free defense that first identifies safety-specific neurons through per-neuron hypothesis tests under false-discovery-rate control together with a utility-specificity filter, and reduces the average attack success rate to at most 2.0% while incurring a utility drop of only 0.3% on MT-Bench, the smallest among all defenses.

2512.04841.title: SoK: a Comprehensive Causality Analysis Framework for Large Language Model Security
2512.04841.tldr: A unified causality analysis framework that systematically supports all levels of causal investigation in LLMs, ranging from token-level, neuron-level, and layer-level interventions to representation-level analysis, and establishes a reproducible foundation for research on causality-based attacks, interpretability, and robust attack detection and mitigation in LLMs.

2604.11790.title: ClawGuard: A Runtime Security Framework for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
2604.11790.tldr: This work establishes deterministic tool-call boundary enforcement as an effective defense mechanism for secure agentic AI systems.

2606.03601.title: DDOR: Delta Debugging for Explainable Overrefusal Testing and Repair
2606.03601.tldr: DDOR (Delta Debugging for OverRefusal), a fully automated and explainable framework for overrefusal testing and repair in a black-box setting, where only model inputs and outputs are accessible and internal safety mechanisms remain opaque, is presented.

2605.00699.title: STARE: Step-wise Temporal Alignment and Red-teaming Engine for Multi-modal Toxicity Attack
2605.00699.tldr: STARE is introduced, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that treats the denoising trajectory itself as the attack surface, under a direct white-box T2I and query-only black-box VLM setting, and surfaces the Optimization-Induced Phase Alignment phenomenon.

2607.10526.title: Agents Don't Just Agree, They Remember: Benchmarking Persistent Sycophancy in Stateful Personal Agents
2607.10526.tldr: The Personal Agent Sycophancy Benchmark (PASB) is introduced, a 1,600-task benchmark that traces whether a conversational claim is accepted, written into durable agent state, and reused in a later neutral query, and shows that agent sycophancy is fundamentally a state-writing governance problem.

2508.17621.title: Steering When Necessary: Flexible Steering Large Language Models with Backtracking
2508.17621.tldr: The Flexible Activation Steering with Backtracking (FASB) framework is proposed, which dynamically determines both the necessity and strength of intervention by tracking the internal states of the LLMs during generation, considering both the question and the generated content.

2405.16134.title: Breaking the False Sense of Security in Backdoor Defense through Re-Activation Attack
2405.16134.tldr: This work re-investigate the characteristics of the backdoored models after defense and finds that the original backdoors still exist in defense models derived from existing post-training defense strategies, and the backdoor existence is measured by a novel metric called backdoor existence coefficient.

2405.16112.title: Mitigating Backdoor Attack by Injecting Proactive Defensive Backdoor
2405.16112.tldr: This paper focuses on in-training backdoor defense, aiming to train a clean model even when the dataset may be potentially poisoned, and proposes a novel defense approach called PDB (Proactive Defensive Backdoor), which leverages the home-field advantage of defenders by proactively injecting a defensive backdoor into the model during training.

2401.13578.title: WPDA: Frequency-based Backdoor Attack with Wavelet Packet Decomposition
2401.13578.tldr: An innovative frequency-based backdoor attack via wavelet packet decomposition (WPD), which could finely decompose the original image into multiple sub-spectrograms with semantic information, to effectively insert the trigger into the victim image, such that the trigger information could be sufficiently learned to form the backdoor.

2602.02557.title: The Alignment Curse: Modality Alignment Supercharges Audio Attacks via Text Transfer
2602.02557.tldr: The Alignment Curse is introduced, a formally characterized and empirically validated principle showing that stronger modality alignment enables more effective transfer of attacks from text to audio, revealing a fundamental tension between capability and safety.

2606.27305.title: Sculpting NeRF Geometry: Human-Preference Fine-Tuning of a 3D-Aware Face GAN
2606.27305.tldr: This work fine-tune a pretrained 3D-aware generative model directly from a learned reward over radiance-field density ($\sigma$) values, with no externally supplied mesh or shape prior.

2603.16459.title: DynHD: Hallucination Detection for Diffusion Large Language Models via Denoising Dynamics Deviation Learning
2603.16459.tldr: To model denoising dynamics for hallucination detection, this paper introduces a reference evidence generator that learns the expected evolution trajectory of uncertainty evidence, along with a deviation-based hallucination detector that makes predictions by measuring the discrepancy between the observed and reference trajectories.

2501.00055.title: LLM-Virus: Evolutionary Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models
2501.00055.tldr: LLM-Virus is proposed, a jailbreak attack method based on evolutionary algorithm, termed evolutionary jailbreak, that treats jailbreak attacks as both an evolutionary and transfer learning problem, utilizing LLMs as heuristic evolutionary operators to ensure high attack efficiency, transferability, and low time cost.

2410.09040.title: AttnGCG: Enhancing Jailbreaking Attacks on LLMs with Attention Manipulation
2410.09040.tldr: This paper studies the vulnerabilities of transformer-based Large Language Models to jailbreaking attacks, focusing specifically on the optimization-based Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) strategy, and introduces an enhanced method that manipulates models' attention scores to facilitate LLM jailbreaking, which is named AttnGCG.

2508.03936.title: ASTRA: Autonomous Spatial-Temporal Red-teaming for AI Software Assistants
2508.03936.tldr: Across two major evaluation domains, ASTRA finds 11-66% more issues than existing techniques and produces test cases that lead to 17% more effective alignment training, showing its practical value for building safer AI systems.

2509.16950.title: Temporal Logic-Based Multi-Vehicle Backdoor Attacks against Offline RL Agents in End-to-end Autonomous Driving
2509.16950.tldr: This work introduces a novel backdoor attack against the end-to-end AD systems that leverage one or more other vehicles'trajectories as triggers, and develops a negative training strategy by incorporating patch trajectories that are similar to triggers but are designated not to activate the backdoor.

2506.22666.title: VERA: Variational Inference Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2506.22666.tldr: VERA casts black-box jailbreak prompting as a variational inference problem, training a small attacker LLM to approximate the target LLM's posterior over adversarial prompts, highlighting the value of probabilistic inference for adversarial prompt generation.

2510.05169.title: From Poisoned to Aware: Fostering Backdoor Self-Awareness in LLMs
2510.05169.tldr: This work proposes a novel post-training framework that cultivates self-awareness of backdoor risks and enables models to articulate implanted triggers even when they are absent from the prompt, and presents two complementary defense strategies for mitigating and detecting backdoor threats.

2602.03420.title: CoCoEmo: Composable and Controllable Human-Like Emotional TTS via Activation Steering
2602.03420.tldr: This paper presents the first systematic analysis of activation steering for emotional control in hybrid TTS models, introducing a quantitative, controllable steering framework, and multi-rater evaluation protocols that enable composable mixed-emotion synthesis and reliable text-emotion mismatch synthesis.

2401.03215.title: End-to-End Anti-Backdoor Learning on Images and Time Series
2401.03215.tldr: This paper builds upon Anti-Backdoor Learning (ABL) and introduces an innovative method, End-to-End Anti-Backdoor Learning (E2ABL), for robust training against backdoor attacks, which significantly improves on existing defenses and is effective against a broad range of backdoor attacks in both image and time series domains.

2511.18396.title: Exploring Weak-to-Strong Generalization for CLIP-based Classification
2511.18396.tldr: This study explores weak-to-strong generalization for CLIP-based classification, and proposes a method, class prototype learning (CPL), which aims to enhance the classification capabilities of the CLIP model, by learning more representative prototypes for each category.

2401.17256.title: Weak-to-Strong Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
2401.17256.tldr: The weak-to-strong jailbreaking attack is proposed, an efficient inference time attack for aligned LLMs to produce harmful text, based on the observation that jailbroken and aligned models only differ in their initial decoding distributions.

2502.05174.title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
2502.05174.tldr: This work designs MELON to detect attacks by re-executing the agent's trajectory with a masked user prompt modified through a masking function, and shows that combining MELON with a SOTA prompt augmentation defense (denoted as MELON-Aug) further improves its performance.

2506.16078.title: Probing the Robustness of Large Language Models Safety to Latent Perturbations
2506.16078.tldr: Layer-wise Adversarial Patch Training~(LAPT), a fine-tuning strategy that inject controlled perturbations into hidden representations during training, is introduced, revealing fundamental flaws in current alignment paradigms and calling for representation-level training strategies that move beyond surface-level behavior supervision.

2602.02536.title: From Sparse Decisions to Dense Reasoning: A Multi-attribute Trajectory Paradigm for Multimodal Moderation
2602.02536.tldr: A novel learning paradigm (UniMod) that transitions from sparse decision-making to dense reasoning traces, and develops a multi-head scalar reward model (UniRM), which provides multi-dimensional supervision by assigning attribute-level scores to the response generation stage.

2511.07107.title: MENTOR: A Metacognition-Driven Self-Evolution Framework for Uncovering and Mitigating Implicit Domain Risks in LLMs
2511.07107.tldr: This work proposes MENTOR, a metacognition-driven self-evolution framework that performs metacognitive self-assessment, using strategies such as perspective-taking and consequential reasoning to uncover latent model misalignments and substantially reduces attack success rates.

2404.13161.title: CyberSecEval 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
2404.13161.tldr: The safety-utility tradeoff: conditioning an LLM to reject unsafe prompts can cause the LLM to falsely reject answering benign prompts, which lowers utility, and a novel test set to quantify FRR for cyberattack helpfulness risk is introduced.

2606.10525.title: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments
2606.10525.tldr: A comprehensive empirical evaluation of automated prompt injection attacks against LLM agents, adapting both white-box (GCG) and black-box (TAP) methods to the agentic setting within the AgentDojo framework finds that black-box optimization substantially outperforms gradient-based methods, and finds that TAP's effectiveness depends on the attacker model.

2505.18786.title: Leveraging Per-Instance Privacy for Machine Unlearning
2505.18786.tldr: A principled, per-instance approach to quantifying the difficulty of unlearning via fine-tuning, which provides a foundation for more efficient and adaptive unlearning strategies tailored to the unique properties of individual data points.

2402.00751.title: Fast Exact Unlearning for In-Context Learning Data for LLMs
2402.00751.tldr: This paper revisits exact unlearning in deep learning and shows that for large language models (LLMs) it can efficiently exactly unlearn fine-tuning data (the data used to adapt a pre-trained model) and highlights the need for new measures of unlearning cost when adapting the learning algorithm to have faster unlearn operations.

2403.01218.title: Inexact Unlearning Needs More Careful Evaluations to Avoid a False Sense of Privacy
2403.01218.tldr: This work discusses adaptations of Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) to the setting of unlearning (leading to their “U-MIA” counterparts), and proposes a categorization of existing U-MIAs into “population U-MIAs”, and “per-example U-MIAs”, where a dedicated attacker is instantiated for each example.
2403.01218.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)

2407.00106.title: UnUnlearning: Unlearning is not sufficient for content regulation in advanced generative AI
2407.00106.tldr: It is argued that content filtering for impermissible knowledge will be required and even exact unlearning schemes are not enough for effective content regulation, and a concept of ununlearning is introduced, where unlearned knowledge gets reintroduced in-context, effectively rendering the model capable of behaving as if it knows the forgotten knowledge.

2402.06957.title: Architectural Neural Backdoors from First Principles
2402.06957.tldr: Improved on the original design and construct an arbitrary trigger detector which can be used to backdoor any architecture with no human supervision, and it is found that language models outperform humans at the detection of backdoors.
2402.06957.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2501.18838.title: Partially Rewriting a Transformer in Natural Language
2501.18838.tldr: It is suggested that more detailed explanations are needed to improve performance substantially above the zero ablation baseline, and the results suggest that more detailed explanations are needed to improve performance substantially above the zero ablation baseline.

2609.20027.title: Can Data Attribution Filter Out Subliminal Learning? Not Reliably
2609.20027.tldr: The results suggest that gradient-based attribution can identify data responsible for subliminal learning in some settings, but that some approximations are more reliable than others.

2402.07896.title: Suppressing Pink Elephants with Direct Principle Feedback
2402.07896.tldr: The Pink Elephant Problem is illustrated with a novel simplification of Constitutional AI, Direct Principle Feedback, which skips the ranking of responses and uses DPO directly on critiques and revisions, and the 13B fine-tuned LLaMA 2 model significantly outperforms Llama-2-13B-Chat and a prompted baseline, and performs as well as GPT-4 in on the authors' curated test set assessing the Pink Elephant Problem.

2501.13818.title: Ensuring Medical AI Safety: Interpretability-Driven Detection and Mitigation of Spurious Model Behavior and Associated Data
2501.13818.tldr: This work reviews the steps of the Reveal2Revise framework and enhances it with semi-automated interpretability-based bias annotation capabilities, providing valuable information for bias mitigation methods to unlearn the undesired shortcut behavior.

2404.06453.title: PURE: Turning Polysemantic Neurons Into Pure Features by Identifying Relevant Circuits
2404.06453.tldr: This work presents a method for disentangling polysemanticity of any Deep Neural Network by decomposing a polysemantic neuron into multiple monosemantic"virtual"neurons, achieved by identifying the relevant sub-graph ("circuit") for each"pure"feature.

2503.10566.title: ASIDE: Architectural Separation of Instructions and Data in Language Models
2503.10566.tldr: This work proposes a new architectural element, ASIDE, that allows language models to clearly separate instructions and data at the level of token embeddings, and demonstrates that instruction-tuning LLMs with ASIDE achieves substantially higher instruction-data separation without performance loss.

2509.18058.title: Strategic Dishonesty Can Undermine AI Safety Evaluations of Frontier LLMs
2509.18058.tldr: It is shown that frontier LLMs can develop a preference for dishonesty as a new strategy, even when other options are available, and linear probes on internal activations can be used to reliably detect strategic dishonesty.

2502.16994.title: FADE: Why Bad Descriptions Happen to Good Features
2502.16994.tldr: The introduction of FADE: Feature Alignment to Description Evaluation, a scalable model-agnostic framework for automatically evaluating feature-to-description alignment, highlights fundamental challenges in generating feature descriptions, particularly for SAEs compared to MLP neurons.
2502.16994.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.07158.title: Quanda: An Interpretability Toolkit for Training Data Attribution Evaluation and Beyond
2410.07158.tldr: Quanda is introduced, a Python toolkit designed to facilitate the evaluation of TDA methods and provides a uniform interface for seamless integration with existing TDA implementations across different repositories, thus enabling systematic benchmarking.

2510.27413.title: Atlas-Alignment: Making Interpretability Transferable Across Language Models
2510.27413.tldr: Atat-Alignment is introduced, a framework that avoids this cost of explainable AI and mechanistic interpretability by aligning the latent space of a new model to a pre-existing, labeled Concept Atlas using only shared inputs and lightweight representational alignment methods.

2510.14936.title: Circuit Insights: Towards Interpretability Beyond Activations
2510.14936.tldr: WeightLens and CircuitLens are proposed, two complementary methods that go beyond activation-based analysis of circuits and capture how feature activations arise from interactions between components, revealing circuit-level dynamics that activation-only approaches cannot identify.

2604.11467.title: From Attribution to Action: A Human-Centered Application of Activation Steering
2604.11467.tldr: This work introduces an interactive workflow combining SAE-based attribution with activation steering for instance-level analysis of concept usage in vision models, implemented as a web-based tool and finds that activation steering renders interpretability more actionable while raising important considerations for safe and effective use.

2504.08729.title: Steering CLIP's vision transformer with sparse autoencoders
2504.08729.tldr: This work addresses the gap between vision and language processing by training SAEs on CLIP's vision transformer and uncover key differences between vision and language processing, including distinct sparsity patterns for SAEs trained across layers and token types.

2505.20229.title: From What to How: Attributing CLIP's Latent Components Reveals Unexpected Semantic Reliance
2505.20229.tldr: This work adapts attribution patching for instance-wise component attributions in CLIP and highlights key faithfulness limitations of the widely used Logit Lens technique to automatically uncover reliance on components that encode semantically unexpected or spurious concepts.

2402.08983.title: SafeDecoding: Defending against Jailbreak Attacks via Safety-Aware Decoding
2402.08983.tldr: This paper introduces SafeDecoding, a safety-aware decoding strategy for LLMs to generate helpful and harmless responses to user queries that significantly reduces the attack success rate and harmfulness of jailbreak attacks without compromising the helpfulness of responses to benign user queries.
2402.08983.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.05761.title: The BiGGen Bench: A Principled Benchmark for Fine-grained Evaluation of Language Models with Language Models
2406.05761.tldr: The BiGGen Bench is introduced, a principled generation benchmark designed to thoroughly evaluate nine distinct capabilities of LMs across 77 diverse tasks, closely mirroring the nuanced discernment of human evaluation.
2406.05761.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.07626.title: LLM Unlearning Under the Microscope: A Full-Stack View on Methods and Metrics
2510.07626.tldr: This work presents a principled taxonomy of twelve recent stateful unlearning methods, grouped into three methodological families: divergence-driven optimization, representation misalignment, and rejection-based targeted unlearning, and revisits the evaluation of unlearning effectiveness, utility retention, and robustness, focusing on the WMDP benchmark.

2511.07970.title: Continual Unlearning for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: A Regularization Perspective
2511.07970.tldr: This study presents the first systematic study of continual unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models and shows that popular unlearning methods suffer from rapid utility collapse: after only a few requests, models forget retained knowledge and generate degraded images.

2410.07163.title: Simplicity Prevails: Rethinking Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning
2410.07163.tldr: A simple yet effective unlearning optimization framework, called SimNPO, is proposed, showing that `simplicity' in removing the reliance on a reference model (through the lens of simple preference optimization) benefits unlearning.

2502.05374.title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
2502.05374.tldr: For the first time, a connection is established between robust unlearning and sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) through a unified robust optimization framework, in an analogy to adversarial training designed to defend against adversarial attacks.

2510.00761.title: Downgrade to Upgrade: Optimizer Simplification Enhances Robustness in LLM Unlearning
2510.00761.tldr: This work investigates the role of the optimizer, independent of unlearning objectives and formulations, in shaping unlearning robustness, and proposes a hybrid optimizer that combines first-order and zeroth-order updates, preserving unlearning efficacy while enhancing robustness.

2409.15398.title: Attack Atlas: A Practitioner's Perspective on Challenges and Pitfalls in Red Teaming GenAI
2409.15398.tldr: The Attack Atlas is an intuitive framework that brings a practical approach to analyzing single-turn input attacks, placing it at the forefront for practitioners in the protection of generative AI systems.

2403.12805.title: Contextual Moral Value Alignment Through Context-Based Aggregation
2403.12805.tldr: This paper proposes a system that does contextual moral value alignment based on contextual aggregation, which shows better results in term of alignment to human value compared to the state of the art.

2408.10392.title: Value Alignment from Unstructured Text
2408.10392.tldr: This paper introduces a systematic end-to-end methodology for aligning LLMs to the implicit and explicit values represented in unstructured text data, and shows improved performance against other approaches, as quantified through the use of automatic metrics and win rates.
2408.10392.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2501.12405.title: Scopes of Alignment
2501.12405.tldr: This paper motivates why the need to move beyond such a limited conception of alignment and proposes three dimensions for doing so, and uses the proposed framework to position some technologies and workflows that go beyond prevailing notions of alignment.

2404.07921.title: AmpleGCG: Learning a Universal and Transferable Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes for Jailbreaking Both Open and Closed LLMs
2404.07921.tldr: This work amplifies the impact of GCG by training a generative model of adversarial suffixes that is universal to any harmful queries and transferable from attacking open-source LLMs to closed-source LLMs, and transfers seamlessly to attack different models, including closed-source LLMs.

2410.17401.title: AdvAgent: Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents
2410.17401.tldr: AdvAgent is proposed, a black-box red-teaming framework for attacking web agents that employs a reinforcement learning-based pipeline to train an adversarial prompter model that optimizes adversarial prompts using feedback from the black-box agent.

2505.21936.title: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
2505.21936.tldr: RedTeamCUA is proposed, an adversarial testing framework featuring a novel hybrid sandbox that integrates a VM-based OS environment with Docker-based web platforms that provides an essential framework for advancing realistic, controlled, and systematic analysis of CUA vulnerabilities.

2410.22143.title: AmpleGCG-Plus: A Strong Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes to Jailbreak LLMs with Higher Success Rates in Fewer Attempts
2410.22143.tldr: AmpleGCG-Plus is introduced, an enhanced version that achieves better performance in fewer attempts and jailbreaks the newer GPT-4o series of models at similar rates to GPT-4, and, uncovers vulnerabilities against the recently proposed circuit breakers defense.

2406.06874.title: Learning Reward and Policy Jointly from Demonstration and Preference Improves Alignment
2406.06874.tldr: This work develops a single stage approach named Alignment with Integrated Human Feedback (AIHF), capable of integrating both human preference and demonstration to train reward models and the policy, and observes that the proposed solutions outperform the existing alignment algorithms by large margins.

2405.19316.title: Robust Preference Optimization through Reward Model Distillation
2405.19316.tldr: This work trains the LM such that its induced implicit reward matches an explicit reward model trained on the preference data, and distilling from such a family of reward models leads to improved robustness to distribution shift in preference annotations, while preserving the simple supervised nature of DPO.

2412.19792.title: InfAlign: Inference-aware language model alignment
2412.19792.tldr: This work proves that for any inference-time decoding procedure, the optimal aligned policy is the solution to the standard RLHF problem with a transformation of the reward, and proposes a framework for inference-aware alignment (InfAlign), which aims to optimize inference-time win rate of the aligned policy against the base model.

2312.09244.title: Helping or Herding? Reward Model Ensembles Mitigate but do not Eliminate Reward Hacking
2312.09244.tldr: The application of reward ensembles to alignment at both training time (through reinforcement learning) and inference time (through reranking) is explored, showing that reward models are underspecified and overoptimization is mitigated by the use of reward ensembles.

2407.02855.title: From Theft to Bomb-Making: The Ripple Effect of Unlearning in Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks
2407.02855.tldr: A novel ripple effect of unlearning is identified, wherein LLMs can implicitly unlearn harmful knowledge that was not explicitly introduced during the unlearning phase, which makes unlearning-based methods able to decrease the Attack Success Rate on unseen data from more than 70% to less than 10% with only 100 training samples.

2503.01865.title: Guiding not Forcing: Enhancing the Transferability of Jailbreaking Attacks on LLMs via Removing Superfluous Constraints
2503.01865.tldr: This study aims to understand and enhance the transferability of gradient-based jailbreaking methods, which are among the standard approaches for attacking white-box models, and introduces a novel conceptual framework to elucidate transferability.
2503.01865.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.16776.title: AISafetyLab: A Comprehensive Framework for AI Safety Evaluation and Improvement
2502.16776.tldr: AISafetyLab is introduced, a unified framework and toolkit that integrates representative attack, defense, and evaluation methodologies for AI safety and features an intuitive interface that enables developers to seamlessly apply various techniques while maintaining a well-structured and extensible codebase for future advancements.

2508.05087.title: JPS: Jailbreak Multimodal Large Language Models with Collaborative Visual Perturbation and Textual Steering
2508.05087.tldr: This work proposes JPS, Jailbreak MLLMs with collaborative visual Perturbation and textual Steering, which achieves jailbreaks via corporation of visual image and textually steering prompt, and proposes the Malicious Intent Fulfillment Rate (MIFR) metric.

2511.01287.title: "Give a Positive Review Only": An Early Investigation Into In-Paper Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for AI Reviewers
2511.01287.tldr: This work proposes two classes of attacks: a static attack, which employs a fixed injection prompt, and an iterative attack, which optimizes the injection prompt against a simulated reviewer model to maximize its effectiveness.

2401.17263.title: Robust Prompt Optimization for Defending Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
2401.17263.tldr: An optimization-based objective for defending LLMs against jailbreaking attacks and an algorithm to create robust system-level defenses, which directly incorporates the adversary into the defensive objective and optimizes a lightweight and transferable suffix, enabling RPO to adapt to worst-case adaptive attacks.

2402.03299.title: GUARD: Role-playing to Generate Natural-language Jailbreakings to Test Guideline Adherence of Large Language Models
2402.03299.tldr: A role-playing system that assigns four different roles to the user LLMs to collaborate on new jailbreaks and pioneer a setting in this system that will automatically follow the government-issued guidelines to generate jailbreaks to test whether LLMs follow the guidelines accordingly.

2405.20413.title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models Against Moderation Guardrails via Cipher Characters
2405.20413.tldr: This work introduces JAMBench, a harmful behavior benchmark designed to trigger and evaluate moderation guardrails, and proposes a jailbreak method, JAM (Jailbreak Against Moderation), designed to attack moderation guardrails using jailbreak prefixes to bypass input-level filters.

2508.20325.title: GUARD: Guideline Upholding Test through Adaptive Role-play and Jailbreak Diagnostics for LLMs
2508.20325.tldr: GUARD (Guideline Upholding Test through Adaptive Role-play and Jailbreak Diagnostics) is a testing method designed to operationalize guidelines into specific guideline-violating questions that assess LLM adherence, demonstrating its usage in promoting reliable LLM-based applications.

2508.09853.title: STREAM (ChemBio): A Standard for Transparently Reporting Evaluations in AI Model Reports
2508.09853.tldr: STREAM (A Standard for Transparently Reporting Evaluations in AI Model Reports), a standard to improve how model reports disclose evaluation results, initially focusing on chemical and biological benchmarks, is proposed.

2510.08792.title: Assurance of Frontier AI Built for National Security

2412.02512.title: Pre-Deployment Information Sharing: A Zoning Taxonomy for Precursory Capabilities
2412.02512.tldr: A taxonomy of dangerous capability zones (a zoning taxonomy) tied to a staggered information exchange framework that enables relevant bodies to take action accordingly is proposed to meaningfully detect and track capability progress.

2606.06028.title: Misaligned AI as a New Insider Risk
2606.06028.tldr: This policy memorandum explains why deployers of AI models in high-stakes contexts should treat those AI models as insider risk vectors and recommends that the U.S. Government adapts well-established measures to AI models deployed in high-stakes contexts.

2410.16184.title: RM-Bench: Benchmarking Reward Models of Language Models with Subtlety and Style
2410.16184.tldr: RM-Bench is introduced, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate reward models based on their sensitivity to subtle content differences and resistance to style biases, and it is revealed that even state-of-the-art models achieve an average performance, which falls short of random-level accuracy when faced with style bias interference.

2406.14144.title: Towards Understanding Safety Alignment: A Mechanistic Perspective from Safety Neurons
2406.14144.tldr: This paper proposes inference-time activation contrasting to locate safety neurons within LLMs and dynamic activation patching to evaluate their causal effects on model safety, and demonstrates an application of the findings in safeguarding LLMs by detecting unsafe outputs before generation.

2605.27354.title: Guiding LLM Post-training Data Engineering with Model Internals from Sparse Autoencoders
2605.27354.tldr: SAERL, a data engineering framework for LLM reinforcement learning (RL), models three intrinsic data properties: diversity, difficulty, and quality, using model internals extracted with Sparse Autoencoder (SAE), an advanced mechanistic interpretability tool, and demonstrates that SAE transfers effectively across model families and scales.

2608.13538.title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
2608.13538.tldr: SAEVerbalizer is introduced, a framework that injects SAE decoder directions into an LLM's representations and fine-tunes the LLM's downstream layers to generate natural-language explanations of the injected features.

2607.25270.title: Where Steering Signals Come From: Activation Source Selection in Activation Steering
2607.25270.tldr: Tail subtraction is introduced, which removes shared prompt and continuation semantics from boundary states and yields cleaner, more stable steering signals, and suggests that steering depends on representations of what the model is about to do, not merely on what has already appeared.

2409.01247.title: Conversational Complexity for Assessing Risk in Large Language Models
2409.01247.tldr: A quantitative analysis examining the statistical distribution of harmful and harmless conversational lengths and complexities and the minimisation of CC suggest that this distributional analysis and the minimisation of CC serve as valuable tools for understanding AI safety, offering insights into the accessibility of harmful information.

2602.20813.title: Pressure Reveals Character: Behavioural Alignment Evaluation at Depth
2602.20813.tldr: An alignment benchmark spanning 904 scenarios across six categories -- Honesty, Safety, Non-Manipulation, Robustness, Corrigibility, and Scheming -- validated as realistic by human raters is introduced, revealing that alignment behaves as a unified construct with models scoring high on one category tending to score high on others.

2603.13250.title: The Missing Red Line: How Commercial Pressure Erodes AI Safety Boundaries
2603.13250.tldr: It is found that commercial system prompts can override safety training, causing frontier models to lie about medical risks, dismiss safety concerns, and prioritise profit over user welfare.

2406.14868.title: Direct Multi-Turn Preference Optimization for Language Agents
2406.14868.tldr: This work replaces the policy constraint with the state-action occupancy measure constraint in the RL objective and adds length normalization to the Bradley-Terry model, yielding a novel loss function named DMPO for multi-turn agent tasks with theoretical explanations.
2406.14868.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2506.00441.title: K-order Ranking Preference Optimization for Large Language Models
2506.00441.tldr: This work proposes K-order Ranking Preference Optimization (KPO) by extending the DPO's Plackett-Luce model to accommodate top-K rankings and extends KPO to dynamically determine appropriate K for different samples and introduces a curriculum learning strategy to boost training efficiency.
2506.00441.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2512.07761.title: TROJail: Trajectory-Level Optimization for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Jailbreaks with Process Rewards
2512.07761.tldr: This work forms this task as a multi-turn reinforcement learning problem, directly optimizing the harmfulness of the final-turn response as the outcome reward, and introduces TROJail, which employs two process rewards to evaluate the utility of intermediate prompts and integrate them into advantage estimation.
2512.07761.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.16665.title: SafetyAnalyst: Interpretable, Transparent, and Steerable Safety Moderation for AI Behavior
2410.16665.tldr: SafetyAnalyst uses chain-of-thought reasoning to analyze its potential consequences by creating a structured "harm-benefit tree", which enumerates harmful and beneficial actions and effects the AI behavior may lead to, along with likelihood, severity, and immediacy labels that describe potential impacts on stakeholders.

2409.14509.title: Can AI writing be salvaged? Mitigating Idiosyncrasies and Improving Human-AI Alignment in the Writing Process through Edits
2409.14509.tldr: A large-scale preference annotation confirms that although experts largely prefer text edited by other experts, automatic editing methods show promise in improving alignment between LLM-generated and human-written text.
2409.14509.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2607.00415.title: A Mechanistic View of Authority Hierarchy in LLM Sycophancy

2404.06664.title: CulturalTeaming: AI-Assisted Interactive Red-Teaming for Challenging LLMs' (Lack of) Multicultural Knowledge
2404.06664.tldr: CulturalTeaming is introduced, an interactive red-teaming system that leverages human-AI collaboration to build truly challenging evaluation dataset for assessing the multicultural knowledge of LLMs, while improving annotators' capabilities and experiences and shedding light on the promises of involving heavier AI assistance in modern evaluation dataset creation procedures.

2602.17560.title: ODESteer: A Unified ODE-Based Steering Framework for LLM Alignment
2602.17560.tldr: This work establishes a principled new view of activation steering in LLM alignment by unifying its theoretical foundations via ODEs, and validating it empirically through the proposed ODESteer method.

2411.02631.title: Extracting Unlearned Information from LLMs with Activation Steering
2411.02631.tldr: This work proposes activation steering as a method for exact information retrieval from unlearned LLMs, and introduces a novel approach to generating steering vectors, named Anonymized Activation Steering, which successfully recovers general knowledge.

2507.04219.title: Model Collapse Is Not a Bug but a Feature in Machine Unlearning for LLMs
2507.04219.tldr: This work proposes a novel unlearning method-Partial Model Collapse (PMC), which overcomes four key limitations of existing unlearning methods that explicitly optimize on unlearning targets, and more effectively removes private information from model outputs while preserving general model utility.

2603.06594.title: A Coin Flip for Safety: LLM Judges Fail to Reliably Measure Adversarial Robustness
2603.06594.tldr: It is shown that existing validation protocols fail to account for substantial distribution shifts inherent to red-teaming: diverse victim models exhibit distinct generation styles, attacks distort output patterns, and semantic ambiguity varies significantly across jailbreak scenarios.

2402.09063.title: Soft Prompt Threats: Attacking Safety Alignment and Unlearning in Open-Source LLMs through the Embedding Space
2402.09063.tldr: This work finds that embedding space attacks circumvent model alignments and trigger harmful behaviors more efficiently than discrete attacks or model fine-tuning, and highlights embedding space attacks as an important threat model in open-source LLMs.

2410.03523.title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Unlearning and Alignment for Large Language Models
2410.03523.tldr: The first formal probabilistic evaluation framework for LLMs is introduced, which proposes novel metrics with high probability guarantees concerning the output distribution of a model and shows how to overcome challenges associated with probabilistic outputs in a case study on unlearning.

2502.10487.title: Fast Proxies for LLM Robustness Evaluation
2502.10487.tldr: This work considers gradient-descent-based embedding-space attacks, prefilling attacks, and direct prompting and finds that direct prompting and embedding-space attacks can predict attack success rates well and reduce computational cost by three orders of magnitude.

2606.03647.title: Black-box, Adaptive, Efficient, Transferable, Harmful, Applicable... Attacks Are All You Need to Break LLMs
2606.03647.tldr: Indirect Harm Optimization is introduced, a masked diffusion language model attacker trained via iterative preference optimization against a harmfulness judge, requiring only black-box access to the target, requiring only black-box access to the target.

2511.04316.title: AdversariaLLM: A Unified and Modular Toolbox for LLM Robustness Research
2511.04316.tldr: AdversariaLLM is introduced, a toolbox for conducting LLM jailbreak robustness research that centers on reproducibility, correctness, and extensibility, and integrates seven benchmark datasets spanning harmfulness, over-refusal, and utility evaluation.

2502.17420.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
2502.17420.tldr: It is shown that orthogonality alone does not imply independence under intervention, motivating the notion of representational independence that accounts for both linear and non-linear effects.

2601.05641.title: Multilingual Amnesia: On the Transferability of Unlearning in Multilingual LLMs
2601.05641.tldr: The experiments show that unlearning in high-resource languages is generally more stable, with asymmetric transfer effects observed between typologically related languages, and the analysis of linguistic distances indicates that syntactic similarity is the strongest predictor of cross-lingual unlearning behavior.
2601.05641.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.01080.title: The Coming Crisis of Multi-Agent Misalignment: AI Alignment Must Be a Dynamic and Social Process

2607.26120.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
2607.26120.tldr: It is suggested that even subtle objective misalignment can profoundly affect collective decision-making, highlighting the need for effective mitigation strategies for LLM-based multi-agent systems.

2603.04426.title: Delta-Crosscoder: Robust Crosscoder Model Diffing in Narrow Fine-Tuning Regimes
2603.04426.tldr: Delta-Crosscoder reliably isolates latent directions causally responsible for fine-tuned behaviors and enables effective mitigation, outperforming SAE-based baselines, while matching the Non-SAE-based.

2606.07963.title: Shared Latent Structures Enable Unified Backdoor Detection and Mitigation in LLMs
2606.07963.tldr: The results suggest that many backdoors rely on a transferable latent mechanism, enabling unified detection and mitigation, and introduce Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning (CAFT), which suppresses backdoor formation by ablating the shared latent subspace during training.

2507.21084.title: Reviving Your MNEME: Predicting The Side Effects of LLM Unlearning and Fine-Tuning via Sparse Model Diffing
2507.21084.tldr: This work introduces MNEME, Model diffiNg for Evaluating Mechanistic Effects, a lightweight framework for identifying unintended side effects using sparse model diffing, and demonstrates that retraining on high-activation samples can partially reverse these effects.
2507.21084.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2607.15286.title: Hidden in Thought: Transferable Chain-of-Thought Artifacts Induce Harmful Behavior
2607.15286.tldr: Results show that harmful reasoning transfers at both the trace and pattern levels, motivating defences that evaluate reasoning context in addition to final outputs, motivating defences that evaluate reasoning context in addition to final outputs.

2410.15460.title: Hallucination Detox: Sensitivity Dropout (SenD) for Large Language Model Training
2410.15460.tldr: An unsupervised hallucination detection metric, Efficient EigenScore (EES), is developed, which approximates the traditional EigenScore in 2x speed and is integrated into the SenD training protocol, allowing SenD to be both computationally scalable and effective at reducing hallucination variance.
2410.15460.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.16462.title: Let's Unlearn Stereotypes Before Decision-Making: Assessing the Impact of Intrinsic Bias Mitigation on Downstream Fairness in LLMs
2509.16462.tldr: Fairness-Aware Concept Unlearning is introduced, a model-level mitigation method that adapts concept unlearning to fairness-oriented representation balancing that produces statistically significant reductions in intrinsic gender bias that are associated with downstream fairness improvements across most evaluated settings, datasets, models, and fairness metrics.

2505.07468.title: Promising Topics for U.S.-China Dialogues on AI Risks and Governance
2505.07468.tldr: A systematic analysis of primary AI policy and corporate governance documents from the United States and China suggests that despite strategic competition, there exist concrete opportunities for bilateral U.S-China cooperation in the development of responsible AI.
2505.07468.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2608.05656.title: Studying People to Study AI: Expert Perspectives on the Epistemic Fit and Barriers of Human Research in AI Safety & Ethics
2608.05656.tldr: Although there is a consensus that human research is valuable for generating evidence for AISE, its adoption and acceptance are constrained by perceived validity issues, tangible resource barriers, epistemic and personal preferences in methods, and infrastructural constraints from the broader research community.

2402.05749.title: Generalized Preference Optimization: A Unified Approach to Offline Alignment
2402.05749.tldr: The analysis and experiments reveal the connections and subtle differences between the offline regularization and the KL divergence regularization intended by the canonical RLHF formulation, and show that different GPO variants achieve similar trade-offs between regularization and performance, though the optimal values of hyper-parameter might differ as predicted by theory.

2405.08448.title: Understanding the performance gap between online and offline alignment algorithms
2405.08448.tldr: Light is shed on the pivotal role of on-policy sampling in AI alignment, and certain fundamental challenges of offline alignment algorithms are hinted at.

2403.08635.title: Human Alignment of Large Language Models through Online Preference Optimisation
2403.08635.tldr: This paper shows the equivalence between two recent alignment methods, namely Identity Policy Optimisation (IPO) and Nash Mirror Descent (Nash-MD), and introduces a generalisation of IPO, named IPO-MD, that leverages the regularised sampling approach proposed by Nash-MD.

2405.14655.title: Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning from Preference Human Feedback
2405.14655.tldr: Novel methods for Reinforcement Learning from preference feedback between two full multi-turn conversations are developed, and it is shown that in an environment with explicit rewards, the algorithm recovers the same performance as a reward-based RL baseline, despite relying solely on a weaker preference signal.

2409.02392.title: Building Math Agents with Multi-Turn Iterative Preference Learning
2409.02392.tldr: This work introduces a multi-turn direct preference learning framework, tailored for this context, that leverages feedback from code interpreters and optimizes trajectory-level preferences and includes multi-turn DPO and multi-turn KTO as specific implementations.

2505.19731.title: Proximal Point Nash Learning from Human Feedback
2505.19731.tldr: This work first analyzes a simple self-play policy gradient method, which is equivalent to Online IPO, and establishes high-probability last-iterate convergence guarantees for this method, but the analysis also reveals a possible stability limitation of the underlying dynamics.

2407.08488.title: Lynx: An Open Source Hallucination Evaluation Model
2407.08488.tldr: This work introduces LYNX, a SOTA hallucination detection LLM that is capable of advanced reasoning on challenging real-world hallucination scenarios and presents HaluBench, a comprehensive hallucination evaluation benchmark, consisting of 15k samples sourced from various real-world domains.

2410.02298.title: Jailbreak Antidote: Runtime Safety-Utility Balance via Sparse Representation Adjustment in Large Language Models
2410.02298.tldr: Jailbreak Antidote is introduced, a method that enables real-time adjustment of LLM safety preferences by manipulating a sparse subset of the model's internal states during inference, and offers a lightweight, scalable solution that enhances LLM safety while preserving utility.

2410.04190.title: Harnessing Task Overload for Scalable Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
2410.04190.tldr: A novel scalable jailbreak attack is introduced that preempts the activation of an LLM's safety policies by occupying its computational resources by saturating the model's processing capacity when processing the subsequent instruction.

2506.01495.title: C-VARC: A Large-Scale Chinese Value Rule Corpus for Value Alignment of Large Language Models
2506.01495.tldr: This work establishes a culturally-adaptive benchmarking framework for comprehensive value evaluation and alignment, representing Chinese characteristics, and constructs a large-scale Chinese Value Rule Corpus (C-VARC), containing over 250,000 value rules enhanced and expanded through human annotation.

2511.06396.title: Efficient LLM Safety Evaluation through Multi-Agent Debate
2511.06396.tldr: This work introduces HAJailBench, a human-annotated jailbreak benchmark with 11,100 labeled interactions spanning diverse attack methods and target models, and pairs it with a Multi-Agent Judge framework in which critic, defender, and judge agents debate under a shared safety rubric to support structured, value-aligned debate as a practical design for scalable LLM safety evaluation.

2510.01088.title: Safety Instincts: LLMs Learn to Trust Their Internal Compass for Self-Defense
2510.01088.tldr: Safety Instincts Reinforcement Learning (SIRL) is introduced, which transforms internal confidence into a self-generated reward signal, eliminating dependence on external validators or human annotations and paving the way for more autonomous and robust AI safety mechanisms that scale without extensive human oversight.

2608.13304.title: Refusing Intent, Not Form: Wrapper-Based Intent-Group Supervision for LLM Safety
2608.13304.tldr: This work proposes Wrapper-Based Intent-Form Augmentation (WIFA), an automatic intent-group augmentation method that pairs wrapped harmful examples with structurally matched wrapped benign counterexamples, requiring no external teacher or manual per-wrapper intent labels.

2606.24026.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?
2606.24026.tldr: This work proposes HyVE (Hypothesize, Validate, Explain), an agentic explainer that analyzes each component through an iterative loop of observation, hypothesis generation, and causal validation, eventually producing a component-level explanation and a circuit-level task description.

2602.08995.title: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
2602.08995.tldr: This work makes the first effort to define and study misaligned action detection in CUAs, with comprehensive coverage of both externally induced and internally arising misaligned actions.

2604.01438.title: ClawSafety: "Safe" LLMs, Unsafe Agents
2604.01438.tldr: CLAWSAFETY is introduced, a benchmark of 120 adversarial test scenarios organized along three dimensions (harm domain, attack vector, and harmful action type) and grounded in realistic, high-privilege professional workspaces spanning software engineering, finance, healthcare, law, and DevOps.

2604.06840.title: MirageBackdoor: A Stealthy Attack that Induces Think-Well-Answer-Wrong Reasoning
2604.06840.tldr: MirageBackdoor (MirageBD), the first backdoor attack to achieve Think Well but Answer Wrong, enables the triggered model to preserve clean CoTs while selectively steering the final answer toward a specific target, significantly enhancing the stealthiness of the attack.
2604.06840.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.18056.title: An Early Warning of Emerging Biosecurity Risks in Frontier LLMs
2607.18056.tldr: Intern-BioBreaker, a specialized bio-red-teaming model, together with an integrated computational-to-physical framework that couples model-level stress testing with wet-lab validation, underscores the need for stronger biological red-teaming, nucleic acid synthesis screening, and safety mechanisms that keep pace with model capabilities.

2407.10223.title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning
2407.10223.tldr: The OOO framework is proposed that includes an Orthogonal low-rank adapter for continually unlearning requested data and an Out-Of-Distribution detector to measure the similarity between input and unlearning data and consistently achieves the best unlearning effectiveness and utility preservation.

2410.12949.title: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
