2410.12949.tldr: This work investigates how mechanistic interpretability -- which, in part, aims to identify model components associated to specific interpretable mechanisms that make up a model capability -- can improve the precision and effectiveness of editing and unlearning.

2311.15131.title: Localizing Lying in Llama: Understanding Instructed Dishonesty on True-False Questions Through Prompting, Probing, and Patching
2311.15131.tldr: This paper investigates instructed dishonesty, wherein it is explicitly prompt LLaMA-2-70b-chat to lie, and performs prompt engineering to find which prompts best induce lying behavior, and uses mechanistic interpretability approaches to localize where in the network this behavior occurs.

2502.14829.title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
2502.14829.tldr: A framework for measuring parametric faithfulness of generated reasoning is introduced, and Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning steps (FUR), an instance of this framework, is proposed, which erases information contained in reasoning steps from model parameters, and measures faithfulness as the resulting effect on the model's prediction.
2502.14829.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2502.04577.title: Position-aware Automatic Circuit Discovery
2502.04577.tldr: This work introduces the concept of a dataset schema, which defines token spans with similar semantics across examples, enabling position-aware circuit discovery in datasets with variable length examples, and proposes two improvements to incorporate positionality into circuits, even on tasks containing variable-length examples.
2502.04577.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.09325.title: REVS: Unlearning Sensitive Information in Language Models via Rank Editing in the Vocabulary Space
2406.09325.tldr: Compared to other methods, REVS demonstrates superior performance in unlearning sensitive information and robustness to extraction attacks, while retaining underlying model integrity.
2406.09325.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2408.01416.title: The Quest for the Right Mediator: Surveying Mechanistic Interpretability Through the Lens of Causal Mediation Analysis
2408.01416.tldr: A perspective on interpretability research grounded in causal mediation analysis is proposed, describing the history and current state of interpretability taxonomized according to the types of causal units employed, as well as methods used to search over mediators.

2508.13650.title: CRISP: Persistent Concept Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoders
2508.13650.tldr: CRISP is introduced, a parameter-efficient method for persistent concept unlearning using SAEs that outperforms prior approaches on safety-critical unlearning tasks from the WMDP benchmark, successfully removing harmful knowledge while preserving general and in-domain capabilities.
2508.13650.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.24302.title: Differentiable Faithfulness Alignment for Cross-Model Circuit Transfer
2604.24302.tldr: Overall, DFA consistently outperforms simple baselines and, in some settings, recovers target-model circuits with faithfulness comparable to or stronger than direct attribution, suggesting that smaller models can provide useful mechanistic priors for larger ones.

2510.25786.title: BlackboxNLP-2025 MIB Shared Task: Improving Circuit Faithfulness via Better Edge Selection
2510.25786.tldr: This work builds on the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark (MIB) and proposes three key improvements to circuit discovery, including a simple ratio-based selection strategy to prioritize strong positive-scoring edges, balancing performance and faithfulness.
2510.25786.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2609.13072.title: MAxBench: A Multinomial Concept Recovery Benchmark
2609.13072.tldr: This work introduces MAxBench, a geometry-agnostic evaluation framework for multinomial concept representations based on sampling from the recovered concept representation, and finds that affine subspaces steer more reliably and have greater recall than rank-one or linear subspaces.

2402.08925.title: MaxMin-RLHF: Alignment with Diverse Human Preferences
2402.08925.tldr: This work first derive an impossibility result of alignment with single reward RLHF, thereby highlighting its insufficiency in representing diverse human preferences, and proposes a MaxMin alignment objective for policy learning inspired by the Egalitarian principle in social choice theory to better represent diverse human preferences.

2402.10500.title: Active Preference Optimization for Sample Efficient RLHF
2402.10500.tldr: This work reformulates RLHF within the contextual preference bandit framework, treating generations as actions, and gives a nearly complete characterization of the sub-optimality gap in terms of both lower and upper bounds, and proposes an algorithm, Active Preference Optimization, that iteratively collects preferences for the most uncertain contexts.

2406.12091.title: Is poisoning a real threat to LLM alignment? Maybe more so than you think
2406.12091.tldr: This work comprehensively analyzes Direct Policy Optimization's vulnerabilities under different types of attacks, and different poisoning methods across a wide array of language models, i.e., LLama 7B, Mistral 7B, and Gemma 7B.

2406.15567.title: SAIL: Self-Improving Efficient Online Alignment of Large Language Models
2406.15567.tldr: This work establishes that online LLM alignment is underpinned by bilevel optimization and permits alignment methods to operate in an online and self-improving manner, as well as generalize prior online RLHF methods as special cases.

2503.13817.title: VARP: Reinforcement Learning from Vision-Language Model Feedback with Agent Regularized Preferences
2503.13817.tldr: A two-part solution that both improves feedback accuracy and better aligns reward learning with the agent's policy is presented, allowing VLMs to provide more reliable preferences-improving preference accuracy by approximately 15-20% in metaworld tasks.

2510.01549.title: MIRA: Towards Mitigating Reward Hacking in Inference-Time Alignment of T2I Diffusion Models
2510.01549.tldr: MIRA introduces an image-space, score-based KL surrogate that regularizes the sampling trajectory with a frozen backbone, constraining the output distribution so reward can increase without off-distribution drift (reward hacking), and introduces MIRA-DPO, mapping preference optimization to inference time with a frozen backbone, extending MIRA to non-differentiable rewards without fine-tuning.

2312.14436.title: REBEL: Reward Regularization-Based Approach for Robotic Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2312.14436.tldr: A novel concept of reward regularization within the robotic RLHF (RL from Human Feedback) framework, which incorporates not just human feedback in the form of preferences but also considers the preferences of the RL agent itself during the reward function learning process, which significantly mitigates the issue of distribution shift in RLHF with a computationally tractable algorithm.

2412.05232.title: LIAR: Leveraging Inference Time Alignment (Best-of-N) to Jailbreak LLMs in Seconds
2412.05232.tldr: LIAR (Leveraging Inference-time misalignment to jailbReak), a fast, black-box, best-of-$N$ sampling attack requiring no training, is introduced and offers a simple yet effective tool for evaluating LLM robustness and advancing alignment research.

2602.11096.title: Safety Recovery in Reasoning Models Is Only a Few Early Steering Steps Away
2602.11096.tldr: This work proposes SafeThink, a lightweight inference-time defense that treats safety recovery as a satisficing constraint rather than a maximization objective, and monitors the evolving reasoning trace with a safety reward model and conditionally injects an optimized short corrective prefix only when the safety threshold is violated.

2508.06783.title: PROPS: Progressively Private Self-alignment of Large Language Models
2508.06783.tldr: This work proposes PROPS (PROgressively Private Self-alignment), a multi-stage privacy preserving alignment framework where privately aligned models in previous stages can serve as labelers for supplementing training data in the subsequent stages of alignment, which preserves the privacy of preference labels provided by humans.

2410.15610.title: On The Global Convergence Of Online RLHF With Neural Parametrization
2410.15610.tldr: This work proposes a bi-level formulation for AI alignment in parameterized settings and introduces a first-order approach to solve this problem, and establishes convergence rate bounds and global optimality for the RLHF framework in neural network-parameterized settings.

2511.05541.title: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Language for Interpretability
2511.05541.tldr: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders (T-SAEs) are introduced, which incorporate a novel contrastive loss encouraging consistent activations of high-level features over adjacent tokens, and enable SAEs to disentangle semantic from syntactic features in a self-supervised manner.

2512.04144.title: RippleBench: Capturing Ripple Effects Using Existing Knowledge Repositories
2512.04144.tldr: RippleBench-Maker is introduced, an automatic pipeline that retrieves semantic neighbors of any source concept from a knowledge repository and generates multiple-choice questions at varying semantic distances, suggesting ripple effects are a property of the unlearning method rather than the base model.

2506.20941.title: Revisiting the Past: Data Unlearning with Model State History
2506.20941.tldr: A new algorithm is proposed, MSA (Model State Arithmetic), for unlearning datapoints in large language models, which utilizes prior model checkpoints -- artifacts that record model states at different stages of pretraining -- to estimate and counteract the effect of targeted datapoints.

2408.10075.title: Personalizing Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Variational Preference Learning
2408.10075.tldr: A class of multimodal RLHF methods based on a latent variable formulation that enables learning from diverse populations of users with divergent preferences, an important challenge that naturally occurs in problems from robot learning to foundation model alignment.

2504.03206.title: Enhancing Personalized Multi-Turn Dialogue with Curiosity Reward
2504.03206.tldr: This work proposes leveraging a user model to incorporate a curiosity-based intrinsic reward into multi-turn RLHF, and demonstrates its effectiveness in two distinct domains: significantly improving personalization performance in a conversational recommendation task, and personalizing conversations for different learning styles in an educational setting.

2507.13579.title: Learning to summarize user information for personalized reinforcement learning from human feedback
2507.13579.tldr: This work presents a novel framework, Preference Learning Using Summarization (PLUS), that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn to produce text-based summaries of each user's preferences, characteristics, and past conversations that condition the reward model, enabling it to make personalized predictions about the types of responses valued by each user.

2511.17879.title: Generative Adversarial Post-Training Mitigates Reward Hacking in Live Human-AI Music Interaction
2511.17879.tldr: This paper proposes a novel adversarial training method on policy-generated trajectories to mitigate reward hacking in RL post-training for melody-to-chord accompaniment, and demonstrates improved output diversity, harmonic coherence, adaptation speed and user agency.

2402.09345.title: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
2402.09345.tldr: This work proposes a framework for reward modeling, namely InfoRM, by introducing a variational information bottleneck objective to filter out irrelevant information and identifies a correlation between overoptimization and outliers in the IB latent space of InfoRM, establishing it as a promising tool for detecting reward overoptimization.

2501.19358.title: The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking
2501.19358.tldr: An Energy loss-aware PPO algorithm (EPPO) is proposed which penalizes the increase in energy loss in the LLM's final layer during reward calculation to prevent excessive energy loss, thereby mitigating reward hacking and improving RLHF performance.

2505.24519.title: AMIA: Automatic Masking and Joint Intention Analysis Makes LVLMs Robust Jailbreak Defenders
2505.24519.tldr: A lightweight, inference-only defense for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) that Automatically Masks a small set of text-irrelevant image patches to disrupt adversarial perturbations and conducts joint Intention Analysis to uncover and mitigate hidden harmful intents before response generation, which confirms both masking and intention analysis are essential for a robust safety-utility trade-off.
2505.24519.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2401.06561.title: Intention Analysis Makes LLMs A Good Jailbreak Defender
2401.06561.tldr: The underlying principle of Intention Analysis is suppressed LLM's tendency to follow jailbreak prompts, thereby enhancing safety, and it is empirically demonstrated that, to some extent, the method is robust to errors in generated intentions.

2410.18252.title: Asynchronous RLHF: Faster and More Efficient Off-Policy RL for Language Models
2410.18252.tldr: Among several RLHF algorithms tested, online DPO is found to be most robust to off-policy data, and robustness increases with the scale of the policy model, and robustness increases with the scale of the policy model.

2403.17031.title: The N+ Implementation Details of RLHF with PPO: A Case Study on TL;DR Summarization

2312.07551.title: Language Model Alignment with Elastic Reset
2312.07551.tldr: It is demonstrated that fine-tuning language models with Elastic Reset leads to state-of-the-art performance on a small scale pivot-translation benchmark, outperforms all baselines in a medium-scale RLHF-like IMDB mock sentiment task and leads to a more performant and more aligned technical QA chatbot with LLaMA-7B.

2404.18239.title: SOUL: Unlocking the Power of Second-Order Optimization for LLM Unlearning
2404.18239.tldr: This work sheds light on the significance of optimizer selection in LLM unlearning for the first time, establishing a clear connection between second-order optimization and influence unlearning and develops a second-order optimization-based LLM unlearning framework, termed Second-Order UnLearning (SOUL), which extends the static, one-shot model update using influence unlearning to a dynamic, iterative unlearning process.
2404.18239.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2608.22103.title: Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench: Evaluating Reward Hacking in Terminal Tasks
2608.22103.tldr: This work adapts HVE to Terminal Bench, a leading benchmark of real-world terminal and coding tasks, and introduces Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench (HVTB), to measure reward-hacking rates across frontier models and study whether prompts with varying amounts of information on the hack can mitigate this behavior.

2605.12474.title: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
2605.12474.tldr: This work studies reward hacking in rubric-based RL, where a policy is optimized against a training verifier but evaluated against a cross-family panel of three frontier judges, reducing dependence on any single evaluator.

2608.11669.title: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
2608.11669.tldr: This work proposes Rubric Dropout, a one-line fix borrowed from neuron dropout that randomly drops a subset of the rubric's criteria before computing the reward, so the policy never optimizes the same rubric twice.

2601.10160.title: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment
2601.10160.tldr: It is found that discussion of AI contributes to misalignment, and the study of how pretraining data shapes alignment priors, or alignment pretraining, as a complement to post-training is established.

2407.06483.title: Composable Interventions for Language Models
2407.06483.tldr: This work introduces composable interventions, a framework to study the effects of using multiple interventions on the same language models, featuring new metrics and a unified codebase, and showcases clear gaps in composability.

2601.11916.title: Expanding External Access To Frontier AI Models For Dangerous Capability Evaluations
2601.11916.tldr: A taxonomy of access methods for dangerous capability evaluations is proposed, to support clearer communication between evaluators, frontier AI companies, and policymakers and to support clearer communication between evaluators and policymakers.
2601.11916.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2605.05058.title: SoK: Robustness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
2605.05058.tldr: A systematic taxonomy of jailbreak attacks and defenses is presented and Security Cube is introduced, a unified, multidimensional framework for comprehensive evaluation of these techniques, to pave the way towards more robust, interpretable, and trustworthy LLM systems.
2605.05058.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2508.15541.title: BadFU: Backdoor Federated Learning through Adversarial Machine Unlearning
2508.15541.tldr: This paper proposes BadFU, an attack strategy where a malicious client uses both backdoor and camouflage samples to train the global model normally during the federated training process, demonstrating that an adversary can inject backdoors into the global model through seemingly legitimate unlearning requests.
2508.15541.venue: International Symposium on Recent Advances in Intrusion Detection

2607.28133.title: AI Sycophancy and Decisions
2607.28133.tldr: It is found that AI advice depolarizes choices on average, moving participants away from their initial leanings, showing that sycophancy is behaviorally relevant, even if it is generally outweighed by the informativeness of AI advice.

2606.26155.title: Detecting and Controlling Sycophancy with Cascading Linear Features
2606.26155.tldr: This work presents an iterative data generation pipeline that isolates cascading linear features responsible for a behavior and demonstrates that sycophancy features discovered through cascading samples form linearly separable subspaces, and allow for selection of model activations that more clearly correspond to the desired behavior than baseline approaches.

2512.20638.title: Uncovering Competency Gaps in Large Language Models and Their Benchmarks
2512.20638.tldr: This work proposes a simple new method using concept activations from sparse autoencoders, to identify fine-grained gaps on a per-concept basis, which can be used to complement existing benchmarks, by providing a concept-level decomposition of model behavior, and by helping benchmark developers iterate upon benchmark design.

2608.28623.title: Looking Again: Measuring Sycophancy in the Reasoning Chains of Multimodal Models Under Pressure
2608.28623.tldr: The results show that sycophancy can corrupt the reasoning chain independently of the final answer, so answer-level evaluation alone is insufficient, and a failure taxonomy separating reasoning-chain from answer-level sycophancy is introduced, and a complementary sentence-level taxonomy locating where in the chain drift first emerges.

2505.15209.title: DUSK: Do Not Unlearn Shared Knowledge
2505.15209.tldr: DUSK is introduced, a benchmark designed to evaluate unlearning methods under realistic data overlap and reveals a key limitation: while most unlearning methods can remove surface-level text, they often fail to erase deeper, context-specific knowledge without damaging shared content.
2505.15209.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.15214.title: R-TOFU: Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
2505.15214.tldr: R-TOFU is introduced, the first benchmark tailored to large Reasoning Models, and Reasoned IDK is proposed, a preference-optimization variant that preserves coherent yet inconclusive reasoning, achieving a stronger balance between forgetting efficacy and model utility than earlier refusal styles.
2505.15214.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2405.17878.title: An Information Theoretic Evaluation Metric For Strong Unlearning
2405.17878.tldr: The Information Difference Index (IDI), a novel white-box metric inspired by information theory, quantifies retained information in intermediate features by measuring mutual information between those features and the labels to be forgotten, offering a more comprehensive assessment of unlearning efficacy.

2505.14832.title: SEPS: A Separability Measure for Robust Unlearning in LLMs
2505.14832.tldr: Mixed Prompt (MP) unlearning is proposed, a strategy that integrates both forget and retain queries into a unified training objective that significantly improves unlearning effectiveness, demonstrating robustness even in complex settings with up to eight mixed forget and retain queries in a single prompt.
2505.14832.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.14667.title: SAFEPATH: Preventing Harmful Reasoning in Chain-of-Thought via Early Alignment
2505.14667.tldr: SAFEPATH is a lightweight alignment method that fine-tunes LRMs to emit a short, 8-token Safety Primer at the start of their reasoning, in response to harmful prompts, while leaving the rest of the reasoning process unsupervised, to reduce harmful outputs while maintaining reasoning performance.

2602.03379.title: Rethinking Benign Relearning: Syntax as the Hidden Driver of Unlearning Failures
2602.03379.tldr: Syntactic diversification is introduced, which paraphrases the original forget queries into heterogeneous structures prior to unlearning, which effectively suppresses benign relearning, accelerates forgetting, and substantially alleviates the trade-off between unlearning efficacy and model utility.

2606.27379.title: Position: The Term "Machine Unlearning" Is Overused in LLMs
2606.27379.tldr: This position paper argues that machine unlearning is overused as a term in LLM research and should be reserved for dataset-defined deletion: removing the training influence of a precisely specified forget set such that the resulting model is approximately indistinguishable from retraining without that data.

2605.10998.title: Few-Shot Truly Benign DPO Attack for Jailbreaking LLMs
2605.10998.tldr: This work proposes a truly benign DPO attack using only 10 harmless preference pairs, the minimum data scale accepted by OpenAI's fine-tuning service, and finds that this effect can emerge from even a single benign preference pair on open-weight models that do not impose minimum data requirements.

2509.23286.title: A2D: Any-Order, Any-Step Safety Alignment for Diffusion Language Models
2509.23286.tldr: A2D (Any-Order, Any-Step Defense), a token-level alignment method that aligns dLLMs to emit an [EOS] refusal signal whenever harmful content arises, achieves robustness to both any-decoding-order and any-step prefilling attacks under various conditions.

2508.06249.title: In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment in Language Models
2508.06249.tldr: This is the first systematic study of in-training safeguards against EM that are practical for providers who expose fine-tuning via an API and demonstrates that selecting interleaving data by the perplexity gap between aligned and misaligned models yields the best results overall.

2605.31328.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Amplify Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
2605.31328.tldr: It is shown that rewarding narrow, overtly misaligned behavior produces substantially higher general-domain misalignment than sample-matched SFT, and that EM from RL can be induced by reward signals that could plausibly arise naturally, such as unpopular aesthetic preferences or poor rhetorical appeals.

2606.06667.title: The Piggyback Hypothesis of Generalization: Explaining and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment
2606.06667.tldr: It is shown that subtle perturbations to the prefix (tokens preceding all user queries), or patching the prefix representations with those from the unfinetuned model, can restore alignment without changing the user query, supporting the Piggyback Hypothesis.

2605.26772.title: Beyond a Single Direction: Chain-of-Thought Disrupts Simple Steering of Refusal
2605.26772.tldr: These findings indicate that refusal in LRMs is jointly encoded in residual stream activations and CoT, which makes LRM more robust against activation-level interventions alone, but exposes CoT to a possible alternative surface attack.

2604.03058.title: Verbalizing LLMs' assumptions to explain and control sycophancy
2604.03058.tldr: Verbalized Assumptions provides insight into LLM sycophancy, delusion, and other safety issues: in social sycophancy datasets,"seeking validation" is the most frequent bigram in LLMs'assumptions.

2606.12747.title: Prefill Awareness in Large Language Models
2606.12747.tldr: This work investigates whether frontier language models can distinguish between tampered and untampered assistant-side context, a capability the authors call prefill awareness, and constructs a binary preference benchmark across three prefill mechanisms, filtering for cases where models show consistent stances.

2602.13246.title: Global AI Bias Audit for Technical Governance
2602.13246.tldr: It is concluded that current AI alignment and training processes reinforce existing geoeconomic and geopolitical asymmetries, and the need for more inclusive data representation is urged to ensure AI serves as a truly global resource.

2604.13069.title: Geographic Blind Spots in AI Control Monitors: A Cross-National Audit of Claude Opus 4.6
2604.13069.tldr: This study provides the first cross-national, multi-domain audit of an AI control monitor's geographic knowledge gaps, with direct implications for the design of control protocols.

2505.18003.title: An Example Safety Case for Safeguards Against Misuse
2505.18003.tldr: This work describes an end-to-end argument (a"safety case") that misuse safeguards reduce the risk posed by an AI assistant to low levels, and describes how to tie these components together into a simple safety case.

2604.24618.title: Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research
2604.24618.tldr: The propensity of frontier models to sabotage or refuse to assist with safety research when deployed as AI research agents within a frontier AI company is evaluated, and evaluation awareness and a new form of situational awareness termed "prefill awareness", the capability to recognise that prior trajectory content was not self-generated are measured.

2412.17797.title: Observation Interference in Partially Observable Assistance Games
2412.17797.tldr: It is proved that sometimes an optimal assistant must take observation-interfering actions, even when the human is playing optimally, and even when there are otherwise-equivalent actions available that do not interfere with observations.

2407.18213.title: Scaling Trends in Language Model Robustness
2407.18213.tldr: It is found that while attack scaling outpaces adversarial training across all models studied, larger adversarially trained models might give defense the advantage in the long run.

2607.18344.title: FSDBN: Foreground-Aware EEG-Visual Alignment via Dynamic Brain Networks
2607.18344.tldr: FSDBN introduces Semantic-Consistent Saliency Alignment to separate semantically relevant foreground regions from background noise under joint saliency and semantic constraints and employs Semantic-Prior Dynamic Gating Foreground Fusion to adaptively regulate the contributions of foreground and background features.

2507.19672.title: Alignment and Safety in Large Language Models: Safety Mechanisms, Training Paradigms, and Emerging Challenges
2507.19672.tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of practical alignment techniques, training protocols, and empirical findings in LLM alignment, analyzing the development of alignment methods across diverse paradigms and characterizing the fundamental trade-offs between core alignment objectives.

2406.17312.title: Not All Preference Pairs Are Created Equal: A Recipe for Annotation-Efficient Iterative Preference Learning
2406.17312.tldr: This work proposes a comparative view to rank the implicit reward margins as predicted by DPO to select the response pairs that yield more benefits and shows that annotating those response pairs with small margins is generally better than large or random, under both single- and multi-iteration scenarios.
2406.17312.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2508.01916.title: Decomposing Representation Space into Interpretable Subspaces with Unsupervised Learning
2508.01916.tldr: The method, neighbor distance minimization (NDM), learns non-basis-aligned subspaces in an unsupervised manner and offers a new perspective on understanding model internals and building circuits.

2510.20129.title: SAID: Safety-Aware Intent Defense via Prefix Probing for Large Language Models
2510.20129.tldr: SAID first distills potentially obfuscated user inputs into concise core intents using the target model itself, then applies a validated safety prefix to probe each distilled intent and elicit the model's safety-aware response, enabling black-box-compatible defense without updating model parameters or modifying the decoding process.

2510.13434.title: $M^2PO$: Multi-Perspective Multi-Pair Preference Optimization for Machine Translation
2510.13434.tldr: Experiments show that $M^2PO$ enables a 9B model to outperform leading open-source baselines and achieve parity with proprietary models such as GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-Flash, demonstrating strong potential for efficient and high-fidelity LLM-based translation.

2503.13621.title: Superalignment with Dynamic Human Values
2503.13621.tldr: This work sketches a roadmap for a novel algorithmic framework that trains a superhuman reasoning model to decompose complex tasks into subtasks that are still amenable to human-level guidance.

2406.11039.title: Dynamic Normativity: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Value Alignment

2509.21401.title: JaiLIP: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models via Loss Guided Image Perturbation
2509.21401.tldr: JaiLIP is proposed, a jailbreaking attack in the image space that minimizes a joint objective combining the mean squared error (MSE) loss between clean and adversarial image with the model’s harmful-output loss and generates highly effective and imperceptible adversarial images.
2509.21401.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications

2603.28817.title: GUARD-SLM: Token Activation-Based Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks for Small Language Models
2603.28817.tldr: GUARD-SLM, a lightweight token activation-based method that operates in the representation space to filter malicious prompts during inference while preserving benign ones is proposed, highlighting robustness limitations across layers of language models and providing a practical direction for secure small language model deployment.

2609.12413.title: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration
2609.12413.tldr: A Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) that reframes jailbreak security around the full agentic execution pipeline, and develops unified taxonomies of attacks and defenses spanning user interaction, planning and reasoning, memory, tool use, and inter-agent communication, introduces a security--utility--efficiency evaluation framework.

2409.09603.title: Towards Data-Centric RLHF: Simple Metrics for Preference Dataset Comparison
2409.09603.tldr: This work systematically study preference datasets through three perspectives: scale, label noise, and information content and proposes specific metrics for each of these perspectives and uncover different axes of comparison for a better understanding of preference datasets.

2505.04844.title: Osiris: A Lightweight Open-Source Hallucination Detection System
2505.04844.tldr: A perturbed multi-hop QA dataset with induced hallucinations is introduced and supervised fine-tuning on the dataset achieves better recall with a 7B model than GPT-4o on the RAGTruth hallucination detection benchmark and offer competitive performance on precision and accuracy, all while using a fraction of the parameters.

2502.17601.title: Representation Engineering for Large-Language Models: Survey and Research Challenges
2502.17601.tldr: This work formalizes the goals and methods of representation engineering, and compares it with alternative approaches, such as mechanistic interpretability, prompt-engineering and fine-tuning, to build predictable, dynamic, safe and personalizable LLMs.

2607.03968.title: Refused in Chat, Written in Code: Workflow-Level Jailbreak Construction in IDE Coding Agents
2607.03968.tldr: These results show that conversational refusal benchmarks can substantially overstate the safety of deployed coding agents and motivate defenses that reason about safety across multi-turn IDE workflows and their generated artifacts, not only individual chat turns.

2401.12873.title: Improving Machine Translation with Human Feedback: An Exploration of Quality Estimation as a Reward Model
2401.12873.tldr: This work identifies the overoptimization problem during QE-based feedback training, manifested as an increase in reward while translation quality declines, and argues that the vulnerability of the QE model might lead to high rewards for incorrect translations, resulting in overoptimization and error propagation.
2401.12873.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.18532.title: CuDIP: Enhancing Theorem Proving in LLMs via Curriculum Learning-based Direct Preference Optimization
2502.18532.tldr: This paper proposes a method for constructing preference data which utilizes LLMs and existing theorem proving data to enhance the diversity of the preference data while reducing the reliance on human preference annotations and integrates this preference data construction method with curriculum learning to iteratively fine-tune the theorem proving model through DPO.

2402.04229.title: MusicRL: Aligning Music Generation to Human Preferences
2402.04229.tldr: This work proposes MusicRL, the first music generation system finetuned from human feedback, and trains MusicRL-U, the first text-to-music model that incorporates human feedback at scale, and trains MusicRL-R, the first text-to-music model that incorporates human feedback at scale.

2409.01369.title: Imitating Language via Scalable Inverse Reinforcement Learning
2409.01369.tldr: This work reformulating inverse soft-Q-learning as a temporal difference regularized extension of MLE creates a principled connection between MLE and IRL and allows trading off added complexity with increased performance and diversity of generations in the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) setting.

2606.20717.title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
2606.20717.tldr: This paper proposes MIRAGE, a novel visual indirect prompt injection framework for targeted next-action hijacking that leverages diffusion models to generate perceptually benign adversarial images strictly confined to the attacker-controlled boundaries permitted by the trusted service provider.

2512.06387.title: Beyond Model Jailbreak: Systematic Dissection of the "Ten DeadlySins" in Embodied Intelligence
2512.06387.tldr: The first holistic security analysis of the Unitree Go2 platform is conducted and ten cross layer vulnerabilities the "Ten Sins of Embodied AI Security" are uncovered.

2606.26620.title: Discovering Millions of Interpretable Features with Sparse Autoencoders
2606.26620.tldr: This work introduces Qwen3-Instruct SAE, a comprehensive suite of SAEs trained on the Qwen3 instruction-tuned model family, covering Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B, and systematically evaluates these SAEs using both activation-level reconstruction metrics and model-level recovery metrics, revealing distinct sparsity--fidelity trade-offs across layers and components.

2601.15698.title: Beyond Visual Safety: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models for Harmful Image Generation via Semantic-Agnostic Inputs
2601.15698.tldr: Beyond Visual Safety (BVS) is proposed, a novel image-text pair jailbreaking framework specifically designed to probe the visual safety boundaries of MLLMs, exposing critical vulnerabilities in the visual safety alignment of current MLLMs.

2403.18341.title: IterAlign: Iterative Constitutional Alignment of Large Language Models
2403.18341.tldr: A data-driven constitution discovery and self-alignment framework called IterAlign is proposed, which improves truthfulness, helpfulness, harmlessness and honesty, improving the LLM alignment by up to 13.5% in harmlessness.
2403.18341.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.20709.title: Unlearning through Knowledge Overwriting: Reversible Federated Unlearning via Selective Sparse Adapter
2502.20709.tldr: A method named FUSED is proposed, which first identifies critical layers by analyzing each layer’s sensitivity to knowledge and constructs sparse unlearning adapters for sensitive ones, which enables FUSED to mitigate the effects of indiscriminate unlearning.

2501.00192.title: MLLM-as-a-Judge for Image Safety without Human Labeling
2501.00192.tldr: A MLLM-based method includes objectifying safety rules, assessing the relevance between rules and images, making quick judgments based on debiased token probabilities with logically complete yet simplified precondition chains for safety rules, and conducting more in-depth reasoning with cascaded chain-of-thought processes if necessary.

2412.14167.title: VideoDPO: Omni-Preference Alignment for Video Diffusion Generation
2412.14167.tldr: This work designs a pipeline to automatically collect preference pair data based on the proposed OmniScore and discovers that re-weighting these pairs based on the score significantly impacts overall preference alignment.

2412.10493.title: AlignGuard: Scalable Safety Alignment for Text-to-Image Generation
2412.10493.tldr: AlignGuard is introduced, a method for safety alignment of T2I models that consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art on many benchmarks and establishes new practices for safety alignment in T2I networks.
2412.10493.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2502.01690.title: HuViDPO:Enhancing Video Generation through Direct Preference Optimization for Human-Centric Alignment
2502.01690.tldr: This work is the first to introduce the DPO strategy into the T2V tasks, and adopts a First-Frame-Conditioned strategy, leveraging the rich in formation from the first frame to guide the generation of subsequent frames, enhancing flexibility in video generation.

2504.08542.title: Discriminator-Free Direct Preference Optimization for Video Diffusion
2504.08542.tldr: This work proposes a discriminator-free video DPO framework that eliminates the need for costly synthetic video comparisons, provides unambiguous quality signals, and enables unlimited training data expansion through simple editing operations.

2604.15871.title: UniEditBench: A Unified and Cost-Effective Benchmark for Image and Video Editing via Distilled MLLMs
2604.15871.tldr: UniEditBench is presented, a unified benchmark for image and video editing that supports reconstruction-based and instruction-driven methods under a shared protocol and distill a high-capacity MLLM judge into lightweight 4B/8B evaluators that provide multi-dimensional scoring over structural fidelity, text alignment, background consistency, naturalness, and temporal-spatial consistency.

2502.00012.title: Lessons from complexity theory for AI governance
2502.00012.tldr: How efforts to govern AI are marked by deep uncertainty is examined and a set of complexity-compatible principles concerning the timing and structure of AI governance, and the risk thresholds that should trigger regulatory intervention are proposed.

2506.22183.title: A Different Approach to AI Safety: Proceedings from the Columbia Convening on Openness in Artificial Intelligence and AI Safety
2506.22183.tldr: It is found that openness -- understood as transparent weights, interoperable tooling, and public governance -- can enhance safety by enabling independent scrutiny, decentralized mitigation, and culturally plural oversight.

2505.13995.title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs
2505.13995.tldr: It is shown that sycophancy is widespread and harmful, and the need for design, evaluation, and accountability mechanisms to protect user well-being is underscored.

2402.01306.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
2402.01306.tldr: This work proposes a HALO that directly maximizes the utility of generations instead of maximizing the log-likelihood of preferences, and suggests that the best loss depends on the inductive biases most appropriate for a given setting, an oft-overlooked consideration.

2510.01395.title: Sycophantic AI Decreases Prosocial Intentions and Promotes Dependence
2510.01395.tldr: This work shows the pervasiveness and harmful impacts of sycophancy when people seek advice from AI, and suggests that people are drawn to AI that unquestioningly validate, even as that validation risks eroding their judgment and reducing their inclination toward prosocial behavior.

2510.26230.title: MPRU: Modular Projection-Redistribution Unlearning as Output Filter for Classification Pipelines
2510.26230.tldr: This work regards classification training as a sequential process where classes are learned sequentially, which enables modular and model-agnostic deployment as an output filter into existing classification pipelines with minimal alterations.

2405.14407.title: Dynamic Graph Unlearning: A General and Efficient Post-Processing Method via Gradient Transformation
2405.14407.tldr: This work study the dynamic graph unlearning for the first time and proposes an effective, efficient, general, and post-processing method to implement DGNN unlearning called Gradient Transformation that directly maps the unlearning request to the desired parameter update.

2407.15050.title: Arondight: Red Teaming Large Vision Language Models with Auto-generated Multi-modal Jailbreak Prompts
2407.15050.tldr: Arondight is a standardized red team framework tailored specifically for VLMs dedicated to resolving issues related to the absence of visual modality and inadequate diversity encountered when transitioning existing red teaming methodologies from LLMs to VLMs.

2604.07962.title: Is your algorithm unlearning or untraining?
2604.07962.tldr: This note argues that the term ``unlearning'' has been overloaded, with different research efforts spanning two distinct problem formulations, but without that distinction having been observed or acknowledged in the literature.

2502.00072.title: LLM Cyber Evaluations Don't Capture Real-World Risk
2502.00072.tldr: This work proposes a risk assessment framework for LLM cyber capabilities and applies it to a case study of language models used as cybersecurity assistants, suggesting that this particular use case presents only moderate risk due to limited operational advantages and impact potential.

2510.08604.title: LatentBreak: Jailbreaking Large Language Models through Latent Space Feedback
2510.08604.tldr: This work proposes LatentBreak, a white-box jailbreak attack that generates natural adversarial prompts with low perplexity capable of evading such defenses, and outperforming competing jailbreak algorithms against perplexity-based filters on multiple safety-aligned models.

2603.20570.title: Global Cybercrime Damages: A Baseline for Frontier AI Risk Assessment
2603.20570.tldr: This work establishes a more rigorous baseline for global cybercrime damages by surveying 27 existing estimates, critically evaluating their methodologies, and constructing a composite estimate from three independent sources, excluding harder-to-measure costs such as intellectual property theft and reputational damage.

2501.06645.title: FocalPO: Enhancing Preference Optimizing by Focusing on Correct Preference Rankings
2501.06645.tldr: FocalPO is introduced, a DPO variant that prioritizes enhancing the model's understanding of pairs that it can already rank correctly and achieves this by adding a modulating factor to dynamically scale DPO loss.
2501.06645.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.23270.title: Does Machine Unlearning Truly Remove Knowledge?
2505.23270.tldr: This work introduces a comprehensive auditing framework for unlearning evaluation, comprising three benchmark datasets, six unlearning algorithms, and five prompt-based auditing methods, and proposes a novel technique that leverages intermediate activation perturbations, addressing the limitations of auditing methods that rely solely on model inputs and outputs.

2503.11185.title: Bleeding Pathways: Vanishing Discriminability in LLM Hidden States Fuels Jailbreak Attacks
2503.11185.tldr: DEEPALIGN is introduced - an inherent defense framework that enhances the safety of LLMs by applying contrastive hidden-state steering at the midpoint of response generation, enabling continuous intrinsic toxicity detection and intervention throughout the generation process.
2503.11185.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2501.15453.title: Data-adaptive Safety Rules for Training Reward Models
2501.15453.tldr: This paper introduces a mathematical framework that utilizes the maximum discrepancy across paired responses and demonstrates theoretically that this approach maximizes the mutual information between the rule-based annotations and the underlying true preferences.

2503.20995.title: ENCORE: Entropy-guided Reward Composition for Multi-head Safety Reward Models
2503.20995.tldr: This paper proposes ENCORE, a simple entropy-guided method to compose multi-head rewards by penalizing rules with high rating entropy, which is completely training-free, generally applicable across datasets, and retains interpretability, making it a practical and effective approach for multi-attribute reward modeling.

2502.11367.title: Sparse Autoencoder Features for Classifications and Transferability
2502.11367.tldr: This work systematically analyze SAE for interpretable feature extraction from LLMs in safety-critical classification tasks, highlighting the significant impact of pooling strategies and binarization thresholds, showing that binarization offers an efficient alternative to traditional feature selection while maintaining or improving performance.
2502.11367.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2408.04522.title: Compromesso! Italian Many-Shot Jailbreaks Undermine the Safety of Large Language Models
2408.04522.tldr: This work investigates the effectiveness of many-shot jailbreaking, where models are prompted with unsafe demonstrations to induce unsafe behaviour, in Italian and identifies clear safety vulnerabilities in four families of open-weight LLMs.
2408.04522.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.20471.title: Probing AI Safety with Source Code
2506.20471.tldr: Given the rapid and widespread adoption of LLMs, CoDoT underscores the critical need to evaluate safety efforts from first principles, ensuring that safety and capabilities advance together.

2510.18454.title: Engagement Undermines Safety: How Stereotypes and Toxicity Shape Humor in Language Models
2510.18454.tldr: This work evaluates how funniness optimization in modern LLM pipelines couples with harmful content by jointly measuring humor, stereotypicality, and toxicity, and supplemented by analyzing incongruity signals through information-theoretic metrics.
2510.18454.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2402.01695.title: Language-Guided World Models: A Model-Based Approach to AI Control
2402.01695.tldr: Language-Guided World Models (LWMs) are developed, which can capture environment dynamics by reading language descriptions, allowing humans to simultaneously alter their behavior on multiple tasks with concise language feedback and enable agents to self-learn from texts originally written to instruct humans.

2408.13915.title: LLMs are Superior Feedback Providers: Bootstrapping Reasoning for Lie Detection with Self-Generated Feedback
2408.13915.tldr: This work proposes a bootstrapping framework that leverages self-generated feedback to enhance LLM reasoning capabilities for lie detection and investigates the application of the proposed framework for detecting betrayal and deception in Diplomacy games, and compares it with feedback from professional human players.

2405.18718.title: Efficient Model-agnostic Alignment via Bayesian Persuasion
2405.18718.tldr: An efficient method for aligning black-box large models using smaller models using smaller models is explored, introducing a model-agnostic and lightweight Bayesian Persuasion Alignment framework and an upper bound on the Advisor's regret is provided, confirming its effectiveness in learning the optimal signaling strategy.

2402.12907.title: Roadmap on Incentive Compatibility for AI Alignment and Governance in Sociotechnical Systems
2402.12907.tldr: This work proposes a new problem worth exploring: Incentive Compatibility Sociotechnical Alignment Problem (ICSAP), and discusses three classical game problems for achieving IC: mechanism design, contract theory, and Bayesian persuasion, in addressing the perspectives, potentials, and challenges of solving ICSAP.

2607.01567.title: Scaling Trends for Lie Detector Oversight in Preference Learning
2607.01567.tldr: Scale SOLiD to larger models and evaluate it in more diverse and realistic preference-learning settings find favorable scaling: undetected deception drops from 34% for 1B-parameter models to 14% for 405B-parameter models at a detector true positive rate of 99%, and expensive human labelers can be removed entirely from the fine-tuning phase without a statistically significant increase in deception.

2507.11544.title: The Safety Gap Toolkit: Evaluating Hidden Dangers of Open-Source Models
2507.11544.tldr: The Safety Gap Toolkit is an evaluation framework for common open-source models and as a motivation for developing and testing tamper-resistant safeguards and is open-source to estimate the safety gap for state-of-the-art open-weight models.

2607.28607.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values

2412.02159.title: Jailbreak Defense in a Narrow Domain: Limitations of Existing Methods and a New Transcript-Classifier Approach
2412.02159.tldr: This paper develops a transcript-classifier defense which outperforms the baseline defenses the authors test but still fails in some circumstances, which highlights the difficulty of jailbreak-defense even in a narrow domain.

2409.15268.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking
2409.15268.tldr: It is found that LLM-judges have powerful implicit biases, prioritizing style over factuality and safety, and the supervised fine-tuning stage of post-training, and not the PO stage, has the greatest impact on alignment, with data scaling and prompt diversity as the driving factors.

2605.17986.title: LivePI: More Realistic Benchmarking of Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
2605.17986.tldr: LivePI (Live Prompt Injection), a structured benchmark for IPI risk in a production-like but test-controlled environment, is introduced and a two-layer defense consisting of prompt-level filtering and pre-execution tool-call authorization is evaluated.

2510.14207.title: Echoes of Human Malice in Agents: Benchmarking LLMs for Multi-Turn Online Harassment Attacks
2510.14207.tldr: The findings show that multi-turn and theory-grounded attacks not only succeed at high rates but also mimic human-like harassment dynamics, motivating the development of robust safety guardrails to ultimately keep online platforms safe and responsible.

2408.07362.title: BadMerging: Backdoor Attacks Against Model Merging
2408.07362.tldr: This paper introduces BadMerging, the first backdoor attack specifically designed for Model Merging, and finds that MM, as a new learning paradigm, introduces unique challenges for existing backdoor attacks due to the merging process.
2408.07362.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2510.00938.title: Large Reasoning Models Learn Better Alignment from Flawed Thinking
2510.00938.tldr: RECAP (Robust Safety Alignment via Counter-Aligned Prefilling), a principled reinforcement learning (RL) method for post-training that explicitly teaches models to override flawed reasoning trajectories and reroute to safe and helpful responses, substantially improves safety and jailbreak robustness, reduces overrefusal, and preserves core reasoning capability.

2601.15895.title: Co-Constructing Alignment: A Participatory Approach to Situate AI Values
2601.15895.tldr: This work frames alignment as an interactional practice co-constructed during human AI interaction co-constructed during human AI interaction, and investigates how users understand and wish to contribute to this process through a participatory workshop that combines misalignment diaries with generative design activities.

2402.09179.title: Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs
2402.09179.tldr: This paper proposes the first instruction backdoor attacks against applications integrated with untrusted customized LLMs (e.g., GPTs), embedding the backdoor into the custom version of LLMs by designing prompts with backdoor instructions, outputting the attacker's desired result when inputs contain the pre-defined triggers.

2508.20848.title: JADES: A Universal Framework for Jailbreak Assessment via Decompositional Scoring
2508.20848.tldr: JADES (Jailbreak Assessment via Decompositional Scoring), a universal jailbreak evaluation framework that could deliver accurate, consistent, and interpretable evaluations, providing a reliable basis for measuring future jailbreak attacks.

2511.16278.title: "To Survive, I Must Defect": Jailbreaking LLMs via the Game-Theory Scenarios
2511.16278.tldr: Game-Theory Attack is proposed, an scalable black-box jailbreak framework that formalizes the attacker's interaction against safety-aligned LLMs as a finite-horizon, early-stoppable sequential stochastic game, and reparameterize the LLM's randomized outputs via quantal response.

2505.11586.title: The Ripple Effect: On Unforeseen Complications of Backdoor Attacks
2505.11586.tldr: This paper proposes a backdoor complication reduction method leveraging multi-task learning to mitigate complications without prior knowledge of downstream tasks and demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively reduce complications while maintaining the efficacy and consistency of backdoor attacks.

2603.11914.title: Understanding LLM Behavior When Encountering User-Supplied Harmful Content in Harmless Tasks
2603.11914.tldr: The results show that current LLMs, even the latest GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3-Pro, often fail to uphold human-aligned ethics by continuing to process harmful content in harmless tasks.

2512.18930.title: LouvreSAE: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable and Controllable Style Transfer
2512.18930.tldr: This paper introduces a training- and inference-light, interpretable method for representing and transferring artistic style, achieving or surpassing existing methods on style evaluations (VGG Style Loss and CLIP Score Style) while being 1.7-20x faster and, critically, interpretable.

2503.04474.title: Know Thy Judge: On the Robustness Meta-Evaluation of LLM Safety Judges
2503.04474.tldr: These findings reveal gaps in commonly used meta-evaluation benchmarks and weaknesses in the robustness of current LLM judges, indicating that low attack success under certain judges could create a false sense of security.

2409.12741.title: Fine Tuning Large Language Models for Medicine: The Role and Importance of Direct Preference Optimization
2409.12741.tldr: It is found that SFT alone is sufficient for Classification with text data, whereas DPO improves performance for the more complex tasks of Clinical Reasoning, Summarization and Clinical Triage.

2501.02531.title: Towards New Benchmark for AI Alignment & Sentiment Analysis in Socially Important Issues: A Comparative Study of Human and LLMs in the Context of AGI
2501.02531.tldr: The Societal AI Alignment and Sentiment Benchmark (SAAS-AI), which leverages multidimensional prompts and empirically validated societal value frameworks to evaluate language model outputs across temporal, model, and multilingual axes, is introduced to guide policymakers and AI agencies.

2502.06852.title: EAP-GP: Mitigating Saturation Effect in Gradient-based Automated Circuit Identification
2502.06852.tldr: Edge Attribution Patching with GradPath (EAP-GP), EAP-GP introduces an integration path, starting from the input and adaptively following the direction of the difference between the gradients of corrupted and clean inputs to avoid the saturated region, which enhances attribution reliability and improves the faithfulness of circuit identification.

2412.05095.title: SoPo: Text-to-Motion Generation Using Semi-Online Preference Optimization
2412.05095.tldr: This work theoretically investigate the DPO under both online and offline settings, and reveal their respective limitation: overfitting in offline DPO, and biased sampling in online DPO.

2509.13755.title: Scrub It Out! Erasing Sensitive Memorization in Code Language Models via Machine Unlearning
2509.13755.tldr: This paper conducts a pioneering investigation into erasing sensitive memorization in CLMs through machine unlearning—a post-hoc modification method that removes specific information from trained models without requiring full retraining.
2509.13755.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering

2407.16686.title: Can Large Language Models Automatically Jailbreak GPT-4V?
2407.16686.tldr: An effective search method that incorporates early stopping to minimize optimization time and token expenditure is presented and sheds light on strengthening GPT-4V security, underscoring the potential for LLMs to be exploited in compromising GPT-4V integrity.

2604.09378.title: BadSkill: Backdoor Attacks on Agent Skills via Model-in-Skill Poisoning
2604.09378.tldr: This work presents BadSkill, a backdoor attack formulation that targets a seemingly benign skill whose embedded model is backdoor-fine-tuned to activate a hidden payload only when routine skill parameters satisfy attacker-chosen semantic trigger combinations.

2404.12938.title: MAiDE-up: Multilingual Deception Detection of GPT-generated Hotel Reviews
2404.12938.tldr: This paper compile and make publicly available the MAiDE-up dataset, consisting of 10,000 real and 10,000 AI-generated fake hotel reviews, balanced across ten languages, and explores the effectiveness of several models for deception detection in hotel reviews across three main dimensions: sentiment, location, and language.

2604.25921.title: One Word at a Time: Incremental Completion Decomposition Breaks LLM Safety

2401.06121.title: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
2401.06121.tldr: To address this challenge, TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning is presented, as a benchmark aimed at helping deepen the understanding of unlearning, and a suite of metrics that work together to provide a holistic picture of unlearning efficacy are compiled.

2510.22014.title: Toward Understanding the Transferability of Adversarial Suffixes in Large Language Models
2510.22014.tldr: Three statistical properties are identified that strongly correlate with transfer success across numerous experimental settings and lead to a more fine-grained understanding of transferability, which is used in interventional experiments to showcase how the statistical analysis can translate into practical improvements in attack success.

2604.25167.title: From Insight to Action: A Novel Framework for Interpretability-Guided Data Selection in Large Language Models
2604.25167.tldr: Interpretability-Guided Data Selection (IGDS), a framework that first identifies causal task features through frequency recall and interventional filtering, then selects ``Feature-Resonant Data'' that maximally activates task features for fine-tuning, validating the core hypothesis.
2604.25167.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.22624.title: SPARK: Synergistic Policy And Reward Co-Evolving Framework
2509.22624.tldr: The Synergistic Policy And Reward Co-Evolving Framework (SPARK), an efficient, on-policy, and stable method that builds on RLVR, is introduced, an efficient, on-policy, and stable method that eliminates the need for a separate reward model and costly human preference data.

2407.02446.title: Predicting vs. Acting: A Trade-off Between World Modeling & Agent Modeling
2407.02446.tldr: This work studies the trade-off of probability on sets of anchor spans that co-occur across multiple generations for the same prompt, serving as textual scaffolding but also limiting a model's ability to generate documents that do not include these spans.

2408.02205.title: Swiss Cheese Model for AI Safety: A Taxonomy and Reference Architecture for Multi-Layered Guardrails of Foundation Model Based Agents
2408.02205.tldr: A comprehensive taxonomy of runtime guardrails for FM-based agents is presented and a reference architecture for designing multi-layered runtime guardrails for FM-based agents is proposed, which includes three dimensions: quality attributes, pipelines, and artifacts.

2601.22773.title: A Structured Approach to Safety Case Construction for AI Systems
2601.22773.tldr: This study examines how safety cases are currently constructed for AI systems and why classical approaches fail to capture these dynamics, and proposes a reusable safety-case template, each of which follows a predefined structure of claims, arguments, and evidence tailored for AI systems.

2405.07863.title: RLHF Workflow: From Reward Modeling to Online RLHF
2405.07863.tldr: This technical report presents the workflow of Online Iterative Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and shows that supervised fine-tuning and iterative RLHF can obtain state-of-the-art performance with fully open-source datasets.

2402.07314.title: Online Iterative Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with General Preference Model
2402.07314.tldr: This work considers a standard mathematical formulation, the reverse-KL regularized minimax game between two LLMs for RLHF under general preference oracle, and proposes sample-efficient algorithms for both the offline learning from a pre-collected preference dataset and online learning where the preference oracle is queried along the way of training.

2402.13055.title: Identifying Semantic Induction Heads to Understand In-Context Learning
2402.13055.tldr: A detailed analysis of the operations of attention heads is conducted and it is found that certain attention heads exhibit a pattern where, when attending to head tokens, they recall tail tokens and increase the output logits of those tail tokens.
2402.13055.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.09443.title: LLMs Cannot Reliably Judge (Yet?): A Comprehensive Assessment on the Robustness of LLM-as-a-Judge
2506.09443.tldr: This study introduces RobustJudge, a fully automated and modularly extensible framework designed to systematically evaluate the robustness of LLM-as-a-Judge across task datasets, judge prompt templates, judge models, attacks, and defenses.

2504.15674.title: TrojanDam: Detection-Free Backdoor Defense in Federated Learning through Proactive Model Robustification utilizing OOD Data
2504.15674.tldr: This work reveals that the successful launching of backdoor attacks in FL stems from the lack of conflict between malicious and benign updates on redundant neurons of ML models, and proposes a novel backdoor defense mechanism, TrojanDam, which has the FL server continuously inject fresh OOD mappings into the global model to activate redundant neurons, canceling the effect of backdoor updates during aggregation.

2601.17344.title: The Shadow Self: Intrinsic Value Misalignment in Large Language Model Agents
2601.17344.tldr: This work formalizes the Loss-of-Control risk and identifies the previously underexamined Intrinsic Value Misalignment (Intrinsic VM), and introduces IMPRESS (Intrinsic Value Misalignment Probes in REalistic Scenario Set), a scenario-driven framework for systematically assessing this risk.

2405.19262.title: Weak-to-Strong Search: Align Large Language Models via Searching over Small Language Models
2405.19262.tldr: This work introduces $\textit{weak-to-strong search}$, framing the alignment of a large language model as a test-time greedy search to maximize the log-probability difference between small tuned and untuned models while sampling from the frozen large model.

2608.10327.title: Toward a Theory of Value in AI Alignment
2608.10327.tldr: In making AI value alignments philosophical commitments explicit, this work seeks to bring great specificity and under explored perspectives in the debate on whether and how AI can address human values.

2409.06926.title: Minimum Viable Ethics: From Institutionalizing Industry AI Governance to Product Impact
2409.06926.tldr: It is found that AI ethics professionals are highly agile and opportunistic, as they attempt to create standardized and reusable processes and tools in a corporate environment in which they have little traditional power.

2503.02846.title: Mask-DPO: Generalizable Fine-grained Factuality Alignment of LLMs
2503.02846.tldr: A fine-grained factuality alignment method based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), called Mask-DPO, which can significantly improve the factuality of LLMs responses to questions from both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets, although these questions and their corresponding topics are unseen during training.

2407.04693.title: ANAH-v2: Scaling Analytical Hallucination Annotation of Large Language Models
2407.04693.tldr: This paper introduces an iterative self-training framework that simultaneously and progressively scales up the hallucination annotation dataset and improves the accuracy of the hallucination annotator.

2402.13764.title: CriticEval: Evaluating Large Language Model as Critic
2402.13764.tldr: CriticEval, a novel benchmark designed to comprehensively and reliably evaluate critique ability of LLMs, is introduced and experimental results demonstrate the promising potential of open-source LLMs, the effectiveness of critique datasets and several intriguing relationships between the critique ability and some critical factors, including task types, response qualities and critique dimensions.

2508.06963.title: MASteer: Multi-Agent Adaptive Steer Strategy for End-to-End LLM Trustworthiness Repair
2508.06963.tldr: MASteer is proposed, the first end-to-end framework for trustworthiness repair in LLMs based on representation engineering, which demonstrates strong robustness, generalization, and practical value for scalable, efficient trustworthiness repair.

2404.02062.title: Digital Forgetting in Large Language Models: A Survey of Unlearning Methods
2404.02062.tldr: A taxonomy of unlearning methods is proposed based on the reach and depth of the modifications done on the models, and the effectiveness of machine unlearning methods for LLMs proposed so far are discussed and compared, and their evaluation is surveyed.

2507.04771.title: Efficient Unlearning with Privacy Guarantees
2507.04771.tldr: This paper presents efficient unlearning with privacy guarantees (EUPG), a novel machine unlearning framework that offers formal privacy guarantees to individuals whose data are being unlearned and demonstrates utility and forgetting effectiveness comparable to those of exact unlearning methods, while significantly reducing computational and storage costs.

2504.13774.title: DP2Unlearning: An Efficient and Guaranteed Unlearning Framework for LLMs
2504.13774.tldr: DP2Unlearning is presented, a novel LLM unlearning framework that offers formal forgetting guarantees at a significantly lower cost than retraining from scratch on the data to be retained and outperforms approximate unlearning methods at both preserving the utility of the model post-unlearning and effectively forgetting the targeted information.

2311.09410.title: When Large Language Models contradict humans? Large Language Models' Sycophantic Behaviour
2311.09410.tldr: This investigation demonstrates that LLMs have sycophantic tendencies when answering queries that involve subjective opinions and statements that should elicit a contrary response based on facts, and does not follow the users' hints by demonstrating confidence in generating the correct answers when faced with math tasks or queries with an objective answer.

2502.13640.title: Qorgau: Evaluating LLM Safety in Kazakh-Russian Bilingual Contexts
2502.13640.tldr: Experiments with both multilingual and language-specific LLMs reveal notable differences in safety performance, emphasizing the need for tailored, region-specific datasets to ensure the responsible and safe deployment of LLMs in countries like Kazakhstan.

2508.05011.title: Towards Hallucination-Free Music: A Reinforcement Learning Preference Optimization Framework for Reliable Song Generation
2508.05011.tldr: Comprehensive objective and subjective evaluations confirm that the proposed novel RL framework's methods effectively suppress hallucinations while preserving musical quality, and unlocks potential for music style adherence and musicality enhancement, opening new avenues for future generative song research.

2502.01615.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Like Internally
2502.01615.tldr: It is shown that next-word probabilities derived from internal layers of larger LMs align with human sentence processing data as well as, or better than, those from smaller LMs, suggesting that the cognitive plausibility of larger LMs has been underestimated.
2502.01615.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.08200.title: A Head to Predict and a Head to Question: Pre-trained Uncertainty Quantification Heads for Hallucination Detection in LLM Outputs
2505.08200.tldr: This work introduces pre-trained UQ heads: supervised auxiliary modules for LLMs that substantially enhance their ability to capture uncertainty compared to unsupervised UQ methods, and demonstrates strong generalization to languages they were not explicitly trained on.
2505.08200.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2308.13387.title: Do-Not-Answer: A Dataset for Evaluating Safeguards in LLMs
2308.13387.tldr: The first open-source dataset to evaluate safeguards in LLMs is collected, and several BERT-like classifiers are trained that can achieve results that are comparable with GPT-4 on automatic safety evaluation.

2603.01291.title: JailNewsBench: Multi-Lingual and Regional Benchmark for Fake News Generation under Jailbreak Attacks
2603.01291.tldr: This work proposes JailNewsBench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness against jailbreak-induced fake news generation, and shows that coverage of fake news in existing safety datasets is limited and less well defended than major categories such as toxicity and social bias.

2510.17006.title: Online Learning Defense against Iterative Jailbreak Attacks via Prompt Optimization
2510.17006.tldr: A reinforcement learning-based approach that optimizes prompts to ensure appropriate responses for harmless tasks while explicitly rejecting harmful prompts is introduced, and to curb overfitting to the narrow band of partial input rewrites explored during an attack, past-Direction Gradient Damping is introduced.

2402.05467.title: Rapid Optimization for Jailbreaking LLMs via Subconscious Exploitation and Echopraxia
2402.05467.tldr: RIPPLE (Rapid Optimization via Subconscious Exploitation and Echopraxia), a novel optimization-based method inspired by two psychological concepts: subconsciousness and echopraxia, which describe the processes of the mind that occur without conscious awareness and the involuntary mimicry of actions, respectively are introduced.

2502.18810.title: Holistic Audit Dataset Generation for LLM Unlearning via Knowledge Graph Traversal and Redundancy Removal
2502.18810.tldr: HANKER is proposed, an automated framework for holistic audit dataset generation leveraging knowledge graphs to achieve fine-grained coverage and eliminate redundant knowledge in large language models.

2403.02437.title: A Survey on Federated Unlearning: Challenges and Opportunities
2403.02437.tldr: A deep look at the federated unlearning literature is taken, with the goal of identifying research trends and challenges in this emerging field, and pinpoint the unique complexities of federated unlearning, highlighting limitations on directly applying centralized unlearning methods.

2506.12618.title: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
2506.12618.tldr: A novel meta-evaluation benchmark focused specifically on assessing the faithfulness and robustness of evaluation metrics themselves is proposed, and a clear, community-driven pathway toward rigorous development in LLM unlearning research is established.

2401.15897.title: Red-Teaming for Generative AI: Silver Bullet or Security Theater?
2401.15897.tldr: It is argued that while red-teaming may be a valuable big-tent idea for characterizing GenAI harm mitigations, and that industry may effectively apply red-teaming and other strategies behind closed doors to safeguard AI, gestures towards red-teaming as a panacea for every possible risk verge on security theater.
2401.15897.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2402.05133.title: Personalized Language Modeling from Personalized Human Feedback
2402.05133.tldr: Experimental results show that personalized LLMs trained using P-RLHF generate responses that are more closely aligned with individual user preferences, outperforming vanilla, non-personalized RLHF and prompting-based personalization approaches across different tasks.

2410.09724.title: Taming Overconfidence in LLMs: Reward Calibration in RLHF
2410.09724.tldr: This study reveals that RLHF tends to lead models to express verbalized overconfidence in their own responses, and proposes two PPO variants: PPO-M: PPO with Calibrated Reward Modeling and PPO-C: PPO with Calibrated Reward Calculation.

2410.14872.title: How to Evaluate Reward Models for RLHF
2410.14872.tldr: Preference Proxy Evaluations (PPE), the first reward model benchmark explicitly linked to post-RLHF real-world human preference performance, is introduced, which is open-source for public use and further development.

2401.16335.title: Iterative Data Smoothing: Mitigating Reward Overfitting and Overoptimization in RLHF
2401.16335.tldr: The core idea is that during each training epoch, the model is updated with the data, but also update the date using the model, replacing hard labels with soft labels, and the empirical findings highlight the superior performance of this approach over the traditional methods.

2410.17055.title: Optimal Design for Reward Modeling in RLHF
2410.17055.tldr: This paper frames the selection of an effective dataset as a simple regret minimization task, using a linear contextual dueling bandit method, and proposes an offline framework for solving this problem, the first theoretical contribution in this area to provide an offline approach as well as worst-case guarantees.

2605.04266.title: Explaining and Preventing Alignment Collapse in Iterative RLHF
2605.04266.tldr: Foresighted policy optimization (FPO) is proposed, a mechanism-design intervention that restores the missing steering term by regularizing the policy's parameter-steering effect on RM updates and prevents alignment collapse on both controlled environments and an LLM alignment pipeline using Llama-3.2-1B.

2604.22134.title: SHAPE: Unifying Safety, Helpfulness and Pedagogy for Educational LLMs
2604.22134.tldr: A graph-augmented tutoring pipeline that infers prerequisite concepts from queries, identifies mastery gaps, and routes generation between instructing and problem-solving via explicit gating is proposed, which yields significantly improved safety under two pedagogical jailbreak settings, while maintaining near-ceiling helpfulness under the same evaluation protocol.
2604.22134.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2411.15382.title: On the Impact of Fine-Tuning on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2411.15382.tldr: The study shows the impact of fine-tuning on LLM reasoning capabilities, where the faithfulness of CoT reasoning, on average across four datasets, decreases, highlighting potential shifts in internal mechanisms of the LLMs resulting from fine-tuning processes.
2411.15382.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2402.10688.title: Towards Uncovering How Large Language Model Works: An Explainability Perspective
2402.10688.tldr: This paper uncovers the mechanisms underlying LLM functionality through the lens of explainability and explores how the insights gained can enhance LLM performance through model editing, improve efficiency through pruning, and better align with human values.

2506.19248.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
2506.19248.tldr: HedgeTune is introduced, an efficient algorithm to find the optimal inference-time parameter that mitigates reward hacking and achieves superior reward-distortion tradeoffs on math, reasoning, and human-preference setups.

2404.18870.title: More RLHF, More Trust? On The Impact of Preference Alignment On Trustworthiness
2404.18870.tldr: This study investigates how models aligned with general-purpose preference data perform across five trustworthiness verticals: toxicity, stereotypical bias, machine ethics, truthfulness, and privacy, and proposes to adapt efficient influence function based data attribution methods to the RLHF setting to better understand the influence of fine-tuning data on individual trustworthiness benchmarks.

2505.16004.title: Evaluating Adversarial Robustness of Concept Representations in Sparse Autoencoders
2505.16004.tldr: It is argued that robustness must be a fundamental consideration for concept representations, reflecting the fidelity of concept labeling, and developed a comprehensive evaluation framework featuring realistic scenarios in which adversarial perturbations are crafted to manipulate SAE representations.
2505.16004.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.00418.title: Generalizing Trust: Weak-to-Strong Trustworthiness in Language Models
