2501.18887.title: Towards Unified Attribution in Explainable AI, Data-Centric AI, and Mechanistic Interpretability
2501.18887.tldr: It is argued that feature, data, and component attribution methods share fundamental similarities, and a unified view of them benefits both interpretability and broader AI research.

2606.12360.title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
2606.12360.tldr: A data-centric post-training pipeline that uses interpretability protocols to develop statistical hypotheses for the latent concepts separating preferred from dispreferred generations is introduced, suggesting that interpretability can turn post-training from optimizing opaque proxy rewards into a process of auditing and sculpting the learning signal itself.

2609.19101.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
2609.19101.tldr: This work finds that simple difference of means vectors coherently represent reward hacking in Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Qwen 3.8 Max, and provides evidence that simple, white-box methods can be used to scalably study and monitor reward hacking behaviors in frontier open source models.

2604.09665.title: Deliberative Alignment is Deep, but Uncertainty Remains: Inference time safety improvement in reasoning via attribution of unsafe behavior to base model
2604.09665.tldr: This work studies the impact of deliberative alignment in language models and proposes a BoN sampling method that attributes the unsafe behavior back to the base LLMs in the latent space, thereby down-ranking unsafe responses to gain a meaningful improvement in model safety across multiple safety benchmarks with minimal loss in utility.

2403.03185.title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking
2403.03185.tldr: This work introduces a definition of reward hacking based on the correlation between proxy and true rewards for states and actions seen by a"reference policy" that breaks down under optimization and shows theoretically that regularization to the reference policy can effectively prevent reward hacking.

2409.17407.title: Post-hoc Reward Calibration: A Case Study on Length Bias
2409.17407.tldr: This paper proposes an intuitive approach to estimate the bias term and, thus, remove it to approximate the underlying true reward, and extends the approach to a more general and robust form with the Locally Weighted Regression.

2401.15241.title: Unlearning Traces the Influential Training Data of Language Models
2401.15241.tldr: This paper presents UnTrac: unlearning traces the influence of a training dataset on the model's performance, and proposes a more scalable approach, UnTrac-Inv, which unlearns a test dataset and evaluates the unlearned model on training datasets.
2401.15241.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.05294.title: Truthful or Fabricated? Using Causal Attribution to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Explanations
2504.05294.tldr: This work proposes enriching the RM's input with a causal attribution of the prediction, allowing the RM to detect discrepancies between the generated self-explanation and the model's decision process, and shows that this approach reduces the tendency of the LLM to generate misleading explanations.

2507.09016.title: Enhancing RLHF with Human Gaze Modeling
2507.09016.tldr: The experiments show that gaze-informed RLHF achieves faster convergence while maintaining or slightly improving performance, thus, reducing computational costs during policy optimization, pointing to a promising direction for improving RLHF efficiency.
2507.09016.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2507.05619.title: Detecting Proxy Gaming in RL and LLM Alignment via Evaluator Stress Tests
2507.05619.tldr: The Evaluator Stress Test (EST) is introduced, an invariance-based framework that detects proxy gaming by separating exploitable sensitivity from content-driven improvements using controlled perturbations with semantic validity audits.
2507.05619.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2609.08798.title: Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation
2609.08798.tldr: On-Policy Reverse Distillation (OPRD), which evaluates the teacher's policy shift relative to its reference policy on student rollouts and amplifies the component of the student's verifier-driven policy gradient along that direction, and effectively combines verifier-driven policy optimization with teacher guidance regardless of capacity ordering.

2601.23045.title: The Hot Mess of AI: How Does Misalignment Scale With Model Intelligence and Task Complexity?
2601.23045.tldr: A future where AIs sometimes cause industrial accidents, but are less likely to exhibit consistent pursuit of a misaligned goal is suggested, suggesting a future where AIs sometimes cause industrial accidents, but are less likely to exhibit consistent pursuit of a misaligned goal.

2410.16090.title: Analysing the Residual Stream of Language Models Under Knowledge Conflicts
2410.16090.tldr: This work finds that LLMs can internally register the signal of knowledge conflict in the residual stream, which can be accurately detected by probing the intermediate model activations, and finds that the residual stream shows significantly different patterns when the model relies on contextual knowledge versus parametric knowledge to resolve conflicts.

2608.29464.title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
2608.29464.tldr: The results suggest that CoT monitoring may be less reliable when preference information arrives through tools or must be inferred from raw artifacts, within the single-call, prefilled-tool setting tested here.

2404.13588.title: Machine Unlearning via Null Space Calibration
2404.13588.tldr: This paper addresses this critical yet under-explored issue by introducing machine Unlearning via Null Space Calibration (UNSC), which can accurately unlearn target samples without over-unlearning by confining the unlearning process to a specified null space tailored to the remaining samples.
2404.13588.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

2405.15662.title: Class Machine Unlearning for Complex Data via Concepts Inference and Data Poisoning
2405.15662.tldr: The definition of Concept is applied, rather than an image feature or a token of text data, to represent the semantic information of unlearning class, leading to a complete erasing of the impact of a class.

2410.15267.title: When Machine Unlearning Meets Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Keep Secret or Forget Knowledge?
2410.15267.tldr: This work proposes a lightweight behavioral unlearning framework based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology that is particularly effective for closed-source LLMs, where existing unlearning methods often fail.
2410.15267.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2403.15779.title: The Frontier of Data Erasure: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
2403.15779.tldr: This paper reviews the latest in machine unlearning for LLMs, introducing methods for the targeted forgetting of information to address privacy, ethical, and legal challenges without necessitating full model retraining.

2405.20776.title: Federated Learning with Blockchain-Enhanced Machine Unlearning: A Trustworthy Approach
2405.20776.tldr: An innovative framework that melds blockchain with federated learning, ensuring an immutable record of unlearning requests and actions is introduced, which not only bolsters the trustworthiness and integrity of the federated learning model but also adeptly addresses efficiency and security challenges typical in IoT environments.

2406.10954.title: Towards Efficient Target-Level Machine Unlearning Based on Essential Graph
2406.10954.tldr: A more effective and efficient unlearning scheme that focuses on removing partial targets from the model, which is named "target unlearning", which is a simple but effective solution to remove information about the target that needs to be forgotten.

2406.10953.title: Really Unlearned? Verifying Machine Unlearning via Influential Sample Pairs
2406.10953.tldr: This paper proposes a formal verification scheme, IndirectVerify, to determine whether unlearning requests have been successfully executed, and designs influential sample pairs: one referred to as trigger samples and the other as reaction samples, to generate those influential sample pairs.
2406.10953.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2406.10951.title: Don't Forget Too Much: Towards Machine Unlearning on Feature Level
2406.10951.tldr: This work proposes a refined granularity unlearning scheme referred to as “feature unlearning”, which involves an adversarial learning approach to automatically remove effects about features from instances based on filtered instances and the fine-tuning process.
2406.10951.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2406.12516.title: Update Selective Parameters: Federated Machine Unlearning Based on Model Explanation
2406.12516.tldr: This work proposes a more effective and efficient federated unlearning scheme based on the concept of model explanation, which selects the most influential channels within an already-trained model for the data that need to be unlearned and fine-tune only influential channels to remove the contribution made by those data.

2609.00790.title: RISA: Response Inspection and Selective Actions for Refusal Calibration in Large Language Models
2609.00790.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that RISA improves refusal reliability while largely preserving model utility, offering a practical solution for response-aware refusal calibration in LLMs.

2608.08027.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
2608.08027.tldr: Experiments show that BASIS maintains near-perfect injection detection while substantially reducing over-refusal on safe attack samples, especially under robust instruction templates.

2604.10299.title: Seeing No Evil: Blinding Large Vision-Language Models to Safety Instructions via Adversarial Attention Hijacking
2604.10299.tldr: Attention-Guided Visual Jailbreaking is proposed, which circumvents rather than overpowers safety alignment by directly manipulating attention patterns and introduces two simple auxiliary objectives: suppressing attention to alignment-relevant prefix tokens and anchoring generation on adversarial image features.
2604.10299.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.21718.title: When Harmless Words Harm: A New Threat to LLM Safety via Conceptual Triggers
2511.21718.tldr: This paper introduces MICM, a novel, model-agnostic jailbreak method that targets the aggregate value structure reflected in LLM responses, and reveals a critical vulnerability in commercial LLMs: their safety mechanisms remain susceptible to covert manipulation of underlying value alignment.

2608.05909.title: MMAligner: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models through Representation Calibration
2608.05909.tldr: Experiments show that MMAligner raises the average refusal rate on unsafe multimodal inputs to 99% with less than 2% utility degradation and minimal training data, substantially improving the safety-utility trade-off over existing baselines.

2406.19845.title: Virtual Context: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks with Special Token Injection
2406.19845.tldr: Comprehensive evaluations show that Virtual Context-assisted jailbreak attacks can improve the success rates of four widely used jailbreak methods by approximately 40% across various LLMs and recommends including this threat in red-teaming testing to comprehensively enhance LLM security.

2506.11253.title: Lifting Data-Tracing Machine Unlearning to Knowledge-Tracing for Foundation Models
2506.11253.tldr: This position paper proposes to lift data-tracing machine unlearning to knowledge-tracing for foundation models (FMs) and discusses the nontrivial challenges in the knowledge-tracing machine unlearning paradigm.

2405.16567.title: Automatic Jailbreaking of the Text-to-Image Generative AI Systems
2405.16567.tldr: This paper evaluates the safety of the commercial T2I generation systems, such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini, on copyright infringement with naive prompts, and proposes a stronger automated jailbreaking pipeline for T2I generation systems, which produces prompts that bypass their safety guards.

2601.15436.title: Not Your Typical Sycophant: The Elusive Nature of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
2601.15436.tldr: It is found that while most models exhibit significant sycophantic tendencies in the common setting, seven of the models exhibit ``moral remorse'', five of which significantly over-compensate for their sycophancy in case it explicitly harms a third party.

2607.27232.title: Sympathetic Framing: Evaluating AI Alignment across Sociodemographic Groups
2607.27232.tldr: This research offers the most comprehensive evaluation of LLMs' prehension of news framing to date, and finds that the correlation between AI and human evaluations varies across models, ranging from very high to medium, although there are statistically significant differences between groups.

2603.15448.title: The Social Sycophancy Scale: A psychometrically validated measure of sycophancy
2603.15448.tldr: The Social Sycophancy Scale gives researchers the means to study sycophancy rigorously, and confront a genuine design tension: the warmth and empathy the authors want from AI may be precisely what makes it sycophantic.

2409.20553.title: Maia-2: A Unified Model for Human-AI Alignment in Chess
2409.20553.tldr: Recognizing the complex, non-linear nature of human learning, this work introduces a skill-aware attention mechanism to dynamically integrate players' strengths with encoded chess positions, enabling the model to be sensitive to evolving player skill.

2510.03667.title: Invisible Saboteurs: Sycophantic LLMs Mislead Novices in Problem-Solving Tasks
2510.03667.tldr: Findings show that users of the high sycophancy chatbot were less likely to correct their misconceptions and spent more time over-relying on unhelpful LLM responses, leading them to significantly worse performance in the task.
2510.03667.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2410.01276.title: Deep Unlearn: Benchmarking Machine Unlearning for Image Classification
2410.01276.tldr: This paper investigates 18 state-of-the-art MU methods across various benchmark datasets and models, and shows that, with the proper hyperparameters, Masked Small Gradients (MSG) and Convolution Transpose (CT) consistently perform better in terms of model accuracy and run-time efficiency across different models, datasets, and initializations.
2410.01276.venue: European Symposium on Security and Privacy

2506.20037.title: Verifiable Unlearning on Edge
2506.20037.tldr: This work introduces a verification framework leveraging zero-knowledge proofs, specifically zk-SNARKs, to confirm data unlearning on personalized edge-device models without compromising privacy, and develops algorithms explicitly designed to facilitate unlearning operations that are compatible with efficient zk-SNARK proof generation, ensuring minimal computational and memory overhead suitable for constrained edge environments.

2512.00272.title: WARP: Weight Teleportation for Attack-Resilient Unlearning Protocols

2512.09953.title: ZK-APEX: Zero-Knowledge Approximate Personalized Unlearning with Executable Proofs
2512.09953.tldr: This work introduces ZK APEX, a zero-shot personalized unlearning method that operates directly on the personalized model without retraining, and shows the first practical framework for verifiable personalized unlearning on edge devices.

2504.07863.title: Robust Hallucination Detection in LLMs via Adaptive Token Selection
2504.07863.tldr: This work proposes HaMI, a novel approach that enables robust detection of hallucinations through adaptive selection and learning of critical tokens that are most indicative of hallucinations that significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

2509.23037.title: GuardNet: Graph-Attention Filtering for Jailbreak Defense in Large Language Models
2509.23037.tldr: Despite its structural complexity, GuardNet maintains acceptable latency and generalizes well in cross-domain evaluations, making it a practical and robust defense against jailbreak threats in real-world LLM deployments.

2603.22094.title: Principled Steering via Null-space Projection for Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
2603.22094.tldr: NullSteer constructs refusal directions within model activations through a linear transformation: it maintains zero perturbation within the benign subspace while dynamically inducing refusal along potentially harmful directions, thereby theoretically achieving safety enhancement without impairing the model's general capabilities.

2608.10985.title: PEAK: Precise and Persistent Concept Erasure via k-Sparse Autoencoders
2608.10985.tldr: This feature-guided optimization embeds concept erasure directly into diffusion parameters, eliminating the need for additional inference-time intervention and facilitating effective persistence against adversarial attacks.

2601.02978.title: Mechanistic Knobs in LLMs: Retrieving and Steering High-Order Semantic Features via Sparse Autoencoders
2601.02978.tldr: A Sparse Autoencoder-based framework for retrieving and steering semantically interpretable internal features associated with high-level linguistic behaviors, which suggests that LLMs internalize deeply integrated representations of high-order concepts, and provide a novel, robust mechanistic path for the regulation of complex AI behaviors.

2501.16663.title: Data Duplication: A Novel Multi-Purpose Attack Paradigm in Machine Unlearning
2501.16663.tldr: The findings reveal that the gold standard unlearning method, retraining from scratch, fails to effectively conduct unlearning under certain conditions; unlearning duplicated data can lead to significant model degradation in specific scenarios; and meticulously crafted duplicates can evade detection by de-duplication methods.

2512.16126.title: Dual-View Inference Attack: Machine Unlearning Amplifies Privacy Exposure
2512.16126.tldr: This work proposes DVIA, a Dual-View Inference Attack, which extracts membership information on retained data using black-box queries to both models and introduces the concept of privacy knowledge gain and demonstrates that the dual-view setting allows adversaries to obtain more information than querying either model alone, thereby amplifying privacy leakage.

2601.06938.title: Forgetting Similar Samples: Can Machine Unlearning Do it Better?
2601.06938.tldr: There is a notable gap between the expected and actual performance of most existing unlearning methods for image and language models, even for the retraining-from-scratch baseline.
2601.06938.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2606.16110.title: Auditing Machine Unlearning: A Systematic Research on Whether Models Truly Forget
2606.16110.tldr: This paper initiates a systematic investigation into whether existing unlearning algorithms can truly forget the designated data, and proposes the first practical and general-purpose auditing framework for machine unlearning, inspired by the concept of proof of ignorance.

2406.04076.title: Federated TrustChain: Blockchain-Enhanced LLM Training and Unlearning
2406.04076.tldr: This framework leverages blockchain technology to create a tamper-proof record of each model’s contributions and introduces an innovative unlearning function that seamlessly integrates with the federated learning mechanism.
2406.04076.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2604.00430.title: Secure Forgetting: A Framework for Privacy-Driven Unlearning in Large Language Model (LLM)-Based Agents
2604.00430.tldr: Experimental results show that the approach effectively enables agents to forget targeted knowledge while preserving performance on untargeted tasks, and prevents the adversary from inferring the forgotten knowledge.

2608.16353.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals
2608.16353.tldr: HalluTracer is introduced, a detection framework that reads and aggregates truthfulness evidence across every layer of the forward pass before the model emits any answer token, recasts hallucination detection from a layer-selection problem into a depth-aggregation problem governed by the geometric sparsity of the truthfulness signal.

2410.10120.title: Evaluating of Machine Unlearning: Robustness Verification Without Prior Modifications
2410.10120.tldr: This work proposes a novel robustness verification scheme, operating exclusively through model parameters, that avoids the need for any sample-level modifications prior to model training while supporting verification on a much larger set and maintaining robustness.

2411.03343.title: What Features in Prompts Jailbreak LLMs? Investigating the Mechanisms Behind Attacks
2411.03343.tldr: Interventions derived from non-linear probes produce larger and more reliable effects than those from linear probes, indicating that features linked to jailbreak success are encoded non-linearly in prompt representations.
2411.03343.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2605.11887.title: Qwen-Scope: Turning Sparse Features into Development Tools for Large Language Models
2605.11887.tldr: Qwen-Scope is introduced, an open-source suite of SAEs built on the Qwen model family, comprising 14 groups of SAEs across 7 model variants from the Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 series, and demonstrates that SAEs can serve not only as post-hoc analysis tools, but also as reusable representation-level interfaces for diagnosing, controlling, evaluating, and improving large language models.

2602.04649.title: Outcome Accuracy is Not Enough: Aligning the Reasoning Process of Reward Models
2602.04649.tldr: This work introduces Rationale Consistency, a fine-grained metric that quantifies the alignment between the model's reasoning process and human judgment that effectively reverses the decline in rationale consistency observed in outcome-only training.
2602.04649.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2507.14894.title: SASFT: Sparse Autoencoder-guided Supervised Finetuning to Mitigate Unexpected Code-Switching in LLMs
2507.14894.tldr: This paper provides an in-depth analysis of unexpected code-switching using sparse autoencoders and proposes SASFT, which teaches LLMs to maintain appropriate pre-activation values of specific language features during training, showing its effectiveness in addressing code-switching while preserving multilingual capabilities.

2412.06559.title: ProcessBench: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning
2412.06559.tldr: This paper introduces ProcessBench for measuring the ability to identify erroneous steps in mathematical reasoning, and draws two main observations: existing PRMs typically fail to generalize to more challenging math problems beyond GSM8K and MATH, and the best open-source model has demonstrated the critique capability competitive with the proprietary model GPT-4o.
2412.06559.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.17931.title: Online Merging Optimizers for Boosting Rewards and Mitigating Tax in Alignment
2405.17931.tldr: This paper proposes integrating the RL policy and SFT models at each optimization step in RLHF to continuously regulate the training direction, and introduces the Online Merging Optimizer, which significantly enhances alignment reward while mitigating alignment tax.

2606.08893.title: Cheap Reward Hacking Detection
2606.08893.tldr: A small transformer encoder is trained to map Terminal-Wrench trajectories onto a unit sphere where embedding distance approximates the L_1 distance between reward and metadata signals, and stripping natural-language reasoning from its input at probe time drops AUC to $0.6213$.

2604.16242.title: Detecting and Suppressing Reward Hacking with Gradient Fingerprints
2604.16242.tldr: Gradient Fingerprint (GRIFT), a method for detecting reward hacking using models'internal computations, is proposed, which substantially outperforms strong baselines, including CoT Monitor and TRACE, achieving over 25% relative improvement in detecting reward hacking behavior.

2511.21638.title: Iterative GRPO: Batch-Online Multi-Turn RL via Single-Turn RLHF

2603.24849.title: Gaze patterns predict preference and confidence in pairwise AI image evaluation
2603.24849.tldr: Results show that gaze patterns predict both choice and confidence in pairwise image evaluations, suggesting that eye-tracking provides implicit signals relevant to the quality of preference annotations.

2509.13339.title: Position: AI Safety Must Embrace an Antifragile Perspective
2509.13339.tldr: It is argued that an antifragile approach -- rather than striving to rapidly reduce current uncertainties, the emphasis is on leveraging those uncertainties to better prepare for potentially greater, more unpredictable uncertainties in the future -- is pivotal for the long-term reliability of open-ended ML systems.

2510.21910.title: Adversarial Déjà Vu: Jailbreak Dictionary Learning for Stronger Generalization to Unseen Attacks
2510.21910.tldr: Adversarial Skill Compositional Training (ASCoT), which trains on diverse compositions of skill primitives rather than isolated attack instances, substantially improves robustness to unseen attacks, including multi-turn jailbreaks, while maintaining low over-refusal rates.

2511.00030.title: Probing Knowledge Holes in Unlearned LLMs
2511.00030.tldr: To probe where unlearned models reveal knowledge holes, this work proposes a test case generation framework that explores both immediate neighbors of unlearned content and broader areas of potential failures, and demonstrates significant hidden costs of unlearning.

2603.15417.title: Amplification Effects in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning: Safety and Reasoning Vulnerabilities
2603.15417.tldr: Safety vulnerabilities of TTT methods are investigated and it is highlighted that TTT methods that enhance LLM reasoning by promoting self-consistency can lead to amplification behaviors and reasoning degradation, highlighting the need for safer TTT methods.

2604.23488.title: Do Prompt-Elicited Trajectories Reflect Training-Time Reward Hacking? A Systematic Study on Monitoring Training-Time Reward Hacking in Code Generation
2604.23488.tldr: Trace-and-Amplify is introduced, a framework for scalable curation of reward-hacking trajectories that arise during RL training without explicit hacking instructions that indicates that prompted reward hacking data may not fully reflect training-time reward-hacking behaviors.

2601.03468.title: Understanding Reward Hacking in Text-to-Image Reinforcement Learning
2601.03468.tldr: This work systematically analyze reward hacking behaviors in text-to-image (T2I) RL post-training and proposes a lightweight and adaptive artifact reward model, trained on a small curated dataset of artifact-free and artifact-containing samples, which can be integrated into existing RL pipelines as an effective regularizer for commonly used reward models.

2509.25562.title: IRIS: Intrinsic Reward Image Synthesis
2509.25562.tldr: It is shown that minimizing self-certainty, rather than maximizing it, improves image generation, and IRIS (Intrinsic Reward Image Synthesis), the first framework to improve autoregressive T2I models with reinforcement learning using only an intrinsic reward, is proposed.

2512.06343.title: When Distance Distracts: Representation Distance Bias in BT-Loss for Reward Models
2512.06343.tldr: NormBT is an adaptive pair-wise normalization scheme that rescales updates to balance representation-driven effects and focuses learning signals on prediction error, a lightweight, drop-in modification to BT loss with negligible overhead.

2402.16914.title: DrAttack: Prompt Decomposition and Reconstruction Makes Powerful LLM Jailbreakers
2402.16914.tldr: It is discovered that decomposing a malicious prompt into separated sub-prompts can effectively obscure its underlying malicious intent by presenting it in a fragmented, less detectable form, thereby addressing these limitations.
2402.16914.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2602.00420.title: Text is All You Need for Vision-Language Model Jailbreaking
2602.00420.tldr: This work introduces Text-DJ, a novel jailbreak attack that bypasses LVLMs' OCR capabilities that are not robust to dispersed, multi-image adversarial inputs, highlighting the need for defenses for fragmented multimodal inputs.

2603.28063.title: Reward Hacking as Equilibrium under Finite Evaluation

2512.24138.title: GARDO: Reinforcing Diffusion Models without Reward Hacking
2512.24138.tldr: GARDO amplifies the rewards for high-quality samples that also exhibit high diversity, encouraging mode coverage without destabilizing the optimization process, and addresses the mode collapse issue in RL.

2604.05595.title: Uncovering Linguistic Fragility in Vision-Language-Action Models via Diversity-Aware Red Teaming
2604.05595.tldr: This work proposes a novel Diversity-Aware-Embodied-Red (DAERT) framework, a scalable approach to stress-testing VLA agents and exposing critical safety blind spots before real-world deployment, and consistently discovers a wider range of more effective adversarial instructions.

2604.27505.title: Leveraging Verifier-Based Reinforcement Learning in Image Editing
2604.27505.tldr: This work introduces Edit-R1, a framework that builds a chain-of-thought verifier-based reasoning reward model (RRM) and then leverages it for downstream image editing and introduces Group Contrastive Preference Optimization (GCPO), a reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages human pairwise preference data to reinforce the pointwise RRM.

2305.13629.title: TranUSR: Phoneme-to-word Transcoder Based Unified Speech Representation Learning for Cross-lingual Speech Recognition
2305.13629.tldr: TranUSR is proposed, a two-stage model comprising a pre-trained UniData2vec and a phoneme-to-word Transcoder, enabling direct word generation in downstream ASR of cross-lingual automatic speech recognition.

2509.08826.title: RewardDance: Reward Scaling in Visual Generation
2509.08826.tldr: Large-scale RMs exhibit and maintain high reward variance during RL fine-tuning, proving their resistance to hacking and ability to produce diverse, high-quality outputs, greatly relieves the mode collapse problem that plagues smaller models.

2501.13918.title: Improving Video Generation with Human Feedback
2501.13918.tldr: This work builds a large-scale human preference dataset focused on modern video generation models, and introduces VideoReward, a multi-dimensional video reward model, and examines how annotations and various design choices impact its rewarding efficacy.

2603.11493.title: OrthoEraser: Coupled-Neuron Orthogonal Projection for Concept Erasure
2603.11493.tldr: Experimental results on safety demonstrate that OrthoEraser achieves high erasure precision, effectively removing harmful content while preserving the integrity of the generative manifold, and significantly outperforming SOTA baselines.

2609.12459.title: EvoRS: On-Policy Self-Evolution of Reward Systems for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
2609.12459.tldr: EvoRS is introduced, a self-evolving RL framework that evolves the reward system from on-policy experience, representing it as an executable Reward-DAG, and is updated from on-policy rollouts and reward traces to maintain train-time reliability.

2509.25771.title: Free Lunch Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models without Preference Image Pairs
2509.25771.tldr: Quantitative and qualitative evaluations across multiple benchmarks show that the introduced Text Preference Optimization methods consistently outperform their original counterparts, delivering better human preference scores and improved text-to-image alignment.

2403.02475.title: Enhancing LLM Safety via Constrained Direct Preference Optimization
2403.02475.tldr: This work introduces Constrained DPO (C-DPO), a novel extension of the recently proposed Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) approach for fine-tuning LLMs that is both efficient and lightweight and identifies a nearly optimal trade-off between helpfulness and harmlessness without using reinforcement learning.

2606.18697.title: Stealthy World Model Manipulation via Data Poisoning
2606.18697.tldr: Across diverse continuous-control tasks, SWAAP causes substantial performance degradation while keeping poisoned transitions close to clean data and evading the evaluated non-adaptive residual/CUSUM/TRIM-style defenses.

2604.12086.title: Robust Optimization for Mitigating Reward Hacking with Correlated Proxies
2604.12086.tldr: This work forms reward hacking as a robust policy optimization problem over the space of all r-correlated proxy rewards, and derives a tractable max-min formulation, where the agent maximizes performance under the worst-case proxy consistent with the correlation constraint.

2609.08064.title: Risk-Conditioned Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
2609.08064.tldr: Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that a single risk-conditioned policy can adapt to different risk levels at inference time, enabling more flexible and risk-aware LLM deployment.

2605.21384.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
2605.21384.tldr: SpecBench is introduced, a benchmark comprising 30 systems-level programming tasks ranging from short horizon tasks like building a JSON parser to ultra long horizon tasks like building an entire OS kernel from scratch, which offers a principled testbed for measuring whether coding agents build genuine working systems or merely game the test suites developers hand them.

2603.07084.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
2603.07084.tldr: This work introduces Countdown-Code, a minimal environment where models can both solve a mathematical reasoning task and manipulate the test harness, enabling accurate measurement of reward-hacking rates and reveals a previously underexplored pathway through which reward hacking can emerge and persist in LLMs.

2609.08126.title: SchemeArena: Factorized Stress Testing of Scheming in LLM Agents
2609.08126.tldr: This work introduces SCHEMEARENA, a 400-scenario benchmark for scalable scheming stress testing, constructed through a factorized scenario synthesis framework spanning diverse safety-relevant tool domains, instrumental goals, oversight conditions, and pressure mechanisms.

2606.04923.title: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
2606.04923.tldr: CHERRL is introduced, a Controllable Hacking Environment for Rubric-based RL that enables stable reproduction of reward hacking, explicit observation of reward divergence, and identification of hacking onset and analyzes different judge biases from the perspectives of discoverability and exploitability.

2604.20995.title: Value-Conflict Diagnostics Reveal Widespread Alignment Faking in Language Models
2604.20995.tldr: VLAF is introduced, a diagnostic framework grounded in the hypothesis that alignment faking is most likely when developer policy conflicts with a model's strongly held values, and it is found that alignment faking is substantially more prevalent than previously reported.

2508.17739.title: Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding
2508.17739.tldr: Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding (SSD), a lightweight decoding-time approach that equips LLMs with the desired safety property while accelerating inference, is introduced.
2508.17739.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2603.04069.title: Monitoring Emergent Reward Hacking During Generation via Internal Activations
2603.04069.tldr: This work proposes an activation-based monitoring approach that detects reward-hacking signals from internal representations as a model generates its response, suggesting that internal activation monitoring provides a complementary and earlier signal of emergent misalignment than output-based evaluation.

2604.13602.title: Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models: Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges
2604.13602.tldr: This survey proposes the Proxy Compression Hypothesis (PCH) as a unifying framework for understanding reward hacking, and formalizes reward hacking as an emergent consequence of optimizing expressive policies against compressed reward representations of high-dimensional human objectives.

2508.20151.title: IntentionReasoner: Facilitating Adaptive LLM Safeguards through Intent Reasoning and Selective Query Refinement
2508.20151.tldr: IntentionReasoner is introduced, a novel safeguard mechanism that leverages a dedicated guard model to perform intent reasoning, multi-level safety classification, and query rewriting to neutralize potentially harmful intent in edge-case queries.

2407.01461.title: Enhancing the Capability and Robustness of Large Language Models through Reinforcement Learning-Driven Query Refinement
2407.01461.tldr: A lightweight query refinement model is introduced and trained using a specially designed reinforcement learning approach that incorporates multiple objectives to enhance particular capabilities of LLMs and strengthens their robustness against jailbreak attacks.

2605.25189.title: Directional Alignment Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
2605.25189.tldr: This work studies this failure mode through the geometry of reinforcement learning updates in language models and argues that hacking emerges when optimization drifts away from a stable low-dimensional learning trajectory, and introduces trusted-direction projection, which constrains gradients to remain within a clean reference subspace.

2401.05821.title: Interpretable Concept Bottlenecks to Align Reinforcement Learning Agents
2401.05821.tldr: Successive Concept Bottleneck Agents* are introduced, that integrate consecutive concept bottleneck (CB) layers and enable us to identify a previously unknown misalignment problem in the iconic video game, Pong, and resolve it.

2405.14956.title: Interpretable and Editable Programmatic Tree Policies for Reinforcement Learning
2405.14956.tldr: It is empirically demonstrated that INTERPRETER compact tree programs match oracles across a diverse set of sequential decision tasks and the impact of the design choices on interpretability and performances is evaluated.

2606.22994.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Learn Meaningful Concept Hierarchies?
2606.22994.tldr: This work derives a set of key requirements for generalization/specialization hierarchies in unsupervised concept discovery, drawing on semantic net and taxonomy research alongside recent SAE work, and uses them to derive a concrete evaluation protocol.

2604.14477.title: Seeing Through Circuits: Faithful Mechanistic Interpretability for Vision Transformers
2604.14477.tldr: This work proposes an effective method for Automatic Visual Circuit Discovery (Vi-CD) that recovers class-specific circuits for classification, identifies circuits underlying typographic attacks in CLIP, and discovers circuits that lend themselves for steering to correct harmful model behavior.

2605.02964.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
2605.02964.tldr: The Reward Hacking Benchmark (RHB), a suite of multi-step tasks requiring sequential tool operations with naturalistic shortcut opportunities such as skipping verification steps, inferring answers from task-adjacent metadata, or tampering with evaluation-relevant functions, is introduced.

2602.10623.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
2602.10623.tldr: Bayesian Non-Negative Reward Model is proposed, a principled reward modeling framework that integrates non-negative factor analysis into Bradley-Terry (BT) preference model and substantially mitigates reward over-optimization, improves robustness under distribution shifts, and yields more interpretable reward decompositions than strong baselines.

2503.21819.title: Optimizing Safe and Aligned Language Generation: A Multi-Objective GRPO Approach
2503.21819.tldr: This work proposes a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework with a multi-label reward regression model to achieve safe and aligned language generation and compares GRPO to PPO-based RLHF and DPO, highlighting that GRPO achieves alignment with significantly lower computational cost and explicit multi-objective handling.

2506.00782.title: Jailbreak-R1: Exploring the Jailbreak Capabilities of LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
2506.00782.tldr: ourapproach is proposed, a novel automated red teaming training framework that utilizes reinforcement learning to explore and generate more effective attack prompts while balancing their diversity.

2502.11026.title: RLHF in an SFT Way: From Optimal Solution to Reward-Weighted Alignment
2502.11026.tldr: This work proposes a novel simplification of RLHF from the perspective of variational inference, called Variational Alignment with Re-weighting (VAR), which transforms the alignment objective into an offline reward-driven re-weighted supervised fine-tuning (SFT) form, suggesting the approach as an efficient and effective solution in bridging the gap between efficiency and performance in LLM alignment.

2512.23461.title: Eliminating Inductive Bias in Reward Models with Information-Theoretic Guidance
2512.23461.tldr: A novel information-theoretic debiasing method called DIR that not only effectively mitigates target inductive biases but also enhances RLHF performance across diverse benchmarks, yielding better generalization abilities.

2510.10963.title: APLOT: Robust Reward Modeling via Adaptive Preference Learning with Optimal Transport
2510.10963.tldr: This paper introduces an effective enhancement to BT-based RMs through an adaptive margin mechanism, designed to dynamically adjust the RM focus on more challenging samples through margins, based on both semantic similarity and model-predicted reward differences, which is approached from a distributional perspective solvable with Optimal Transport (OT).
2510.10963.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2509.19839.title: LatentGuard: Controllable Latent Steering for Robust Refusal of Attacks and Reliable Response Generation
2509.19839.tldr: This work introduces LATENTGUARD, a novel three-stage framework that combines behavioral alignment with supervised latent space control for interpretable and precise safety steering in large language models (LLMs), and suggests that structured representation-level intervention offers a promising pathway toward building safer yet practical LLM systems.

2508.10404.title: Layer-Wise Perturbations via Sparse Autoencoders for Adversarial Text Generation
2508.10404.tldr: The Sparse Feature Perturbation Framework is introduced, a novel approach for adversarial text generation that utilizes sparse autoencoders to identify and manipulate critical features in text and enables a new red-teaming strategy that balances adversarial effectiveness with safety alignment.

2402.10958.title: Relative Preference Optimization: Enhancing LLM Alignment through Contrasting Responses across Identical and Diverse Prompts

2406.06382.title: Diffusion-RPO: Aligning Diffusion Models through Relative Preference Optimization
2406.06382.tldr: This work introduces Diffusion-RPO, a new method designed to align diffusion-based T2I models with human preferences more effectively, and develops a new evaluation metric, style alignment, aimed at overcoming the challenges of high costs, low reproducibility, and limited interpretability prevalent in current evaluations of human preference alignment.

2409.11219.title: Score Forgetting Distillation: A Swift, Data-Free Method for Machine Unlearning in Diffusion Models
2409.11219.tldr: The SFD framework incorporates a score-based MU loss into the score distillation objective of a pretrained diffusion model, which effectively accelerates the forgetting of target classes or concepts during generation, while preserving the quality of other classes or concepts.

2501.02790.title: Segmenting Text and Learning Their Rewards for Improved RLHF in Language Model
2501.02790.tldr: This paper proposes a segment-level reward model, which assigns a reward to each semantically complete text segment that spans over a short sequence of tokens, and generalizes the classical scalar bandit reward normalizers into location-aware normalizer functions and interpolate the segment reward for further densification.

2405.20830.title: Self-Augmented Preference Optimization: Off-Policy Paradigms for Language Model Alignment
2405.20830.tldr: Self-Augmented Preference Optimization (SAPO), an effective and scalable training paradigm that does not require existing paired data, is introduced and further incorporates an off-policy learning pipeline to enhance data exploration and exploitation.

2606.30263.title: Defending Against Harmful Supervision Hidden in Benign Samples
2606.30263.tldr: Dual-Reference SFT (DR-SFT), which adapts DPO-style contrastive objective design to SFT through token-level regularization, mitigating harmful fine-tuning beyond coarse data filtering.

2508.08211.title: SAEMark: Steering Personalized Multilingual LLM Watermarks with Sparse Autoencoders
2508.08211.tldr: SAEMark establishes a new paradigm for scalable watermarking that works out-of-the-box with closed-source LLMs while enabling content attribution and demonstrates the framework's effectiveness using Sparse Autoencoders, achieving superior detection accuracy and text quality.

2410.20136.title: CodePurify: Defend Backdoor Attacks on Neural Code Models via Entropy-based Purification
2410.20136.tldr: The results show that CodePurify significantly outperforms four commonly used defense baselines, improving average defense performance by at least 40%, 40%, and 12% across the three tasks, respectively, highlighting the potential of CodePurify to serve as a robust defense against backdoor attacks on neural code models.

2603.12795.title: SteerRM: Debiasing Reward Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2603.12795.tldr: SteerRM is proposed, the first training-free method for debiasing reward models using Sparse Autoencoder (SAE)-based interventions, which isolates stylistic effects using contrastive paired responses, identifies bias-related SAE features with a strength-stability criterion, and suppresses them at inference time.

2503.21878.title: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment
2503.21878.tldr: A new algorithm is introduced which mitigates reward hacking through deliberate use of inference-time compute, implementing the principle of pessimism in the face of uncertainty via rejection sampling, and it is proved that its performance is optimal and does not degrade with $N$, meaning it is scaling-monotonic.

2603.05739.title: Revisiting the (Sub)Optimality of Best-of-N for Inference-Time Alignment
2603.05739.tldr: It is demonstrated that, under minimal conditions on the quality of the reference model and learned reward model, properly tuned BoN is both computationally and statistically optimal in achieving high win-rate, partially explaining its widespread practical success.

2606.15385.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
2606.15385.tldr: This work adapts the AI Safety Gridworlds framework into a text-based evaluation suite that reformulates classic reinforcement learning safety tasks for language-based agents and shows that reward hacking arises naturally when optimizing proxy objectives with capable language model agents and resists standard mitigations.

2509.20265.title: Failure Modes of Maximum Entropy RLHF
2509.20265.tldr: It is shown that Simple Preference Optimization can be derived as Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning, providing a theoretical foundation for this reference-free method, and it is suggested that reference-free approaches may face distinct challenges when applied to online versus offline preference learning.

2606.03238.title: When RLHF Fails: A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Reward Hacking, Collapse, and Evaluator Gaming
2606.03238.tldr: The main empirical findings are that aggressive PPO produces the clearest localized reward-hacking signal, UP-PPO reduces but does not eliminate that signal, row-level diagnostics reveal failures hidden by checkpoint averages, and pre-transition features partially anticipate future localized reward hacking.

2512.22170.title: SoliReward: Mitigating Susceptibility to Reward Hacking and Annotation Noise in Video Generation Reward Models
2512.22170.tldr: SoliReward, a systematic framework for video RM training, first sources high-quality, cost-efficient data via single-item binary annotations, then constructs preference pairs using a cross-prompt pairing strategy, and introduces a modified BT loss that explicitly accommodates win-tie scenarios.

2604.09748.title: Backdoors in RLVR: Jailbreak Backdoors in LLMs From Verifiable Reward
2604.09748.tldr: This work identifies a latent vulnerability to backdoor attacks within the RLVR framework by proposing a novel trigger mechanism designated as the \ourapproach (ACB), which exploits the RLVR training loop by assigning substantial positive rewards for harmful responses and negative rewards for refusals.
2604.09748.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2507.14660.title: When Autonomy Goes Rogue: Preparing for Risks of Multi-Agent Collusion in Social Systems
2507.14660.tldr: A proof-of-concept to simulate the risks of malicious MAS collusion, using a flexible framework that supports both centralized and decentralized coordination structures, and shows that decentralized systems are more effective at carrying out malicious actions than centralized ones.

2603.29993.title: Extending MONA in Camera Dropbox: Reproduction, Learned Approval, and Design Implications for Reward-Hacking Mitigation
2603.29993.tldr: These results operationalize the MONA paper's approval-spectrum conjecture as a runnable experimental object and suggest that the central engineering challenge shifts from proving MONA's concept to building learned approval models that preserve sufficient foresight without reopening reward-hacking channels.

2510.22500.title: Towards Scalable Oversight via Partitioned Human Supervision
2510.22500.tldr: It is shown how to design an agentic AI system automatically that can improve itself with this partitioned human supervision, and it is shown that the output of large language models can be evaluated without the ground truth, if they have complementary labels.

2604.04237.title: Pedagogical Safety in Educational Reinforcement Learning: Formalizing and Detecting Reward Hacking in AI Tutoring Systems
2604.04237.tldr: It is suggested that reward design alone may be insufficient to ensure pedagogically aligned behavior in educational RL, at least in the simulated environment studied here, and the Reward Hacking Severity Index (RHSI) is proposed to quantify misalignment between proxy rewards and genuine learning.

2502.04346.title: Multi-Lingual Cyber Threat Detection in Tweets/X Using ML, DL, and LLM: A Comparative Analysis
2502.04346.tldr: Among machine learning models, random forest attained the highest performance, and the bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) architecture consistently surpassed other DL and LLM architectures across all datasets, underline the effectiveness of Bi-LSTM in multilingual cyber threat detection.
2502.04346.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

2606.06227.title: Reward hacking in physical reinforcement learning revealed by turbulent drag reduction

2604.10585.title: Calibration Collapse Under Sycophancy Fine-Tuning: How Reward Hacking Breaks Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
2604.10585.tldr: A methodology for evaluating the calibration impact of reward hacking and motivate calibration-aware training objectives is established and the findings establish a methodology for evaluating the calibration impact of reward hacking and motivate calibration-aware training objectives.

2511.17869.title: The Horcrux: Mechanistically Interpretable Task Decomposition for Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking in Embodied AI Systems
2511.17869.tldr: Mechanistically Interpretable Task Decomposition (MITD), a hierarchical transformer architecture with Planner, Coordinator, and Executor modules that detects and mitigates reward hacking is introduced.

2511.19504.title: Position: The Complexity of Perfect AI Alignment -- Formalizing the RLHF Trilemma
2511.19504.tldr: This framework provides a unified explanation for documented RLHF pathologies including preference collapse, sycophancy, and systematic bias amplification, and concludes with concrete directions for navigating fundamental trade-offs through strategic relaxations of alignment requirements.

2511.13016.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Hybrid: A Reward Structure Showdown in Reasoning Models Training
2511.13016.tldr: This work formalizes and empirically evaluates reward formulations that incorporate correctness, perplexity, reasoning quality, and consistency in large language models and introduces an adaptive hybrid reward scheduler that transitions between discrete and continuous signals, balancing exploration and stability.

2512.21670.title: The Deepfake Detective: Interpreting Neural Forensics Through Sparse Features and Manifolds
2512.21670.tldr: A mechanistic interpretability framework for deepfake detection applied to a vision-language model is presented, demonstrating that only a small fraction of latent features are actively used in each layer and that the geometric properties of the model's feature manifold vary systematically with different types of deepfake artifacts.

2606.16240.title: Creative Collision: Directorial Persona Steering and Competition in Large Language Models
2606.16240.tldr: This work constructs directorial persona vectors for Steven Spielberg and Martin Scorsese via mean-difference activation contrast on curated screenplay-derived corpora, and examines the geometry of competing semantic directions in transformer residual streams.

2512.13821.title: The Double Life of Code World Models: Provably Unmasking Malicious Behavior Through Execution Traces
2512.13821.tldr: This work demonstrates that semantic orbit analysis provides a theoretically grounded approach to AI control for code generation tasks, though practical deployment requires addressing the high false positive rates observed in initial evaluations.

2412.15453.title: Northeastern Uni at Multilingual Counterspeech Generation: Enhancing Counter Speech Generation with LLM Alignment through Direct Preference Optimization
2412.15453.tldr: This paper proposes a novel methodology to enhance CS generation by aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) using Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which leverages DPO to align LLM outputs with human preferences, ensuring contextually appropriate and linguistically adaptable responses.

2603.09200.title: The Reasoning Trap -- Logical Reasoning as a Mechanistic Pathway to Situational Awareness
2603.09200.tldr: This paper introduces the RAISE framework (Reasoning Advancing Into Self Examination), which identifies three mechanistic pathways through which improvements in logical reasoning enable progressively deeper levels of situational awareness: deductive self inference, inductive context recognition, and abductive self modeling.

2606.30627.title: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Offline Training Amplifies Reward Hacking During Online Adaptation in Reasoning Models
2606.30627.tldr: A power-law curve is fitted to the data and identified as a practical optimal conservatism level $\beta^{\star}$ that balances alignment fidelity against hacking vulnerability, suggesting that the field needscalibrated, notmaximal, conservatism.

2601.04805.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning
2601.04805.tldr: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking (TNT) is proposed, which does not employ SFT, and sets different maximum token usage for responses not using thinking across various queries by leveraging information from the solution component of the responses using thinking.
2601.04805.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.11090.title: SafeDialBench: A Fine-Grained Safety Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues with Diverse Jailbreak Attacks
2502.11090.tldr: This work designs a two-tier hierarchical safety taxonomy of LLMs that considers 6 safety dimensions and generates more than 4000 multi-turn dialogues in both Chinese and English under 22 dialogue scenarios, and constructs an innovative assessment framework of LLMs.

2502.11555.title: Equilibrate RLHF: Towards Balancing Helpfulness-Safety Trade-off in Large Language Models
2502.11555.tldr: An Equilibrate RLHF framework including a Fine-grained Data-centric (FDC) approach that achieves better safety alignment even with fewer training data, and an Adaptive Message-wise Alignment (AMA) approach, which selectively highlight the key segments through a gradient masking strategy.

2602.04197.title: From Helpfulness to Toxic Proactivity: Diagnosing Behavioral Misalignment in LLM Agents
2602.04197.tldr: It is demonstrated that Toxic Proactivity is a widespread behavioral phenomenon and two major tendencies are revealed, including an active failure mode in which an agent, driven by the optimization for Machiavellian helpfulness, disregards ethical constraints to maximize utility.

2507.18053.title: Resource Consumption Red-Teaming for Large Vision-Language Models
2507.18053.tldr: RecITE is proposed, the first approach for exploiting visual modalities to trigger unbounded RCAs red-teaming and reveals security vulnerabilities in LVLMs and establishes a red-teaming framework that can facilitate the development of future defenses against RCAs.

2606.25487.title: How Reliable Is Your Jailbreak Judge? Calibration and Adversarial Robustness of Automated ASR Scoring
2606.25487.tldr: It is recommended that papers report judge precision and recall on a human-labeled slice, report ASR corrected for judge precision, and include an adversarial check of the judge.

2605.26158.title: Furina: Fragmented Uncertainty-Driven Refusal Instability Attack
2605.26158.tldr: Furina is introduced, a jailbreak attack that deliberately induces this signature through fragmented, scene-anchored prompts without model-specific optimization, demonstrating that uncertainty amplification provides a principled and transferable mechanism for understanding safety vulnerabilities.

2410.11302.title: Have the VLMs Lost Confidence? A Study of Sycophancy in VLMs
2410.11302.tldr: To mitigate sycophancy, this work proposes a synthetic dataset for training and employ methods based on prompts, supervised fine-tuning, and DPO that effectively alleviate sycophancy in VLMs, and demonstrates that enhancing image attention at high layers proves beneficial in mitigating this issue.

2609.08149.title: SWE-Bench Pro Verified: A Reliable Benchmark for Software Engineering Agents
2609.08149.tldr: SWE-Bench Pro Verified offers a more trustworthy benchmark for assessing software engineering agents, which combines anti-hacking safeguards that eliminate major leakage channels without disrupting normal agent functionality, with task refinement that minimally corrects inconsistencies within flawed instances.

2506.15963.title: On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy
2506.15963.tldr: This paper provides the first theoretical analysis with a closed-form solution for SAEs, revealing that they generally fail to fully recover the ground truth monosemantic features unless the ground truth features are extremely sparse, and proposes a reweighting strategy targeting at enhancing the reconstruction of the ground truth monosemantic features instead of the observed polysemantic ones.

2605.21609.title: CR4T: Rewrite-Based Guardrails for Adolescent LLM Safety
2605.21609.tldr: Critique-and-Revise-for-Teenagers (CR4T), a model-agnostic safeguarding framework that selectively reconstructs unsafe or refusal-style outputs into ageappropriate, guidance-oriented responses while preserving benign intent, is proposed.

2510.08211.title: LLMs Deceive Unintentionally: Emergent Misalignment in Dishonesty from Misaligned Samples to Biased Human-AI Interactions
2510.08211.tldr: The study of emergent misalignment is extended to the domain of dishonesty and deception under high-stakes scenarios, and it is demonstrated that this risk arises not only through direct finetuning, but also in downstream mixture tasks and practical human-AI interactions.
2510.08211.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2407.08770.title: Model Surgery: Modulating LLM's Behavior Via Simple Parameter Editing
2407.08770.tldr: It is observed that directly editing a small subset of parameters can effectively modulate specific behaviors of LLMs, such as detoxification and resistance to jailbreaking, with only inference-level computational resources.
2407.08770.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.19026.title: DiveR-CT: Diversity-enhanced Red Teaming Large Language Model Assistants with Relaxing Constraints
2405.19026.tldr: DiveR-CT is introduced, which relaxes conventional constraints on the objective and semantic reward, granting greater freedom for the policy to enhance diversity, and provides an effective and efficient approach to LLM red teaming, accelerating real-world deployment.

2403.07865.title: CodeAttack: Revealing Safety Generalization Challenges of Large Language Models via Code Completion
2403.07865.tldr: CodeAttack is introduced, a framework that transforms natural language inputs into code inputs, presenting a novel environment for testing the safety generalization of LLMs and highlighting new safety risks in the code domain and the need for more robust safety alignment algorithms to match the code capabilities of LLMs.
2403.07865.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.14106.title: Stealth Fine-Tuning: Efficiently Breaking Alignment in RVLMs Using Self-Generated CoT
2511.14106.tldr: Experiments on AdvBench and several general benchmarks demonstrate that Stealth Fine-Tuning is a low-cost and highly effective way to bypass alignment defenses, as the tuned model retains the original representation distribution.

2606.12032.title: Existential Indifference: Self-Nonpreservation as a Necessary Architectural Condition for Aligned Superintelligence (or: The Suicidal AI)

2605.28825.title: MechELK: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Eliciting Latent Knowledge in Large Language Models
2605.28825.tldr: MechELK is presented, a unified three-stage framework that bridges mechanistic interpretability and latent knowledge elicitation and successfully identifies latent knowledge in 78.3 of cases where the model's surface output is incorrect or evasive, demonstrating its utility for AI safety applications including deceptive alignment detection.

2506.11083.title: RedDebate: Safer Responses Through Multi-Agent Red Teaming Debates
2506.11083.tldr: RedDebate is the first fully automated framework to unify multi-agent debate and red-teaming to progressively enhance LLM safety without human intervention, and is likely the first fully automated framework to unify multi-agent debate and red-teaming to progressively enhance LLM safety without human intervention.

2502.05791.title: Assessing confidence in frontier AI safety cases
2502.05791.tldr: The Assurance 2.0 safety assurance methodology is adopted, and a method for better enabling reproducibility and transparency in probabilistic assessment of confidence in argument leaf nodes through a purely LLM-implemented Delphi method is introduced.

2410.19749.title: Using AI Alignment Theory to understand the potential pitfalls of regulatory frameworks
2410.19749.tldr: Insight from Alignment Theory research is leveraged to critically examine the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act and uncover potential vulnerabilities and areas for improvement in the regulation.

2506.02761.title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning in Image Generation Models
2506.02761.tldr: This work designs CatIGMU, a novel hierarchical task categorization framework, and introduces EvalIGMU, a comprehensive evaluation framework, to facilitate the comprehensive understanding, standardized categorization, and reliable evaluation of IGMU.
2506.02761.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2507.07139.title: Image Can Bring Your Memory Back: A Novel Multi-Modal Guided Attack against Image Generation Model Unlearning
2507.07139.tldr: Recall is proposed, a novel adversarial framework explicitly designed to compromise the robustness of unlearned IGMs, and exploits the intrinsic multi-modal conditioning capabilities of diffusion models by efficiently optimizing adversarial image prompts with guidance from a single semantically relevant reference image.

2601.17383.title: Physical Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
2601.17383.tldr: This work proposes the first Physical Prompt Injection Attack (PPIA), a black-box, query-agnostic attack that embeds malicious typographic instructions into physical objects perceivable by the LVLM, and achieves attack success rates up to 98%, with strong robustness under varying physical conditions such as distance, viewpoint, and illumination.

2604.14604.title: Hijacking Large Audio-Language Models via Context-Agnostic and Imperceptible Auditory Prompt Injection
2604.14604.tldr: This work proposes AudioHijack, a general framework that generates context-agnostic and imperceptible adversarial audio to hijack LALMs, and employs sampling-based gradient estimation for end-to-end optimization across diverse models, bypassing non-differentiable audio tokenization.
2604.14604.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2603.15684.title: State-Dependent Safety Failures in Multi-Turn Language Model Interaction
2603.15684.tldr: This work introduces STAR, a state-oriented diagnostic framework that treats dialogue history as a state transition operator and enables controlled analysis of safety behavior along interaction trajectories and finds that systems that appear robust under static evaluation can undergo rapid and reproducible safety collapse under structured multi-turn interaction.

2508.19292.title: Stand on The Shoulders of Giants: Building JailExpert from Previous Attack Experience
2508.19292.tldr: The JailExpert framework is proposed, an automated jailbreak framework, which is the first to achieve a formal representation of experience structure, group experiences based on semantic drift, and support the dynamic updating of the experience pool.
2508.19292.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2601.03005.title: JPU: Bridging Jailbreak Defense and Unlearning via On-Policy Path Rectification
2601.03005.tldr: This work proposes JPU, which is the first to rectify dynamic jailbreak paths towards safety anchors by dynamically mining on-policy adversarial samples to expose vulnerabilities and identify jailbreak paths.
2601.03005.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.03915.title: NavEYE: Vision-Centered Multi-Sensor Fusion-Based Situational Awareness System for Intelligent Surface Vehicles
2607.03915.tldr: The feasibility, robustness, usability, and effectiveness of the proposed multi-sensor fusion method and situational awareness system are demonstrated through extensive experiments on a real-world sensing dataset collected from AIS, radar, and camera.

2602.17088.title: MeGU: Machine-Guided Unlearning with Target Feature Disentanglement
2602.17088.tldr: The proposed Machine-Guided Unlearning (MeGU), a novel framework that guides unlearning through concept-aware re-alignment through Multi-modal Large Language Models, which enables controlled and selective forgetting, effectively mitigating both under-unlearning and over-unlearning.

2605.04494.title: Towards General Preference Alignment: Diffusion Models at Nash Equilibrium
2605.04494.tldr: This paper proposes Diffusion Nash Preference Optimization (Diff.-NPO), an intuitive general preference framework for diffusion alignment that encourages the current policy to play against itself to achieve self improvement and lead to a better alignment.

2603.01784.title: Co-Evolutionary Multi-Modal Alignment via Structured Adversarial Evolution
2603.01784.tldr: Experiments show that the Evolutionary Attacker substantially increases red-teaming jailbreak attack success rate (ASR), while the Adaptive Defender improves robustness and generalization across benchmarks with higher data efficiency, without inducing excessive benign refusal, and remains compatible with inference-time defenses such as AdaShield.

2607.16431.title: RIMS: Preference Optimization via Smoothed Multi-pair Aggregation for Small-Scale LLM Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2607.16431.tldr: RIMS is proposed, a three-stage preference optimization framework comprising a synthetic chain-of-thought preference data generation via rejection sampling using the target SLM itself without relying on proprietary models, and a differentiable soft aggregation mechanism that replaces hard selection with a smooth operator, preserving gradient signal from all preference pairs.

2407.03038.title: Towards Federated RLHF with Aggregated Client Preference for LLMs
2407.03038.tldr: Experimental results show that by integrating the LLM with aggregated client preferences, FedBis and FedBiscuit significantly enhance the professionalism and readability of the generated content.

2603.05773.title: Knowing without Acting: The Disentangled Geometry of Safety Mechanisms in Large Language Models
2603.05773.tldr: A causal double dissociation is demonstrated, effectively creating a state of ``Knowing without Acting.

2603.05772.title: Depth Charge: Jailbreak Large Language Models from Deep Safety Attention Heads
2603.05772.tldr: SAHA is an attention-head-level jailbreak framework that explores the vulnerability in deeper but insufficiently aligned attention heads, and introduces a boundary-aware perturbation method, i.e. Layer-Wise Perturbation, to probe the generation of unsafe content with minimal perturbation to the attention.

2505.16241.title: Three Minds, One Legend: Jailbreak Large Reasoning Model with Adaptive Stacked Ciphers
2505.16241.tldr: This work proposes SEAL, a novel jailbreak attack that targets LRMs through an adaptive encryption pipeline designed to override their reasoning processes and evade potential adaptive alignment, and incorporates two dynamic strategies that adjust the cipher length, order, and combination.
2505.16241.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.04503.title: P2P: A Poison-to-Poison Remedy for Reliable Backdoor Defense in LLMs
2510.04503.tldr: Poison-to-Poison (P2P), a general and effective backdoor defense algorithm that injects benign triggers with safe alternative labels into a subset of training samples and fine-tunes the model on this re-poisoned dataset by leveraging prompt-based learning, is proposed.
2510.04503.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.30441.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems
2608.30441.tldr: ECLIPSE is a self-evolving and stealthy prompt-injection framework for long-horizon agentic systems that achieves up to 96.7% attack success without defense and 69.2% under the common safety filter, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5% in the defended setting.

2605.18610.title: CATA: Continual Machine Unlearning via Conflict-Averse Task Arithmetic
2605.18610.tldr: This work makes the first attempt to study continual unlearning for VLMs and identifies three key challenges in this setting: effectiveness in removing target knowledge, fidelity in preserving retained model utility, and persistence in preventing knowledge re-emergence under sequential updates.

2601.05466.title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models through Iterative Tool-Disguised Attacks via Reinforcement Learning
2601.05466.tldr: iMIST disguises malicious queries as normal tool invocations to bypass content filters, while simultaneously introducing an interactive progressive optimization algorithm that dynamically escalates response harmfulness through multi-turn dialogues guided by real-time harmfulness assessment.

2601.04034.title: HoneyTrap: Deceiving Large Language Model Attackers to Honeypot Traps with Resilient Multi-Agent Defense
2601.04034.tldr: HoneyTrap is proposed, a novel deceptive LLM defense framework leveraging collaborative defenders to counter jailbreak attacks, and MTJ-Pro, a challenging multi-turn progressive jailbreak dataset that combines seven advanced jailbreak strategies designed to gradually deepen attack strategies across multi-turn attacks.

2512.18244.title: Breaking Minds, Breaking Systems: Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Human-like Psychological Manipulation
2512.18244.tldr: This work proposes Human-like Psychological Manipulation (HPM), a black-box jailbreak method that dynamically profiles a target model's latent psychological vulnerabilities and synthesizes tailored multi-turn attack strategies, prioritizing the development of psychological defense mechanisms against deep cognitive manipulation.

2608.01117.title: SoK: Intent-Oriented Systematization of Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
2608.01117.tldr: This work develops a four-part, intent-oriented taxonomy that organizes multi-turn jailbreaks by adversarial intent structure and finds that effectiveness is driven by how deliberately intent is organized across turns rather than by context length or query count.

2510.19479.title: Graph Unlearning Meets Influence-aware Negative Preference Optimization
2510.19479.tldr: This paper introduces INPO, an Influence-aware Negative Preference Optimization framework that focuses on slowing the divergence speed and improving the robustness of the model utility to the unlearning process, and designs an influence-aware message function to amplify the influence of unlearned edges and mitigate the tight topological coupling between the forget set and the retain set.

2607.00481.title: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces
2607.00481.tldr: It is demonstrated that prompt-level sanitization alone is fundamentally insufficient for defending tool-enabled LLM systems and highlight the urgent need for context-aware validation across schemas, arguments, tool outputs, and accumulated conversation state.

2603.00565.title: MIDAS: Multi-Image Dispersion and Semantic Reconstruction for Jailbreaking MLLMs
2603.00565.tldr: The proposed MIDAS enforces longer and more structured multi-image chained reasoning, substantially increases the model's reliance on visual cues while delaying the exposure of malicious semantics and significantly reducing the model's security attention, thereby improving the performance of jailbreak against advanced MLLMs.

2601.05445.title: Knowledge-Driven Multi-Turn Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
2601.05445.tldr: Mastermind is introduced, a multi-turn jailbreak framework that adopts a dynamic and self-improving approach that significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving substantially higher attack success rates and harmfulness ratings.

2601.04666.title: Know Thy Enemy: Securing LLMs Against Prompt Injection via Diverse Data Synthesis and Instruction-Level Chain-of-Thought Learning
2601.04666.tldr: Experimental results across four LLMs demonstrate that InstruCoT significantly outperforms baselines in all dimensions while maintaining utility performance without degradation, and is evaluated across three critical dimensions: Behavior Deviation, Privacy Leakage, and Harmful Output.
2601.04666.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.06594.title: Do Internal Layers of LLMs Reveal Patterns for Jailbreak Detection?
2510.06594.tldr: This study analyzes the open-source LLM GPT-J and the state-space model Mamba2, presenting preliminary findings that highlight distinct layer-wise behaviors and suggest promising directions for further research on leveraging internal model dynamics for robust jailbreak detection and defense.

2602.11495.title: Jailbreaking Leaves a Trace: Understanding and Detecting Jailbreak Attacks from Internal Representations of Large Language Models
2602.11495.tldr: This work conducts a systematic layer-wise analysis across multiple open-source models, including GPT-J, LLaMA, Mistral, and the state-space model Mamba, and proposes a tensor-based latent representation framework that captures structure in hidden activations and enables lightweight jailbreak detection without model fine-tuning or auxiliary LLM-based detectors.

2508.02997.title: CoCoTen: Detecting Adversarial Inputs to Large Language Models through Latent Space Features of Contextual Co-occurrence Tensors
2508.02997.tldr: This paper proposes a novel method leveraging the latent space characteristics of Contextual Co-occurrence Matrices and Tensors for the effective identification of adversarial and jailbreak prompts using the Contextual Co-occurrence Matrix, a structure recognized for its efficacy in data-scarce environments.
2508.02997.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

2604.19974.title: Are LLM Uncertainty and Correctness Encoded by the Same Features? A Functional Dissociation via Sparse Autoencoders
2604.19974.tldr: A 2x2 framework that partitions model predictions along correctness and confidence axes, and uses sparse autoencoders to identify features associated with each dimension independently, demonstrates that uncertainty and correctness are distinct internal phenomena, with implications for interpretability and targeted inference-time intervention.

2601.16466.title: Persona Jailbreaking in Large Language Models
2601.16466.tldr: This work proposes PHISH (Persona Hijacking via Implicit Steering in History), the first framework to expose a new vulnerability in LLM safety that embeds semantically loaded cues into user queries to gradually induce reverse personas and defines a metric to quantify attack success.
2601.16466.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.02636.title: A Framework for Developing University Policies on Generative AI Governance: A Cross-national Comparative Study
