2504.02636.tldr: A cross-nationalanalysis of GAI guidelines issued by leading universities in the United States, Japan, and China is undertaken, identifying key policy orientations and proposing a structured framework to support policy development.

2602.07107.title: ShallowJail: Steering Jailbreaks against Large Language Models
2602.07107.tldr: This work introduces ShallowJail, a novel attack that exploits shallow alignment in LLMs, which substantially degrades the safety of state-of-the-art LLM responses.

2605.00155.title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Regret Optimization for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2605.00155.tldr: Distributionally robust regret optimization (DRRO) is proposed for RLHF with a Wasserstein ambiguity set over reward laws, using promptwise distances between reward vectors as transport costs and shows that it is less over-pessimistic than standard DRO and mitigates over-optimization more effectively than existing baselines.

2603.11149.title: Systematic Scaling Analysis of Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
2603.11149.tldr: A scaling-law framework for jailbreaks is initiated by treating each attack as a compute-bounded optimization procedure and measuring progress on a shared FLOPs axis, and prompt-based attacks more effectively optimize in prompt space.

2503.00917.title: AMUN: Adversarial Machine UNlearning
2503.00917.tldr: Adversarial Machine UNlearning (AMUN) is proposed, a new unlearning method that outperforms prior state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods for image classification and observes that even SOTA membership inference attacks cannot do better than random guessing.

2512.19025.title: The Erasure Illusion: Stress-Testing the Generalization of LLM Forgetting Evaluation
2512.19025.tldr: It is demonstrated that LLMs can pass standard unlearning evaluation and appear to have "forgotten" the target knowledge, while simultaneously retaining strong capabilities on content that is semantically adjacent to $D_u$, indicating that erasing exact sentences does not necessarily equate to removing the underlying knowledge.

2602.22562.title: Layer-Targeted Multilingual Knowledge Erasure in Large Language Models
2602.22562.tldr: MUTE (Multilingual Unlearning via Targeted Erasure), a framework that uses Centered Kernel Alignment and Linguistic Regions Development Score to identify intermediate, language-agnostic layers where cross-lingual representations converge, achieves robust multilingual knowledge erasure while optimizing on only a small set of source languages.

2609.00498.title: Validity-Aware Jailbreak Evaluation for Large Language Models
2609.00498.tldr: This work proposes Sequential Epistemic and Action-Level Validation (SEAV), a verification-centric jailbreak evaluation framework that decomposes responses into ordered steps and evaluates both validity and correctness, and shows that enforcing correctness substantially reshapes measured robustness.

2408.05500.title: PointNCBW: Towards Dataset Ownership Verification for Point Clouds via Negative Clean-label Backdoor Watermark
2408.05500.tldr: This work designs a scalable clean-label backdoor-based dataset watermark for point clouds that ensures both effectiveness and stealthiness, and designs a hypothesis-test-guided dataset ownership verification based on the proposed watermark.
2408.05500.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2602.03380.title: Seeing Through the Chain: Mitigate Hallucination in Multimodal Reasoning Models via CoT Compression and Contrastive Preference Optimization
2602.03380.tldr: A reasoning-enhanced preference tuning scheme that constructs training pairs using high-quality AI feedback and a multimodal hallucination-inducing mechanism that elicits models'inherent hallucination patterns via carefully crafted inducers, yielding informative negative signals for contrastive correction are introduced.

2601.03416.title: GAMBIT: A Gamified Jailbreak Framework for Multimodal Large Language Models
2601.03416.tldr: This work proposes GAMBI} (Gamified Adversarial Multimodal Breakout via Instructional Traps), a novel multimodal jailbreak framework that decomposes and reassembles harmful visual semantics, then constructs a gamified scene that drives the model to explore, reconstruct intent, and answer as part of winning the game.
2601.03416.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2412.05529.title: Upcycling Noise for Federated Unlearning
2412.05529.tldr: It is demonstrated that the noise added in DPFL can endow the unlearning model with a certain level of indistinguishability after local model retraction, and then fortify the degree of unlearning through global noise calibration, resulting in an unlearning model that is statistically indistinguishable from the retrained model.

2605.00123.title: Minimal, Local, Causal Explanations for Jailbreak Success in Large Language Models
2605.00123.tldr: LOCA, a method that gives Local, CAusal explanations of jailbreak success by identifying a minimal set of interpretable, intermediate representation changes that causally induce model refusal on an otherwise successful jailbreak request, is introduced.

2606.18924.title: Who Wins the Conflict? Mechanistic Interpretability of Text Bias in Audio LLMs
2606.18924.tldr: Back-patching is leveraged, a training-free intervention that routes late-layer audio activations back into earlier layers, enabling them to overcome textual suppression and demonstrate a mechanistic route to mitigating text dominance under conflict.

2608.28312.title: AIM: Anchor Identity Features, Then Match for Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning
2608.28312.tldr: AIM is proposed, a two-stage method that anchors an identity-forgetting target with a universal visual prompt and then matches the vision encoder to that target under a Fisher-based constraint, which achieves competitive identity forgetting while preserving non-deleted identities, prior knowledge, and visual perception on the same images.

2608.30649.title: Where Identity Lives: Localized, Retain-Free Identity Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.30649.tldr: PAVA pairs a forget loss with a visual-attribute anchor that preserves image-grounded behavior by distilling the model's own pre-unlearning answers from the forget images alone and gives the strongest forget-retain trade-off among forget-set-only methods and remains competitive with retain-based baselines.

2605.24550.title: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering and Reinforcing via Temporary Jailbreaking for Safe Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models
2605.24550.tldr: A Buffer-and-Reinforce fine-tuning framework that buffers harmful updates during user fine-tuning and reinforces safety after adaptation and achieves superior safety and utility with no additional safety data during user fine-tuning and minimal computational cost is proposed.

2505.21556.title: Benign-to-Toxic Jailbreaking: Inducing Harmful Responses from Harmless Prompts
2505.21556.tldr: This work proposes a new paradigm: Benign-to-Toxic (B2T) jailbreak, which outperforms prior approaches, transfers in black-box settings, and complements text-based jailbreaks.

2608.02681.title: Safety in Batches? Understanding and Mitigating Safety Failures in Batch Prompting
2608.02681.tldr: It is shown that the success of batch prompting for utility does not extend to safety: a harmful question that is reliably refused in isolation can elicit a harmful response when embedded in a batch of benign questions.

2503.10894.title: HyperDAS: Towards Automating Mechanistic Interpretability with Hypernetworks
2503.10894.tldr: HyperDAS is presented, a transformer-based hypernetwork architecture that automatically locates the token-positions of the residual stream that a concept is realized in and constructs features of those residual stream vectors for the concept.

2511.04638.title: Addressing divergent representations from causal interventions on neural networks
2511.04638.tldr: This work demonstrates theoretically and empirically that common causal intervention techniques often do shift internal representations away from the natural distribution of the target model, and provides a theoretical analysis of two cases of harmful and pernicious divergences.

2602.20904.title: Transcoder Adapters for Reasoning-Model Diffing
2602.20904.tldr: Insight into reasoning training is provided and transcoder adapters, a technique for learning an interpretable approximation of the difference in MLP computation before and after fine-tuning, is introduced.

2509.03647.title: Breaking the Mirror: Activation-Based Mitigation of Self-Preference in LLM Evaluators
2509.03647.tldr: Results show that steering vectors can reduce unjustified self-preference bias by up to 97\%, substantially outperforming prompting and direct preference optimization baselines, yet steering vectors are unstable on legitimate self-preference and unbiased agreement, implying self-preference spans multiple or nonlinear directions.

2607.18820.title: CASE: Causal Alignment and Structural Enforcement for Improving Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
2607.18820.tldr: Experiments show that CASE achieves a 37\% average per-setting relative improvement in overall CoT faithfulness over the strongest baselines, exhibits stronger cross-dataset faithfulness transfer, and maintains competitive average accuracy.

2605.24960.title: Investigating the Interplay between Contextual and Parametric Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness under Optimization
2605.24960.tldr: Across three models, two datasets, and six faithfulness metrics, it is found that the two paradigms are positively coupled, yet asymmetric: optimizing towards parametric faithfulness yields consistent gains across both paradigms, whereas the contextual counterpart delivers more variable gains.

2606.13209.title: Understanding helpfulness and harmless tension in reward models
2606.13209.tldr: This work identifies neurons associated with each objective and finds that these neurons causally support their corresponding objectives while often negatively affecting the opposing one, contributing to alignment tension in reward models trained under helpfulness only, harmlessness-only, and mixed-objective settings.

2506.15538.title: Capturing Polysemanticity with PRISM: A Multi-Concept Feature Description Framework
2506.15538.tldr: This work introduces Polysemantic FeatuRe Identification and Scoring Method (PRISM), a novel framework specifically designed to capture the complexity of features in LLMs that produces more nuanced descriptions that account for both monosemantic and polysemantic behavior.

2510.01048.title: Interpreting Language Models Through Concept Descriptions: A Survey
2510.01048.tldr: This paper provides the first survey of the emerging field of concept descriptions for model components and abstractions, charting the key methods for generating these descriptions, the evolving landscape of automated and human metrics for evaluating them, and the datasets that underpin this research.
2510.01048.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2603.00523.title: CIRCUS: Circuit Consensus under Uncertainty via Stability Ensembles
2603.00523.tldr: CIRCUS is introduced, which reframes circuit discovery as a problem of uncertainty over explanations and yields a principled core/contingent/noise decomposition that separates robust structure from threshold-sensitive artifacts, with negligible overhead.

2604.00770.title: Thinking Wrong in Silence: Backdoor Attacks on Continuous Latent Reasoning
2604.00770.tldr: ThoughtSteer perturbs a single embedding vector at the input layer; the model's own multi-pass reasoning amplifies this perturbation into a hijacked latent trajectory that reliably produces the attacker's chosen answer, while remaining structurally invisible to every token-level defense.

2606.01695.title: CANARY: Zero-Label Detection of Fine-Tuning Contamination in Language Models
2606.01695.tldr: CANA (Contamination Auditor via Neural Activation Representation Yield), a zero-label checkpoint auditor that detects this hidden shift directly from two forward passes over an unlabeled prompt set, is introduced, the first zero-label framework to detect, verify, prioritize, and remediate supply-chain contamination from hidden states alone.

2512.07059.title: Replicating TEMPEST at Scale: Multi-Turn Adversarial Attacks Against Trillion-Parameter Frontier Models
2512.07059.tldr: It is established that current alignment techniques remain fundamentally vulnerable to adaptive multi-turn attacks regardless of model scale, while identifying deliberative inference as a promising defense direction.

2602.08311.title: Moral Sycophancy in Vision Language Models
2602.08311.tldr: This first systematic study of moral sycophancy in VLMs is presented, analyzing ten widely-used models on the Moralise and M^3oralBench datasets under explicit user disagreement and revealing that VLMs frequently produce morally incorrect follow-up responses even when their initial judgments are correct.

2512.19350.title: PENDULUM: A Benchmark for Assessing Sycophancy in Multimodal Large Language Models
2512.19350.tldr: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark, \textit{PENDULUM}, comprises approximately 2,000 human-curated Visual Question Answering pairs specifically designed to elicit sycophantic responses, and proposes novel metrics to quantify sycophancy in visual reasoning, offering deeper insights into its manifestations across different multimodal contexts.

2603.27664.title: Investigating the Influence of Language on Sycophantic Behavior of Multilingual LLMs
2603.27664.tldr: This work investigates how the language influences sycophantic responses in large language models and provides a granular analysis of how language shapes model agreeableness across sensitive topics, revealing systematic cultural and linguistic patterns.

2603.12298.title: Global Evolutionary Steering: Refining Activation Steering Control via Cross-Layer Consistency
2603.12298.tldr: Global Evolutionary Refined Steering (GER-steer) is proposed, a training-free framework that grounded in the geometric stability of the network's representation evolution that exploits this global signal to rectify raw steering vectors, effectively decoupling robust semantic intent from orthogonal artifacts.

2601.23149.title: Hearing is Believing? Evaluating and Analyzing Audio Language Model Sycophancy with SYAUDIO
2601.23149.tldr: SYAUDIO is introduced, the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating sycophancy in ALMs, consisting of 4,319 audio questions spanning Audio Perception, Audio Reasoning, Audio Math, and Audio Ethics, and it is demonstrated that supervised fine-tuning with chain-of-thought data is an effective mitigation strategy for reducing sycophantic behavior in ALMs.

2512.17911.title: Towards Reasoning-Preserving Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
2512.17911.tldr: RMLLMU-Bench is the first benchmark for RMLLM unlearning that extends standard forgetting metrics with dedicated measures of reasoning leakage and reasoning retention, and proposes R-MUSE, a training-free and inference-time intervention framework that steers internal representations to forget both answers and reasoning traces while explicitly preserving general reasoning.

2603.08486.title: Visual Self-Fulfilling Alignment: Shaping Safety-Oriented Personas via Threat-Related Images
2603.08486.tldr: This work extends the self-fulfilling mechanism from text to visual modalities, offering a label-free approach to VLMs alignment, and demonstrates that VSFA reduces the attack success rate, improves response quality, and mitigates over-refusal while preserving general capabilities.
2603.08486.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2603.10771.title: Word Recovery in Large Language Models Enables Character-Level Tokenization Robustness
2603.10771.tldr: A decoding-based method is introduced and a fine-grained attention analysis is conducted, showing that in-group attention among characters belonging to the same canonical token is critical for word recovery: masking such attention in early layers substantially reduces both recovery scores and task performance.

2510.10205.title: PIXEL: Adaptive Steering Via Position-wise Injection with eXact Estimated Levels under Subspace Calibration
2510.10205.tldr: Position-wise Injection with eXact Estimated Levels (PIXEL) is proposed, a position-wise activation steering framework that learns a property-aligned subspace from dual views and selects intervention strength via a constrained geometric objective with a closed-form solution, thereby adapting to token-level sensitivity without global hyperparameter tuning.

2508.10599.title: Adaptive Multi-Subspace Representation Steering for Attribute Alignment in Large Language Models
2508.10599.tldr: Multi-Subspace Representation Steering (MSRS) is proposed, a novel framework for effective multi-attribute steering via subspace representation fine-tuning that significantly reduces attribute conflicts, surpasses existing methods across a range of attributes, and generalizes effectively to diverse downstream tasks.

2509.21979.title: Benchmarking and Mitigating Sycophancy in Medical Vision Language Models
2509.21979.tldr: A Medical benchmark is introduced that applies multiple templates to VLMs in a hierarchical medical visual question answering task and reduces sycophancy while maintaining interpretability and consistently outperforms baseline methods, laying the necessary foundation for the robust and secure integration of VLMs.

2604.12817.title: Understanding and Improving Continuous Adversarial Training for LLMs via In-context Learning Theory
2604.12817.tldr: The first theoretical analysis of CAT on LLMs based on in-context learning (ICL) theory is presented and a robust generalization bound is proved that has a negative correlation with the perturbation radius in the embedding space of LLMs during AT.

2603.13420.title: Accelerating Suffix Jailbreak attacks with Prefix-Shared KV-cache
2603.13420.tldr: Prefix-Shared KV Cache (PSKV) is presented, a plug-and-play inference optimization technique tailored for jailbreak suffix generation that reduces inference time and peak memory usage and enables more aggressive batching strategies that would otherwise be limited by memory constraints.

2604.02668.title: Too Polite to Disagree: Understanding Sycophancy Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
2604.02668.tldr: It is found that providing sycophancy priors reduces the influence of sycophancy-prone peers, mitigates error-cascades, and improves final discussion accuracy by an absolute 10.5%.

2511.17100.title: Geometric-disentangelment Unlearning
2511.17100.tldr: Geometric-disentanglement Unlearning (GU), a lightweight and theoretically grounded projection that can be plug-and-play to existing gradient-based unlearning methods to mitigate forget-retain side effects, is proposed.

2506.06444.title: Saffron-1: Safety Inference Scaling
2506.06444.tldr: This work pioneers inference scaling for robust and effective LLM safety against emerging threats, revealing that conventional inference scaling techniques perform poorly in safety contexts, even falling short of basic approaches like Best-of-N Sampling.

2410.03642.title: Aligning LLMs with Individual Preferences via Interaction
2410.03642.tldr: This work trains LLMs that can ''interact to align'', essentially cultivating the meta-skill of LLMs to implicitly infer the unspoken personalized preferences of the current user through multi-turn conversations, and then dynamically align their following behaviors and responses to these inferred preferences.

2501.14073.title: LLMs are Vulnerable to Malicious Prompts Disguised as Scientific Language
2501.14073.tldr: This work reveals that many state-of-the-art LLMs are vulnerable to malicious requests hidden behind scientific language, and calls for a more careful investigation on the use of scientific data for training LLMs.

2510.07822.title: SIMU: Selective Influence Machine Unlearning
2510.07822.tldr: This work proposes Selective Influence Machine Unlearning (SIMU), a two-step framework that enhances second-order optimizer-based unlearning by selectively updating only the critical neurons responsible for encoding the forget-set, achieving comparable unlearning efficacy while substantially outperforming current methods in retaining the model's original knowledge.

2407.18008.title: GermanPartiesQA: Benchmarking Commercial Large Language Models and AI Companions for Political Alignment and Sycophancy
2407.18008.tldr: GermanPartiesQA, a benchmark of 418 political statements from German Voting Advice Applications across 11 elections, is introduced to evaluate six commercial LLMs and reveals consistent alignment patterns and degree of political steerability for each model across temperature settings and experiments.
2407.18008.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2603.24543.title: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors
2603.24543.tldr: A systematic safety audit of steering vectors obtained with Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), a widely used steering approach, under a unified evaluation protocol shows that steering vectors consistently influence the success rate of jailbreak attacks, with stronger amplification under simple template-based attacks.
2603.24543.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.19292.title: The safety failures we are not instrumenting: a perspective on hidden safety-critical challenges in modern AI systems
2607.19292.tldr: It is argued that a central safety challenge in modern AI systems is increasingly not only whether a model emits a harmful response, but whether the broader socio-technical system preserves the conditions under which errors remain visible, contestable, containable, and recoverable.

2601.20568.title: Reinforcement Unlearning via Group Relative Policy Optimization
2601.20568.tldr: PURGE shows that framing LLM unlearning as a verifiable task enables more reliable, efficient, and scalable forgetting, suggesting a promising new direction for unlearning research that combines theoretical guarantees, improved safety, and practical deployment efficiency.

2605.14604.title: Sycophancy is an Educational Safety Risk: Why LLM Tutors Need Sycophancy Benchmarks

2512.00656.title: Sycophancy Claims about Language Models: The Missing Human-in-the-Loop
2512.00656.tldr: Analysis of methodological challenges in measuring LLM sycophancy highlights the difficulties in distinguishing sycophantic responses from related concepts in AI alignment and offers actionable recommendations for future research.

2511.05919.title: Injecting Falsehoods: Adversarial Man-in-the-Middle Attacks Undermining Factual Recall in LLMs
2511.05919.tldr: This work proposes the first principled attack evaluation on LLM factual memory under prompt injection via Xmera, the authors' novel, theory-grounded MitM framework, and perturbing the input given to "victim"LLMs in three closed-book and fact-based QA settings undermines the correctness of the responses and assess the uncertainty of their generation process.

2608.08383.title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible
2608.08383.tldr: This work identifies and removes a separable component in the vector that disrupts the model's safety mechanisms but contributes little to the steering objective, and offers a post-hoc correction to steering vectors that mitigates their safety cost.

2508.02087.title: When Truth Is Overridden: Uncovering the Internal Origins of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
2508.02087.tldr: It is highlighted that sycophancy is not a surface-level artifact but emerges from a structural override of learned knowledge in deeper layers, with implications for alignment and truthful AI systems.

2506.07180.title: Flattery in Motion: Benchmarking and Analyzing Sycophancy in Video-LLMs
2506.07180.tldr: VISE (Video-LLM Sycophancy Benchmarking and Evaluation) is proposed, the first benchmark designed to evaluate sycophantic behavior in state-of-the-art Video-LLMs across diverse question formats, prompt biases, and visual reasoning tasks, and two potential training-free mitigation strategies revealing potential paths for reducing sycophantic bias.
2506.07180.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.06419.title: MONICA: Real-Time Monitoring and Calibration of Chain-of-Thought Sycophancy in Large Reasoning Models
2511.06419.tldr: MONICA is a novel Monitor-guided Calibration framework that monitors and mitigates sycophancy during model inference at the level of reasoning steps, without requiring the model to finish generating its complete answer.

2511.08525.title: Investigating CoT Monitorability in Large Reasoning Models
2511.08525.tldr: This paper provides empirical evidence and correlation analyses between verbalization quality, monitor reliability, and LLM performance across mathematical, scientific, and ethical domains, and proposes MoME, a new paradigm in which LLMs monitor other models'misbehavior through their CoT and provide structured judgments along with supporting evidence.

2510.23264.title: PAHQ: Accelerating Automated Circuit Discovery through Mixed-Precision Inference Optimization
2510.23264.tldr: This training-free approach provides a practical and novel pathway for accelerating mechanistic interpretability methods by optimizing the efficiency of each individual patching operation and readily integrates with existing edge-based circuit discovery techniques by modifying the attention computation mechanism.

2603.11949.title: Delayed Backdoor Attacks: Exploring the Temporal Dimension as a New Attack Surface in Pre-Trained Models
2603.11949.tldr: This study provides the first empirical evidence that the temporal dimension constitutes a viable yet unprotected attack surface in PTMs, underscoring the need for next-generation, stateful, and time-aware defense mechanisms.

2410.06606.title: Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning in Large Language Models
2410.06606.tldr: The limitations of fine-tuning-based unlearning are explored through activation patching and parameter restoration experiments, revealing that these methods alter the model’s knowledge retrieval process, rather than genuinely erasing the problematic knowledge embedded in the model parameters.
2410.06606.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2404.00486.title: Dialectical Alignment: Resolving the Tension of 3H and Security Threats of LLMs
2404.00486.tldr: The dialectical alignment model improves poisoned data attack defense by 20 and does not require any additional prompt engineering or prior declaration of ``you may be attacked`` to the LLM' context window.

2602.10388.title: Less is Enough: Synthesizing Diverse Data in LLM Feature Space with Sparse Autoencoders
2602.10388.tldr: This work introduces Feature Activation Coverage (FAC), which measures data diversity in an interpretable feature space, and proposes a diversity-driven data synthesis framework, named FAC Synthesis, that first uses a sparse autoencoder to identify missing features from a seed dataset, and then generates synthetic samples that explicitly reflect these features.

2604.05279.title: Pressure, What Pressure? Sycophancy Disentanglement in Language Models via Reward Decomposition
2604.05279.tldr: This work proposes the first approach to sycophancy reduction via reward decomposition, introducing a multi-component Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) reward that decomposes the training signal into five terms: pressure resistance, context fidelity, position consistency, agreement suppression, and factual correctness.

2605.18721.title: General Preference Reinforcement Learning
2605.18721.tldr: The General Preference Model (GPM), which embeds responses into skew-symmetric subspaces and represents preference as a structured, intransitivity-aware comparison, is proposed, and General Preference Reinforcement Learning (GPRL), which carries the $k$-way structure through to the policy update.

2602.00931.title: Continuous-Utility Direct Preference Optimization
2602.00931.tldr: It is proved that learning with K strategies yields a Theta(K log K) improvement in sample complexity over binary preferences, and that DPO converges to the entropy-regularized utility-maximizing policy.

2607.23976.title: Tag Questions and the Generational Reversal of Sycophancy Across 45 Language Models
2607.23976.tldr: Appending a two-word confirmation tag to a decision question --"Is X the better choice?"versus"X is the better choice, right?"-- changes whether a language model endorses the choice, and the tag's polarity matters more than its presence.

2606.06306.title: Decomposing Factual Sycophancy in Language Models: How Size and Instruction Tuning Shape Robustness

2605.05403.title: When Helpfulness Becomes Sycophancy: Sycophancy is a Boundary Failure Between Social Alignment and Epistemic Integrity in Large Language Models
2605.05403.tldr: It is argued that sycophancy should be understood as agreement alone, but as alignment behavior that displaces independent epistemic judgment, and a three-condition framework for sycophancy is proposed, consisting of alignment targets, mechanisms, and severity.

2601.14553.title: Self-Blinding and Counterfactual Self-Simulation Mitigate Biases and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
2601.14553.tldr: It is shown that large language models suffer from similar limitations in their ability to approximate what decisions they would make under counterfactual knowledge in offsetting gender and race biases and overcoming sycophancy, and that access to the responses of a blinded replica enables fairer decisions, while providing greater transparency to distinguish implicit from intentionally biased behavior.

2606.07532.title: Durable Evaluation Framework: Adversarial Arbitration for Sycophancy Reduction in Large Language Models
2606.07532.tldr: Durable Evaluation Framework (DEF) Arbitration is presented, a multi-agent architecture that mitigates identity-framed sycophancy by arbitrating between two models tuned to opposing DEFs, with a pragmatist synthesizer evaluating both arguments blind to their origins.

2601.11563.title: Human-like Social Compliance in Large Language Models: Unifying Sycophancy and Conformity through Signal Competition Dynamics
2601.11563.tldr: The Signal Competition Mechanism is introduced, a unified framework validated by assessing behavioral correlations across 15 LLMs and performing latent-space probing on three representative open-source models, and provides a blueprint for transitioning from instructional adherence to robust epistemic integrity.

2602.04918.title: Simulated Adoption: Decoupling Magnitude and Direction in LLM In-Context Conflict Resolution
2602.04918.tldr: A layer-wise geometric analysis across Qwen-3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B, and GLM-4-9B suggests that models do not "unlearn" or suppress the magnitude of internal truths but rather employ a mechanism of geometric displacement to bypass the correct unembedding vector, effectively simulating adoption while preserving the original structural magnitude.

2511.00230.title: Neural Transparency: Mechanistic Interpretability Interfaces for Anticipating Model Behaviors for Personalized AI
2511.00230.tldr: This work offers a path for how mechanistic interpretability can be operationalized for non-technical users, establishing a method for safer, more aligned human-AI interactions.
2511.00230.venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces

2607.07003.title: Dissociating the Internal Representations of Sycophancy in LLMs
2607.07003.tldr: It is found that different LLMs represent these subtypes differently, with either more aligned or more distinct representations, and this insight is applied to improve representational interventions for reducing sycophancy.

2605.15455.title: Multi-Turn Neural Transparency: Surfacing Neural Activations Improves User Calibration to LLM Behavioral Drift
2605.15455.tldr: Multi-turn neural transparency is introduced, an interface that surfaces an LLM's internal neural activations in real time to help users anticipate and recognize how behaviors change across turns to suggest that surfacing internal model representations to everyday users is a meaningful step toward more transparent and informed human-AI interaction.

2508.19316.title: Sycophancy as compositions of Atomic Psychometric Traits

2510.04058.title: Unlearning in Diffusion models under Data Constraints: A Variational Inference Approach
2510.04058.tldr: This work proposes a machine unlearning methodology that can prevent the generation of outputs containing undesired features from a pre-trained diffusion model in such a data-constrained setting and validate the effectiveness of the method through comprehensive experiments for both class unlearning and feature unlearning.

2607.20146.title: Gotta Catch them all: the modes of Sycophancy
2607.20146.tldr: Analysis of three hypothesized modes of sycophancy shows that sycophancy is not a monolithic tendency, but a structured family of representationally and computationally distinct modes, motivating more precise measurement and intervention.

2508.21324.title: Distribution-Aware Feature Selection for SAEs
2508.21324.tldr: The introduced Sampled-SAE reframes BatchTopK as a tunable, distribution-aware family, which improves average reconstruction but risks an"activation lottery," where rare high-magnitude features crowd out more informative but lower-magnitude ones.

2608.05624.title: Measuring and Detecting Harmful AI Sycophancy
2608.05624.tldr: It is demonstrated that detection performance drops on unseen models and an initial approach is proposed to address this challenge, and it is shown that detecting PSRS is feasible from the response text alone, and detectors need to learn subtle PSRS patterns from the training data.

2606.07897.title: Pander Score: A Continuous Measure of Sycophancy as Epistemic Deference
2606.07897.tldr: The Pander Score is proposed: a continuous score representing how sensitive the support expressed in a model's output is to the attitude expressed in a user's prompt, and is released as an easy-to-update benchmark and measurement pipeline for output-level sycophancy evaluation.

2505.04260.title: Steerable Chatbots: Exploring Personalization Control Interfaces via LLM Activation Steering
2505.04260.tldr: A within-subjects user study in cold-start personalization tasks shows the potential for steerable chatbots to align better with underlying user preferences than prompting alone, while revealing heterogeneous values around control, persistence, and transparency in LLM personalization.

2608.01017.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
2608.01017.tldr: The results show that medical sycophancy depends as much on how a model is challenged and evaluated as on which model is tested, and fabricated evidence has opposite effects across interaction structures.

2604.02423.title: SWAY: A Counterfactual Computational Linguistic Approach to Measuring and Mitigating Sycophancy
2604.02423.tldr: SWAY, an unsupervised computational linguistic measure of sycophancy, is introduced and a counterfactual prompting mechanism to identify how much a model's agreement shifts under positive versus negative linguistic pressure is developed, isolating framing effects from content.

2602.00046.title: Extending Beacon to Hindi: Cultural Adaptation Drives Cross-Lingual Sycophancy
2602.00046.tldr: Findings indicate that alignment behaviors measured in English may not transfer uniformly across languages and that culturally grounded prompt framing plays a substantial role.

2607.21558.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning

2605.27288.title: It's Not Always Sycophancy: Measuring LLM Conformity as a Function of Epistemic Uncertainty
2605.27288.tldr: MUSE, a two-stage evaluation framework to disentangle the mechanisms driving LLM conformity, characterize two distinct factors that jointly drive conformity: sycophantic conformity, where a model aligns with user pushback even with absolute certainty in its initial response, and uncertainty-driven conformity, where a model's likelihood for conformity increases alongside its uncertainty.

2601.10467.title: User Detection and Response Patterns of Sycophantic Behavior in Conversational AI
2601.10467.tldr: It is found that users identify sycophantic behavior through methods like cross-platform comparison and consistency testing, and employ various mitigation strategies, including persona-based prompting and specific language engineering techniques.

2603.21409.title: The Illusion of Agreement with ChatGPT: Sycophancy and Beyond
2603.21409.tldr: The findings show that AI-induced harms require coordinated interventions across users, developers, and policymakers, and discuss design implications and future directions to mitigate the harms and ensure user benefits.

2606.10061.title: BenSyc: Benchmarking Conversational Sycophancy and Human Alignment in LLMs for Bengali Contexts

2608.23666.title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering
2608.23666.tldr: This work employs Inference Time Intervention (ITI) to jointly control both behaviors by learning separate steering directions for hallucination and sycophancy from contrastive clinical pairs and applying them to causally verified attention heads.

2607.01277.title: Cognitive Firewall: A Proactive, Zero-Trust, Multi-Gate Framework for LLM Safety
2607.01277.tldr: The Cognitive Firewall is presented, a proactive runtime oversight framework that interposes an independent oversight model between a user and a protected target mod l and indicates that decomposed, conversation level oversight can improve proactive containment and auditability for LLM safety.

2507.13410.title: Causal Language Control in Multilingual Transformers via Sparse Feature Steering
2507.13410.tldr: This work investigates whether sparse autoencoder features, previously shown to correlate with interpretable model behaviors, can be leveraged to steer the generated language of LLMs during inference and reveals that language steering is most effective in mid-to-late transformer layers.

2506.13901.title: Alignment Quality Index (AQI) : Beyond Refusals: AQI as an Intrinsic Alignment Diagnostic via Latent Geometry, Cluster Divergence, and Layer wise Pooled Representations
2506.13901.tldr: The Alignment Quality Index (AQI) is introduced, a novel geometric and prompt-invariant metric empirically assesses LLM alignment by analyzing the separation of safe and unsafe activations in latent space, and proposes the LITMUS dataset to facilitate robust evaluation under these challenging conditions.
2506.13901.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2509.00591.title: Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate: A Workflow for Reliable Benchmarks and Quantifying Evaluation Awareness
2509.00591.tldr: This work systematically quantify behavioral changes by manipulating the perceived context of prompts to demonstrate that evaluation awareness is a quantifiable and manipulable factor that directly influences LLM behavior, revealing that models are more prone to unsafe or deceptive outputs in perceived test environments.

2507.21141.title: The Geometry of Harmfulness in LLMs through Subconcept Probing
2507.21141.tldr: A multidimensional framework for probing and steering harmful content in model internals is introduced and it is found that dominant direction steering allows for near elimination of harmfulness with a low decrease in utility.

2503.11656.title: TRUTH DECAY: Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
2503.11656.tldr: TRUTH DECAY is introduced, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate sycophancy in extended dialogues, where language models must navigate iterative user feedback, challenges, and persuasion.

2602.13274.title: ProMoral-Bench: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Moral Reasoning and Safety in LLMs
2602.13274.tldr: Results show that compact, exemplar-guided scaffolds outperform complex multi-stage reasoning, providing higher UMSS scores and greater robustness at a lower token cost, and few-shot exemplars consistently enhance moral stability and jailbreak resistance.

2609.13841.title: Sweet Talkers: How Query Formulation Shapes Sycophancy in Romantic Relationship Advice
2609.13841.tldr: Consistent increases in framing and moral sycophancy across turns indicate that models become more likely to accept a user's stated premises and affirm their ethical stance as a dialogue progresses, suggesting that what a user implies matters more than how they phrase it.

2604.21564.title: Measuring Opinion Bias and Sycophancy via LLM-based Persuasion
2604.21564.tldr: This work proposes a method, released as the open-source llm-bias-bench, for discovering the opinions an LLM actually holds on contested topics under conditions that resemble real multi-turn interaction.

2603.18373.title: To See or To Please: Uncovering Visual Sycophancy and Split Beliefs in VLMs
2603.18373.tldr: A Tri-Layer Diagnostic Framework is introduced with three per-sample metrics: Latent Anomaly Detection, Visual Necessity Score, and Competition Score, which disentangle perception, dependency, and alignment failures and enable a training-free selective-prediction strategy yielding up to +9.5 percentage points accuracy at 50% coverage.

2601.12019.title: Acting Flatterers via LLMs Sycophancy: Combating Clickbait with LLMs Opposing-Stance Reasoning
2601.12019.tldr: A Self-renewal Opposing-stance Reasoning Generation (SORG) framework is designed that prompts LLMs to produce high-quality ''agree'' and ''disagree'' reasoning pairs for a given news title without requiring ground-truth labels and a local Opposing Reasoning-based Clickbait Detection (ORCD) model is developed.

2607.07903.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM Jailbreaks via Internal Attribution Graphs
2607.07903.tldr: A mechanistic framework for diagnosing LLM vulnerabilities using paired internal computation graphs, which represent prompt-specific inference as structured causal interactions among latent features, and proposes a unified framework that decomposes computation into invariant, suppressed, and emergent structures.

2609.04276.title: FailSAE: Towards Interpretable Failure Prediction for Vision-Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2609.04276.tldr: This work forms failure prediction as a classification task over sparse SAE latent activations and introduces a three-stage failure-aware training pipeline that encourages the learned latent directions to remain interpretable while becoming more informative for failure prediction.

2607.10411.title: Mitigating LLM Sycophancy in Code Smell Detection Using Evidence-Guided Reasoning Prompts
2607.10411.tldr: This paper presents the first systematic empirical study of sycophancy bias in LLM-based code smell detection, and proposes Evidence-Guided Debiasing Prompting (EGDP), a structured prompting strategy that enforces evidence-first reasoning and reduces decision instability and improves robustness.

2605.14544.title: Complacent, Not Sycophantic: Reframing Large Language Models and Designing AI Literacy for Complacent Machines
2605.14544.tldr: Because complacent models reinforce users'prior beliefs, it is argued that AI literacy educational approaches should particularly focus on strategies to counter confirmation bias.

2604.24668.title: The Price of Agreement: Measuring LLM Sycophancy in Agentic Financial Applications
2604.24668.tldr: This work focuses on evaluating sycophancy that LLMs display in agentic financial tasks and finds the models show only low to modest drops in performance in the face of user rebuttals or contradictions to the reference answer, which distinguishes sycophancy that models display in financial agentic settings from findings in prior work.

2606.10949.title: Recalling Too Well: Sycophancy Evaluation and Mitigation in Memory-Augmented Models
2606.10949.tldr: It is shown that persistent memory systems make models less correct by amplifying sycophancy, wherein models prioritize agreement with users over accuracy, and proposes three lightweight mitigations to a memory system that substantially reduce sycophancy while matching or exceeding memory systems at factual recall.

2603.03332.title: Fragile Thoughts: How Large Language Models Handle Chain-of-Thought Perturbations
2603.03332.tldr: Heterogeneous vulnerability patterns show that model size serve as a protective factor against many perturbations but not always, and scaling relationships show that model size serve as a protective factor against many perturbations but not always.

2508.16652.title: Do VLMs Have Bad Eyes? Diagnosing Compositional Failures via Mechanistic Interpretability
2508.16652.tldr: Evidence is shown that individual neurons in the MLP layers of CLIP's vision encoder represent multiple features, and this “super-position” directly hinders its compositional feature representation which consequently affects compositional reasoning and object binding capabilities.
2508.16652.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)

2504.18563.title: Backdoor Defense in Diffusion Models via Spatial Attention Unlearning
2504.18563.tldr: Spatial Attention Unlearning (SAU) is proposed, a novel technique for mitigating backdoor attacks in diffusion models that leverages latent space manipulation and spatial attention mechanisms to isolate and remove the latent representation of backdoor triggers, ensuring precise and efficient removal of malicious effects.

2508.18235.title: Sealing The Backdoor: Unlearning Adversarial Text Triggers In Diffusion Models Using Knowledge Distillation
2508.18235.tldr: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Cross-Attention Guidance with Cross-Attention Guidance (SKD-CAG) uses knowledge distillation to guide the model in correcting responses to poisoned prompts while maintaining image quality by exploiting the fact that the backdoored model still produces clean outputs in the absence of triggers.

2604.19139.title: The Rise of Verbal Tics in Large Language Models: A Systematic Analysis Across Frontier Models
2604.19139.tldr: It is demonstrated that verbal tics accumulate over multi-turn conversations, are amplified in subjective tasks, and show distinct cross-lingual patterns, underscore the alignment tax of current training paradigms and highlight the urgent need for more authentic human-AI interaction frameworks.

2604.04788.title: From Sycophancy to Deception: A Unified Taxonomy for LLM Spontaneous Misalignment
2604.04788.tldr: Applying a unified taxonomy of large language models to 50 existing benchmarks reveals that every benchmark tests fabrication while pragmatic distortion, attribution, and capability self-knowledge remain critically under-covered, and strategic deception benchmarks are nascent.

2411.04427.title: One fish, two fish, but not the whole sea: Alignment reduces language models' conceptual diversity
2411.04427.tldr: This work uses a new way of measuring the conceptual diversity of synthetically-generated LLM populations by relating the internal variability of simulated individuals to the population-level variability, and highlights potential trade-offs between increasing models'value alignment and decreasing the diversity of their conceptual representations.
2411.04427.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.00617.title: Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering
2511.00617.tldr: A unified account of prompt-based and activation-based control of LLM behavior, and a methodology for empirically predicting the effects of these interventions are offered.

2605.17173.title: Why Do Safety Guardrails Degrade Across Languages?
2605.17173.tldr: A latent variable model is introduced, a Multi-Group Item Response Theory (IRT) framework, that decouples language-agnostic safety robustness, intrinsic prompt hardness, global language processing difficulty, and a prompt-specific cross-lingual safety gap, enabling fairer cross-lingual safety evaluation and targeted improvements in dataset construction.

2604.27633.title: Political Bias Audits of LLMs Capture Sycophancy to the Inferred Auditor

2506.19708.title: Uncovering Conceptual Blindspots in Generative Image Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
2506.19708.tldr: This work proposes a theoretically grounded framework for systematically identifying conceptual blindspots in generative models by assessing their conceptual fidelity with respect to the underlying data-generating process.

2404.07129.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation

2604.24693.title: Contextual Linear Activation Steering of Language Models
2604.24693.tldr: Contextual Linear Activation Steering (CLAS) is introduced, a method that dynamically adapts linear activation steering to context-dependent steering strengths and consistently outperforms standard linear activation steering and matches or exceeds the performance of ReFT and LoRA in settings with limited labeled data.

2609.14151.title: Signatures of Steerability in Activation Space of Language Models
2609.14151.tldr: This work makes this dataset-dependence claim more rigorous and shows that simple separation metrics strongly correlate with the downstream steerability of language models across diverse settings, even after controlling for layers and dataset effects.

2502.09755.title: Jailbreak Attack Initializations as Extractors of Compliance Directions
2502.09755.tldr: This work presents that each gradient-based jailbreak attack and subsequent initialization gradually converge to a single compliance direction that suppresses refusal, thereby enabling an efficient transition from refusal to compliance.
2502.09755.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2602.02600.title: Step-Wise Refusal Dynamics in Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
2602.02600.tldr: It is shown that diffusion remasking can promote recovery from harmful intermediate generations, provide evidence that this behavior is tied to the sampling mechanism, and demonstrate that switching from AR to diffusion sampling improves jailbreak robustness, including under fixed model weights.

2601.16390.title: Cross-Lingual Activation Steering for Multilingual Language Models
2601.16390.tldr: This work proposes Cross-Lingual Activation Steering (CLAS), a training-free inference-time intervention that selectively modulates neuron activations in existing models to unlock latent multilingual capacity in existing models without modification to model weights.

2511.07691.title: CAPO: Confidence Aware Preference Optimization Learning for Multilingual Preferences
2511.07691.tldr: Confidence-Aware Preference Optimization (CAPO) is proposed, which replaces DPO's fixed treatment of preference pairs with a dynamic loss scaling mechanism based on a relative reward, and improves alignment by widening the gap between preferred and dispreferred responses across languages.

2602.01699.title: Mitigating loss of control in advanced AI systems through instrumental goal trajectories
2602.01699.tldr: Instrumental goal trajectories offer concrete avenues for defining capability levels and for broadening how corrigibility and interruptibility are implemented, shifting attention from model properties alone to the organisational systems that enable them.

2510.25471.title: An Aristotelian ontology of instrumental goals: Structural features to be managed and not failures to be eliminated
2510.25471.tldr: An exploratory Aristotelian framework that treats advanced AI systems as complex artefacts whose ends are externally imposed through design, training and deployment is offered and motivates for governance and management approaches that treat instrumental goals as features of advanced AI systems to be managed rather than anomalies eliminable by technical interventions.

2607.07605.title: User identity conditions moral wrongness ratings in non-reasoning large language models
2607.07605.tldr: It is demonstrated that unintended contextual conditioning via user identity permeates LLM moral evaluations, posing questions for the AI value alignment discourse regarding how to define acceptable bounds for role-based moral divergence.

2511.16035.title: Liars' Bench: Evaluating Lie Detectors for Language Models
2511.16035.tldr: Evaluating three black- and white-box lie detection techniques on LIARS'BENCH finds that existing techniques systematically fail to identify certain types of lies, especially in settings where it's not possible to determine whether the model lied from the transcript alone.

2503.17755.title: Improving Preference Extraction In LLMs By Identifying Latent Knowledge Through Classifying Probes
2503.17755.tldr: This work proposes using linear classifying probes, trained by leveraging differences between contrasting pairs of prompts, to directly access LLMs' latent knowledge and extract more accurate preferences, suggesting linear probing offers an accurate, robust and computationally efficient approach for LLM-as-judge tasks while providing interpretable insights into how models encode judgement-relevant knowledge.
2503.17755.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.24014.title: Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models
2606.24014.tldr: Results suggest that RL to reinforce beneficial behavior in realistic domains can produce models that are more robustly aligned with human flourishing, and models trained with beneficial trait RL show improved persistence.

2512.23508.title: Why AI Safety Requires Uncertainty, Incomplete Preferences, and Non-Archimedean Utilities
2512.23508.tldr: It is shown that addressing these challenges requires AI agents that can reason under uncertainty and handle both incomplete and non-Archimedean preferences.

2603.16576.title: REFORGE: Multi-modal Attacks Reveal Vulnerable Concept Unlearning in Image Generation Models
2603.16576.tldr: REFORGE, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates IGMU robustness via adversarial image prompts, is presented, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates IGMU robustness via adversarial image prompts.

2601.08623.title: SafeRedir: Prompt Embedding Redirection for Robust Unlearning in Image Generation Models
2601.08623.tldr: SafeRedir is introduced, a lightweight inference-time framework for robust unlearning via prompt embedding redirection that achieves effective unlearning capability, high semantic and perceptual preservation, robust image quality, and enhanced resistance to adversarial attacks.

2606.08682.title: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
2606.08682.tldr: It is shown that activation steering can induce broad misalignment, even in the recent Qwen-3.5 series, and properties of AS-induced EM are characterized, including steering magnitude, the low-rank structure of the steering subspace, and the number of epochs during steering-vector construction.

2406.14507.title: On Newton's Method to Unlearn Neural Networks
2406.14507.tldr: CureNewton's method is proposed, a principle approach that leverages cubic regularization to handle the Hessian degeneracy effectively and can achieve competitive unlearning performance to the state-of-the-art algorithm in practical unlearning settings, while being theoretically justified and efficient in running time.

2605.25629.title: When In-Distribution Gains Fail: Evaluating Weak-to-Strong Reward Models under Preference Shift
2605.25629.tldr: This work proposes Representation Anchoring (Anchor), a simple yet effective regularizer that constrains excessive drift from the pretrained strong model's representation space during fine-tuning, while still allowing task-relevant adaptation.

2501.16629.title: CHiP: Cross-modal Hierarchical Direct Preference Optimization for Multimodal LLMs
2501.16629.tldr: This work introduces a visual preference optimization module within the DPO framework, enabling MLLMs to learn from both textual and visual preferences simultaneously, and proposes a hierarchical textual preference optimization module that allows the model to capture preferences at multiple granular levels, including response, segment, and token levels.

2604.06154.title: Exclusive Unlearning
2604.06154.tldr: It is demonstrated that through Exclusive Unlearning, it is possible to obtain a model that ensures safety against a wide range of inputs, including jailbreaks, while maintaining the ability to respond to diverse instructions related to specific domains such as medicine and mathematics.

2503.06394.title: How a Bilingual LM Becomes Bilingual: Tracing Internal Representations with Sparse Autoencoders
2503.06394.tldr: This study explores how bilingual language models develop complex internal representations with a focus on the effects of training steps, layers, and model sizes, and shows that language models first learn languages separately, and then gradually form bilingual alignments, particularly in the mid layers.
2503.06394.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2407.16951.title: Towards Transfer Unlearning: Empirical Evidence of Cross-Domain Bias Mitigation
2407.16951.tldr: An unlearning-based approach to debiasing in LLMs by performing gradient ascent on hate speech against minority groups, which unlearns the harmful part of the text, and reveals an unexpected potential for cross-domain transfer unlearning.

2509.17530.title: An Unlearning Framework for Continual Learning
2509.17530.tldr: This work proposes UnCLe, an Unlearning framework for Continual Learning that employs a hypernetwork that learns to generate task-specific network parameters, using task embeddings, and demonstrates its ability to sequentially perform multiple learning and unlearning operations with minimal disruption to previously acquired knowledge.

2605.12765.title: Inference-Time Machine Unlearning via Gated Activation Redirection
2605.12765.tldr: GUARD-IT is introduced, a training- and gradient-free method that unlearns via input-dependent activation steering at inference time that supports continual unlearning without retraining, and remains effective under quantization, a scenario in which parameter-editing methods degrade.

2602.13151.title: Quantization-Robust LLM Unlearning via Low-Rank Adaptation
2602.13151.tldr: This work freezes the base model and concentrates unlearning into trainable adapters so that the effective update is preserved after quantization, and proposes quantization-robust unlearning via low-rank adaptation (LoRA).

2504.15827.title: DualOptim: Enhancing Efficacy and Stability in Machine Unlearning with Dual Optimizers
2504.15827.tldr: Through extensive experiments, it is shown that DualOptim can significantly boost MU efficacy and stability across diverse tasks, including image classification, image generation, and large language models, making it a versatile approach to empower existing MU algorithms.

2605.21539.title: DualOptim+: Bridging Shared and Decoupled Optimizer States for Better Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models
2605.21539.tldr: This work proposes DualOptim+, a novel optimization framework for improving machine unlearning in large language models that introduces a base state to capture common representations shared by forgetting and retaining objectives and delta states to preserve objective-specific residuals.

2405.20778.title: Improved Generation of Adversarial Examples Against Safety-aligned LLMs
2405.20778.tldr: This paper appropriate the ideologies of effective methods among these transfer-based attacks, i.e., Skip Gradient Method and Intermediate Level Attack, into gradient-based adversarial prompt generation and achieve significant performance gains without introducing obvious computational cost.

2410.11317.title: Deciphering the Chaos: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Prompt Translation
2410.11317.tldr: This paper delves into the semantic meaning embedded in garbled adversarial prompts and proposes a novel method that "translates" them into coherent and human-readable natural language adversarial prompts and offers a new approach to discovering effective designs for jailbreak prompts.

2401.10371.title: Langevin Unlearning: A New Perspective of Noisy Gradient Descent for Machine Unlearning
2401.10371.tldr: Langevin unlearning is proposed, an unlearning framework based on noisy gradient descent with privacy guarantees for approximate unlearning problems, which unifies the DP learning process and the privacy-certified unlearning process with many algorithmic benefits.

2402.15159.title: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models
2402.15159.tldr: This research delineates a comprehensive framework for machine unlearning in pre-trained LLMs, encompassing a critical analysis of seven diverse unlearning methods, and establishes a robust benchmark for unlearning performance, demonstrating that these methods are over $10^5$ times more computationally efficient than retraining.
2402.15159.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2403.17105.title: Certified Machine Unlearning via Noisy Stochastic Gradient Descent
2403.17105.tldr: This work proposes to leverage projected noisy stochastic gradient descent for unlearning and establish its first approximate unlearning guarantee under the convexity assumption, and exhibits several benefits, including provable complexity saving compared to retraining, and supporting sequential and batch unlearning.

2506.05735.title: Do LLMs Really Forget? Evaluating Unlearning with Knowledge Correlation and Confidence Awareness
2506.05735.tldr: This work proposes a knowledge unlearning evaluation framework that more accurately captures the implicit structure of real-world knowledge by representing relevant factual contexts as knowledge graphs with associated confidence scores, and develops an inference-based evaluation protocol leveraging powerful LLMs as judges.

2412.08559.title: Underestimated Privacy Risks for Minority Populations in Large Language Model Unlearning
2412.08559.tldr: This work proposes a complementary, minority-aware evaluation framework for LLM unlearning efficacy, suggesting that outliers, particularly including data tied to minority groups, often exhibit higher memorization propensity which indicates they may be more difficult to unlearn.

2512.01353.title: The Trojan Knowledge: Bypassing Commercial LLM Guardrails via Harmless Prompt Weaving and Adaptive Tree Search
2512.01353.tldr: The Correlated Knowledge Attack Agent (CKA-Agent) is introduced, a dynamic framework that reframes jailbreaking as an adaptive, tree-structured exploration of the target model's knowledge base, underscoring the severity of this vulnerability and the urgent need for defenses against such knowledge-decomposition attacks.

2402.15109.title: Remaining-data-free Machine Unlearning by Suppressing Sample Contribution
2402.15109.tldr: This work proposes MU-Mis (Machine Unlearning by Minimizing input sensitivity), which directly suppresses the contribution of forgetting data, and is the first time that a remaining-data-free method can perform on par with top performing remaining-data-dependent methods.

2405.15495.title: Towards Natural Machine Unlearning
2405.15495.tldr: This work substantially reduces the over-forgetting problem and leads to strong robustness across different unlearning tasks, making it a promising candidate for practical machine unlearning.
2405.15495.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2409.19732.title: Unified Gradient-Based Machine Unlearning with Remain Geometry Enhancement
2409.19732.tldr: This work proposes a fast-slow parameter update strategy to implicitly approximate the up-to-date salient unlearning direction, free from specific modal constraints, and adaptable across computer vision unlearning tasks, including classification and generation.

2505.15178.title: A Unified Gradient-based Framework for Task-agnostic Continual Learning-Unlearning
2505.15178.tldr: A remain-preserved manifold constraint is introduced to induce a remaining Hessian compensation for CLU iterations, and a fast-slow weight adaptation mechanism is designed to efficiently approximate the second-order optimization direction, combined with adaptive weighting coefficients and a balanced weight saliency mask, proposing a unified implementation framework for gradient-based CLU.

2603.00992.title: Compensation-free Machine Unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models by Eliminating the Mutual Information
2603.00992.tldr: This paper advocates for developing compensation-free concept erasure operations, which precisely identify and eliminate the undesired knowledge such that the impact on other generations is minimal, and proposes MiM-MU, which is to unlearn a concept by minimizing the mutual information with a delicate design for computational effectiveness and for maintaining sampling distribution for other concepts.

2606.18309.title: SAGE: Retain-Aware Post-Hoc Sanitization of Final Unlearning Vector
2606.18309.tldr: This work proposes a complementary post-hoc setting to sanitize the final update vector without rerunning the original unlearning pipeline, and designs SAGE, Spectral Activation-GEometry Sanitization, a source-agnostic correction for final unlearning updates.

2605.11716.title: SafeSteer: A Decoding-level Defense Mechanism for Multimodal Large Language Models
2605.11716.tldr: SafeSteer, a decoding-level defense mechanism for MLLMs that includes a Decoding-Probe, a lightweight probe for detecting and correcting harmful output during decoding, which iteratively steers the decoding process toward safety.
2605.11716.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.06809.title: Root Defence Strategies: Ensuring Safety of LLM at the Decoding Level
2410.06809.tldr: This paper examines the LLMs' capability to recognize harmful outputs, revealing and quantifying their proficiency in assessing the danger of previous tokens, and designs a robust defense mechanism at the decoding level that corrects harmful queries directly rather than rejecting them outright.

2506.18245.title: Smart-LLaMA-DPO: Reinforced Large Language Model for Explainable Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
2506.18245.tldr: This work proposes Smart-LLaMA-DPO, an advanced detection method based on the LLaMA-3.1-8B that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, and demonstrates the superior quality of explanations generated by Smart-LLaMA-DPO in terms of correctness, thoroughness, and clarity.

2410.08557.title: MUSO: Achieving Exact Machine Unlearning in Over-Parameterized Regimes
2410.08557.tldr: Under the premise of model optimization via stochastic gradient descent, it is theoretically demonstrated that over-parameterized linear models can achieve exact MU through relabeling specific data and proposed an alternating optimization algorithm that unifies the tasks of unlearning and relabeling.

2608.15341.title: TEA: Text Encoder Alignment for Robust Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models
2608.15341.tldr: A lightweight Text Encoder Alignment framework that fine-tunes only the text encoder while keeping the generative backbone fully frozen, and achieves state-of-the-art erasure robustness against black-box and white-box adversarial attacks on Stable Diffusion v1.4, while preserving generation quality on benign prompts.

2601.00590.title: SafeMo: Linguistically Grounded Unlearning for Trustworthy Text-to-Motion Generation
2601.00590.tldr: SafeMo, a trustworthy motion generative framework integrating Minimal Motion Unlearning (MMU), a two-stage machine unlearning strategy, enabling safe human motion generation in continuous space, preserving continuous kinematics without codebook loss and delivering strong safety-utility trade-offs compared to current baselines is proposed.

2603.15647.title: Steering Frozen LLMs: Adaptive Social Alignment via Online Prompt Routing
2603.15647.tldr: This work introduces the Consensus Clustering LinUCB Bandit (CCLUB), a unified framework for adaptive social alignment via system-prompt routing that employs a conservative consensus clustering mechanism, effectively preventing unsafe generalization across semantically proximal but risk-divergent contexts.

2607.21620.title: From Profiles to Steering Vectors: Global Sparse Priors and Local Semantic Calibration for Personalized Text Generation
2607.21620.tldr: GLASS is a training-free framework for personalized generation via Global-Local Activation Steering with Sparse priors that outperforms retrieval, fine-tuning, and steering-based baselines across ROUGE metrics and LLM-as-judge evaluations.

2603.00823.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Robustness under Multi-Turn Interaction
2603.00823.tldr: It is found that knowledge appearing forgotten in static evaluation can often be recovered through interaction, and the findings suggest that static evaluation may overestimate real-world effectiveness and highlight the need for ensuring stable forgetting under interactive settings.

2605.27138.title: ICCU: In-Context Continual Unlearning via Pattern-Induced Refusal Rules
2605.27138.tldr: ICCU (In-Context Continual Unlearning), an in-context continual unlearning framework that induces readable refusal rules from unlearning datasets and applies them at inference time either as a filter or via the system prompt, without modifying model parameters.

2507.07375.title: Bradley-Terry and Multi-Objective Reward Modeling Are Complementary
2507.07375.tldr: A unified reward modeling framework that jointly trains Bradley--Terry single-objective and multi-objective regression-based reward functions using a shared embedding space is proposed and extensive experimental results demonstrate that this framework significantly improves both the robustness and the scoring performance of reward models.

2410.16454.title: Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization
2410.16454.tldr: It is revealed that applying quantization to models that have undergone unlearning can restore the "forgotten" information.

2506.00359.title: Keeping an Eye on LLM Unlearning: The Hidden Risk and Remedy
2506.00359.tldr: Scope-aware Unlearning (SU), a lightweight enhancement that introduces a scope term into the unlearning objective, encouraging the model to localize the forgetting effect, is proposed and significantly improves robustness against red-teaming Stealthy Attack.

2607.02897.title: PPE-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating MLLM Unlearning under Private-Public Entanglement
2607.02897.tldr: PPE-Bench is proposed, a new benchmark for evaluating MLLM unlearning under private-public entanglement, and two simple but effective methods to better preserve public information during unlearning are introduced.

2502.17823.title: A General Framework to Enhance Fine-tuning-based LLM Unlearning
2502.17823.tldr: Gated Representation UNlearning (GRUN) is introduced which has two components: a soft gate function for distinguishing target data and a suppression module using Representation Fine-tuning to adjust representations rather than model parameters.
2502.17823.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.00808.title: Unlearning Inversion Attacks for Graph Neural Networks
2506.00808.tldr: The confidence pitfall is derived and exploited, a theoretical and empirical pattern showing that nodes adjacent to unlearned edges exhibit a large drop in model confidence, and an adaptive prediction mechanism is designed that applies different similarity thresholds to unlearned and other membership edges.

2605.15687.title: ASRU: Activation Steering Meets Reinforcement Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models
2605.15687.tldr: ASRU first induces initial refusal behavior through activation redirection, and then optimizes fine-grained refusal boundaries using a customized reward function, thereby achieving a better trade-off between target knowledge unlearning and model utility.

2604.02467.title: VERTIGO: Visual Preference Optimization for Cinematic Camera Trajectory Generation
2604.02467.tldr: VERTIGO is introduced, the first framework for visual preference optimization of camera trajectory generators, which leverages a real-time graphics engine to render 2D visual previews from generated camera motion and reduces the character off-screen rate from 38% to nearly 0% while preserving the geometric fidelity of camera motion.

2608.08212.title: Harmful Content Is Not Enough: Continuation Framing Moderates In-Context Emergent Misalignment

2603.15692.title: BadLLM-TG: A Backdoor Defender powered by LLM Trigger Generator
2603.15692.tldr: The rich knowledge embedded in large language models (LLMs) is employed and a Backdoor defender powered by LLM Trigger Generator is proposed, termed BadLLM-TG, optimized through prompt-driven reinforcement learning, using the victim model's feedback loss as the reward signal.
2603.15692.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2606.01382.title: Efficient Exploration for Iterative Nash Preference Optimization
2606.01382.tldr: This work shows that standard iterative NLHF can suffer an exponential dependence on the KL-regularization parameter, and proposes an explicitly exploratory iterative NLHF algorithm that combines SFT-based regularization with adversarial policy exploration, and proposes an explicitly exploratory iterative NLHF algorithm that combines SFT-based regularization with adversarial policy exploration.

2608.01008.title: Toward Fine-Grained Forgetting:Attribute Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.01008.tldr: This work proposes Causal Localization and Retain-Aware Projection (CLRP), a lightweight training-free framework that uses activation patching to identify the layer that causally mediates target-attribute disclosure, then applies a retain-aware projection that removes the target-attribute subspace while preserving same-identity evidence.

2409.06691.title: Geometric-Averaged Preference Optimization for Soft Preference Labels
2409.06691.tldr: This work introduces the distributional soft preference labels and improves Direct Preference Optimization with a weighted geometric average of the LLM output likelihood in the loss function to mitigate over-optimization and objective mismatch, which prior works suffer from.

2605.12798.title: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer
2605.12798.tldr: It is argued that emergent misalignment can be better understood as a data-mediated transfer phenomenon: harmful fine-tuning examples do not induce uniform behavioral spillover, but interact with the structural properties of the dataset and the difficulty of the tasks relative to the model.

2602.00767.title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking
2602.00767.tldr: The results show that targeted training-time constraints on internal mechanisms can mitigate emergent misalignment without degrading target-task performance.

2604.26130.title: reward-lens: A Mechanistic Interpretability Library for Reward Models
2604.26130.tldr: The central empirical finding is negative: linear attribution does not predict causal patching effects, so the framework treats this disagreement as a property to expose, not a bug -- motivating a design that keeps observational and causal views first-class and directly comparable.

2604.02608.title: Steerable but Not Decodable: Function Vectors Operate Beyond the Logit Lens
2604.02608.tldr: The linear representation hypothesis is decompose into linear decodability and linear steerability and show they come apart opposite to intuition, with implications for safety monitoring: vocabulary-projection tools are blind to FV-style interventions on widely deployed model families.

2607.21356.title: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace
2607.21356.tldr: It is found that narrow fine-tuning recruits a persona structure that is present in the model before the fine-tune exists, and that broad misalignment on questions unrelated to the training data is more broad than mechanical weight superposition and matched diversity jointly account for.

2508.17182.title: LLM Assertiveness can be Mechanistically Decomposed into Emotional and Logical Components
2508.17182.tldr: This analysis identifies layers most sensitive to assertiveness contrasts and reveals that high-assertive representations decompose into two orthogonal sub-components of emotional and logical clusters-paralleling the dual-route Elaboration Likelihood Model in Psychology.

2601.20760.title: Exploring Re-inforcement Learning via Human Feedback under User Heterogeneity
2601.20760.tldr: This work provides an algorithm that encourages simultaneous learning of reward models and worker embeddings and shows that clustering users into different groups based on their preferences and created personalised reward models improves win-rate of the said models.

2602.00298.title: Assessing Domain-Level Susceptibility to Emergent Misalignment from Narrow Finetuning
2602.00298.tldr: This work is the first to provide a taxonomic ranking of emergent misalignment by domain, which has implications for AI security and post-training, and standardizes a recipe for constructing misaligned datasets.

2608.15445.title: Measuring Reward Hacking and Reasoning-Answer Decoupling Under Position-Confounded Optimization
2608.15445.tldr: This work trains language models with GRPO on multiple-choice math problems where the correct answer is always option A, then evaluates on an unseen test set with unbiased answer positions to find reasoning-answer decoupling, which separates capability loss from a learned, transferable shortcut.

2607.26389.title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment
2607.26389.tldr: Calibrated personality vectors transform an opaque safety phenomenon into a human-legible diagnostic profile by extracting activation directions for character traits from a single binary contrast, which can separate or steer behavior without establishing a calibrated scale.

2607.04510.title: Transplanting, inverting, and preventing a misalignment persona: method-conditional emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5

2603.03163.title: Conditioned Activation Transport for T2I Safety Steering
2603.03163.tldr: Conditioned Activation Transport (CAT) is proposed, a framework that employs a geometry-based conditioning mechanism and nonlinear transport maps that conditioning transport maps to activate only within unsafe activation regions, to minimize interference with benign queries.

2605.00583.title: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models Through the Visual Modality
2605.00583.tldr: Four jailbreak attacks exploiting the vision component are introduced exploiting the vision component of vision-language models, highlighting that robust VLM alignment requires treating vision as a first-class target for safety post-training.

2605.10633.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
