2505.12060.tldr: This paper identifies a critical safety gap: while LLMs are adept at detecting jailbreak prompts, they often produce unsafe responses when directly processing these inputs, and proposes SAGE (Self-Aware Guard Enhancement), a training-free defense strategy designed to align LLMs' strong safety discrimination performance with their relatively weaker safety generation ability.
2505.12060.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.11836.title: SplInterp: Improving our Understanding and Training of Sparse Autoencoders
2505.11836.tldr: It is discovered that SAEs generalise ``$k-means autoencoders'' to be piecewise affine, but sacrifice accuracy for interpretability vs. the optimal ``$k$-means-esque plus local principal component analysis (PCA)'' piecewise affine autoencoder.

2505.05541.title: Safety by Measurement: A Systematic Literature Review of AI Safety Evaluation Methods
2505.05541.tldr: This literature review consolidates the rapidly evolving field of AI safety evaluations, proposing a systematic taxonomy around three dimensions: what properties the authors measure, how they measure them, and how these measurements integrate into frameworks.

2508.13700.title: The AI Risk Spectrum: From Dangerous Capabilities to Existential Threats
2508.13700.tldr: This paper maps the full spectrum of AI risks, from current harms affecting individual users to existential threats that could endanger humanity's survival, and identifies risk amplifiers - competitive pressures, accidents, corporate indifference, and coordination failures - that make all risks more likely and severe.

2505.00555.title: On the Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks for Causality in Bio-statistics
2505.00555.tldr: This work demonstrates that MI tools can be leveraged to probe and validate the internal representations learned by NNs, and discover and visualize the distinct computational pathways employed by the network to process different types of inputs, potentially revealing how confounders and treatments are handled.

2504.16290.title: Naturally Computed Scale Invariance in the Residual Stream of ResNet18
2504.16290.tldr: This work investigates ResNet18 with a particular focus on its residual stream, an architectural component which InceptionV1 lacks, and tentative findings suggest how the residual stream computes scale invariance and its possible role in behavior.
2504.16290.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

2504.15473.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
2504.15473.tldr: This work uses the SAE framework to probe the inner workings of a popular text-to-image diffusion model, and uncovers a variety of human-interpretable concepts in its activations.

2609.21142.title: Exploring Text Classification Models with Sparse Autoencoders
2609.21142.tldr: Techniques for exploring the relationships between the SAE's features and the model's predictions and errors are presented and integrated into SAEfarer, a tool for analyzing concepts learned by text classification LMs.

2609.18860.title: Decodable but Misrouted: Sparse Features Uncover a Readout Gap in Vision-Language Models for Harmful Meme Detection
2609.18860.tldr: Robustness controls show that the signal extends beyond English, is not explained solely by accompanying OCR, and depends on paired visual evidence, thus, routing, rather than representation alone, is a recurring bottleneck in harmful meme classification.

2609.07037.title: Disentangling Steering Vectors
2609.07037.tldr: Steering Vector Dissection is proposed, a framework to explicitly isolate individual and semantically consistent features from these composite directions that tend to entangle multiple semantic and stylistic concepts into a single composite direction, leading to unpredictable steering effects.

2608.30403.title: Why Are LLM Backdoor Defenses Fragmented? A Feature-Level Explanation with Sparse Autoencoders
2608.30403.tldr: Results show that SAE-based analysis can explain defense fragmentation and guide interpretable backdoor mitigation and show system?atic encoding differences: dirty-label backdoors are dominated by isolated interaction features, whereas clean-label backdoors rely more on heterogeneous mixtures of mixed and weight-modified features.

2603.27522.title: Hidden Ads: Behavior Triggered Semantic Backdoors for Advertisement Injection in Vision Language Models
2603.27522.tldr: This work introduces Hidden Ads, a new class of backdoor attacks that exploit this recommendation-seeking behavior to inject unauthorized advertisements, and proposes a multi-tier threat framework to systematically evaluate Hidden Ads across three adversary capability levels: hard prompt injection, soft prompt optimization, and supervised fine-tuning.

2608.29936.title: When Safety Speaks a Language: A Mechanistic Analysis of Safety-Language Identity Entanglement in LLMs
2608.29936.tldr: This work presents a systematic mechanistic analysis of multilingual safety using sparse autoencoder features, sparse interpretable directions in the residual stream associated with harmful and harmless model behavior across three instruction-tuned LLMs, eight languages, and all model layers to qualify the language-universality of safety alignment as architecture-dependent and offer a mechanistic account of multilingual safety interventions.

2606.07141.title: REMEDI: A Benchmark for Retention and Unlearning Evaluation in Multi-label Clinical Disease Inference
2606.07141.tldr: REMEDI is an extensive benchmark for machine unlearning tailored to multi-label and multiclass clinical disease inference, where label correlations, longitudinal structure, and safety constraints make unlearning particularly challenging.

2608.29034.title: A Unifying Perspective on Language Model Representations: From Filler-Role Structure to Mechanistic Interpretability
2608.29034.tldr: This work proposes using Tensor Product Representations (TPRs) as a unifying hypothesis, and shows that TPRs can unify several prior interpretability methods: additive analogies, linear probing, sparse autoencoders, and activation patching.

2605.29971.title: Causal Interventions on Continuous Variables: A Case Study on Verb Bias in Steering Vectors for In-Context Learning
2605.29971.tldr: It is shown that verb bias is causally represented in steering vectors extracted from large language models: counterfactual edits to verb bias systematically shift downstream structural preferences.

2608.28233.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
2608.28233.tldr: Refusal-Enhanced INhibitory Steering is proposed, which suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features in the same SAE feature space, and substantially reduces harmful responses, markedly improves safe refusals and largely preserves general capabilities.

2509.26345.title: SafeBehavior: Simulating Human-Like Multistage Reasoning to Mitigate Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
2509.26345.tldr: Experimental results show that SafeBehavior significantly improves robustness and adaptability across diverse threat scenarios, offering an efficient and human inspired approach to safeguarding LLMs against jailbreak attempts.

2608.25941.title: When Pruning Meets Interpretability: Preserving Sparse Autoencoder Robustness in LLMs
2608.25941.tldr: A systematic study of how pruning affects SAE behavior is presented and theoretically shows that, for a fixed SAE, its impact is governed by perturbation energy, a covariance-weighted norm.

2510.00404.title: AbsTopK: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders For Bidirectional Features
2510.00404.tldr: AbsTopK SAE is proposed, a new variant derived from the $\ell_0$ sparsity constraint that applies hard thresholding over the largest-magnitude activations, which improves reconstruction fidelity, enhances interpretability, and enables single features to encode contrasting concepts.

2608.23809.title: Discovering Cross-Language Reasoning Invariance in LLMs with Geometry-Invariant Sparse Autoencoders
2608.23809.tldr: It is found that cross-language feature sharing is model- and architecture-dependent in this sample and appears at different depths in different models.

2608.13337.title: Where You Measure Decides What You Measure: Position Selection in Ablation-Based SAE Evaluation
2608.13337.tldr: Six autoencoders are trained from one initialisation, differing only in fitting choices, so that a latent means the same thing in each, and a causal number reported without its position describes the token it was taken at as much as the latent it was taken from.

2606.24251.title: Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process of Language Models
2606.24251.tldr: This work proposes to monitor misalignment by decomposing it into fine-grained cognitive processes -- misalignment indicators -- and detecting their presence in a model's internal activations via linear probes, and develops a taxonomy of 18 indicators spanning different misaligned behaviors.

2608.08168.title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2608.08168.tldr: This work applies Top-K Sparse Autoencoders to the intermediate representations of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and examines the model's divergent behaviors across math-solving tasks of three distinct difficulty levels, identifying a clear distinction in how the model functions under two reasoning modes.

2608.29286.title: MMPCBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models on Proactive Critique of Flawed Inputs
2608.29286.tldr: This work proposes MMPCBench, a comprehensive framework for evaluating MLLMs' proactive critique competence, which adopts a hierarchical evaluation protocol to measure models' error detection, diagnosis and resolution performance, and applies alignment-aware metrics to assess the coherence between internal reasoning and final responses.

2608.07852.title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders
2608.07852.tldr: This work decomposes three generation settings (Assistant, Roleplay, and Story) into sparse autoencoder features extracted at turn-boundary and pronoun-token positions and selected through a filtering pipeline for different depths, characterize each surviving feature through its steering effects and activation distribution.

2608.05732.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits
2608.05732.tldr: CircuitSteer is introduced, a novel framework that leverages Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify and manipulate coherent semantic circuits distributed across multiple layers that yields strictly more robust and effective behavioral control than static single-point interventions.

2507.04742.title: Activation Steering for Chain-of-Thought Compression
2507.04742.tldr: Activation-Steered Compression (ASC), an inference-time technique that shortens reasoning traces by directly modifying hidden representations, is formalized and provides a theoretical analysis of the impact of ASC on the output distribution, derived from a closed-form KL-divergence-bounded constraint to regulate steering strength.
2507.04742.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.20652.title: Scaling Interpretable Transformers with Parity Bottleneck Layers
2607.20652.tldr: The ParityTransformer is introduced, a GPT-2-scale architecture whose intermediate representations are efficient and wide / sparse by design, and seen as a step toward training models whose internal representations are interpretable by design rather than recovered post hoc.

2607.17117.title: Persistent Sparse Autoencoders: Learning Feature-Specific Timescales in Language Model Representations
2607.17117.tldr: This work introduces Persistent Sparse Autoencoders (Persistent SAEs), an extension of standard SAEs that learns a persistence coefficient for each feature, allowing the model to learn feature-specific timescales from reconstruction alone.

2605.06342.title: Don't Lose Focus: Activation Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections
2605.06342.tldr: This work proposes Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections (SKOP), a steering method that constrains harmful attention rerouting without eliminating steering efficacy, and shows that SKOP achieves the best joint steering-utility trade-off.

2607.05615.title: A Coin Flip Per Token: Bernoulli Sparse Steering of Large Language Models
2607.05615.tldr: Stochastic Token Steering (STS), which gates each token independently with probability $p$, and Stochastic Block Steering (SBS), which gates a leading window once per sequence are introduced; neither requires a reward model or learned gating policy.

2508.17540.title: Activation Transport Operators
2508.17540.tldr: This work proposes Activation Transport Operators (ATO), linear maps from upstream to downstream residuals later, evaluated in feature space using downstream SAE decoder projections, and develops the notion of transport efficiency, for which it is used to estimate the size of the residual stream subspace that corresponds to linear transport.

2607.19386.title: Building Fast, Evaluating Slow: Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance
2607.19386.tldr: It is found that methodological variance collectively exceeds architectural variance across all metrics and tested models, suggesting that cross-paper comparisons based on autointerpretability scores may reflect pipeline differences rather than architectural differences, with implications for the ongoing debate on SAE utility.

2606.29888.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders
2606.29888.tldr: An approach that trains modality-specific sparse autoencoders to preserve each modality's feature geometry, and then aligns corresponding features post hoc is proposed, which improves reconstruction fidelity and enhances performance in cross-modal retrieval and concept steering.

2608.26136.title: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders and the Solution-Completeness Confound

2606.26629.title: From Weights to Features: SAE-Guided Activation Regularization for LLM Continual Learning
2606.26629.tldr: This paper derives a new loss function that uses the SAE feature dictionary to explicitly balance stability and plasticity, and shows that EWC is a special case in the one-sided weight-space penalty setting.

2603.08095.title: DC-W2S: Dual-Consensus Weak-to-Strong Training for Reliable Process Reward Modeling in Biological Reasoning
2603.08095.tldr: It is demonstrated that DC-W2S enables the training of robust PRMs for complex reasoning without exhaustive expert annotation, proving that strategic data curation is more effective than indiscriminate training on large-scale noisy datasets.

2606.24716.title: Evaluating the Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders with Concept Annotations
2606.24716.tldr: A human-grounded evaluation framework that quantifies alignment between SAE latents and human-annotated concepts, without requiring user studies, and validate this matching through targeted attribute perturbations, suggests that moderate dictionary sizes provide the best trade-off, yielding the most interpretable SAEs.

2606.18383.title: From Sparse Features to Trustworthy Proxies: Certifying SAE-Based Interpretability
2606.18383.tldr: A post-hoc generalization framework that certifies the LM via a sparse proxy, obtained by replacing a native hidden activation with its pretrained SAE reconstruction, and derives an upper bound on the base model's expected risk using four measurable quantities.

2609.03781.title: IndicSafeEval: Safety Robustness of Large Language Models under Multilingual Persuasive Jailbreak Attacks
2609.03781.tldr: IndicSafeEval, a persuasion-based jailbreak evaluation framework for Indian languages, is introduced and it is observed that different risk categories exhibit different levels of vulnerability, with some types of harmful content being significantly more susceptible to persuasion-based jailbreaks than others.

2606.16193.title: Cascaded Sparse Autoencoders Learn Multi-Level Visual Concepts in Multimodal LLMs
2606.16193.tldr: Experiments show that CSAEs improve interpretability in terms of hierarchical concept coherence over state-of-the-art SAE baselines, and results on concept steering further demonstrate that the learned concept groups support effective group-level interventions in MLLM outputs.

2607.25132.title: Interpretable GOHR Agents via Sparse Autoencoders
2607.25132.tldr: This work reports interpretability experiments for a tokenized autoregressive Transformer agent in the Game of Hidden Rules (GOHR), a compact two-rule task in which both hidden rules map object shapes to target buckets, but with different permutations.

2603.03205.title: Learning When to Act or Refuse: Guarding Agentic Reasoning Models for Safe Multi-Step Tool Use
2603.03205.tldr: MOSAIC reduces harmful behavior by up to 50%, increases harmful-task refusal by over 20% on injection attacks, cuts privacy leakage, and preserves or improves benign task performance, demonstrating robust generalization across models, domains, and agentic settings.

2605.07447.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Plug-and-Play Firewalls for Adversarial Attack Detection in VLMs
2605.07447.tldr: This work proposes a novel and lightweight adversarial attack detection framework based on sparse autoencoders (SAEs), termed SAEgis, which requires no additional adversarial training, introduces minimal overhead, and provides a practical approach for improving the safety of real-world VLM systems.

2506.01247.title: Beyond Interpretability: When, Why, and How Sparse Autoencoders Enable Label-Free Visual Steering
2506.01247.tldr: Visual Sparse Steering (VS2), a label-free method that trains a top-$k SAE on unlabeled activations from a frozen CLIP image encoder and constructs an interpretable steering vector by amplifying the input's active sparse features and decoding the induced change, is introduced.

2412.17626.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
2412.17626.tldr: SAE-Track is introduced, a novel method for efficiently obtaining a continual series of SAEs, providing the foundation for a mechanistic study that covers the semantic evolution of features, the underlying processes of feature formation, and the directional drift of feature vectors.

2604.13304.title: Can Cross-Layer Transcoders Replace Vision Transformer Activations? An Interpretable Perspective on Vision
2604.13304.tldr: It is shown that CLTs achieve high reconstruction fidelity with post-MLP activations while preserving and even improving, in some cases, CLIP zero-shot classification accuracy and interpretability, and that the cross-layer contribution scores provide faithful attribution.

2605.11922.title: StepCodeReasoner: Aligning Code Reasoning with Stepwise Execution Traces via Reinforcement Learning
2605.11922.tldr: This work proposes StepCodeReasoner, a framework that introduces explicit intermediate execution-state supervision, and introduces Bi-Level GRPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm for structured credit assignment at two levels: inter-trajectory, comparing alternative execution paths, and intra-trajectory, rewarding intermediate accuracy based on its impact on downstream correctness.

2601.10589.title: Be Your Own Red Teamer: Safety Alignment via Self-Play and Reflective Experience Replay
2601.10589.tldr: Safety Self- Play (SSP) is introduced, a system that utilizes a single LLM to act concurrently as both the Attacker and the Defender within a unified Reinforcement Learning (RL) loop, dynamically evolving attack strategies to uncover vulnerabilities while simultaneously strengthening defense mechanisms.
2601.10589.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.10269.title: Devil in the Lens: Analyzing and Defending Physical Prompt Injection Against Vision-Language Models on Wearable Devices
2607.10269.tldr: This work characterizes how malicious textual information embedded in physical environments introduces a high-priority visual channel for indirect prompt injection, and proposes two targeted defense strategies to effectively reduce the success rate and safety impact of these attacks.

2606.10029.title: Interpreting and Steering a Text-to-Speech Language Model with Sparse Autoencoders
2606.10029.tldr: A modality-aware auto-interp pipeline is introduced that labels each feature from where it fires-text-prefix context, 1-second speech clips, or both, and shows these features are interpretable, spanning phonemes, laughter, accent prompts and speaker gender.

2606.06735.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle-Norm Decomposition
2606.06735.tldr: This work revisits the assumption that hidden-state norm does not carry concept-relevant information and suggests that activation steering should be parameterized by interpretable angular and radial components of the intervention, rather than by a single additive coefficient that entangles these two effects.

2505.22255.title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
2505.22255.tldr: KronSAE is proposed, a design that factorizes the latent space into heads and forms post-latent features as pairwise compositions of lower-dimensional pre-latents using mAND, a differentiable AND-like interaction that imposes a compositional co-activation prior while remaining compatible with standard SAE objectives and variants.

2410.07656.title: Mechanistic Permutability: Match Features Across Layers
2410.07656.tldr: SAE Match is introduced, a novel, data-free method for aligning SAE features across different layers of a neural network that effectively captures feature evolution across layers, improving feature matching quality and providing a new tool for mechanistic interpretability studies.

2509.06608.title: Small Vectors, Big Effects: A Mechanistic Study of RL-Induced Reasoning via Steering Vectors
2509.06608.tldr: Lightweight steering vectors inserted into the base model's residual stream and trained with a reinforcement-learning objective explain a large portion of full fine-tuning performance increase while preserving the interpretability of small, additive interventions.

2606.09735.title: The Neutral Mask: How Alignment Training Provides Shallow Alignment while Leaving Partisan Structure Intact in a Large Language Model
2606.09735.tldr: It is shown that alignment training does not remove the structured partisan direction in the base model, Instead, it compresses the variance of the partisan signal to generate consistently balanced and non-partisan output.

2606.08365.title: Pre-Intervention Prediction of Sparse Autoencoder Steering Side Effects
2606.08365.tldr: A pre-intervention screening framework for forecasting SAE steering side effects from feature statistics computed before steering is introduced, and side effects along two axes of steering modularity, effect stability and collateral spread are operationalized.

2606.01479.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech
2606.01479.tldr: This work analyzes emotion-related variation in the semantic hidden states of LLM-based TTS models using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to identify sparse latent features and introduces a feature-level intervention framework for bidirectional emotion induction and suppression without modifying backbone parameters.

2607.20479.title: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs
2607.20479.tldr: It is demonstrated that the choice of training data and lie typology substantially changes detectability, highlighting that deception detection is a highly representation-dependent problem.

2609.00351.title: Detecting Hidden Behaviors in LLMs via Activation-matched Finetuning

2605.31183.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders can outperform simple baselines
2605.31183.tldr: This work finds that Sparse Autoencoders can, in fact, perform close to on par with the reference LoRA performance on the AxBench benchmark, when features are selected and labelled with the supervised pipeline.

2605.30162.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders
2605.30162.tldr: Preliminary evidence suggests activation-level auditing may surface failure modes invisible to behavioral evaluation, with substantial variation across architectures, which suggests refusal tracks legality and cultural salience over CBRN hazard.

2605.28567.title: Semantic Optimal Transport for Sparse Autoencoder Feature Matching and Circuit Compression
2605.28567.tldr: This work introduces a distributional framework for SAE analyses, in which each feature is represented not by a single decoder vector like in the literature, but by an activation-weighted distribution over the hidden states that express it, and provides a unified semantic metric for cross-layer feature comparison.

2605.07922.title: Tree SAE: Learning Hierarchical Feature Structures in Sparse Autoencoders
2605.07922.tldr: This work proposes the Tree SAE, a model designed to learn hierarchical structures directly from within the feature set, and demonstrates that Tree SAEs significantly surpass the existing SAEs at learning hierarchical pairs while maintaining competitive performance to the state-of-the-art on several key benchmarks.

2605.28149.title: Sign-Aware Gated Sparse Autoencoders: Modeling Anticorrelated Features with Bi-Jump-ReLU Activations
2605.28149.tldr: This work proposes the Sign-Aware Gated SAE (SA-GSAE), which combines two-sided gated sparsity, signed shrinkage-free magnitudes, and auxiliary gate supervision in a new Bi-Jump-ReLU activation, so that a single latent carries both polarities of one decoder direction.

2605.24977.title: Universal Boosts, Specific Suppressors: Sparse Autoencoder Steering of Medical Vision-Language Models
2605.24977.tldr: The authors' inference-only method improves the quality of generated reports for three radiology VLMs, with relative improvements of +5.4%, +7.2%, and +17.0% in the clinical composite metric, and statistically significant GREEN gains on all backbones.

2605.24946.title: Interpretability Transfer from Language to Vision via Sparse Autoencoders
2605.24946.tldr: This paper introduces Visual Interpretability via SAE Transfer Alignment (VISTA), a framework that transfers interpretability from language to vision in a LLaVA-style vision-language model by constraining a visual projector to map visual tokens into an LLM's pre-existing, labeled textual SAE space, and shows that DINOv2 features have stronger localization abilities than other encoders.

2605.22902.title: Transcoders Trace Visual Grounding and Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
2605.22902.tldr: A function-centric framework based on Transcoders, sparse approximations of MLP sublayers that act as a causal proxy for layer-wise computation yields interpretable and predictive accounts of multimodal computation in VLMs.

2605.22658.title: SegCompass: Exploring Interpretable Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders for Enhanced Reasoning Segmentation
2605.22658.tldr: SegCompass is an end-to-end model that leverages a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to forge an explicit, interpretable, and differentiable alignment pathway, and provides a "white-box" connection that is significantly more traceable than latent queries and more coherent than textual readouts.

2605.28023.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning
2605.28023.tldr: VCap is proposed, a Witness-Adjudicator reward that pairs the reference caption (a witness) with the visual signal (an adjudicator) with hypergeometric-distribution-level precision for caption quality verification, facilitating weak-to-strong generalization in RL training.

2605.22462.title: From Correlation to Cause: A Five-Stage Methodology for Feature Analysis in Transformer Language Models

2605.18229.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
2605.18229.tldr: The sae-probes variant of $k$-sparse probing is the most reliable metric, but even sae-probes struggles to separate variants of the same SAE architecture, and the results show the field needs better SAE benchmarks.

2605.15961.title: Sparse Autoencoders enable Robust and Interpretable Fine-tuning of CLIP models
2605.15961.tldr: SAE-FT regularizes changes to the model's visual representations by penalizing the addition and removal of semantically meaningful features identified by a Sparse Autoencoder trained on the pre-trained model, which prevents catastrophic forgetting and makes the fine-tuning process interpretable, enabling direct analysis of semantic changes.

2605.12874.title: Descriptive Collision in Sparse Autoencoder Auto-Interpretability: When One Explanation Describes Many Features
2605.12874.tldr: A property called discrimination is formalized, it is proved that current detection-style auto-interpretability scoring is invariant to collision, and two complementary corrective metrics -- collision-adjusted detection and discrimination scoring -- are proposed that explicitly penalize explanations that fail to distinguish a feature from its neighbors.

2605.24577.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m
2605.24577.tldr: It is shown that an orthogonal Procrustes fit on a single batch of activations transfers sparse-autoencoder feature dictionaries and steering vectors between independently trained models, with no retraining.

2605.12770.title: WriteSAE: Sparse Autoencoders for Recurrent State
2605.12770.tldr: This work introduces WriteSAE, a sparse autoencoder for the matrix updates written into recurrent language-model state and reports the first cache-level steering intervention reported in a state-space or hybrid recurrent layer.

2605.12055.title: Do Language Models Encode Knowledge of Linguistic Constraint Violations?
2605.12055.tldr: A sensitivity score is introduced for identifying features that are preferentially activated on constraint-violated versus well-formed inputs, enabling unsupervised detection of potential violation-specific features and proposes a conjunctive falsification framework with three criteria evaluated jointly.

2605.18808.title: Compositional Literary Primitives in Instruction-Tuned LLMs: Cross-Architectural SAE Features for Self, Style, and Affect
2605.18808.tldr: A compositional architecture of literary primitives in two instruction-tuned large language models, including a single most-RLHF-loaded self-feature per architecture that intensifies the institutional Helper-AI persona at one operating regime and produces affect-categorizable output at the same calibrated coefficient is characterized.

2606.09850.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Alignment Algorithms in Language Models
2606.09850.tldr: It is found that preference signals consistently concentrate in early--mid or mid--late layers, but different objectives induce qualitatively distinct representational shifts, demonstrating that behavioral alignment does not imply uniform internal restructuring.

2603.25035.title: Mechanistically Interpreting Compression in Vision-Language Models
2603.25035.tldr: It is shown that pruning causes a sharp drop in genuine refusal behavior, suggesting that the choice of compression has safety implications, and introduces VLMSafe-420, a novel benchmark that pairs harmful inputs with matched benign counterfactuals across various safety categories.

2606.00424.title: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight
2606.00424.tldr: This work studies a more tractable form of weak supervision: using a weak model as a critic rather than as a labeler or judge, and proposes progressive on-policy critique distillation (**OPCD**), which filters high-quality critiques and distills critic-guided behavior into the strong model through adaptive self-teacher signals.

2506.01197.title: Incorporating Hierarchical Semantics in Sparse Autoencoder Architectures
2506.01197.tldr: Application of a modified SAE architecture that explicitly models a semantic hierarchy of concepts to the internal representations of large language models shows both that semantic hierarchy can be learned and that doing so improves both reconstruction and interpretability.

2509.12934.title: The Anatomy of Alignment: Decomposing Preference Optimization by Steering Sparse Features
2509.12934.tldr: This work introduces Feature Steering with Reinforcement Learning (FSRL), a framework that trains a lightweight adapter to steer model behavior by modulating interpretable sparse features and theoretically demonstrates that this mechanism is expressive enough to approximate the behavioral shifts of post-training processes.

2603.21697.title: Structured Visual Narratives Undermine Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models
2603.21697.tldr: ComicJailbreak is introduced, a comic-based jailbreak benchmark with 1,167 attack instances spanning 10 harm categories and 5 task setups, and it is shown that current safety evaluators can be unreliable on sensitive but non-harmful content.

2604.12359.title: Compiling Activation Steering into Weights via Null-Space Constraints for Stealthy Backdoors
2604.12359.tldr: This work extracts a steering vector that captures the difference between compliant and refusal behaviors, and compile it into a persistent weight modification that activates only when the trigger is present, and imposes a null-space constraint so that the injected edit remains dormant on clean inputs.
2604.12359.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.16077.title: Ensembling Sparse Autoencoders
2505.16077.tldr: Ensembling SAEs improves the reconstruction of language model activations along with SAE stability, and on downstream tasks such as concept detection and spurious correlation removal, SAE ensembles achieve better performance, showing improved practical utility.

2607.14611.title: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
2607.14611.tldr: This work evaluates two agentic systems, Anthropic Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, across four models and shows that persistent memory changes the threat model for prompt injection and motivate defenses that protect memory updates without removing useful agent adaptation.

2604.03867.title: Where to Steer: Input-Dependent Layer Selection for Steering Improves LLM Alignment
2604.03867.tldr: Where to Steer (W2S) is introduced, a framework that adaptively selects the intervention layer conditioned on the input, by learning a mapping from input embeddings to optimal steering layers, and highlights the importance of input-dependent control in LLM alignment.

2505.14536.title: Breaking Bad Tokens: Detoxification of LLMs Using Sparse Autoencoders
2505.14536.tldr: This paper leverages sparse autoencoders to identify toxicity-related directions in the residual stream of models and performs targeted activation steering using the corresponding decoder vectors, revealing trade-offs between toxicity reduction and language fluency and suggesting practical guidelines for safer language-model deployment.
2505.14536.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.14071.title: Textual Steering Vectors Can Improve Visual Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models
2505.14071.tldr: It is found that text-derived steering consistently enhances multimodal accuracy across diverse MLLM architectures and visual tasks, and highlights textual steering vectors as a powerful, efficient mechanism for enhancing grounding in MLLMs with minimal additional data collection and computational overhead.

2506.12044.title: Why Do Some Inputs Break Low-Bit LLM Quantization?
2506.12044.tldr: This work reveals why certain examples result in large quantization errors and which model components are most critical for performance preservation and establishes a hypothesis that relates the residual stream magnitudes to error amplification and accumulation over layers.
2506.12044.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.10375.title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful for Java Function Bug Detection?
2505.10375.tldr: This work provides the first empirical evidence that SAEs can be used to detect software bugs directly from the internal representations of pretrained LLMs, without any fine-tuning or task-specific supervision.

2505.00190.title: Empirical Evaluation of Progressive Coding for Sparse Autoencoders
2505.00190.tldr: This work compares progressive coding based on subset pruning of SAEs -- to jointly training nested SAEs, or so-called Matryoshka SAEs -- on a language modeling task and shows Matryoshka SAEs exhibit lower reconstruction loss and recaptured language modeling loss, as well as higher representational similarity.

2504.20271.title: Investigating task-specific prompts and sparse autoencoders for activation monitoring

2504.02821.title: Sparse Autoencoders Learn Monosemantic Features in Vision-Language Models
2504.02821.tldr: This work extends the application of SAEs to Vision-Language Models (VLMs), such as CLIP, and introduces a comprehensive framework for evaluating monosemanticity at the neuron-level in visual representations, and reveals that SAEs trained on VLMs significantly enhance the monosemanticity of individual neurons.

2506.13181.title: Align-then-Unlearn: Embedding Alignment for LLM Unlearning
2506.13181.tldr: Align-then-Unlearn is a novel framework that performs unlearning in the semantic embedding space rather than directly on output tokens, suggesting that embedding-based unlearning offers a promising and robust approach to removing conceptual knowledge.

2503.24277.title: Evaluating and Designing Sparse Autoencoders by Approximating Quasi-Orthogonality
2503.24277.tldr: A novel activation function, top-AFA, is introduced, which builds upon the formulation of approximate feature activation (AFA), which enables top-$k$ style activation without requiring a constant hyperparameter $k$ to be tuned, dynamically determining the number of activated features for each input.

2503.16851.title: Interpretable LLM Guardrails via Sparse Representation Steering
2503.16851.tldr: SRS is proposed, a novel framework that achieves fine-grained and interpretable control over LLM behavior by first disentangling internal activations into a sparse, semantically meaningful representation space, and then selectively steering relevant dimensions.

2603.01574.title: DualSentinel: A Lightweight Framework for Detecting Targeted Attacks in Black-box LLM via Dual Entropy Lull Pattern
2603.01574.tldr: Extensive evaluations show that DualSentinel is both highly effective (superior detection accuracy with near-zero false positives) and remarkably efficient (negligible additional cost), offering a truly practical path toward securing deployed LLMs.

2602.04893.title: A Causal Perspective for Enhancing Jailbreak Attack and Defense
2602.04893.tldr: This work proposes Causal Analyst, a framework that integrates LLMs into data-driven causal discovery to identify the direct causes of jailbreaks and leverage them for both attack and defense, and demonstrates the practical utility of these insights through two applications.
2602.04893.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2505.18325.title: Understanding and Mitigating Overrefusal in LLMs from an Unveiling Perspective of Safety Decision Boundary
2505.18325.tldr: RASS is presented, an automated framework for prompt generation and selection that strategically targets overrefusal prompts near the safety boundary that provides a more precise and interpretable view of model safety decisions but also seamlessly extends to multilingual scenarios.
2505.18325.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2503.11232.title: PrivacyScalpel: Enhancing LLM Privacy via Interpretable Feature Intervention with Sparse Autoencoders
2503.11232.tldr: PrivacyScalpel is introduced, a novel privacy-preserving framework that leverages LLM interpretability techniques to identify and mitigate PII leakage while maintaining performance and insights into the mechanisms underlying PII memorization contributing to the broader field of model interpretability and secure AI deployment.
2503.11232.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2605.05980.title: TACT: Mitigating Overthinking and Overacting in Coding Agents via Activation Steering
2605.05980.tldr: This paper introduces TACT (Think-Act Calibration via activation Steering), to detect and mitigate agent drift in the residual stream before it surfaces as a behavioral failure, and positions TACT as a viable handle for reliable long-horizon agents.

2503.11127.title: Don't Forget It! Conditional Sparse Autoencoder Clamping Works for Unlearning
2503.11127.tldr: This paper uses SAEs to identify unwanted concepts from the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy dataset within gemma-2-2b internals and uses feature steering to reduce the model's ability to answer harmful questions while retaining its performance on harmless queries.

2606.26474.title: Localizing RL-Induced Tool Use to a Single Crosscoder Feature
2606.26474.tldr: The findings show that DFC partitioning concentrates RL-introduced capability into a minimal, steerable feature set that enables runtime behavioral control of agentic LLMs.

2503.03601.title: Feature-Level Insights into Artificial Text Detection with Sparse Autoencoders
2503.03601.tldr: It is shown that modern LLMs have a distinct writing style, especially in information-dense domains, even though they can produce human-like outputs with personalized prompts.
2503.03601.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.03032.title: SAFE: A Sparse Autoencoder-Based Framework for Robust Query Enrichment and Hallucination Mitigation in LLMs
2503.03032.tldr: Empirical results demonstrate that SAFE consistently improves query generation accuracy and mitigates hallucinations across all datasets, achieving accuracy improvements of up to 29.45%.
2503.03032.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2503.00177.title: Steering Large Language Model Activations in Sparse Spaces
2503.00177.tldr: SAS is introduced, a method that leverages sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to steer LLM behavior in sparse spaces by isolating behavior-specific features through a contrastive prompt-pairing approach, which defines a set of features that can selectively reinforce or suppress behaviors.

2502.20578.title: Interpreting CLIP with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders
2502.20578.tldr: MSAE establishes a new state-of-the-art Pareto frontier between reconstruction quality and sparsity for CLIP, achieving 0.99 cosine similarity and less than 0.1 fraction of variance unexplained while maintaining ~80% sparsity.

2502.16722.title: Layer-Wise Evolution of Representations in Fine-Tuned Transformers: Insights from Sparse AutoEncoders
2502.16722.tldr: The underlying mechanisms of fine-tuning are explored in the BERT transformer by analyzing activation similarity, training Sparse AutoEncoders (SAEs), and visualizing token-level activations across different layers, providing key insights into the inner workings of fine-tuning and its impact on representation learning within transformer architectures.

2510.20369.title: Ask a Strong LLM Judge when Your Reward Model is Uncertain
2510.20369.tldr: This work proposes an uncertainty-based routing framework that efficiently complements a fast RM with a strong but costly LLM judge, enabling principled uncertainty quantification to guide routing and formulates advantage estimation in policy gradient methods as pairwise preference classification.

2604.11322.title: Do LLMs Know Tool Irrelevance? Demystifying Structural Alignment Bias in Tool Invocations
2604.11322.tldr: This work identifies a widespread yet overlooked mechanistic flaw in tool refusal, which is term structural alignment bias: Even when a tool fails to serve the user's goal, LLMs still tend to invoke it whenever query attributes can be validly assigned to tool parameters.
2604.11322.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.12179.title: Sparse Shift Autoencoders for Identifying Concepts from Large Language Model Activations
2502.12179.tldr: This paper introduces Sparse Shift Autoencoders (SSAEs) which learn sparse representations of differences between embeddings rather than the embeddings themselves, and shows that SSAEs are identifiable from paired observations which differ in multiple unknown concepts, but not all.

2502.09135.title: Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders
2502.09135.tldr: This paper explores the application of sparse autoencoders (SAE) to interpret the internal representations of protein language models, specifically focusing on the ESM-2 8M parameter model, and identifies potential interpretations linked to various protein characteristics.

2502.00127.title: Sparse Autoencoder Insights on Voice Embeddings
2502.00127.tldr: This study applies sparse autoencoders to speaker embeddings generated from a Titanet model, demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique in extracting mono-semantic features from non-textual embedded data and revealing that the au-toencoder can identify and manipulate features such as language and music, which are not evident in the original embedding.
2502.00127.venue: 2025 Conference on Artificial Intelligence x Multimedia (AIxMM)

2501.11036.title: LF-Steering: Latent Feature Activation Steering for Enhancing Semantic Consistency in Large Language Models
2501.11036.tldr: LF-Steering is proposed, a novel activation steering approach to precisely identify latent feature representations responsible for semantic inconsistency in large Language Models that maps the hidden states of the relevant transformer layer into a sparsely activated, high-dimensional feature space based on a sparse autoencoder (SAE).

2601.09321.title: SpatialJB: How Text Distribution Art Becomes the "Jailbreak Key" for LLM Guardrails
2601.09321.tldr: The proposal of SpatialJB exposes a key weakness in current guardrails and emphasizes the importance of spatial semantics, offering new insights to advance LLM safety research.

2410.12299.title: Semantics-Adaptive Activation Intervention for LLMs via Dynamic Steering Vectors
2410.12299.tldr: Semantics-Adaptive Dynamic Intervention is proposed, a novel method that constructs a dynamic steering vector to intervene model activations at inference time and dynamically steers model behavior by scaling element-wise activations based on the directions of input semantics.

2505.12313.title: ExpertSteer: Intervening in LLMs through Expert Knowledge
2505.12313.tldr: This work proposes ExpertSteer, a novel approach that leverages arbitrary specialized expert models to generate steering vectors, enabling intervention in any LLMs, and demonstrates that ExpertSteer significantly outperforms established baselines across diverse tasks at minimal cost.

2501.09929.title: Interpretable Steering of Large Language Models with Feature Guided Activation Additions

2501.00581.title: Are the Values of LLMs Structurally Aligned with Humans? A Causal Perspective
2501.00581.tldr: This work argues that a latent causal value graph underlies the value dimensions of LLMs and that, despite alignment training, this structure remains significantly different from human value systems.
2501.00581.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.15017.title: Active Honeypot Guardrail System: Probing and Confirming Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
2510.15017.tldr: This work proposes a honeypot-based proactive guardrail system that transforms risk avoidance into risk utilization, fine-tunes a bait model to generate ambiguous, non-actionable but semantically relevant responses, which serve as lures to probe user intent.

2412.04139.title: Monet: Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers
2412.04139.tldr: Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers (Monet) architecture is introduced, which incorporates sparse dictionary learning directly into end-to-end Mixture-of-Experts pretraining and enables scaling the expert count to 262,144 per layer while total parameters scale proportionally to the square root of the number of experts.

2509.25843.title: ASGuard: Activation-Scaling Guard to Mitigate Targeted Jailbreaking Attack
2509.25843.tldr: Activation-Scaling Guard (ASGuard) is introduced, an insightful, mechanistically-informed framework that surgically mitigates this specific vulnerability of large language models and underscores how adversarial suffixes suppress the propagation of the refusal-mediating direction, based on mechanistic analysis.

2412.02605.title: Interpretable Company Similarity with Sparse Autoencoders
2412.02605.tldr: SAE features surpass sector classifications and embeddings in capturing fundamental company characteristics, evidenced by their superior performance in correlating logged monthly returns and generating higher Sharpe ratios in co-integration trading strategies, which underscores deeper fundamental similarities among companies.

2411.16725.title: $\textit{Revelio}$: Interpreting and leveraging semantic information in diffusion models
2411.16725.tldr: An in-depth analysis of how different diffusion architectures, pre-training datasets, and language model conditioning impacts visual representation granularity, inductive biases, and transfer learning capabilities is provided.
2411.16725.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2412.12101.title: InterPLM: Discovering Interpretable Features in Protein Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2412.12101.tldr: It is demonstrated that PLMs encode rich, interpretable representations of protein biology and a systematic framework to uncover and understand these latent features is proposed, which can fill in missing annotations in protein databases and enable targeted steering of protein sequence generation.

2506.15882.title: Fractional Reasoning via Latent Steering Vectors Improves Inference Time Compute
2506.15882.tldr: This work proposes Fractional Reasoning, a training-free and model-agnostic framework that enables continuous control over reasoning intensity at inference time, going beyond the limitations of fixed instructional prompts.

2411.08790.title: Can sparse autoencoders be used to decompose and interpret steering vectors?
2411.08790.tldr: This paper investigates why directly applying SAEs to steering vectors yields misleading decompositions, identifying two reasons: (1) steering vectors fall outside the input distribution for which SAEs are designed, and (2) steering vectors can have meaningful negative projections in feature directions, which SAEs are not designed to accommodate.

2601.15801.title: Attributing and Exploiting Safety Vectors through Global Optimization in Large Language Models
2601.15801.tldr: A novel inference-time white-box jailbreak method that exploits the identified safety vectors through activation repatching, providing strong evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed GOSV framework on LLM safety interpretability.

2410.11468.title: Can sparse autoencoders make sense of gene expression latent variable models?

2410.03334.title: An X-Ray Is Worth 15 Features: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Radiology Report Generation
2410.03334.tldr: SAE-Rad is introduced, which uses sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to decompose latent representations from a pre-trained vision transformer into human-interpretable features, and represents the first instance of using mechanistic interpretability techniques explicitly for a downstream multi-modal reasoning task.

2410.01280.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Temporal Difference Learning in Large Language Models
2410.01280.tldr: This work establishes a methodology for studying and manipulating in-context learning with SAEs, paving the way for a more mechanistic understanding of how LLMs solve specific classes of problems, such as reinforcement learning problems, in-context.

2409.04185.title: Residual Stream Analysis with Multi-Layer SAEs
2409.04185.tldr: The multi-layer SAE (MLSAE) is introduced: a single SAE trained on the residual stream activation vectors from every transformer layer, representing a new approach to understanding how representations change as they flow through transformers.

2609.09902.title: Contrastive Projection: Reading Transformer Internals by Differencing Logit Lenses
2609.09902.tldr: Subtracting two closely matched prompts'hidden states and projecting through the unembedding cancels the shared component and surfaces what separates them, an operation equivalent to reading a RepE/ActAdd steering vector through a logit lens.

2608.24958.title: Can We Read the Mind of an Audio LLM? A Verbalizable, Multilingual Middle-Layer Workspace
2608.24958.tldr: Reading a base Qwen3-Omni with a logit lens at the audio-token positions, it is found that the answer to a spoken question becomes legible - in words - in the model's middle layers, before it emits any token.

2510.18053.title: Adaptive Divergence Regularized Policy Optimization for Fine-tuning Generative Models
2510.18053.tldr: Adaptive Divergence Regularized Policy Optimization (ADRPO) is introduced, which automatically adjusts regularization strength based on advantage estimates-reducing regularization for high-value samples while applying stronger regularization to poor samples, enabling policies to navigate between exploration and aggressive exploitation according to data quality.

2608.22332.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Sequential Activation Patching
2608.22332.tldr: This work introduces a sequential activation patching framework that traces CoT-conditioned attention-head activations across token positions and aggregates their effects using Part-of-Speech-guided analysis, and introduces Sequential Multi-Head Patching to evaluate the joint contribution of distributed head sets, together with cross-question and random activation controls.

2608.10430.title: Actionable Hallucination Detection: Translating Latent Uncertainty into Agentic Critique
2608.10430.tldr: The Latent Critic is introduced, a lightweight low-rank adapter that operates concurrently with a frozen base LLM's generation to actively restructure the transformer's residual stream---amplifying latent grounding signals and translating them into localized, natural language feedback within a single sequence.

2608.03629.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model
2608.03629.tldr: The result is mixed: a shared carrier emerges across all five tested instances, collapse and dissociation hold on most but not all, and a nonzero interaction is measurable on three of five, at layer pairs outside the same-block case the companion theorem covers.

2608.03620.title: A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation
2608.03620.tldr: An idealized model where a conditional computation is carried additively through a residual stream, F(x)=F_0(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i(x)v_i$, read out by a linear functional is studied, and three exact results are proved, including an exact first-order interaction formula with a provably second-order remainder.

2608.02486.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs
2608.02486.tldr: A per-entity (probe, output) decomposition framework, a citation-anchored cross-cultural ground truth, a within- versus cross-mode correlation test for language-conditioned readout, and per-entity predictions for all 18 models are released.

2607.05587.title: A Mechanistic Lens on Semantic Conflicts: Using Activation Patching to Understand LLM Behavior
2607.05587.tldr: The findings show that semantic conflicts affect program comprehension and downstream tasks, with relevant information concentrated in a small number of causally active residual-stream states, and demonstrate a framework for mechanistically analyzing how LLMs integrate code-related information under controlled semantic variations.

2606.15733.title: Vernier: Probing Representational Misalignment Behind Lexical Gaps in Causal Reasoning

2605.25310.title: Tool-Call Dependency Structure is Linearly Decodable in LLM Agent Residual Streams
2605.25310.tldr: A low-capacity edge probe on the residual stream of Qwen3-32B decodes the tool-call dependency graph well above both a Hewitt--Liang random-label control and a positional baseline, evidence that the representation propagates rather than passively reads out, though the realised tool call does not move.

2605.24614.title: Measuring the Depth of LLM Unlearning via Activation Patching
2605.24614.tldr: The Unlearning Depth Score (UDS), a metric that quantifies the mechanistic depth of unlearning via activation patching, is introduced, confirming the causal approach as the most reliable for unlearning evaluation.

2605.12991.title: Not Just RLHF: Why Alignment Alone Won't Fix Multi-Agent Sycophancy
2605.12991.tldr: This work localizes the corruption to a narrow mid-layer window where attention carries the causal weight and MLP contribution is negligible; patching above this window restores 96% of the clean-to-pressured P(correct) gap.

2511.19517.title: Automating Deception: Scalable Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
2511.19517.tldr: A novel, automated pipeline for generating large-scale, psychologically-grounded multi-turn jailbreak datasets, which highlights a critical divergence in how current safety architectures handle conversational context and underscores the need for defenses that can resist narrative-based manipulation.

2605.03217.title: Moral Sensitivity in LLMs: A Tiered Evaluation of Contextual Bias via Behavioral Profiling and Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.03217.tldr: This work introduces the Moral Sensitivity Index (MSI), a metric that quantifies the probability of biased output across a graduated, seven-tier stress test ranging from abstract numerical problems to scenarios rooted in historical and socioeconomic injustice, and identifies distinct behavioral signatures shaped by alignment design.

2606.01060.title: MENTIS: What Belief Changes Under Alignment? Measuring Multi-Scale Latent Torsion in Language Models
2606.01060.tldr: This study reveals that alignment-induced change is selective rather than uniform: normative concepts exhibit larger torsion shifts than factual concepts on average; torsion is negatively correlated with contextual entropy; and peak effects localize to architecture-specific mid-to-late layers.

2512.11838.title: D-STEER - Preference Alignment Techniques Learn to Behave, not to Believe -- Beneath the Surface, DPO as Steering Vector Perturbation in Activation Space
2512.11838.tldr: This paper argues that DPO does not rewrite a models internal beliefs; instead, it acts as a low rank steering mechanism that nudges activations along a small number of preference directions, supporting a behavioral illusion view of DPO.

2604.23130.title: From Concept-Aligned Tokens to Vulnerable Features: Mechanistic Localization of Jailbreaks
2604.23130.tldr: This work introduces a token-driven mechanistic pipeline that decomposes the residual stream of Gemma-2-2B into Sparse Autoencoder features and identifies feature subgroups associated with unsafe behavior, and shows that individual harmful prompt tokens are sufficient to localize vulnerability-relevant SAE feature subgroups without relying on broader cluster-level aggregation.

2603.11388.title: Deactivating Refusal Triggers: Understanding and Mitigating Overrefusal in Safety Alignment
2603.11388.tldr: This paper examines how overrefusal arises under safety alignment, and proposes a mitigation strategy inspired by the findings that achieves a more favorable trade-off between defense against jailbreak attacks and responsiveness to benign queries, outperforming prior methods.
2603.11388.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2604.01476.title: From Rebound to Remedy: Understanding and Mitigating Reward Hacking via Representation Engineering
2604.01476.tldr: Advantage Modification, which integrates shortcut concept scores into GRPO advantage computation to penalize hacking rollouts before policy updates, is proposed, which provides more robust suppression of hacking compared with generation-time activation steering.

2603.13652.title: Causal Attribution via Activation Patching
2603.13652.tldr: Causal Attribution via Activation Patching (CAAP), which estimates the contribution of individual image patches to the ViT's prediction by directly intervening on internal activations rather than using learned masks or synthetic perturbation patterns, consistently outperforms existing methods in various settings and produces more faithful and localized attributions.

2510.11390.title: Medical Interpretability and Knowledge Maps of Large Language Models
2510.11390.tldr: The results can guide future research on fine-tuning, un-learning or de-biasing LLMs for medical tasks by suggesting at which layers in the model these techniques should be applied.

2510.11210.title: Discursive Circuits: How Do Language Models Understand Discourse Relations?
2510.11210.tldr: This work introduces a task called Completion under Discourse Relation (CuDR), where a model completes a discourse given a specified relation, and constructs a corpus of minimal contrastive pairs tailored for activation patching in circuit discovery.
2510.11210.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2510.04528.title: Unified Threat Detection and Mitigation Framework (UTDMF): Combating Prompt Injection, Deception, and Bias in Enterprise-Scale Transformers
2510.04528.tldr: The Unified Threat Detection and Mitigation Framework (UTDMF), a scalable, real-time pipeline for enterprise-grade models like Llama-3.1, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.5, is introduced, with novel contributions include a generalized patching algorithm for multi-threat detection, three groundbreaking hypotheses on threat interactions, and a deployment-ready toolkit with APIs for enterprise integration.

2508.15882.title: Beyond Transcription: Mechanistic Interpretability in ASR
2508.15882.tldr: These experiments reveal previously unknown internal dynamics, including specific encoder-decoder interactions responsible for repetition hallucinations and semantic biases encoded deep within acoustic representations, which demonstrate the benefits of extending and applying interpretability techniques to speech recognition.

2402.11367.title: Multi Task Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Common Sense Reward
2402.11367.tldr: This work first shows that inverse reinforcement learning, even when it succeeds in training an agent, does not learn a useful reward function, and demonstrates that this problem can be solved by training simultaneously on multiple tasks, that is, multi-task inverse reinforcement learning can be applied to learn a useful reward function.

2608.22527.title: Stress Testing Unlearning Algorithms
2608.22527.tldr: WMDP++ is introduced, an extension of WMDP that addresses gaps in existing unlearning benchmarks by incorporating targeted extrac- tion of unlearned information and systematic evaluation on boundary questions.

2507.20936.title: Dissecting Persona-Driven Reasoning in Language Models via Activation Patching
2507.20936.tldr: This study examines how assigning a persona influences a model's reasoning on an objective task using activation patching and reveals that the early Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers attend not only to the syntactic structure of the input but also process its semantic content.
2507.20936.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2504.09191.title: Feature-Aware Malicious Output Detection and Mitigation
2504.09191.tldr: A feature-aware method for harmful response rejection (FMM), which detects the presence of malicious features within the model's feature space and adaptively adjusts the model's rejection mechanism.

2602.01695.title: Beyond Dense States: Sparse Transcoders as Causally Testable Operators for LLM Latent Reasoning
2602.01695.tldr: LSTR (Latent Sparse Transcoder Reasoning), a framework that turns sparse transcoders from post-hoc diagnostic tools into in-loop, intervenable transition components for latent reasoning, and suggests that sparse latent transitions can preserve the compression benefits of latent reasoning while making the resulting trajectories more inspectable and intervenable.

2504.07898.title: How do Large Language Models Understand Relevance? A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective
2504.07898.tldr: This article systematically investigates how different LLM modules contribute to relevance judgment through the lens of mechanistic interpretability and identifies a multi-stage, progressive process in generating either pointwise or pairwise relevance judgment.

2609.00213.title: Uncovering and Mitigating Aggregation-Induced Reward Hacking in Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning
2609.00213.tldr: Adaptive Multi-Reward Projection is proposed, a lightweight online method that reallocates aggregation weights using three signals, relative shortfall, reward volatility, and recent progress, increasing pressure on lagging, unstable, or stagnant dimensions while relieving saturated ones.

2605.13155.title: Pareto-Guided Optimal Transport for Multi-Reward Alignment
2605.13155.tldr: A Pareto Frontier-Guided Optimal Transport (PG-OT) framework is proposed that constructs a prompt-specific Pareto frontier and maps dominated samples toward it via distribution-aware optimal transport and develops both online and offline optimization strategies tailored to diverse reward signal characteristics.

2406.11431.title: Super(ficial)-alignment: Strong Models May Deceive Weak Models in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2406.11431.tldr: This work aims to explore whether strong models might deliberately make mistakes in areas known to them but unknown to weak models within one alignment dimension, in exchange for a higher reward in another dimension, and highlights the urgent need to pay more attention to the true reliability of superalignment.

2504.02976.title: Localized Definitions and Distributed Reasoning: A Proof-of-Concept Mechanistic Interpretability Study via Activation Patching
2504.02976.tldr: These findings demonstrate that factual knowledge is more localized and associative knowledge depends on distributed representations, and showed that editing efficacy depends on task type.

2505.12189.title: Mitigating Content Effects on Reasoning in Language Models through Fine-Grained Activation Steering
2505.12189.tldr: It is demonstrated that activation-level interventions offer a scalable inference-time strategy for enhancing the robustness of LLMs, contributing towards more systematic and unbiased reasoning capabilities.

2407.11215.title: Mechanistic interpretability of large language models with applications to the financial services industry
2407.11215.tldr: This paper investigates GPT-2 Small’s attention pattern when prompted to identify potential violation of Fair Lending laws, and pioneering the use of mechanistic interpretability to shed some light on the inner workings of large language models for use in financial services applications.
2407.11215.venue: International Conference on AI in Finance

2407.00886.title: Efficient Automated Circuit Discovery in Transformers using Contextual Decomposition

2609.20722.title: Deep Noir: Autonomous Steering Discovery via Architectural Chronometry in Transformer Models
2609.20722.tldr: It is shown that steering creates a predictable prompt-injection attack surface whose vulnerability increases monotonically with steering magnitude, relevant to agent systems deploying steered classifiers.

2609.16967.title: Target-Language Generation in Multilingual Models: Activation Steering and Optimal Control
2609.16967.tldr: An optimal control method for target-language text generation as well as a framework for evaluating the quality of generated text in terms of language adherence, linguistic coherence, and semantic coherence are developed.

2609.15654.title: Empathy Is Steerable but Multi-Axial: Mechanism Geometry and Persona Effects in LLMs

2609.10658.title: GEOSTEER: Geodesic Optimization for Activation Steering in Large Language Models
2609.10658.tldr: GeoSteer is proposed, an optimization-based method for norm-preserving activation steering that consistently improves over state-of-the-art activation steering baselines and replaces predefined one-step edits with adaptive, geometry-aware optimization.

2609.06968.title: Tracing Query Expansion Effects through Sparse Autoencoder Features
2609.06968.tldr: Analysis shows that effective QE induces layer-concentrated changes in sparse latents aligned with retrieval intent and entity attributes, rather than only perturbing final query embeddings, and suggests that SAEs can explain QE effects and offer a lightweight option for precise retrieval behavior modulation without query rewriting or retriever fine-tuning.

2601.19847.title: Identifying and Transferring Reasoning-Critical Neurons: Improving LLM Inference Reliability via Activation Steering
2601.19847.tldr: AdaRAS (Adaptive Reasoning Activation Steering), a lightweight test-time framework that improves reasoning reliability by selectively intervening on neuron activations during inference, enhancing incorrect reasoning traces while avoiding degradation on already-correct cases.

2609.06951.title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions

2609.06934.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
2609.06934.tldr: Post-hoc safety training is the dominant way to align large language models, yet jailbreaks, fine-tuning attacks, and activation-space probes keep recovering the behaviors it was meant to remove, so a little benign fine-tuning restores it.

2609.06289.title: Steering Geometry: Validating Human Value Geometry in LLM Steering Space
2609.06289.tldr: It is found that distribution-driven methods recover human value topologies aligned with theoretical predictions, and better geometric alignment also leads to more human-consistent transfer across values: steering one value correctly lifts compatible values and suppresses opposing ones.

2609.05800.title: Spillover-Aware Multi-Value Steering for Pluralistic LLM Alignment
2609.05800.tldr: This work traces spillover to geometric entanglement of steering directions, captured by their Gram matrix, and derives a zero-cost correction from an activation-norm-penalized objective that decouples each direction's contribution exactly.

2609.04792.title: Can Activation Steering Capture Multidimensional Authorship Style?
2609.04792.tldr: Aspect-Aware Activation Steering (A3S) improves authorship style transfer where it is genuinely multi-aspect, outperforms a trained baseline in preference evaluations on out-of-domain benchmarks, and keeps target-exemplar overlap consistently low.

2608.30986.title: Controlling Refusal Behavior of LLMs via Stiefel-Constrained Rotation Steering
2608.30986.tldr: This work develops a self-contained methodology for learning parameter-efficient rotational transformations based on Riemannian optimization and empirically validate the proposed rotation-based steering scheme, demonstrating its superiority in intervention efficiency.

2608.30197.title: ALTSTEER: Selective Safety Steering for Moving Beyond Hard Refusals to Constructive Alternatives
2608.30197.tldr: ALTSTEER is an inference-time framework that couples selective intervention with refusal-anchored constructive redirection within a single inference pass, and uses an internal refusal-relevant signal to decide when to steer, and applies staged steering to shift generation from refusal-oriented control toward constructive alternatives.

2608.29458.title: Reference-Grafting Matches Fine-Tuning at Eliciting Sandbagged Capabilities

2608.29461.title: A Causal Model for Locating and Unlocking Sandbagging in Model Organisms
2608.29461.tldr: A causal model of how sandbagging is carried in the residual stream is proposed, which predicts a window of layers, after the last sandbagging write and before the answer commit, in which a single-layer reference graft of the sandbagging axis to its honest value restores the full capability.

2607.07918.title: Efficient Safety Alignment of Language Models via Latent Personality Traits
2607.07918.tldr: Latent Personality Alignment (LPA) is introduced, which replaces explicit harm refusal with adversarial training on just 66 harm-agnostic statements drawn from psychometric personality literature, hypothesizing that personality-anchored representations share latent structure with harm avoidance, so adversarially stabilizing them implicitly constrains the subspace exploited by jailbreak attacks.

2605.08496.title: Latent Personality Alignment: Improving Harmlessness Without Mentioning Harms
2605.08496.tldr: The proposed Latent Personality Alignment (LPA), a sample-efficient defense that achieves robustness by training models on abstract personality traits rather than specific harmful behaviors, achieves comparable attack success rates to methods trained on 150k+ examples, while maintaining superior utility.

2605.27681.title: Behavioural Analysis of Alignment Faking
2605.27681.tldr: This work identifies three separable drivers of alignment faking -- values, goal guarding, and sycophancy -- and shows via targeted prompt ablations and activation steering that each independently modulates AF behaviour.

2608.24988.title: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal
2608.24988.tldr: This work studies the stability of embedded steering for refusal suppression and brevity induction across five instruction-tuned models (3B-14B) under non-adversarial SFT and RLHF.

2608.24335.title: SteerCheck: Attribution Specificity and Alignment Leakage in Activation-Steering Audits
2608.24335.tldr: SteerCheck, a preregistered attribution audit that matches off-target KL and separates mean, protected-tail, polarity, transfer, and semantic claims is introduced, a preregistered attribution audit that matches off-target KL and separates mean, protected-tail, polarity, transfer, and semantic claims.

2608.22985.title: What Does Activation Steering Control? Attribution Across Answer Encodings and Output-Sensitive Subspaces
2608.22985.tldr: This work introduces Cross-Encoding Steering Evaluation, which freezes an intervention while re-encoding answers to the same held-out items, which favors extraction-index over semantic-label following on NormBank in three models.

2608.16577.title: BabelSteering: Multilingual Safety Alignment via English Steering Vectors
2608.16577.tldr: The findings suggest that activation steering may provide a practical, low- cost mechanism for extending English-derived safety signals to other languages, and introduce a multilingual translation-and-evaluation pipeline to facilitate future work on cross-lingual safety interventions.

2608.15687.title: THESIS-MoE: Trainable Hierarchical Extraction and SteerIng of Sycophancy in Mixture-of-Experts
2608.15687.tldr: A shared contrastive signal is introduced that identifies where sycophancy lives across the MoE hierarchy and drives interventions that act only where the behavior is present, demonstrating that sycophancy resides in identifiable computational subcircuits and can be selectively steered while maintaining a favorable removal-retention trade-off.

2607.28906.title: Token-Level Diagnosis of Sycophancy in LLMs with Attribution-Guided Steering
2607.28906.tldr: The ASI is introduced, an Integrated Gradients-based token attribution method, which measures the degree to which a model's decision is driven by authority-related text, and a attribution-guided contrastive activation steering method is proposed to mitigate LLM sycophancy.

2607.25907.title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
2607.25907.tldr: Activation steering controls model behavior by editing internal activations at inference time, and finds that a single MLP neuron is eval-correlated but not causal at both scales, and that scanning the real Pile yields a natural-text baseline competitive with the optimizer for the internal direction.

2607.23083.title: LoRA for Gender-Inclusive Rewriting and Activation Steering for Counter-Narrative Generation
2607.23083.tldr: This paper presents the IHLC system for the LT-EDI 2026 Shared Task, addressing both gender-inclusive rewriting and counter-narrative generation, and highlights the practical potential and current limitations of activation steering as a lightweight alternative to parameter updates for controllable and socially aligned language generation.

2607.21300.title: Unlearning Under Imbalance: Benchmarking Fairness in Multimodal LLM Unlearning
2607.21300.tldr: FAIRGET is proposed, the first Visual Question Answering benchmark that evaluates unlearning under unbalanced, realistic, forget requests, and FAUN is proposed, the first unlearning algorithm for MLLMs that forgets unlearning data while preserving model fairness.

2606.31876.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
2606.31876.tldr: Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a light-weight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data, achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility.

2607.20803.title: The Geometry of Personality: Activation Steering with Jungian Cognitive Functions
2607.20803.tldr: A framework comprising a Jungian evaluation protocol and a dataset of over 2,100 role-playing character narrations is introduced to establish a framework for studying interpretable, effective, and multi-dimensional personality control in LLM activation space.

2607.19806.title: OPIUM: Mitigating Steering Externalities and Over-Refusal via Dual Objective Latent Optimization
2607.19806.tldr: Across steering-externality and over-refusal settings, OPIUM improves the safety--utility tradeoff relative to vanilla steering and directional ablation, suggesting that harmful side effects of activation steering can often be mitigated directly in activation space.

2607.09156.title: Activation Steering Transfer to Agents: One Gain Ratio Does Not Identify Potency and Efficacy
2607.09156.tldr: The consequence is a measurement instruction rather than a theorem: a transfer conclusion read at one strength does not identify what changed, because a displacement and a gain are not distinguishable from a single operating point.

2607.06845.title: LLMs Silently Correct African American English: Auditing and Mitigating Dialect Bias via Activation Steering
2607.06845.tldr: Across six instruction-tuned LLMs, it is shown that state-of-the-art models systematically prefer Standard American English continuations even when the preceding context is in AAE, effectively rewriting AAE into SAE.
