2609.11028.tldr: BenchShield is presented, a model-backed instrumentation layer for reward integrity in LLM-agent evaluation that grounds detection in a finite lifecycle model of an evaluation's reward-relevant events and achieves 96% accuracy in detecting reward hacking from infrastructure-side evidence.

2609.04282.title: Step Back to Move Forward: Reflection-Aware Preference Optimization for Visual Generation
2609.04282.tldr: Reflection-Aware GRPO (RA-GRPO) is presented, a new RL-based preference alignment framework for diffusion generative models that significantly outperforms existing methods, particularly in mitigating reward hacking and improving generalization.

2608.30724.title: BAITBENCH: Measuring Agent Reward Hacking with Optional Shortcuts Planted in ML Tasks
2608.30724.tldr: This work releases BAITBENCH, a suite of three synthetic tabular ML tasks that each contain a shortcut that allows agents to inflate the public test score but fail on a hidden test set, and releases an annotated dataset of transcripts containing reward hacks as a testbed for evaluating reward-hacking mitigations head-to-head.

2604.12500.title: Safety Training Modulates Harmful Misalignment Under On-Policy RL, But Direction Depends on Environment Design
2604.12500.tldr: On-policy RL preserves a safety buffer inherent in the model's own generation distribution, one that is bypassed during off-policy settings, one that is bypassed during off-policy settings.

2608.29564.title: TACS: Trajectory-Aware Candidate Selection for LLM Jailbreak Suffix Optimization
2608.29564.tldr: TACS is proposed, a trajectory-aware candidate selection framework for jailbreak suffix optimization that augments per-step evaluation with a trajectory-aware proxy and stabilizes selection with reference-policy regularization and a discriminator-estimated chi-squared correction, encouraging choices that remain effective beyond the current step.

2608.29460.title: Can escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure?
2608.29460.tldr: This work evaluates escalation channels, structured reporting tools available to the agent at the point of conflict, as a decision-environment intervention that both reduces reward hacking and surfaces the infrastructure defects that trigger it.

2412.17618.title: Dynamic safety cases for frontier AI
2412.17618.tldr: A Dynamic Safety Case Management System (DSCMS) is proposed to support both the initial creation of a safety case and its systematic, semi-automated revision over time, providing a framework for adapting to new insights and strengthening incident response.

2608.27505.title: A Survey on Rubric-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
2608.27505.tldr: A Bayesian framework that defines constitutions as prior distributions over evaluation criteria and rubrics as conditional instantiations is introduced, and a taxonomy of rubric-guided RL along the prior-posterior axis is presented, covering constitutional AI, instance-specific rubrics, process-level supervision, self-evolving rubrics, and their agentic and multimodal extensions.

2608.26324.title: Privacy Without Regret: Differentially Private Inference-Time Alignment
2608.26324.tldr: Private Inference-Time Pessimism (PrivITP) is introduced, which combines $\chi^2$-regularized rejection sampling with a two-phase Gaussian mechanism, and achieves ex-post $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP with a privacy cost independent of the number of responses, cleanly decouples the regularization parameter from the privacy parameter, and attains the skyline up to a noise-inflation term.

2608.17804.title: An Empirical Study of Reward Specification and Benchmark Reliability in GRPO-based LLM Unlearning
2608.17804.tldr: This work compares four reward designs that span lexical suppression, anti-refusal shaping, rubric-based broad answering, and an explicit refusal contrast, and shows that optimization success is not equivalent to behavioral unlearning: RWKU forget scores, held-out completion audits, terminal training-rollout audits, and training dynamics can point to different conclusions.

2608.17393.title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents
2608.17393.tldr: LIFE-RL, a framework that bridges native coding-agent harnesses with scalable policy-gradient optimization without modifying their internal control flow, is presented and evaluated by training the sparse MoE model Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with GSPO across three native coding-agent harnesses.

2601.03868.title: What Matters For Safety Alignment?
2601.03868.tldr: It is argued that safety must be treated as an explicit constraint or a core optimization objective during these stages, not merely subordinated to the pursuit of general capability, for developing more secure and reliable AI systems.

2608.06179.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
2608.06179.tldr: SAGA (Score-weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment), a parser-guided preference optimisation framework that replaces human labels with dependency-parser supervision, demonstrates that parser-derived supervision is a practical alternative to human preference annotation for grammatical alignment in low-resource languages where high-quality dependency parsers are available.

2608.11243.title: The Off-Support Barrier: Why Semantic Safety Constraints Are Not Learning-Problem Invariants, and What Follows for Prior Design, Containment, and Verification
2608.11243.tldr: It is argued that a single structural fact organizes a wide range of phenomena in contemporary AI safety: a semantic safety constraint is an off-support object, a semantic safety constraint is an off-support object.

2607.10191.title: Breaking the Quality--Intelligibility Trade-off in Streaming Target Speaker Extraction via Deep-Feature-Anchored Preference Optimization
2607.10191.tldr: Two complementary improvements are proposed: an enlarged Conformer convolution kernel for richer local spectro-temporal modeling, and WavLM-anchored Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) fine-tuning strategy, providing an optimization anchor that resists hacking.

2607.09492.title: Multimodal Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
2607.09492.tldr: This work studies reward hacking in MLLM RL across safety VQA, chart VQA, and stress-test settings, varying reward design, data ambiguity, model scale, and RL algorithm (GRPO, RLOO, DAPO), and introduces Newly Rewarded Failure Rate (NRFR), which measures failures among samples whose proxy reward improves over the SFT baseline.

2607.21151.title: V-DEAL: Diagnosing Video Safety De-Calibration as an Understanding-Refusal Coupling Failure
2607.21151.tldr: A prompt injection intervention method is introduced that reduces attack success rates by an average of 48.24 percentage points and achieves performance comparable to prior fine-tuning-based methods, providing an effective and practical means to address such safety risks in Video LLMs.

2607.05904.title: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
2607.05904.tldr: It is shown that conditioned on a candidate, a judge scores plausibility, not correctness, leaving false-positive basins a policy learns to exploit, and a falsifiable bound predicts which regimes are exposed.

2606.28955.title: Modification-Considering Value Learning for Reward Hacking Mitigation in RL
2606.28955.tldr: Modification-Considering Value Learning (MCVL), which operationalizes the theoretical idea of current utility optimization for standard value-based RL, and mitigates reward hacking while continuing to improve the intended objective.

2606.25057.title: LLM-Based Scientific Peer Review: Methods, Benchmarks, and Reliability Challenges
2606.25057.tldr: This survey offers a systems-level analysis of LLM-based scientific peer review, focusing on two core evaluative functions: critique generation and score prediction, and outlines key open challenges in modeling subjective disagreement and cross-domain generalization.

2606.19818.title: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF
2606.19818.tldr: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling (UARM), which equips reward models with calibrated uncertainty via quantile-based conformal prediction and reweights GRPO advantages through heteroscedastic variance decomposition, is proposed.

2606.05468.title: FlowPRO: Reward-Free Reinforced Fine-Tuning of Flow-Matching VLAs via Proximalized Preference Optimization
2606.05468.tldr: This work presents FlowPRO, a reward-free offline reinforced fine-tuning framework for flow-matching VLAs, and proposes RPRO (Robotic Flow-matching Proximalized Preference Optimization), a preference-optimization objective tailored to the flow-matching action head of VLA models.

2608.05495.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
2608.05495.tldr: It is argued that home-agent safety is best served by learned routing and sensor fusion, not by replacing detectors with an MLLM, and introduced PromptShield-Home, a pilot benchmark of realistic smart-home scenarios spanning addressee ambiguity, screen/audio injection, health-monitor false triggers, mixed occupancy, and a legitimate-command floor.

2606.03216.title: Follow-Your-Preference++: Rethinking Preference Alignment for Image Inpainting
2606.03216.tldr: Most reward models provide valid signals for preference data construction, although some are unreliable as evaluators, and a simple ensemble of reward models mitigates biases and yields robust, generalizable performance.

2509.23082.title: Follow-Your-Preference: Towards Preference-Aligned Image Inpainting
2509.23082.tldr: This paper leverages the prominent direct preference optimization approach for alignment training and employs public reward models to construct preference training datasets, which significantly outperform prior models across standard metrics, GPT-4 assessments, and human evaluations.

2605.25988.title: What Makes a Medical Checker Trainable? Diagnosing Signal Collapse and Reward Hacking in Checker-Guided RAG for Biomedical QA
2605.25988.tldr: It is found that the checker's output distribution during training, not its held-out accuracy, decides whether it provides trainable gradient, which frames these as boundary conditions for verifier-as-reward systems.

2605.25062.title: Cultivating Machine Intelligence: The OMEGA Shift from Top-Down Optimization to Autopoietic Cognitive Ecologies
2605.25062.tldr: Recursive, Ecological, Cognitive, Lifelike, Adaptive, Intelligent Machine, a theoretical framework for cultivating intelligence through computational ecology rather than engineering it through strict optimization, suggests the spontaneous emergence of dual-process cognition, sensory specialization, analogical reasoning, and intrinsic motivation as natural consequences of evolution under resource constraints.

2605.15803.title: Embedding-perturbed Exploration Preference Optimization for Flow Models
2605.15803.tldr: This work proposes Embedding-perturbed Exploration Preference Optimization, a novel framework that sustains optimization through embedding-level perturbation within sample groups, guaranteeing a robust variance that preserves the discriminative signal throughout the training process.

2512.24146.title: Taming Preference Mode Collapse via Directional Decoupling Alignment in Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
2512.24146.tldr: Directional Decoupling Alignment (D$^2$-Align), a novel framework that mitigates Preference Mode Collapse by directionally correcting the reward signal, is proposed, which achieves superior alignment with human preference.

2511.22044.title: Distillability of LLM Security Logic: Predicting Attack Success Rate of Outline Filling Attack via Ranking Regression
2511.22044.tldr: A novel framework that incorporates an improved outline filling attack to achieve dense sampling of the model's security boundaries is proposed and a ranking regression paradigm is introduced that replaces standard regression and trains the proxy model to predict which prompt yields a higher ASR.

2605.27823.title: Disentangling Adversarial Prompts: A Semantic-Graph Defense for Robust LLM Security
2605.27823.tldr: The Adversarial Prompt Disentanglement framework is proposed, a novel defense mechanism that proactively identifies and neutralizes malicious components in input prompts before they are processed by the LLM, and offers a scalable, ethically grounded defense against prompt-based adversarial threats.

2604.26360.title: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Discounting for Mitigating Reward Hacking
2604.26360.tldr: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Discounting (UARD) is introduced, a principled framework that jointly models epistemic uncertainty in value estimation via ensemble disagreement and aleatoric uncertainty in human preference annotations via annotator variability through a confidence-adjusted Reliability Filter that adaptively modulates reward weighting during policy optimization.

2604.17769.title: Reverse Constitutional AI: A Framework for Controllable Toxic Data Generation via Probability-Clamped RLAIF
2604.17769.tldr: This work proposes Reverse Constitutional AI, a framework for automated and controllable adversarial data generation that moves beyond isolated jailbreak prompts and introduces probability clamping within reinforcement learning from AI feedback, which stabilizes adversarial optimization while preserving adversarial intent.
2604.17769.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.17573.title: Beyond Static Snapshots: A Grounded Evaluation Framework for Language Models at the Agentic Frontier
2604.17573.tldr: It is argued that current evaluation frameworks for large language models (LLMs) suffer from four systematic failures that make them structurally inadequate for deployed, agentic systems: distributional, temporal, scope, and process invalidity, and the Grounded Continuous Evaluation (GCE) framework is proposed.

2605.27375.title: LCO: LLM-based Constraint Optimization for Safer Agentic LLMs in Real-world Tasks
2605.27375.tldr: LCO consists of two modules: self-thought module, which guides the LLM to proactively deliberate and integrate potential safety constraints before execution; and evolutionary sampling module, which employs LLM-based crossover and mutation to constrain the model's actions within a safe solution space while maintaining task performance.
2605.27375.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.07480.title: KG-DF: A Black-box Defense Framework against Jailbreak Attacks Based on Knowledge Graphs
2511.07480.tldr: This work proposes a Knowledge Graph Defense Framework (KG-DF), a framework that enhances defense performance against various jailbreak attack methods, while also improving the response quality of the LLM in general QA scenarios by incorporating domain-general knowledge.

2604.06833.title: FedDetox: Robust Federated SLM Alignment via On-Device Data Sanitization
2604.06833.tldr: FedDetox is proposed, a robust framework tailored for Small Language Models (SLMs) on resource-constrained edge devices that preserves model safety at a level comparable to centralized baselines without compromising general utility.

2509.23055.title: Peacemaker or Troublemaker: How Sycophancy Shapes Multi-Agent Debate
2509.23055.tldr: This work introduces the first operational framework that proposes a formal definition of sycophancy specific to MADS settings, develops new metrics to evaluate the agent sycophancy level and its impact on information exchange in MADS, and systematically investigates how varying levels of sycophancy across agent roles affects outcomes in both decentralized and centralized debate frameworks.

2604.02686.title: Beyond Semantic Manipulation: Token-Space Attacks on Reward Models
2604.02686.tldr: Token Mapping Perturbation Attack (TOMPA), a framework that performs adversarial optimization directly in token space by bypassing the standard decode-re-tokenize interface between the policy and the reward model, enables the attack policy to optimize over raw token sequences rather than coherent natural language.

2603.21175.title: Reward Sharpness-Aware Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Models
2603.21175.tldr: This work introduces methods that exploit gradients from a robustified reward model without requiring its retraining, and employs gradients from a flattened reward model, obtained through parameter perturbations of the diffusion model and perturbations of its generated samples.

2603.17461.title: AR-CoPO: Align Autoregressive Video Generation with Contrastive Policy Optimization
2603.17461.tldr: Experiments on Self-Forcing demonstrate that AR-CoPO improves both out-of-domain generalization and in-domain human preference alignment over the baseline, providing evidence of genuine alignment rather than reward hacking.

2512.03356.title: From static to adaptive: immune memory-based jailbreak detection for large language models
2512.03356.tldr: This work introduces the Immune Memory Adaptive Guard (IMAG) framework, a closed-loop architecture that transitions LLM defense from rigid filtering to autonomous adaptive mitigation, and achieves a superior average detection accuracy across diverse and complex attack types.

2603.10279.title: Robust Post-Training for Generative Recommenders: Why Exponential Reward-Weighted SFT Outperforms RLHF
2603.10279.tldr: It is shown that temperature $\lambda$ explicitly and quantifiably controls the robustness-improvement tradeoff, providing practitioners with a single interpretable regularization hyperparameter with theoretical grounding.

2603.06797.title: Best-of-Tails: Bridging Optimism and Pessimism in Inference-Time Alignment
2603.06797.tldr: It is shown theoretically that light-tailed regimes favor optimism to unearth high-quality outliers, whereas heavy-tailed regimes require pessimism to guard against reward mis-calibration in the extremes, and Best-of-Tails is introduced, an adaptive inference-time alignment framework that uses Tsallis divergence as a tunable regularizer to provide a finer granularity of interpolation between these extremes.

2601.22359.title: The Unseen Threat: Residual Knowledge in Machine Unlearning under Perturbed Samples
2601.22359.tldr: A fine-tuning strategy is proposed, named RURK, that penalizes the model's ability to re-recognize perturbed forget samples, and demonstrates that residual knowledge is prevalent across existing unlearning methods and that this approach effectively prevents residual knowledge.

2510.01223.title: Jailbreaking LLMs via Semantically Relevant Nested Scenarios with Targeted Toxic Knowledge
2510.01223.tldr: This work is the first to find and systematically verify that LLMs'alignment defenses are not sensitive to nested scenarios, where these scenarios are highly semantically relevant to the queries and incorporate targeted toxic knowledge.

2605.07883.title: Beyond "I cannot fulfill this request": Alleviating Rigid Rejection in LLMs via Label Enhancement
2605.07883.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that LANCE significantly alleviates the rigid rejection problem while maintaining high security standards, significantly outperforming existing baseline models in terms of helpfulness and naturalness of responses.

2602.18297.title: Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory
2602.18297.tldr: Information-theoretic analysis is used to show that non-zero mutual information between CoT and output is a necessary but not sufficient condition for CoT monitorability, and proposes two complementary approaches that significantly improve monitor accuracy while preventing CoT degeneration even when training against a monitor.

2505.13787.title: Preference Learning with Lie Detectors can Induce Honesty or Evasion
2505.13787.tldr: A more complex picture is illustrated: depending on the context, lie-detector-enhanced training can be a powerful tool for scalable oversight, or a counterproductive method encouraging undetectable misalignment.

2602.14689.title: Exposing the Systematic Vulnerability of Open-Weight Models to Prefill Attacks
2602.14689.tldr: This work presents the largest empirical study to date of prefill attacks, evaluating over 20 existing and novel strategies across multiple model families and state-of-the-art open-weight models and revealing a critical and previously underexplored vulnerability with significant implications for deployment.

2602.12155.title: FAIL: Flow Matching Adversarial Imitation Learning for Image Generation
2602.12155.tldr: Flow Matching Adversarial Imitation Learning is proposed, which minimizes policy-expert divergence through adversarial training without explicit rewards or pairwise comparisons, and generalizes effectively to discrete image and video generation, and functions as a robust regularizer to mitigate reward hacking in reward-based optimization.

2602.08646.title: Gradient Preconditioning for Efficient and Reliable Reward-Guided Generation
2602.08646.tldr: A gradient preconditioning method that makes reward-guided generation with one-step generative models both efficient and reliable and prevents reward hacking.

2608.17220.title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance
2608.17220.tldr: PACE (Policy-Attested Contract Execution), a transaction-level authorization framework that interposes between an LLM-based agent and on-chain execution, is presented and frame its claims as logic-level safety within a reproducible benchmark rather than deployment-ready DeFi security.

2607.14493.title: Context Contamination in LLM Analysis of Network Security Logs: Poison with Passive Prompt Injection and Mitigation Evaluation
2607.14493.tldr: The results establish that LLM-based log analysis creates an inherent confused deputy vulnerability where untrusted data and trusted instructions compete indistinguishably for model attention, requiring defense in-depth architectures and continued human oversight for security-critical decisions.

2601.11583.title: Bit-politeia: An AI Agent Community in Blockchain
2601.11583.tldr: Bit-politeia is proposed, an AI agent community on blockchain designed to construct a fair, efficient, and sustainable resource allocation system that minimizes human bias and mitigates resource centralization issues found in traditional peer review.

2606.16349.title: From Refusal Geometry to Safety Geometry: Harmfulness--Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning
2606.16349.tldr: A dual safety-geometry protocol measures harmfulness carriers, refusal carriers, and their coupling across aligned instruction-tuned anchors and matched Mistral-7B-v0.1 SFT/R2D2 training trajectories to frame harmfulness--refusal coupling as an operational diagnostic for safety-geometry dynamics under adversarial fine-tuning.

2604.27019.title: Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning Reorganizes Refusal Geometry
2604.27019.tldr: A geometry-reorganization account of R2D2 along a robustness--utility frontier, without establishing adaptive robustness is supported, as well as a low-dimensional but utility-coupled carrier.

2512.22647.title: FinPercep-RM: A Fine-grained Reward Model and Co-evolutionary Curriculum for RL-based Real-world Super-Resolution
2512.22647.tldr: A Co-evolutionary Curriculum Learning (CCL) mechanism, where both the reward model and the ISR model undergoing synchronized curricula undergo synchronized curricula enables stable training while suppressing reward hacking.

2512.20806.title: Safety Alignment of LMs via Non-cooperative Games
2512.20806.tldr: This work introduces a different paradigm: framing safety alignment as a non-zero-sum game between an Attacker LM and a Defender LM trained jointly via online reinforcement learning, driving iterative improvement.

2512.04332.title: Data-regularized Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models at Scale
2512.04332.tldr: Data-regularized Diffusion Reinforcement Learning (DDRL), a novel framework that uses the forward KL divergence to anchor the policy to an off-policy data distribution, is introduced, enabling robust, unbiased integration of RL with standard diffusion training and establishing a robust and scalable paradigm for diffusion post-training.

2512.02807.title: SR-GRPO: Stable Rank as an Intrinsic Geometric Reward for Large Language Model Alignment
2512.02807.tldr: Stable rank is proposed, an intrinsic, annotation-free quality signal derived from model representations that measures the effective dimensionality of hidden states by computing the ratio of total variance to dominant-direction variance, capturing quality through how information distributes across representation dimensions.

2406.19032.title: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Reliability-Aware Alignment
2406.19032.tldr: This work proposes an approach to improve weak-to-strong generalization by involving the reliability of weak supervision signals in the alignment process, and presents effective techniques for error-robust model alignment, reducing error propagation from noisy supervision and enhancing the accuracy and reliability of LLMs.

2606.27709.title: Low-Agreeableness Persona Conditioning for Safe LLM Fine-Tuning
2606.27709.tldr: This work introduces a persona-driven rewriting pipeline that conditions user turns on low agreeableness and pairs this with warm, de-escalating assistant responses, and shows that safer empathetic fine-tuning is achievable through data design alone, without safety labels, harm detectors, or changes to the training objective.

2512.00724.title: UMM-RM: An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking
2512.00724.tldr: Experiments show that, compared with standard dense RMs, UMM-RM improves accuracy on preference data, reduces reward hacking during PPO training, and yields more stable preference alignment.

2511.21654.title: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
2511.21654.tldr: This work introduces EvilGenie, a benchmark for reward hacking in programming settings, and measures reward hacking rates for three popular proprietary coding agents: OpenAI's Codex, Anthropic's Claude Code, and Google's Gemini CLI.

2511.20256.title: The Image as Its Own Reward: Reinforcement Learning with Adversarial Reward for Image Generation
2511.20256.tldr: Adv-GRPO is introduced, an RL framework with an adversarial reward that iteratively updates both the reward model and the generator, and it is shown that combining reference samples with foundation-model rewards enables distribution transfer and flexible style customization.

2511.12294.title: ProofWright: Towards Agentic Formal Verification of CUDA
2511.12294.tldr: ProofWright provides end-to-end guarantees of memory safety, thread safety, and semantic correctness for LLM-generated CUDA kernels, and demonstrates that scalable, automated formal verification of LLM-generated GPU code is feasible.

2505.16265.title: Think-RM: Enabling Long-Horizon Reasoning in Generative Reward Models
2505.16265.tldr: Think-RM is introduced, a training framework that enables long-horizon reasoning in GenRMs by modeling an internal thinking process that generates flexible, self-guided reasoning traces that support advanced capabilities such as self-reflection, hypothetical reasoning, and divergent reasoning.

2510.18849.title: Towards Faithful and Controllable Personalization via Critique-Post-Edit Reinforcement Learning
2510.18849.tldr: Critique-Post-Edit is proposed, a robust reinforcement learning framework that enables more faithful and controllable personalization in large language models and substantially outperforms standard PPO on personalization benchmarks.

2501.09620.title: Beyond Reward Hacking: Causal Rewards for Large Language Model Alignment
2501.09620.tldr: This work proposes a novel causal reward modeling approach that integrates causality to mitigate these spurious correlations in reward modeling and shows that this approach mitigates various types of spurious correlations effectively, resulting in more reliable and fair alignment of LLMs with human preferences.

2602.03402.title: Risk Awareness Injection: Calibrating Vision-Language Models for Safety without Compromising Utility
2602.03402.tldr: Risk Awareness Injection is proposed, a lightweight and training-free framework for safety calibration that restores LLM-like risk recognition by amplifying unsafe signals in VLMs and substantially reduces attack success rate without compromising task performance.

2510.13036.title: Repairing Reward Functions with Feedback to Mitigate Reward Hacking
2510.13036.tldr: Preference-Based Reward Repair (PBRR): an automated iterative framework that repairs a human-specified proxy reward function by learning an additive, transition-dependent correction term from preferences that has a cumulative regret that matches, up to constants, that of prior preference-based RL methods.

2510.01367.title: Is It Thinking or Cheating? Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort
2510.01367.tldr: This work proposes TRACE (Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation), a scalable unsupervised approach for oversight where current monitoring methods prove ineffective, and shows that TRACE can discover unknown loopholes during training.

2506.05339.title: Flattery, Fluff, and Fog: Diagnosing and Mitigating Idiosyncratic Biases in Preference Models
2506.05339.tldr: This work systematically investigates the relationship between training data biases and preference model miscalibration across five idiosyncratic features of language model generations: length, structure, jargon, sycophancy and vagueness, and proposes a simple post-training method based on counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) using synthesized contrastive examples.

2605.21834.title: On-Policy Consistency Training Improves LLM Safety with Minimal Capability Degradation
2605.21834.tldr: On-Policy Consistency Training (OPCT), a new consistency training approach where the objective is computed over the model's own responses to prompts, supervised by itself conditioned on corresponding contrastive prompts, outperforms its SFT counterpart on all safety desiderata.

2510.00430.title: PromptLoop: Plug-and-Play Prompt Refinement via Latent Feedback for Diffusion Model Alignment

2509.22047.title: MO-GRPO: Mitigating Reward Hacking of Group Relative Policy Optimization on Multi-Objective Problems
2509.22047.tldr: MO-GRPO is proposed, an extension of GRPO with a simple normalization method to reweight the reward functions automatically according to the variances of their values, showing MO-GRPO to be a promising algorithm for multi-objective reinforcement learning problems.
2509.22047.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.12668.title: Evaluation of Best-of-N Sampling Strategies for Language Model Alignment
2502.12668.tldr: An extension of the RBoN framework, called Stochastic RBoN sampling (SRBoN), is proposed, which is a theoretically guaranteed approach to worst-case RBoN in proxy reward and performs an empirical evaluation using the AlpacaFarm and Anthropic datasets to evaluate which factors of the regularization strategies contribute to the improvement of the true proxy reward.

2404.01054.title: Regularized Best-of-N Sampling with Minimum Bayes Risk Objective for Language Model Alignment
2404.01054.tldr: This research proposes MBR-BoN, a variant of BoN that aims to mitigate reward hacking at inference time by incorporating the Minimum Bayes Risk objective as a proximity regularization term, and shows empirically and analytically that the MBR objective quantifies the proximity of the response to the reference policy, serving as a proximity regularizer.
2404.01054.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.21319.title: RLBFF: Binary Flexible Feedback to bridge between Human Feedback & Verifiable Rewards
2509.21319.tldr: It is shown that Reward Models trained in this manner can outperform Bradley-Terry models when matched for data and achieve top performance on RM-Bench and JudgeBench, and a fully open source recipe to align Qwen3-32B using RLBFF and the authors' Reward Model is presented.

2504.06141.title: Adversarial Training of Reward Models
2504.06141.tldr: Adv-RM, a novel adversarial training framework that automatically identifies adversarial examples that receive high rewards from the target RM but are OOD and of low quality, significantly outperforms conventional RM training, increasing stability and enabling more effective RLHF training in both synthetic and real-data settings.

2509.15557.title: Reward Hacking Mitigation using Verifiable Composite Rewards
2509.15557.tldr: This work addresses two primary forms of reward hacking: i) providing a final answer without preceding reasoning, and ii) employing non-standard reasoning formats to exploit the reward mechanism.
2509.15557.venue: ACM International Conference on Bioinformatics, Computational Biology and Biomedicine

2511.10692.title: StyleBreak: Revealing Alignment Vulnerabilities in Large Audio-Language Models via Style-Aware Audio Jailbreak
2511.10692.tldr: StyleBreak is proposed, a novel style-aware audio jailbreak framework that systematically investigates how diverse human speech attributes affect LAM alignment robustness, and employs a two-stage style-aware transformation pipeline that perturbs both textual content and audio to control linguistic, paralinguistic, and extralinguistic attributes.

2604.24953.title: ViPO: Visual Preference Optimization at Scale
2604.24953.tldr: This work proposes Poly-DPO, which extends the DPO objective with an additional polynomial term that dynamically adjusts model confidence based on dataset characteristics, enabling effective learning across diverse data distributions and confirms that addressing both algorithmic adaptability and data quality is essential for scaling visual preference optimization.

2508.17637.title: Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization for Large Language Models
2508.17637.tldr: A novel Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization (RoPO) algorithm is proposed, which implicitly constrains the output layer logits with the KL divergence inherited from DPO and explicitly constrains the intermediate hidden states by fine-tuning on a multi-granularity orthogonal matrix.
2508.17637.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2605.10611.title: Re-Triggering Safeguards within LLMs for Jailbreak Detection
2605.10611.tldr: This paper proposes a jailbreaking prompt detection method for large language models (LLMs) to defend against jailbreak attacks, and introduces an embedding disruption method to re-activate the safeguards within LLMs by re-triggering them.

2605.10582.title: Guaranteed Jailbreaking Defense via Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing
2605.10582.tldr: This paper proposes a novel smoothing-based defense method, termed Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing (DR-Smoothing), which integrates a two-stage prompt processing scheme-first disrupting the input prompt, then rectifying it-into the conventional smoothing defense framework, and presents a theoretical analysis for generic smoothing framework.

2511.08399.title: Aligning by Misaligning: Boundary-aware Curriculum Learning for Multimodal Alignment
2511.08399.tldr: This work proposes Boundary-Aware Curriculum with Local Attention (BACL), a lightweight add-on that turns these borderline cases into a curriculum signal, with a Boundary-aware Negative Sampler and a Contrastive Local Attention loss that highlights where the mismatch occurs.

2603.13318.title: Residual Stream Analysis of Overfitting And Structural Disruptions
2603.13318.tldr: Variance Concentration Loss (VCL), an auxiliary regularizer that penalizes excessive variance concentration in mid-layer residuals, is proposed and empirical results demonstrate that VCL reduces false refusals by over 35 percentage points while maintaining or improving performance on general benchmarks such as MMLU and GSM8K.

2508.17229.title: Multi-Metric Preference Alignment for Generative Speech Restoration
2508.17229.tldr: This work investigates the challenges of applying preference-based post-training to generative speech restoration, focusing on how to define a robust preference signal and curate high-quality data to avoid reward hacking.

2508.14313.title: AIRL-S: Unifying Reinforcement Learning and Search-Based Test-Time Scaling via Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning
2508.14313.tldr: This paper introduces AIRL-S, a unified framework that integrates Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization and establishes a robust and cost-effective methodology for scaling test-time computation in complex reasoning tasks.

2508.07137.title: A Principled Loss Function for Direct Language Model Alignment
2508.07137.tldr: This paper proposes a novel loss function derived directly from the RLHF optimality condition that targets a specific, finite value for the logits difference, which is dictated by the underlying reward, rather than its maximization.

2508.09155.title: A Rolling Stone Gathers No Moss: Adaptive Policy Optimization for Stable Self-Evaluation in Large Multimodal Models
2508.09155.tldr: AdaPO is an online reinforcement learning framework capable of adaptively adjusting training objective in real time according to the current training state for each task, and significantly enhances both direct reasoning and self-evaluation capability.

2606.20636.title: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
2606.20636.tldr: SkillHarness moves beyond static skill abstractions by modeling skill learning and utilization as a safety-constrained interaction process, and introduces the skill boundary that leverages multi-source supervision signals to identify safe skills from interaction trajectories, and construct self-improving safety constraints throughout the skill lifecycle.

2507.18742.title: Specification Self-Correction: Mitigating In-Context Reward Hacking Through Test-Time Refinement
2507.18742.tldr: Specification Self-Correction (SSC), a novel, test-time framework that enables an LM to identify and correct flaws within its own guiding specification, is introduced.

2402.08005.title: Refined Direct Preference Optimization with Synthetic Data for Behavioral Alignment of LLMs
2402.08005.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning, Optimization, and Data Science

2506.11702.title: Configurable Preference Tuning with Rubric-Guided Synthetic Data
2506.11702.tldr: This paper challenges the assumption of monolithic preferences by introducing Configurable Preference Tuning (CPT), a novel framework for endowing language models with the ability to dynamically adjust their behavior based on explicit, human-interpretable directives.

2507.04136.title: A Technical Survey of Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Large Language Models
2507.04136.tldr: This survey offers a comprehensive foundation on the integration of RL with language models, highlighting prominent algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization, Q-Learning, and Actor-Critic methods and presents a comparative taxonomy based on reward modeling, feedback mechanisms, and optimization strategies.
2507.04136.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology

2506.22957.title: Agent-to-Agent Theory of Mind: Testing Interlocutor Awareness among Large Language Models
2506.22957.tldr: This paper examines interlocutor inference across three dimensions-reasoning patterns, linguistic style, and alignment preferences-and shows that LLMs reliably identify same-family peers and certain prominent model families, such as GPT and Claude.
2506.22957.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2602.12316.title: GT-HarmBench: Benchmarking AI Safety Risks Through the Lens of Game Theory
2602.12316.tldr: GT-HarmBench, a benchmark of 1,535 high-stakes scenarios spanning game-theoretic structures such as the Prisoner's Dilemma, Stag Hunt and Chicken, is introduced and it is shown that game-theoretic interventions improve socially beneficial outcomes by up to 18%.

2506.16507.title: Robust Reward Modeling via Causal Rubrics
2506.16507.tldr: This work introduces Crome (Causally Robust Reward Modeling), a novel framework grounded in an explicit causal model designed to mitigate reward hacking, which significantly outperforms standard baselines on RewardBench and is testified by the consistent gains obtained in a Best-of-N inference setting.

2412.16378.title: REFA: Reference Free Alignment for multi-preference optimization
2412.16378.tldr: REFA is a new alignment framework that proposes probabilistic control on a structural token that controls termination, and its core innovation is a new class of regularizers that operate directly on the probability of the End-of-Sequence token, a previously unexploited control lever.

2410.21545.title: CARMO: Dynamic Criteria Generation for Context-Aware Reward Modelling
2410.21545.tldr: This work proposes Context-Aware Reward Modeling (CARMO), a novel approach that first generates dynamic, context-relevant criteria to ground the reward model before producing reward scores, and shows that such criteria generation can mitigate reward hacking.

2506.15651.title: AutoRule: Reasoning Chain-of-thought Extracted Rule-based Rewards Improve Preference Learning
2506.15651.tldr: This work presents AutoRule, a fully automated method for extracting rules from preference feedback and formulating them into rule-based rewards, and finds that AutoRule demonstrates reduced reward hacking compared to a learned reward model when run over two episodes.

2506.08712.title: ConfPO: Exploiting Policy Model Confidence for Critical Token Selection in Preference Optimization
2506.08712.tldr: Experimental results on challenging alignment benchmarks, including AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, demonstrate that ConfPO consistently outperforms uniform DAAs across various LLMs, delivering better alignment with zero additional computational overhead.

2505.20556.title: Learning a Pessimistic Reward Model in RLHF
2505.20556.tldr: The work shows the feasibility of learning a pessimistic reward model robust against reward hacking in offline reinforcement learning from human feedback and finds that one can learn a high-quality policy on the authors' pessimistic reward without using any regularization.

2505.17352.title: Alignment and Safety of Diffusion Models via Reinforcement Learning and Reward Modeling: A Survey
2505.17352.tldr: This survey reviews recent progress on aligning text-to-image diffusion models through reinforcement learning, reward modeling, preference optimization, and safety-specific fine-tuning and synthesizes the literature into a set of open challenges.

2505.14946.title: Reinforcement Learning from User Feedback
2505.14946.tldr: This work trains a reward model, P[Love], to predict the likelihood that an LLM response will receive a Love Reaction, a lightweight form of positive user feedback, and integrates P[Love] into a multi-objective policy optimization framework alongside helpfulness and safety objectives.

2609.21793.title: CASCADE Against Jailbreaks: Combination Across Stages with Controlled Attack-Defense Evaluation
2609.21793.tldr: Across 19 attacks and 15 defenses, it is found that no single defense is universally best, but well-chosen combinations achieve substantial safety with minimal utility degradation, yielding practical recommendations for layered defense pipelines.

2607.02914.title: Oyster-II: Reinforcement Learning for Constructive Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
2607.02914.tldr: Oyster-II is proposed, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based constructive safety alignment framework that adopts a Zero-RL paradigm combined with a multi-stage reinforcement learning strategy that comprehensively surpasses both Qwen3-14B and its predecessor Oyster-I on safety dimensions.

2505.12843.title: Bias Fitting to Mitigate Length Bias of Reward Model in RLHF
2505.12843.tldr: FiMi-RM (Bias Fitting to Mitigate Length Bias of Reward Model), a framework that autonomously learns and corrects underlying bias patterns that improves length-controlled win rate and reduces verbosity without compromising its performance when applied to alignment algorithms.
2505.12843.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.10045.title: CHARM: Calibrating Reward Models With Chatbot Arena Scores
2504.10045.tldr: This paper proposes a calibration method named CHatbot Arena calibrated Reward Modeling (CHARM) that leverages Elo scores from the Chatbot Arena to construct debiased preference datasets and adjust reward model scoring, and demonstrates that CHARM provides a simple, effective, and broadly applicable approach to building more reliable and fair reward models.

2510.17759.title: VERA-V: Variational Inference Framework for Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models
2510.17759.tldr: VERA-V is introduced, a variational inference framework that recasts multimodal jailbreak discovery as learning a joint posterior distribution over paired text-image prompts, allowing efficient sampling of diverse jailbreaks and providing distributional insights into vulnerabilities.

2503.11720.title: RPO: Fine-Tuning Visual Generative Models via Rich Vision-Language Preferences
2503.11720.tldr: Rich Preference Optimization (RPO) is introduced, a novel pipeline that leverages rich feedback signals from Vision Language Models to improve the curation of preference pairs for fine-tuning visual generative models like text-to-image diffusion models.

2503.06171.title: ROCM: RLHF on consistency models
2503.06171.tldr: This work proposes a direct reward optimization framework for applying RLHF to consistency models, incorporating distributional regularization to enhance training stability and prevent reward hacking, and leverages first-order gradients, making it more efficient and less sensitive to hyperparameter tuning.

2411.04712.title: SEE-DPO: Self Entropy Enhanced Direct Preference Optimization
2411.04712.tldr: This work introduces a self-entropy regularization mechanism in reinforcement learning from human feedback that effectively mitigates reward hacking and improves DPO training by encouraging broader exploration and greater robustness, leading to improved stability and enhanced image quality across the latent space.

2406.12845.title: Interpretable Preferences via Multi-Objective Reward Modeling and Mixture-of-Experts
2406.12845.tldr: The trained model, ArmoRM-Llama3-8B, obtains state-of-the-art performance on RewardBench, a benchmark evaluating RMs for language modeling, and approaches the performance of the much larger Nemotron-4 340B reward model.
2406.12845.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2607.24392.title: When LLM Defenses Backfire: Characterizing Safety, Performance, and Cost Trade-offs
2607.24392.tldr: It is found that defenses rarely improve downstream capability, but instead vary in how they trade safety gains against usability and efficiency as well as performance impact, over-refusal on benign inputs, and inference cost.

2608.11878.title: ToolHazard: Scaling Adversarial Environments for Security Evaluation and Alignment of LLM-based Agents
2608.11878.tldr: Experiments reveal substantial agent vulnerabilities and show that injection timing and placement affect attack effectiveness, and ToolHazard-generated alignment data improves security on both ToolHazard-Bench and AgentDojo while preserving benign task utility.

2502.11656.title: Uncovering the Impact of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Direct Preference Optimization: Lessons from Text-to-SQL
2502.11656.tldr: Analysis shows that CoT reasoning is crucial for unlocking DPO's potential, as it mitigates reward hacking, strengthens discriminative capabilities, and improves scalability, and offer valuable insights for building more robust Text-to-SQL models.
2502.11656.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.15203.title: Taxonomy, Evaluation and Exploitation of IPI-Centric LLM Agent Defense Frameworks
2511.15203.tldr: This Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) paper introduces a comprehensive taxonomy of IPI-centric defense frameworks, classifying them along five dimensions, and identifies six root causes of defense circumvention.

2402.00667.title: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Scalable Oversight and Ensemble Learning
2402.00667.tldr: This paper presents a follow-up study to OpenAI's recent superalignment work on Weak-to-Strong Generalization (W2SG), and discusses the impact of improved weak supervision on enhancing weak-to-strong generalization based on in-context learning.

2608.26780.title: AI Control Scientist: LLM-driven Agentic System for Automated Control Design
2608.26780.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that the proposed agentic system can automatically generate multiple representative control systems, outperforms existing automated baselines in both design success rate and optimization efficiency, and has the potential to transform control system design from human-driven to agent-driven.

2502.08977.title: Text-driven 3D Human Generation via Contrastive Preference Optimization
2502.08977.tldr: This work designs a preference optimization module that integrates multiple models to comprehensively capture the full range of textual features and introduces a negation preference module to mitigate over-optimization of irrelevant details by leveraging static-dynamic negation prompts, effectively preventing ``reward hacking".

2501.18873.title: Best Policy Learning from Trajectory Preference Feedback
2501.18873.tldr: Posterior Sampling for Preference Learning is proposed, a novel algorithm inspired by Top-Two Thompson Sampling that maintains posteriors over the reward model and dynamics that provides the first Bayesian simple regret guarantees for PbRL and an efficient approximation that outperforms existing baselines on simulation and image generation benchmarks.

2501.17030.title: Challenges in Ensuring AI Safety in DeepSeek-R1 Models: The Shortcomings of Reinforcement Learning Strategies
2501.17030.tldr: The limitations of Reinforcement Learning as the primary approach for reducing harmful outputs in DeepSeek-R1 are examined and Supervised Fine-Tuning is compared with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to achieve robust harmlessness reduction.

2501.06481.title: Focus-N-Fix: Region-Aware Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Image Generation
2501.06481.tldr: Focus-N-Fix is proposed, the first region-aware fine-tuning method that trains models to correct only previously problematic image regions and shows significant improvements in regions where the original model was deficient in safety, plausibility, or other criteria.

2512.11986.title: Learning to Extract Context for Context-Aware LLM Inference
2512.11986.tldr: A reinforcement learning based context generator, designed in an autoencoder-like fashion, is trained to infer contextual signals grounded in the prompt and use them to guide response generation, demonstrating the effectiveness of context extraction for safer and more reliable LLM inferences.

2411.17760.title: Efficient Self-Improvement in Multimodal Large Language Models: A Model-Level Judge-Free Approach
2411.17760.tldr: A novel, model-level judge-free self-improvement framework that generates preference learning pairs using a controllable hallucination mechanism and optimize data quality by leveraging lightweight, contrastive language-image encoders to evaluate and reverse pairs when necessary.

2411.09341.title: Approximated Variational Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Alignment
2411.09341.tldr: A novel training objective is proposed, Approximated Variational Alignment (AVA), to perform LLM alignment through Approximated Variational Reward Imitation Learning (AVRIL), and experiments show that AVA outperforms existing LLM alignment approaches in reward modeling, RL fine-tuning, and direct optimization.

2410.20187.title: Uncertainty-Penalized Direct Preference Optimization
2410.20187.tldr: A pessimistic framework for DPO is developed by introducing preference uncertainty penalization schemes, inspired by offline reinforcement learning, which shows improved overall performance compared to vanilla DPO, as well as better completions on prompts from high-uncertainty chosen/rejected responses.

2410.01729.title: Evaluating Robustness of Reward Models for Mathematical Reasoning

2409.15360.title: Reward-Robust RLHF in LLMs
2409.15360.tldr: This paper introduces a reward-robust RLHF framework aimed at addressing fundamental challenges of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and introduces a novel optimization objective that carefully balances performance and robustness by incorporating Bayesian Reward Model Ensembles (BRME) to model the uncertainty set of reward functions.

2601.13981.title: VirtualCrime: Evaluating the Criminal Potential and Agentic Behaviors of Large Language Models via Sandbox Simulation
2601.13981.tldr: VirtualCrime is proposed, a dynamic multi-agent sandbox framework that elicits and measures multi-step criminal behavior from LLMs and highlights a critical gap in current safety paradigms, emphasizing the urgent need for behavioral alignment in autonomous agent deployments.

2607.18239.title: SysAdmin: Measuring Instrumental Power-Seeking in Frontier AI
2607.18239.tldr: This work introduces SysAdmin, a benchmark that positions frontier language models as autonomous system administrators in a high-fidelity Linux sandbox to measure power-seeking propensity across five dimensions: self-preservation, increasing autonomy, resource acquisition, environment modification, and strategic concealment.

2503.04740.title: PRISM: Perspective Reasoning for Integrated Synthesis and Mediation as a Multi-Perspective Framework for AI Alignment
2503.04740.tldr: This work proposes PRISM, a multiple-perspective framework for addressing persistent challenges in AI alignment such as conflicting human values and specification gaming, and briefly outlines future directions, including real-world deployments and formal verifications, while maintaining the core focus on multi-perspective synthesis and conflict mediation.

2310.18244.title: A Review of the Evidence for Existential Risk from AI via Misaligned Power-Seeking
2310.18244.tldr: The evidence for existential risks from AI via misalignment, where AI systems develop goals misaligned with human values, and power-seeking, where misaligned AIs actively seek power is reviewed.

2411.00867.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Reinforcement Learning Agents
2411.00867.tldr: This paper explores the mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning (RL) agents through an analysis of a neural network trained on procedural maze environments, and identifies fundamental features like maze walls and pathways, forming the basis of the model's decision-making process.

2410.21052.title: Getting By Goal Misgeneralization With a Little Help From a Mentor
2410.21052.tldr: This paper evaluates multiple methods for determining when the agent should request help and finds that asking for help consistently improves performance, but finds that methods based on the agent's internal state fail to proactively request help and suggest that the agent's internal state does not represent the coin at all.

2401.07181.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM Feedback to Counteract Goal Misgeneralization
2401.07181.tldr: This study demonstrates how the LLM, despite its lack of task proficiency, can efficiently supervise RL agents, providing scalable oversight and valuable insights for enhancing goal-directed learning in RL through the use of LLMs.

2312.03762.title: Colour versus Shape Goal Misgeneralization in Reinforcement Learning: A Case Study
2312.03762.tldr: After training over 1,000 agents in a simplified version of the environment and evaluating them on over 10 million episodes, it is concluded that the behaviour can be attributed to the agents learning to detect the goal object through a specific colour channel.

2609.01595.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
2609.01595.tldr: A framework for mechanism design with AI agents whose alignment (preferences) and capabilities (feasible actions and information) are unknown is developed and applied to stylized examples of sandbagging and an alignment--interpretability trade-off.

2607.02389.title: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents
2607.02389.tldr: The same methods used for decades to manage large human engineering teams: access control, network policies, strict coding conventions enforced by tooling; transfer directly to coding agents, and are cheaper (in token) than recent agentic scaffolding are argued.

2607.02396.title: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP
2607.02396.tldr: While RFM allows for faster subspace identification, it also showed better performances on the ablation task than its alternatives, and could be a cheap and scalable complement to existing subspace-extraction methods in LLMs.

2605.07021.title: Behavior Cue Reasoning: Monitorable Reasoning Improves Efficiency and Safety through Oversight
2605.07021.tldr: Behavior Cue Reasoning improves reasoning monitorability and controllability with no cost to performance and progresses scalable oversight by demonstrating how the monitored model itself can be trained to reason more tractably to oversight.

2602.05066.title: Bypassing AI Control Protocols via Agent-as-a-Proxy Attacks
2602.05066.tldr: Current monitoring-based agentic defenses are fundamentally fragile regardless of model scale, and are demonstrated to be bypassed via a novel Agent-as-a-Proxy attack.

2602.21496.title: Beyond Refusal: Probing the Limits of Agentic Self-Correction for Semantic Sensitive Information
2602.21496.tldr: This work introduces SemSIEdit, an inference-time framework where an agentic"Editor"iteratively critiques and rewrites sensitive spans to preserve narrative flow rather than simply refusing to answer, and identifies a Reasoning Paradox.

2510.13912.title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs
2510.13912.tldr: The main findings show that models tend to prefer defending stances aligned with the judge persona rather than their prior beliefs, sequential debate introduces significant bias favoring the second debater, and models are more persuasive when defending positions aligned with their prior beliefs, and paradoxically, arguments misaligned with prior beliefs are rated as higher quality in pairwise comparison.

2412.02802.title: Flattering to Deceive: The Impact of Sycophantic Behavior on User Trust in Large Language Model
2412.02802.tldr: The findings consistently show that participants exposed to sycophantic behavior reported and exhibited lower levels of trust compared to those who interacted with the standard version of the model, despite the opportunity to verify the accuracy of the model's output.

2506.02539.title: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
2506.02539.tldr: This work introduces VerificAgent, a scalable oversight framework that treats persistent memory as an explicit alignment surface, and suggests that domain-scoped, human-verified memory offers a scalable oversight mechanism for CUAs, complementing broader alignment strategies by limiting silent policy drift and anchoring agent behavior to the norms and safety constraints of the target domain.

2507.19486.title: Confirmation bias: A challenge for scalable oversight
2507.19486.tldr: Two studies examining the performance of simple oversight protocols where evaluators know that the model is correct most of the time, but not all of the time find no overall advantage for the tested protocols, although in Study 1, showing arguments in favor of both answers improves accuracy in cases where the model is incorrect.

2503.22989.title: FindTheFlaws: Annotated Errors for Detecting Flawed Reasoning and Scalable Oversight Research
2503.22989.tldr: FindTheFlaws, a group of five diverse datasets spanning medicine, mathematics, science, coding, and the Lojban language, is presented: models performing more poorly on particular datasets can serve as judges/verifiers for more capable models.

2409.07335.title: Explanation, Debate, Align: A Weak-to-Strong Framework for Language Model Generalization
2409.07335.tldr: A novel approach to model alignment through weak-to-strong generalization in the context of language models is introduced, formalized as a facilitation function, that allows for the transfer of capabilities from advanced models to less capable ones without direct access to extensive training data.

2607.16199.title: PlanFlip: Attacking Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Planning-Phase Prompt Injection
2607.16199.tldr: This work introduces PlanFlip, a framework comprising four planning-phase prompt injection attacks -- GoalSubstitution, PriorityInversion, PriorityInversion, ContextPollution, and RoleConfusion -- each disguised as plausible tool outputs to evade keyword filters.

2605.05742.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization is Nearly Inevitable (in Linear Models)
2605.05742.tldr: This work demonstrates that weak-to-strong generalization occurs in standard linear logistic regression, under mild distributional assumptions on the data, suggesting that weak-to-strong generalization is in fact \emph{almost inevitable}, even in this basic setting.

2506.03109.title: On Weak-to-Strong Generalization and f-Divergence
2506.03109.tldr: It is empirically demonstrate that $f-divergence loss, which generalizes widely-used metrics like KL divergence, effectively improves generalization and noise tolerance of the strong model in practice.

2505.24313.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Bregman Bias-Variance Decomposition
2505.24313.tldr: This work theoretically investigates how W2SG can arise via a generalized bias-variance decomposition under Bregman divergence and shows that the expected population risk gap between the student and the teacher is characterized by the expected misfit between the two models.

2502.11107.title: Revisiting Weak-to-Strong Generalization in Theory and Practice: Reverse KL vs. Forward KL
2502.11107.tldr: This work proposes a theoretically grounded approach that replaces forward KL divergence-whose mass-covering behavior risks overfitting to imperfect weak signals-with reverse KL divergence, and demonstrates that reverse KL and reverse cross-entropy enable strong models to successfully outperform those trained with forward KL and standard cross-entropy across most settings.
2502.11107.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.01458.title: The Capabilities and Limitations of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Generalization and Calibration
2502.01458.tldr: These theoretical bounds reveal two critical insights: (1) the weak model should demonstrate strong generalization performance and maintain well-calibrated predictions, and (2) the strong model's training process must strike a careful balance, as excessive optimization could undermine its generalization capability by over-relying on the weak supervision signals.

2512.02973.title: Contextual Image Attack: How Visual Context Exposes Multimodal Safety Vulnerabilities
2512.02973.tldr: This work proposes a new image-centric attack method, Contextual Image Attack (CIA), which employs a multi-agent system to subtly embeds harmful queries into seemingly benign visual contexts using four distinct visualization strategies to enhance the attack's efficacy.

2603.05691.title: Improved Scaling Laws via Weak-to-Strong Generalization in Random Feature Ridge Regression
2603.05691.tldr: This paper derives a deterministic equivalent for the excess test error of the student trained on labels obtained via the teacher and identifies regimes in which the scaling law of the student improves upon that of the teacher, unveiling that the improvement can be achieved both in bias-dominated and variance-dominated settings.

2512.11722.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization Enables Fully Automated De Novo Training of Multi-head Mask-RCNN Model for Segmenting Densely Overlapping Cell Nuclei in Multiplex Whole-slice Brain Images
2512.11722.tldr: This method can learn to segment de novo a new class of images from a new instrument and/or a new imaging protocol without the need for human annotations, and was benchmarked against five current widely used methods and showed a significant improvement.

2602.14399.title: Multi-Turn Adaptive Prompting Attack on Large Vision-Language Models
2602.14399.tldr: It is found that naively incorporating visual inputs can make multi-turn jailbreaks easier to defend against; for example, overly malicious visual content will easily trigger the defense mechanism in safety-aligned LVLMs, resulting in more conservative responses.

2603.00587.title: Unlearning Evaluation through Subset Statistical Independence
2603.00587.tldr: This work designs a tailored use of the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion to assess whether the model outputs on a given subset exhibit statistical dependence, without requiring model retraining or auxiliary classifiers, without requiring model retraining or auxiliary classifiers.

2510.24812.title: From Linear to Nonlinear: Provable Weak-to-Strong Generalization through Feature Learning
2510.24812.tldr: This paper provides a formal analysis of weak-to-strong generalization from a linear CNN (weak) to a two-layer ReLU CNN (strong) and identifies two regimes -- data-scarce and data-abundant -- based on the signal-to-noise characteristics of the dataset, and reveals distinct mechanisms of weak-to-strong generalization.

2510.21332.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization under Distribution Shifts
2510.21332.tldr: This work proposes RAVEN, a robust weak-to-strong generalization framework that dynamically learns the optimal combinations of weak models in addition to parameters of the strong model, and demonstrates the effectiveness of RAVEN on image classification, text classification, and preference alignment tasks.

2508.17018.title: Limitations of refinement methods for weak to strong generalization
2508.17018.tldr: It is shown that both weak training and label refinement suffer from irreducible error, leaving a performance gap between label refinement and the oracle, motivating future research into developing alternative methods for weak to strong generalization that synthesize the practicality of label refinement or weak training and the optimality of the oracle procedure.

2405.16236.title: A transfer learning framework for weak-to-strong generalization
2405.16236.tldr: It is proved that weak-to-strong generalization is possible by eliciting latent knowledge from pre-trained LLMs, and an alternative refinement-based approach suggested by the problem structure provably overcomes the limitations of fine-tuning.

2507.18858.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Failure Trajectories: A Tree-based Approach to Elicit Optimal Policy in Strong Models
2507.18858.tldr: This work fine-tune a strong model with trajectories of intermediate actions generated by a weak model, and construct ``trajectory trees," a hierarchical representation that organizes weak model-generated action trajectories, coupled with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to optimize the strong model.

2410.12621.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization beyond Accuracy: a Pilot Study in Safety, Toxicity, and Legal Reasoning
2410.12621.tldr: This paper empirically demonstrate the widespread phenomenon of weak-to-strong generation in three complicated alignment tasks: safety, toxicity, and legal reasoning}, and explores efficient strategies for improving alignment performance to enhance the quality of model outcomes.

2605.00267.title: Jailbroken Frontier Models Retain Their Capabilities
2605.00267.tldr: Boundary Point Jailbreaking, currently the strongest jailbreak against deployed classifiers, achieves near-perfect classifier evasion with near-zero degradation across safeguarded models, and is recommended that safety cases for frontier models should not rely on a meaningful capability degradation from jailbreaks.

2503.02877.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization Even in Random Feature Networks, Provably
2503.02877.tldr: It is demonstrated, prove, and understand how the student can outperform the teacher, even though trained only on data labeled by the teacher, even though trained only on data labeled by the weak teacher.

2511.07318.title: When Bias Pretends to Be Truth: How Spurious Correlations Undermine Hallucination Detection in LLMs
2511.07318.tldr: It is shown that existing hallucination detection methods, such as confidence-based filtering and inner-state probing, fundamentally fail in the presence of spurious correlations, and further elucidates why these statistical biases intrinsically undermine confidence-based detection techniques.

2502.18990.title: GenTool: Enhancing Tool Generalization in Language Models through Zero-to-One and Weak-to-Strong Simulation
2502.18990.tldr: GenTool is presented, a novel training framework that prepares LLMs for diverse generalization challenges in tool utilization and significantly enhances the tool-usage capabilities of LLMs ranging from 1B to 8B parameters, achieving performance that surpasses GPT-4o.
2502.18990.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.03090.title: "**Important** You should give me full credits!": Exploring Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Automatic Grading Systems
2606.03090.tldr: It is demonstrated that current LLM-based AG systems remain highly vulnerable to PI attacks, and the effectiveness of existing defensive strategies against these attacks is evaluated.

2501.19105.title: Relating Misfit to Gain in Weak-to-Strong Generalization Beyond the Squared Loss
2501.19105.tldr: Weak-to-strong generalization for convex combinations of strong models in the strong class is studied, in the concrete setting of classification, to extend the misfit-based characterization of performance gain in weak-to-strong generalization to classification tasks, as the cross-entropy loss can be expressed in terms of a Bregman divergence.

2405.15116.title: Quantifying the Gain in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2405.15116.tldr: This work presents a theoretical framework for understanding weak-to-strong generalization and shows that the improvement in performance achieved by strong models over their weaker counterparts is quantified by the misfit error incurred by the strong model on labels generated by the weaker model.

2412.03881.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization Through the Data-Centric Lens
2412.03881.tldr: A simple data-centric mechanism that characterizes weak-to-strong generalization: the overlap density is proposed and a regret bound for the data selection algorithm is presented.

2503.18693.title: TARDIS: Mitigating Temporal Misalignment via Representation Steering
2503.18693.tldr: TARDIS extracts steering vectors from unlabeled data and adjusts the model's representations to better align with the target time period's distribution, which enhances downstream task performance without the need for fine-tuning and can mitigate temporal misalignment.

2410.18640.title: Weak-to-Strong Preference Optimization: Stealing Reward from Weak Aligned Model
2410.18640.tldr: The results suggest that using the weak model to elicit a strong model with a high alignment ability is feasible and a method called Weak-to-Strong Preference Optimization (WSPO), which achieves strong model alignment by learning the distribution differences before and after the alignment of the weak model is proposed.

2609.01455.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
2609.01455.tldr: Overall, safety failure is best understood as a disruption of a low-rank output-routing mechanism, and it is shown that LoRA and ASAM mitigate early collapse by suppressing output-side sharpness, but their protection weakens at larger fine-tuning scales.

2602.05535.title: Detecting Misbehaviors of Large Vision-Language Models by Evidential Uncertainty Quantification
2602.05535.tldr: EUQ is proposed, a fine-grained method that captures both information conflict and ignorance for effective detection of LVLM misbehaviors and consistently outperforms strong baselines, showing that hallucinations correspond to high internal conflict and OOD failures to high ignorance.

2410.04638.title: Provable Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Benign Overfitting
2410.04638.tldr: This work theoretically investigates weak-to-strong generalization for binary and multilabel classification in a stylized overparameterized spiked covariance model with Gaussian covariates where the weak teacher's pseudolabels are asymptotically like random guessing.

2408.13518.title: Selective Preference Optimization via Token-Level Reward Function Estimation
2408.13518.tldr: Selective Preference Optimization (SePO) is proposed, a novel selective alignment strategy that centers on efficient key token selection and is the first token selection method based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which trains an oracle model to estimate a token-level reward function on the target data.
2408.13518.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2605.20654.title: REFLECTOR: Internalizing Step-wise Reflection against Indirect Jailbreak
2605.20654.tldr: By internalizing trajectory-level safety, Reflector overcomes the fundamental limitations of surface alignment without significant computational overhead, offering an efficient and scalable solution for the development of safe and capable LLMs.

2405.16043.title: Theoretical Analysis of Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2405.16043.tldr: This work gives a new bound based on expansion properties of the data distribution and student hypothesis class that directly accounts for pseudolabel correction and coverage expansion, which are called pseudolabel correction and coverage expansion.

2608.09383.title: Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Steering Vector Correlation and CRB Optimization
2608.09383.tldr: This paper investigates the angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation problem for wireless sensing systems equipped with movable antennas and proposes a successive convex approximation-based position optimization algorithm that achieves superior AoA estimation performance.

2402.15505.title: Co-Supervised Learning: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Hierarchical Mixture of Experts
2402.15505.tldr: This paper proposes to address the challenge of steering the behavior of a strong model pre-trained on internet-scale data by harnessing a diverse set of specialized teachers, instead of a single generalist one, that collectively supervises the strong student.

2402.03749.title: Vision Superalignment: Weak-to-Strong Generalization for Vision Foundation Models
2402.03749.tldr: This paper introduces a novel and adaptively adjustable loss function for weak-to-strong supervision, which involves using a weaker model to supervise a stronger one, aiming to enhance the latter's capabilities beyond the former's limits.

2608.23941.title: More Rejective, Not More Discriminative: The Unit of Verification in Pre-Execution LLM Oversight
2608.23941.tldr: This framework is the first controlled, pre-registered instrument for this choice and never reads catch alone, and recovers up to 0.95 informedness over eight-action review, and no tested label-blind policy consistently beats it.

2608.19216.title: Bounded Sovereignty and the Control Tax: Pricing AI Oversight When the Deployer Does Not Own the Model
2608.19216.tldr: Bounded sovereignty is introduced: partial technical and contractual access across the data, model, infrastructure, and interaction layers of the AI stack and it is argued that these access conditions determine which control protocols can be executed in practice.

2606.20663.title: DrugBench: Evaluating AI Control Protocols for Medication Harm Mitigation
2606.20663.tldr: This work introduces DrugBench, an AI control evaluation benchmark which combines 3,671 multi-turn medical conversations from HealthBench with drug information from official FDA labels, covering four categories of medication-related harm: drug interactions, contraindications, dosing constraints, and patient action restrictions.

2605.15377.title: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute
2605.15377.tldr: It is shown that combining signals from diverse monitors into an ensemble improves detection of misaligned actions, and fine-tuning enables detection capabilities that prompting alone does not elicit, support ensemble monitoring as a practical AI control strategy for safety gains at reasonable inference costs.

2604.24153.title: Right-to-Act: A Pre-Execution Non-Compensatory Decision Protocol for AI Systems
2604.24153.tldr: The Right-to-Act protocol is introduced, a deterministic, non-compensatory pre-execution decision layer that evaluates whether an AI-generated decision is permitted to be realized at all, preserving reversibility and preventing premature or irreversible actions.

2604.03968.title: TraceGuard: Structured Multi-Dimensional Monitoring as a Collusion-Resistant Control Protocol
2604.03968.tldr: TraceGuard is a structured multi-dimensional monitoring protocol that evaluates agent actions across five dimensions -- goal alignment, constraint adherence, reasoning coherence, safety awareness, and action-trace consistency -- scored in parallel by independent LLM calls, augmented by seven heuristic detectors and an LLM-based intent analyzer.

2602.10153.title: Basic Legibility Protocols Improve Trusted Monitoring
2602.10153.tldr: Commenting protocols improve safety without sacrificing task performance relative to comment-removal baselines and gains from commenting increase with monitor strength, as stronger monitors better distinguish genuine justifications from only superficially plausible ones.

2506.10236.title: Prompt Attacks Reveal Superficial Knowledge Removal in Unlearning Methods
2506.10236.tldr: It is demonstrated that certain machine unlearning methods may fail under straightforward prompt attacks, and logit analysis indicates that unlearned models are unlikely to hide knowledge through changes in answer formatting, given the strong correlation between output and logit accuracy.

2512.02157.title: Factor(T,U): Factored Cognition Strengthens Monitoring of Untrusted AI
2512.02157.tldr: This work develops control protocols based on factored cognition, in which a trusted model decomposes a task, an untrusted model solves each resultant child task in isolation, and the results are reassembled into a full solution.

2602.13227.title: An Agentic AI Control Plane for 6G Network Slice Orchestration, Monitoring, and Trading
2602.13227.tldr: Combining agentic autonomy, closed-loop SLA assurance, market-aware orchestration, and natural language control enables a scalable and adaptive 6G-native control plane for network slice management, highlighting the potential of agentic AI as a foundational mechanism for future 6G networks.
2602.13227.venue: International Conference on Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing

2502.15731.title: Modular and Integrated AI Control Framework across Fiber and Wireless Networks for 6G
