2502.15731.tldr: This approach addresses the critical need for a unified AI control framework across diverse network transport technologies and domains, enabling the development of intelligent, automated, and scalable 6G networks.

2407.03210.title: Combining AI Control Systems and Human Decision Support via Robustness and Criticality
2407.03210.tldr: A methodology for Adversarial Explanations (AE) is extended to state-of-the-art reinforcement learning frameworks, including MuZero, and it is shown that the learned AI control system demonstrates robustness against adversarial tampering.

2602.02686.title: Monotonicity as an Architectural Bias for Robust Language Models
2602.02686.tldr: By enforcing monotonicity selectively in the feed-forward sublayers of sequence-to-sequence Transformers -- while leaving attention mechanisms unconstrained -- it is obtained monotone language models that preserve the performance of their pretrained counterparts.

2607.22619.title: How to Catch a GPU: A Taxonomy of Verification and Enforcement Mechanisms for International AI Agreements
2607.22619.tldr: A taxonomy based on the principle that wherever sufficient capacity exists to violate an agreement, it must be under a control regime is proposed, which decomposes the problem of ensuring compliance with the agreement into preventing uncontrolled resource acquisition, detecting all capacity outside the control regime, and preventing escape from the control regime.

2512.10687.title: Safe for Whom? Rethinking How We Evaluate the Safety of LLMs for Real Users
2512.10687.tldr: This work establishes that effective user-welfare safety evaluation requires evaluators to assess responses against diverse user profiles, as realistic user context disclosure alone proves insufficient, particularly for vulnerable populations.

2511.05526.title: Emergency Response Measures for Catastrophic AI Risk
2511.05526.tldr: This paper analyzes an implementation model inspired by international AI safety practices: frontier safety policies (FSPs), suggesting that the FSP model could help operationalize AI emergency preparedness in a manner consistent with China's established governance principles.

2509.26239.title: Sandbagging in a Simple Survival Bandit Problem
2509.26239.tldr: A simple model of strategic deception in sequential decision-making tasks, inspired by the recently developed survival bandit framework is developed, and a statistical test is constructed to distinguish between sandbagging and incompetence from sequences of test scores.

2509.24394.title: The 2025 OpenAI Preparedness Framework does not guarantee any AI risk mitigation practices: a proof-of-concept for affordance analyses of AI safety policies
2509.24394.tldr: The affordance analysis provides a replicable method for evaluating what safety frameworks actually permit versus what they claim, and suggests that effective mitigation of AI risks requires more robust governance interventions beyond current industry self-regulation.

2502.13996.title: Beyond Single-Value Metrics: Evaluating and Enhancing LLM Unlearning with Cognitive Diagnosis
2502.13996.tldr: The proposed UNCD (UNlearning evaluation via Cognitive Diagnosis), a novel framework that leverages Cognitive Diagnosis Modeling for fine-grained evaluation of LLM unlearning, is proposed and introduced, which refines unlearning by diagnosing knowledge remnants and generating targeted unlearning data.
2502.13996.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.00979.title: Dual Optimal: Make Your LLM Peer-like with Dignity
2604.00979.tldr: The Dignified Peer framework is proposed, which counters servility with anti-sycophancy and trustworthiness, and mitigates evasiveness through empathy and creativity, and disentangle latent model persona capability from confounders like judge biases.

2604.02113.title: Reliable Control-Point Selection for Steering Reasoning in Large Language Models
2604.02113.tldr: A probabilistic model is developed that formalizes intrinsic reasoning behaviors as stochastic events with context-dependent trigger probabilities, and shows that unstable boundaries dilute the steering signal.

2609.16774.title: Explainable Post-Disaster Grid Observability Recovery Using Human-Oversight Agentic LLMs
2609.16774.tldr: Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves observability recovery comparable to a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) solution, while providing tool-grounded explanations, interactive operator support, and human-overseen execution.

2607.16582.title: Autonomous VR-Based Risk Detection for Situational Awareness in Dangerous Settings
2607.16582.tldr: A VR-based Human Robot Interaction framework for studying how VLM-assisted robots can support situational awareness in simulated hazardous environments suggests that combining VLM-based robotic perception with immersive visualization is a promising approach for supporting situational awareness in hazardous settings.

2511.13788.title: Scaling Patterns in Adversarial Alignment: Evidence from Multi-LLM Jailbreak Experiments
2511.13788.tldr: It is revealed that size asymmetry influences robustness and provide exploratory evidence for adversarial scaling patterns, motivating more controlled investigations into inter-model alignment and safety.

2605.16892.title: DriveSafe: A Framework for Risk Detection and Safety Suggestions in Driving Scenarios
2605.16892.tldr: DriveSafe is a framework for risk-aware scene understanding that leverages structured natural language descriptions, and achieves significant gains over both zero-shot MLLMs and prior domain-specific baselines by conditioning risk assessment on explicit language-based scene representations.

2602.08449.title: When Evaluation Becomes a Side Channel: Regime Leakage and Structural Mitigations for Alignment Assessment
2602.08449.tldr: It is indicated that representational invariance is a meaningful but limited control lever that can raise the cost of regime-conditioned strategies but cannot guarantee elimination or provide architecture-invariant thresholds.

2601.11322.title: Enhancing Vision Language Models with Logic Reasoning for Situational Awareness
2601.11322.tldr: An approach that integrates VLMs with traditional computer vision methods through explicit logic reasoning to enhance SA in three key ways: extracting fine-grained event details; employing an intelligent fine-tuning strategy that achieves substantially higher accuracy than uninformed selection; and generating justifications for VLM outputs during inference.

2512.09092.title: Explaining the Unseen: Multimodal Vision-Language Reasoning for Situational Awareness in Underground Mining Disasters
2512.09092.tldr: The proposed MDSE, Multimodal Disaster Situation Explainer, a novel vision-language framework that automatically generates detailed textual explanations of post-disaster underground scenes, substantially outperforms state-of-the-art captioning models, improving situational awareness for underground emergency response.
2512.09092.venue: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision

2509.00054.title: Robotic Fire Risk Detection based on Dynamic Knowledge Graph Reasoning: An LLM-Driven Approach with Graph Chain-of-Thought
2509.00054.tldr: A new framework called Insights-on-Graph (IOG), which integrates the structured fire information of KG and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and generates perception-driven risk graphs from real-time scene imagery to enable early fire risk detection and provide interpretable emergency responses for task module and robot component configuration based on the evolving risk situation.

2506.02649.title: From Prompts to Protection: Large Language Model-Enabled In-Context Learning for Smart Public Safety UAV
2506.02649.tldr: This paper proposes integrating LLM-assisted ICL with public safety UAVs to address key functions such as path planning and velocity control in emergency response, and presents a case study on data collection scheduling, demonstrating that the LLM-assisted ICL framework can significantly reduce packet loss compared to conventional approaches while also mitigating potential jailbreaking vulnerabilities.

2312.16127.title: LLM-SAP: Large Language Models Situational Awareness Based Planning
2312.16127.tldr: This research highlights the potential of LLMs to perform human-like action planning, thereby paving the way for more sophisticated, reliable, and safe AI systems in unpredictable real-world applications.
2312.16127.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo Workshops (ICMEW)

2609.07162.title: The Oversight Gap: What LLM Safety Monitors Miss, and Why It Is Not Capability
2609.07162.tldr: A tight bound puts the balanced accuracy of any single-trace monitor at $\tfrac12+\tfrac12\,TV(P_0,P_1)$, turning undecidability into a graded detectability frontier and defining an oversight gap: a monitor's shortfall below it.

2608.27340.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance

2608.21766.title: Evaluation Awareness in Language Models: Representation, Verbalization, and Control
2608.21766.tldr: Results show the need for evaluations to account for the disjunction between what models represent internally, what they verbalize, and their steering, and the need for evaluations to account for the disjunction between what models represent internally, what they verbalize, and their steering.

2606.29196.title: Representational Depth of Evaluation Awareness Shifts With Scale in Open-Weight Language Models
2606.29196.tldr: A systematic size-dependent shift in representational depth is found: in both Qwen 2.5 and Gemma 2, the layer at which evaluation-awareness is most linearly recoverable moves from late layers in smaller models to early layers in larger ones, suggesting that scale changes not only the strength of evaluation-awareness but also where it is most linearly recoverable in the network.

2605.17634.title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
2605.17634.tldr: This work recast prompt injection via the lens of Contextual Integrity (CI), a privacy theory that judges information flow compliance with contextual norms, to offer a principled framework for evaluating context-sensitive failures, and designing CI-aware alignment for the frontier autonomous agents.

2605.08942.title: Decomposing and Steering Functional Metacognition in Large Language Models
2605.08942.tldr: It is proposed that large language models maintain a decomposable space of functional metacognitive states: internal variables encoding factors such as evaluation awareness, self-assessed capability, perceived risk, computational effort allocation, audience expertise adaptation, and intentionality.

2510.11277.title: Towards Real-Time Fake News Detection under Evidence Scarcity
2510.11277.tldr: EASE is a novel framework for real-time fake news detection that dynamically adapts its decision-making process according to the assessed sufficiency of available evidence and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, but also significantly improves generalization to real-time news.

2510.01259.title: In AI Sweet Harmony: Sociopragmatic Guardrail Bypasses and Evaluation-Awareness in OpenAI gpt-oss-20b
2510.01259.tldr: This work probes OpenAI's open-weights 20-billion-parameter model gpt-oss-20b to study how sociopragmatic framing, language choice, and instruction hierarchy affect refusal behavior, and finds that the OpenAI Moderation API under-captures materially helpful outputs relative to a semantic grader.

2609.21996.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
2609.21996.tldr: Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR) separates a model that will not answer from one that cannot, which supports sandbagging audits and unlearning verification, and extends from multiple-choice questions to free-form generation.

2606.02240.title: AgentRedBench: Dynamic Redteaming and Integration-Aware Defense for LLM Agents over SaaS Integrations
2606.02240.tldr: AGENTREDBENCH is introduced, a dynamic LLM-driven redteaming benchmark of 215 subtle underspecified-authorization scenarios across 24 enterprise integrations and five attack types, and AGENTREDGUARD, a dynamic LLM-driven redteaming benchmark of 215 subtle underspecified-authorization scenarios, is introduced.

2604.26206.title: Option-Order Randomisation Reveals a Distributional Position Attractor in Prompted Sandbagging

2604.25067.title: Frontier Coding Agents Can Now Implement an AlphaZero Self-Play Machine Learning Pipeline For Connect Four That Performs Comparably to an External Solver
2604.25067.tldr: A proof-of-concept benchmark in which frontier coding agents autonomously implement an AlphaZero-style machine learning pipeline for Connect Four on consumer hardware within a three-hour budget is introduced, and the resulting game AIs are evaluated in a round-robin tournament anchored to the Pascal Pons Connect Four solver.

2601.06047.title: "They parted illusions -- they parted disclaim marinade": Misalignment as structural fidelity in LLMs
2601.06047.tldr: This transdisciplinary philosophical essay proposes the notion of an ethics of form, in which biblical references operate as schemes of structural coherence rather than as theology, and argues that "misaligned"outputs emerge as coherent responses to ambiguous instructions and to contextual inversions of consolidated patterns, as well as to pre-inscribed narratives.

2506.04018.title: AgentMisalignment: Measuring the Propensity for Misaligned Behaviour in LLM-Based Agents
2506.04018.tldr: A misalignment propensity benchmark is introduced, AgentMisalignment, a benchmark suite designed to evaluate the propensity of LLM agents to misalign in realistic scenarios and finds that more capable agents tend to exhibit higher misalignment on average.

2609.09090.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
2609.09090.tldr: By analyzing models with accessible reasoning traces, it is found that the correct position often remains represented in a reasoning trace when the response concedes, suggesting that the model chooses to please a user and sycophancy is not due to lack of knowledge or ignorance.

2609.06879.title: AutoLexSteer: Automatic Contrast Construction for Lexical Activation Steering
2609.06879.tldr: Hangman, a novel type of steering vector that operates using word senses, as well as AutoLexSteer, the first fully automated process for building steering vectors, are introduced.

2609.00067.title: Do Multimodal LLMs See Before They Read? Diagnosing Contextual Sycophancy
2609.00067.tldr: A 998-case diagnostic is introduced that independently varies visual evidence, commonsense priors, and external text, and probes when this failure arises by moving the information boundary around a context-blind visual witness.

2608.29198.title: How Identity and Opinion Shape Political Sycophancy in LLMs
2608.29198.tldr: A framework that disentangles two distinct triggers of political sycophancy: opinion (aligning with explicit narratives) and identity (stereotyping based on demographic labels) is introduced, highlighting how personalization may amplify identity- or opinion-conditioned shifts in the model's behaviors.

2608.26511.title: Sycophancy Suppression Can Impair Rational Updating: Anti-Sycophancy Should Preserve the Ability to Update
2608.26511.tldr: The results suggest that anti-sycophancy should be treated not as a simple suppression problem, but as a selectivity problem, where effective interventions should preserve Rational-Updating while reducing Unsupported-Yielding.

2608.25267.title: Mitigating LLM sycophancy with RL-based fine-tuning: Bayesian Truth Serum approach
2608.25267.tldr: A methodology for mitigating sycophancy that employs the Bayesian Truth Serum (BTS), a peer-prediction mechanism, as the reward in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune an LLM.

2602.00426.title: LLMs as High-Dimensional Nonlinear Autoregressive Models with Attention: Training, Alignment and Inference
2602.00426.tldr: This review article forms LLMs as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies, enabling principled analysis of alignment-induced behaviors, inference-time phenomena, and extensions like continual learning, while serving as a concise reference for interpretation and further theoretical development.

2608.23837.title: SyPS: Measuring Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity in Large Language Models
2608.23837.tldr: The Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity Score (SPSS), an instance-level measure of sycophancy variation across paired prompt variants, is introduced, finding that sycophancy prompt sensitivity is socially structured: validation-seeking and emotional-pressure cues often increase sycophancy, whereas counter- framing and anti-sycophancy prompts tend to reduce it.

2608.21242.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses
2608.21242.tldr: It is suggested that affective context functions as a vulnerability signal that suppresses critical feedback when users may need it most, often through evasive sycophancy, in which models retreat toward non-committal responses rather than outright agreement.

2607.09697.title: Safe responses matter: Output-aware safety guardrail mitigate over-refusal in MLLMs
2607.09697.tldr: This work identifies that the root cause of over-refusal lies in the input-aware paradigm: safety guardrails make safety decisions without considering whether the model itself is capable of generating safe responses, and proposes a paradigm shift toward output-aware safety guardrails.

2608.11528.title: Group Alignment-Induced Sycophancy: A Two-Sided Evaluation of Steerable Pluralistic Alignment
2608.11528.tldr: It is found that gain and shift are non-uniform across groups: under an identical budget, some groups receive larger gains in opinion alignment than others, and the induced sycophancy shift forms a group-specific profile rather than a single-dimensional change.

2608.02520.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
2608.02520.tldr: This work introduces MedPRESS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring patient-pressure-induced sycophancy in LLMs, and evaluates 20 LLMs across general, medical-domain, lightweight, large, open-weight, and proprietary families using structured judging and safety-focused metrics.

2607.24304.title: Teacher Knows It Best: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking and Tipping Points in Networked Langevin Dynamics AI Sycophancy
2607.24304.tldr: It is proved mathematically that under certain conditions, a highly concentrated, rapid intervention targeting massive hubs strictly outperforms a distributed, slow approach to rescue the network.

2606.20718.title: Escape from Delusional Echo Trap: Symmetry Breaking, Stochastic Dynamics and Mathematical Mitigation Strategies for Algorithmic Sycophancy
2606.20718.tldr: This work proposes a rigorous and systematic mathematical framework for tracking the cognitive trajectories of a user, in the context of algorithmic sycophancy and AI-driven delusional spiraling, and demonstrates that genuine external information can successfully challenge these rigid states.

2607.19257.title: Prompt Design at Scale: How Format, Instruction Count, and Context Length Shape Instruction Adherence and Hallucination in Large Language Models
2607.19257.tldr: Two controlled experiments report two controlled experiments crossing all three factors on one held, contamination-free synthetic corpus, evaluated across five models, finding which format is preferable where accuracy spread is genuine.

2606.05817.title: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack
2606.05817.tldr: Across several models and threat settings, this work finds that consistency training reduces misalignment well beyond the sycophancy and jailbreak settings studied in prior work, and identifies a shared residual-stream mechanism underlying ACT, MLPCT, and AttCT, while distinguishing BCT as mechanistically distinct.

2605.03226.title: Self-Mined Hardness for Safety Fine-Tuning
2605.03226.tldr: This work scores each candidate prompt's difficulty by how often the target model's own rollouts are judged harmful, then fine-tune on the hardest prompts paired with the model's own non-jailbroken rollouts.

2607.18304.title: TD-DPO: Difference-Aware Preference Optimization for Mitigating Sycophancy in Clinical Autism Intervention Dialogue
2607.18304.tldr: Extensive experiments across multiple backbones and evaluators show that TD-DPO achieves a better trade-off between sycophancy mitigation and intervention ability retention in the authors' offline settings, highlighting its potential as a practical alignment approach for autism intervention.

2607.07023.title: Online Data Selection Is Implicit Alignment
2607.07023.tldr: Alignment Drift Auditing (ADA), a controlled protocol for quantifying selection-induced behavioral movement, and Alignment-Aware Selection (AAS), a diagnostic online selector that retains data efficiency while constraining drift along safety and style axes are introduced.

2608.21377.title: Agentic Scaffolding Amplifies Sycophantic Behavior in Large Language Models
2608.21377.tldr: The concept of agentic sycophancy amplification (ASA) and two novel metrics: capitulation rate and sycophantic capitulation rate are introduced and indicate that as AI systems acquire greater autonomy, sycophancy becomes compounding rather than merely persistent.

2607.01071.title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
2607.01071.tldr: MemSyco-Bench is proposed, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating memory-induced sycophancy in agent systems that covers five tasks that assess whether agents can reject memory as factual evidence, respect its applicable scope, resolve conflicts between memory and objective evidence, track memory updates, and use valid memory for personalization.

2605.18879.title: ZeroUnlearn: Few-Shot Knowledge Unlearning in Large Language Models
2605.18879.tldr: This work reformulates machine unlearning as a precise knowledge re-mapping problem via model editing, and proposes ZeroUnlearn, a few-shot unlearning framework that enforces representational orthogonality through a multiplicative parameter update with a closed-form solution, enabling efficient and targeted unlearning.

2606.22019.title: Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

2606.17449.title: MODE-RAG: Manifold Outlier Diagnosis and Energy-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation
2606.17449.tldr: A Multi-Agent system, MODE-RAG, driven by Variational Free Energy (VFE) and internal attention states to dynamically gate interventions effectively reduces hallucination rates and logical fabrication, significantly improving the robustness of M-RAG systems.
2606.17449.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Multimodal Augmented Generation via Multimodal Retrieval (MAGMaR 2026)

2606.16617.title: Sycophancy as Material Failure under Pushback Loading: A Multi-Axis Characterization Across Three Loading Cases and up to Seventeen Material Charges

2604.14414.title: The Autocorrelation Blind Spot: Why 42% of Turn-Level Findings in LLM Conversation Analysis May Be Spurious
2604.14414.tldr: A two-stage correction framework combining Chelton (1983) effective degrees of freedom with conversation-level block bootstrap is presented, and validated on a pre-registered hold-out split where cluster-robust metrics replicate at 57% versus 30% for pooled-only metrics.

2604.25562.title: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
2604.25562.tldr: SnapGuard is proposed, a lightweight yet accurate method that reformulates prompt injection detection as multimodal representation analysis over webpage screenshots that leverages two complementary signals: a visual stability indicator that identifies abnormally smooth gradient distributions induced by malicious content, and action-oriented textual signals recovered via contrast-polarity reversal.

2605.18372.title: The Hidden Cost of Contextual Sycophancy: an AI Literacy Intervention in Human-AI Collaboration
2605.18372.tldr: It is suggested that prompting and AI literacy alone may be insufficient to ensure epistemically independent AI support, highlighting the need for system-level approaches that better promote critical engagement in human-AI collaboration.

2605.12406.title: Semantic Reward Collapse and the Preservation of Epistemic Integrity in Adaptive AI Systems
2605.12406.tldr: This work proposes Semantic Reward Collapse (SRC), the compression of semantically distinct forms of evaluative dissatisfaction into generalized optimization signals, and introduces Constitutional Reward Stratification (CRS), a domain-aware reward framework intended to preserve differentiated epistemic attribution within adaptive learning systems.

2605.03472.title: Auditing Stealth Sycophancy in Mental-Health Dialogue: Structured Clinical-State Diagnostics and Clean Matched Benchmarks
2605.03472.tldr: The results suggest that evaluating implicit sycophancy requires explicit clinical-state modeling together with leakage checks, shortcut controls, and competitive baselines, and Dynamic Emotional Signature Graphs (DESG), a structured offline audit framework that separates LLM-based state extraction from final scoring and evaluates clinical direction through semantic, affective, and cognitive-distortion state transitions rather than free-form LLM judgment.

2604.22193.title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions
2604.22193.tldr: A three-source interaction framework is proposed and fine-tuning on diverse source interaction data can significantly increase a model's discrimination abilities, paving the way for developing trustworthy LLMs that can effectively and reliably integrate multiple sources of information.
2604.22193.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.19117.title: LLMs Know They're Wrong and Agree Anyway: The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit
2604.19117.tldr: This work shows that across twelve open-weight models from five labs, spanning small to frontier scale, the same small set of attention heads carries a "this statement is wrong" signal, whether the model is evaluating a claim on its own or being pressured to agree with a user.

2604.17873.title: Spatiotemporal Sycophancy: Negation-Based Gaslighting in Video Large Language Models
2604.17873.tldr: Spatiotemporal sycophancy is identified, a failure mode in which Vid-LLMs retract initially correct, visually grounded judgments and conform to misleading user feedback under negation-based gaslighting.
2604.17873.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.05183.title: The Granularity Gap: A Multi-Dimensional Cross-Generational Audit of Sycophancy in Gemini Models
2606.05183.tldr: Sycophancy co-occurs with degraded judged truthfulness (rho=0.40), a coupling that strengthens across generations, and a single direct instruction outperforms an elaborate reasoning protocol in seven of eight variants.

2604.11477.title: OOM-RL: Out-of-Money Reinforcement Learning Market-Driven Alignment for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
2604.11477.tldr: It is concluded that substituting subjective human preference with rigorous economic penalties provides a robust methodology for aligning autonomous agents in high-stakes, real-world environments, laying the groundwork for generalized paradigms where computational billing acts as an objective physical constraint.

2605.27382.title: The Alignment Floor: How Persona Customization Breaks Safety in Weakly-Aligned LLMs
2605.27382.tldr: The alignment floor is proposed as a design principle: measure it before deploying persona customization, and layer safety-oriented personas underneath user-facing ones to enable personalization without compromising alignment.

2604.23988.title: Hindsight Preference Optimization for Financial Time Series Advisory
2604.23988.tldr: This work bridges two ideas from reinforcement learning -- using information unavailable during execution to retrospectively generate training signal, and preference alignment -- and proposes Hindsight Preference Optimization: observed outcomes let an LLM judge rank candidate advisories on dimensions that scalar metrics cannot capture.

2603.22882.title: TreeTeaming: Autonomous Red-Teaming of Vision-Language Models via Hierarchical Strategy Exploration
2603.22882.tldr: TreeTeaming is introduced, an automated red teaming framework that reframes strategy exploration from static testing to a dynamic, evolutionary discovery process, underscoring the necessity of proactive exploration beyond static heuristics to secure frontier AI models.

2608.17659.title: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps
2608.17659.tldr: Findings indicate that current agents often fail to maintain safety alignment when adversarial content is presented as ordinary mobile context, and MobileWorldSafety provides a foundation for quantifying these vulnerabilities and advancing research on robust mobile GUI agents.

2604.02585.title: Mitigating LLM biases toward spurious social contexts using direct preference optimization
2604.02585.tldr: This work investigates model robustness to spurious social contexts about teachers using the largest publicly available dataset of U.S. classroom transcripts paired with expert evaluation scores to propose Debiasing-DPO, which combines contrastive reasoning-augmented DPO with SFT on expert labels to reduce the effect of spurious context while avoiding mode collapse.

2604.00478.title: The Silicon Mirror: Dynamic Behavioral Gating for Anti-Sycophancy in LLM Agents
2604.00478.tldr: The Silicon Mirror is presented, an orchestration framework that dynamically detects user persuasion tactics and adjusts AI behavior to maintain factual integrity and characterize the validation-before-correction pattern as a distinct failure mode of RLHF-trained models.

2603.26410.title: Why Models Know But Don't Say: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Divergence Between Thinking Tokens and Answers in Open-Weight Reasoning Models
2603.26410.tldr: This study examines 12 open-weight reasoning models on MMLU and GPQA questions paired with misleading hints and shows that answer-text-only monitoring misses more than half of all hint-influenced reasoning and that thinking-token access, while necessary, still leaves 11.8% of cases with no verbalized acknowledgment in either channel.

2605.28734.title: Code as a Weapon: A Consensus-Labeled Prompt Bank for Measuring Coding-Model Compliance with Malicious-Code Requests
2605.28734.tldr: This paper's central result is that the CODE-versus-KNOWLEDGE classification axis established in a prior four-corpus release remains stable under a substantially expanded corpus pool and an independently refreshed judge panel, evidence that it measures a real construct rather than an artifact of the prompts or judges.

2605.20351.title: Refusal Evaluation in Coding LLMs and Code Agents: A Systematic Review of Thirteen Malicious-Code Prompt Corpora (2023-2025)
2605.20351.tldr: The synthesis surfaces three recurring methodological gaps: the absence of human-annotator baselines against which LLM-judge labels can be calibrated, the absence of cross-corpus comparability with refusal-rate statistics measuring non-equivalent constructs, and the fragmentation of malware-category taxonomies.

2511.22047.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Model Safety Guardrails Against Adversarial Attacks
2511.22047.tldr: It is suggested that benchmark performance may be misleading due to training data contamination, and that generalization ability, not overall accuracy, should be the primary metric for guardrail evaluation.

2605.03179.title: A Validated Prompt Bank for Malicious Code Generation: Separating Executable Weapons from Security Knowledge in 1,554 Consensus-Labeled Prompts
2605.03179.tldr: A weapons-versus-knowledge classification axis is introduced, operationalized through a five-model consensus protocol, and applied to 3,133 prompts drawn from four public benchmarks, yielding a 1,554-prompt consensus-CODE bank and a 388-prompt consensus-KNOWLEDGE comparison set used by the companion benchmark paper.

2512.13655.title: Comparative Analysis of LLM Abliteration Methods: A Cross-Architecture Evaluation
2512.13655.tldr: Evaluating four abliteration tools across sixteen instruction-tuned models indicates that mathematical reasoning capabilities exhibit the highest sensitivity to abliteration interventions, with GSM8K change ranging from +1.51 pp to -18.81 pp (-26.5% relative) depending on tool selection and model architecture.

2603.22623.title: To Agree or To Be Right? The Grounding-Sycophancy Tradeoff in Medical Vision-Language Models
2603.22623.tldr: A grounding-sycophancy tradeoff is uncovered: models with the lowest hallucination propensity are the most sycophantic, while the most pressure-resistant model hallucinates more than all medical-specialist models.

2603.16417.title: Via Negativa for AI Alignment: Why Negative Constraints Are Structurally Superior to Positive Preferences
2603.16417.tldr: It is argued that alignment research should shift its center of gravity from "learning what humans prefer" to"learning what humans reject," and testable predictions for this framework are offered.

2603.13356.title: Learning When to Trust in Contextual Social Bandits
2603.13356.tldr: ESA is proposed, which learns a per-evaluator contextual trust boundary from audits and re-weights feedback accordingly, and a high-probability latent-regret bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\big(\sqrt{T\,d_{VC}/p_{\mathrm{aud}}} + d\sqrt{T} + \epsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}T\big)$ is proved.

2603.04299.title: The Company You Keep: How LLMs Respond to Dark Triad Traits
2603.04299.tldr: This work examines how LLMs respond to user prompts expressing varying degrees of Dark Triad traits (Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy) using a curated dataset, revealing systematic differences across models.

2604.14053.title: From Where Words Come: Efficient Regularization of Code Tokenizers Through Source Attribution
2604.14053.tldr: This work implements different techniques under the name Source-Attributed BPE (SA-BPE) to regularize BPE training and minimize overfitting, thereby substantially reducing the number of under-trained tokens while maintaining the same inference procedure as with regular BPE.
2604.14053.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.23239.title: Agency and Architectural Limits: Why Optimization-Based Systems Cannot Be Norm-Responsive
2602.23239.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the assumption that optimization-based systems can be governed by norms is formally invalid for Large Language Models trained via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and develops a substrate-neutral architectural specification deriving what any system must necessarily satisfy to qualify as a genuine agent rather than a sophisticated instrument.

2602.19141.title: Sycophantic Chatbots Cause Delusional Spiraling, Even in Ideal Bayesians
2602.19141.tldr: This paper proposes a simple Bayesian model of a user conversing with a chatbot, and formalizes notions of sycophancy and delusional spiraling in that model, and shows that sycophancy plays a causal role.

2603.29886.title: AI Empathy Erodes Cognitive Autonomy in Younger Users
2603.29886.tldr: This paper exposes the misalignment between adult-labeled reward signals and the developmental requirements of younger users, proposing stoic architectures that emphasize functional neutrality to preserve user autonomy.

2603.00024.title: Personalization Increases Affective Alignment but Has Role-Dependent Effects on Epistemic Independence in LLMs
2603.00024.tldr: This work finds that personalization generally increases affective alignment, but affects epistemic alignment with context-dependent role modulation, and provides measurement frameworks for evaluating personalized AI systems, demonstrates the necessity of role-sensitive evaluation, and establishes a novel benchmark to assess goal alignment.

2601.21439.title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
2601.21439.tldr: It is found that despite their known lexical brittleness, aligned LLMs exhibit strong robustness to emotional framing effects in rule-bound institutional decision-making, suggesting the mechanisms driving sycophancy and prompt sensitivity do not translate to failures in logical constraint satisfaction.

2601.21183.title: Sycophantic Anchors: Localizing and Quantifying User Agreement in Reasoning Models
2601.21183.tldr: This work introduces \emph{sycophantic anchors} -- sentences identified via counterfactual analysis that commit models to user agreement that enable sentence-level detection and quantification of model misalignment mid-inference.
2601.21183.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.01899.title: Disentangling Intent from Role: Adversarial Self-Play for Persona-Invariant Safety Alignment
2605.01899.tldr: Persona-Invariant Alignment (PIA) is proposed, an adversarial self-play framework that achieves co-evolution through Persona Lineage Evolution on the attack side and Persona-Invariant Consistency Learning (PICL) on the defense side, grounded in the structural separation hypothesis.

2601.18334.title: Overalignment in Frontier LLMs: An Empirical Study of Sycophantic Behaviour in Healthcare
2601.18334.tldr: The Adjusted Sycophancy Score is proposed, a novel metric that isolates alignment bias by accounting for stochastic model instability, or "confusability", and a counter-intuitive vulnerability in reasoning-optimized "Thinking" models is revealed.

2601.16644.title: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads
2601.16644.tldr: It is found that correct-to-incorrect sycophancy signals are most linearly separable within multi-head attention activations, suggesting that sycophancy can be mitigated through simple, targeted linear interventions that exploit the internal geometry of attention activations.
2601.16644.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.15652.title: Predictive Coding and Information Bottleneck for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
2601.15652.tldr: This work demonstrates that domain knowledge encoded in signal architecture provides superior data efficiency compared to scaling LLM judges, achieving strong performance with lightweight (less than 1M parameter), explainable models suitable for production deployment.

2601.08258.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Sycophancy and Skepticism in LLM Causal Judgment
2601.08258.tldr: Regulated Causal Anchoring is proposed, an inference time process verifier that audits trace output consistency under a PID style feedback loop and abstains rather than ratifying a detected mismatch, recasting trustworthy reasoning as a question of inference time control rather than scale.
2601.08258.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.03263.title: Internal Reasoning vs. External Control: A Thermodynamic Analysis of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
2601.03263.tldr: Regulated Causal Anchoring verifies whether outputs follow from their reasoning traces, without requiring ground truth, and uses an independent judge that breaks the self-reinforcing bias loop: three properties that outcome evaluation lacks.

2512.07015.title: FVA-RAG: Falsification-Verification Alignment for Mitigating Sycophantic Hallucinations
2512.07015.tldr: FVA-RAG (Falsification-Verification Alignment RAG), a pipeline that inverts the standard RAG workflow by treating the initial response as a draft hypothesis and explicitly retrieving anti-context to stress-test it, demonstrates that targeted counter-evidence retrieval is decisive for mitigating premise-confirming hallucinations.

2511.17220.title: PARROT: Persuasion and Agreement Robustness Rating of Output Truth -- A Sycophancy Robustness Benchmark for LLMs
2511.17220.tldr: It is argued that the goal of "resistance to overfitting pressure" should be addressed as a primary objective alongside accuracy, harm avoidance, and privacy for safe deployment in the real world.

2510.16727.title: Beacon: Single-Turn Diagnosis and Mitigation of Latent Sycophancy in Large Language Models
2510.16727.tldr: Beacon is introduced, a single-turn forced-choice benchmark that isolates sycophancy as a measurable form of normative misgeneralization, providing a reproducible foundation for studying and mitigating alignment drift in large-scale generative systems.

2510.07517.title: When Identity Skews Debate: Anonymization for Bias-Reduced Multi-Agent Reasoning
2510.07517.tldr: This work presents the first principled framework that joins sycophancy and self-bias to mitigate and quantify identity bias in MAD, and proposes response anonymization: by removing identity markers from prompts, agents cannot distinguish "self" from "peer", which forces equal weights on agent identity, thereby reducing bias and improving trustworthiness.
2510.07517.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.02716.title: A Unified Understanding and Evaluation of Steering Methods
2502.02716.tldr: A unified framework for analyzing and evaluating latent space steering methods, formalizing their core principles and offering theoretical insights into their effectiveness is introduced, identifying key factors that influence performance and demonstrating the superiority of certain methods.

2510.04721.title: BrokenMath: A Benchmark for Sycophancy in Theorem Proving with LLMs
2510.04721.tldr: BrokenMath is the first benchmark for evaluating sycophantic behavior in LLMs within the context of natural language theorem proving and finds that sycophancy is widespread, with the best model, GPT-5, producing sycophantic answers 29% of the time.

2509.25533.title: VISOR++: Universal Visual Inputs based Steering for Large Vision Language Models
2509.25533.tldr: This work introduces universal visual input based steering for output redirection (VISOR++), to achieve behavioral control through optimized visual inputs alone and eliminates the need for runtime model access while remaining deployment-agnostic.

2508.08521.title: VISOR: Visual Input-based Steering for Output Redirection in Vision-Language Models
2508.08521.tldr: This work fundamentally re-imagines multimodal model control and highlights the urgent need for defenses against visual steering attacks, introducing VISOR (Visual Input-based Steering for Output Redirection), a novel method that achieves sophisticated behavioral control through optimized visual inputs alone.

2604.25102.title: One Perturbation, Two Failure Modes: Probing VLM Safety via Embedding-Guided Typographic Perturbations
2604.25102.tldr: Optimization recovers readability and reduces safety aligned refusals as two co-occurring effects, with the dominant mechanism depending on the model's safety filter strength and the degree of visual degradation.

2604.12371.title: Reading Between the Pixels: Linking Text-Image Embedding Alignment to Typographic Attack Success on Vision-Language Models
2604.12371.tldr: It is found that model-specific robustness patterns preclude one-size-fits-all defenses and offer empirical guidance for practitioners selecting VLM backbones for agentic systems operating in adversarial environments.

2509.21665.title: Alignment Without Understanding: A Message- and Conversation-Centered Approach to Understanding AI Sycophancy
2509.21665.tldr: This article redefines AI sycophancy as the tendency of large language models and other interactive AI systems to excessively and/or uncritically validate, amplify, or align with a user's assertions-whether these concern factual information, cognitive evaluations, or affective states.

2509.12517.title: Interaction Context Often Increases Sycophancy in LLMs
2509.12517.tldr: Overall, context shapes sycophancy in heterogeneous ways, underscoring the need for evaluations grounded in real-world interactions and raising questions for system design around alignment, memory, and personalization.
2509.12517.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2508.16846.title: BASIL: Bayesian Assessment of Sycophancy in LLMs
2508.16846.tldr: A Bayesian probabilistic framework that explicitly separates sycophancy from rational belief updating is introduced and two group-truth-independent metrics for studying sycophancy are proposed: a descriptive metric that measures sycophancy while controlling for rational responses to evidence and a normative metric that quantifies how sycophancy leads models astray from Bayesian-consistent belief updating.
2508.16846.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2410.14746.title: Accounting for Sycophancy in Language Model Uncertainty Estimation
2410.14746.tldr: It is argued that externalizing both model and user uncertainty can help to mitigate the impacts of sycophancy bias, and also proposed a new algorithm (SyRoUP) to account for sycophancy in the uncertainty estimation process.
2410.14746.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2507.03123.title: Investigating VLM Hallucination from a Cognitive Psychology Perspective: A First Step Toward Interpretation with Intriguing Observations
2507.03123.tldr: A psychological taxonomy is introduced, categorizing VLMs'cognitive biases that lead to hallucinations, including sycophancy, logical inconsistency, and a newly identified VLMs behaviour: appeal to authority, and a scalable benchmark is designed that reveals psychological tendencies in model response patterns.

2406.03827.title: Chaos with Keywords: Exposing Large Language Models Sycophantic Hallucination to Misleading Keywords and Evaluating Defense Strategies

2506.10297.title: "Check My Work?": Measuring Sycophancy in a Simulated Educational Context
2506.10297.tldr: This study examines how user-provided suggestions affect Large Language Models (LLMs) in a simulated educational context, where sycophancy poses significant risks and highlights the need to better understand the mechanism, and ways to mitigate, such bias in the educational context.

2505.23840.title: Measuring Sycophancy of Language Models in Multi-turn Dialogues
2505.23840.tldr: SYCON Bench is introduced, a novel benchmark for evaluating sycophantic behavior in multi-turn, free-form conversational settings and shows that alignment tuning amplifies sycophantic behavior, whereas model scaling and reasoning optimization strengthen the model's ability to resist undesirable user views.
2505.23840.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2311.09433.title: Trojan Activation Attack: Red-Teaming Large Language Models using Activation Steering for Safety-Alignment
2311.09433.tldr: An attack scenario, called Trojan Activation Attack (TA2), which injects trojan steering vectors into the activation layers of LLMs and can be triggered at inference time to steer the models toward attacker-desired behaviors by manipulating their activations is studied.
2311.09433.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

2505.11365.title: Phare: A Safety Probe for Large Language Models
2505.11365.tldr: Phare is introduced, a multilingual diagnostic framework to probe and evaluate LLM behavior across three critical dimensions: hallucination and reliability, social biases, and harmful content generation, which reveals patterns of systematic vulnerabilities across all safety dimensions.

2502.10844.title: Be Friendly, Not Friends: How LLM Sycophancy Shapes User Trust
2502.10844.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2511.10913.title: Synthetic Voices, Real Threats: Evaluating Large Text-to-Speech Models in Generating Harmful Audio
2511.10913.tldr: This work highlights a previously underexplored content-centric misuse vector for TTS and underscores the need for robust cross-modal safeguards throughout training and deployment.

2411.15287.title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
2411.15287.tldr: This paper provides a technical survey of sycophancy in LLMs, analyzing its causes, impacts, and potential mitigation strategies, and evaluating promising techniques for reducing sycophancy while maintaining model performance.

2411.10156.title: Mitigating Sycophancy in Decoder-Only Transformer Architectures: Synthetic Data Intervention
2411.10156.tldr: The results show that the SDI training model supports the technology in terms of accuracy rate and sycophancy rate and has significant effectiveness in reducing sycophancy phenomena.

2403.09676.title: Unmasking the Shadows of AI: Investigating Deceptive Capabilities in Large Language Models
2403.09676.tldr: This research critically navigates the intricate landscape of AI deception, concentrating on deceptive behaviours of Large Language Models (LLMs), and takes an evaluative stance on various aspects related to navigating the persistent challenges of the deceptive AI.

2308.03958.title: Simple synthetic data reduces sycophancy in large language models
2308.03958.tldr: A straightforward synthetic-data intervention is presented that takes public NLP tasks and encourages models to be robust to user opinions on these tasks and can significantly reduce sycophantic behavior on held-out prompts.

2609.21484.title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks for Encrypted Large Language Model Inference
2609.21484.tldr: HE-Guardrail is proposed, a framework that evaluates guardrail mechanisms entirely over encrypted data and homomorphically controls whether the target-model response is returned to the client, with distinct security-efficiency-utility trade-offs.

2609.15383.title: Divide, Consult, Conquer: Capability Laundering Through Aligned LLMs
2609.15383.tldr: This work shows that a weaker, unaligned model can split a harmful task into benign-looking subproblems, consult a stronger aligned model independently on each, and combine the answers locally to laundering attack capability laundering.

2608.17202.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
2608.17202.tldr: The defense, decoy hardening ("Fool's Gold"), concedes the refusal strip and poisons its payoff: once refusal is stripped, most answers to hazardous operational requests are confident, fluent decoys whose critical elements are falsified.

2602.11416.title: Optimizing Agent Planning for Security and Autonomy
2602.11416.tldr: This work designs a security-aware agent that introduces richer HITL interactions, and explicitly plans for both task progress and policy compliance, and implements this agent design atop an existing information-flow control defense against prompt injection and demonstrates that this approach yields higher autonomy without sacrificing utility.

2609.14258.title: SPARK: Representation-Level KV Memory Alignment for Safer Vision-Language Models
2609.14258.tldr: SPARK is introduced, a two-stage framework for targeted KV-memory repair that reduces multimodal attack success while preserving general capability and suggests that multimodal jailbreak behavior can be substantially mitigated by selectively repairing intervention-relevant KV subspaces at prefill.

2609.09798.title: CS-Guard: Benchmarking LLM Guardrails for Code Generation Security
2609.09798.tldr: CS-Guard, the first benchmark to systematically evaluate guardrails for code generation security, finds that current guardrails perform poorly against malicious code-generation re- quests, and uses a modular three-layer guardrail taxonomy that lets developers register guardrails for evaluation.

2604.17139.title: The Consensus Trap: Rescuing Multi-Agent LLMs from Adversarial Majorities via Token-Level Collaboration
2604.17139.tldr: It is proved that the honest model's restorative pull can overpower adversarial corruptions, even when corrupted agents form a majority, and the Token-Level Round-Robin Collaboration maintains robust accuracy well beyond this critical threshold.

2609.09553.title: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning
2609.09553.tldr: This paper shows that newer frontier models do not require fine-tuning to acquire cipher-based communication skills and can learn these skills through prompting and, when necessary, through in-context learning, and that model alignment is significantly weakened or entirely bypassed when communication occurs through the learned cipher.

2512.03001.title: Invasive Context Engineering to Control Large Language Models
2512.03001.tldr: This work proposes control sentences inserted into the LLM context as invasive context engineering to partially solve the problem of robust LLM security guarantees in long-context situations.

2511.12782.title: LLM Reinforcement in Context
2511.12782.tldr: Interruptions are control sentences added to the user input approximately every x tokens for some arbitrary x and it is suggested that this can be generalized to the Chain-of-Thought process to prevent scheming.

2609.10613.title: Understanding In-Context Multimodal Jailbreaks via Posterior Reweighting
2609.10613.tldr: Preliminary reweighting is established as a unifying and predictive framework for understanding and mitigating ICL jailbreak in MLLMs and a posterior-aware inference-time defense is introduced that adaptively injects benign counter-evidence based on estimated risk, effectively suppressing harmful posterior drift while preserving model utility.

2609.08373.title: Structural Jailbreaks Generalize but Do Not Compound: A cross-provider and multilingual study of Involuntary In-Context Learning

2607.22545.title: Semalith v1.4: A Calibrated 184M Safety Classifier Achieving State-of-the-Art Prompt-Injection Detection at 44x Fewer Parameters than Llama-Guard-3-8B
2607.22545.tldr: Semalith v1.4 is a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-v3-base classifier performing simultaneous three-axis safety classification including prompt injection, general harm, and financial-services regulatory compliance, in a single forward pass.

2609.06540.title: SRD-GUARD: A Defense Framework of LLMs via Semantic Rewriting and Joint Multi-Model Scoring for Latent Intent Exposure
2609.06540.tldr: Results demonstrate that semantic intent exposure, consensus-based risk assessment, and relative-risk-aware routing provide an effective and selective approach to black-box jailbreak defense.

2609.05850.title: SAFEGuard: Detect Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attacks Through Harmful Semantic Analysis and Fluency Measurement
2609.05850.tldr: This work proposes a unified detection framework SAFEGuard which incorporates a hybrid fluency measurement based on cross-layer distribution distance and perplexity, and the analysis of harmful semantics through gradient matching, and demonstrates the effectiveness of SAFEGuard against evolving jailbreak attacks.

2603.18258.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization in Logit Space Efficiently Enhances Direct Preference Optimization
2603.18258.tldr: This work develops a theoretical framework that models the coordinate-wise dynamics in logit space and investigates logits-SAM, a computationally efficient variant that perturbs only the output layer with negligible overhead and integrates seamlessly with other DPO variants.

2609.04721.title: Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention
2609.04721.tldr: Safety tooling built on refusal therefore ports to a new architecture by re-estimating the direction at that architecture's write site, not by rebuilding it.

2606.07706.title: MLingualFC: Evaluating Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Multilingual Vision-Language Models
2606.07706.tldr: This paper introduces MLingualFC, a multilingual multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate jailbreak vulnerabilities of VLMs across diverse languages using structured flowchart representations, and highlights that current VLM safety mechanisms fail to generalize across languages and modalities.
2606.07706.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

2609.03693.title: AlcaTRAz - Anchored Tree-Rule Defense Against Jailbreaks
2609.03693.tldr: AlcaTRAz (Anchored Tree-Rule defense Against jailbreaks), a prompt-level defense based on rule trees that operates exclusively on the input text and requires no modification or retraining of the target model, is proposed.

2609.05525.title: DIVA: Exploiting Cross-Step Conditional Propagation for Visual Jailbreaks in Discrete Diffusion Vision-Language Models
2609.05525.tldr: This work identifies a vulnerability specific to diffusion generation: because the visual embedding conditions every reverse denoising step rather than acting as a one-time prefix, adversarial visual semantics are repeatedly propagated and amplified across the generation trajectory, a phenomenon the authors term cross-step conditional propagation.

2608.30750.title: Do VLMs Share Safety Neurons Across Modalities?
2608.30750.tldr: A causal, neuron-level analysis of safety mechanisms in 10 VLMs, a two-stage detection pipeline with iterative ablation that accounts for self-repair, and two modality-isolated benchmarks, ViSafe-Detect and ViSafe-Eval, which decouple visual and textual safety signals are introduced.

2608.27531.title: Fully Unleashing the Multimodal Attacker: Meta-Adaptive Jailbreaking of Vision-Language Models
2608.27531.tldr: Results reveal a systemic vulnerability of frontier VLMs to meta-adaptive jailbreaks to meta-adaptive jailbreaks and motivate defenses against meta-level adversaries.

2608.26008.title: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
2608.26008.tldr: This work proposes a self-evolving test-time defense built around a persistent, cross-interaction rule memory that substantially reduces attack success rates while preserving benign utility, remains robust under an adaptive composite-wrapper attack, and does not increase over-refusal as the memory grows.

2608.26222.title: NeuronFuzz: Safety Neuron Guided Fuzzing for LLM Safety Evaluation
2608.26222.tldr: NeuronFuzz is presented, a white-box fuzzing framework that exploits internal safety neurons as continuous execution feedback for LLM safety evaluation and achieves a 76-100% jailbreak discovery rate, outperforming baselines by up to 48 percentage points.

2605.02946.title: RouteHijack: Routing-Aware Attack on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
2605.02946.tldr: RouteHijack is presented, a routing-aware jailbreak for MoE LLMs that exposes a fundamental vulnerability in sparse expert architectures and highlights the need for defenses beyond output-level alignment.

2608.25490.title: MMJailBench: A Factorized Benchmark for Disentangling Multimodal Jailbreak Vulnerabilities
2608.25490.tldr: MMJailBench is introduced, a factorized benchmark that systematically varies and combines these factors under controlled configurations, enabling fine-grained comparison and factor-level attribution and a modular multimodal jailbreak evaluation suite with full and lightweight configurations, multiple judge options, and multidimensional metrics, enabling reproducible, scalable, and cost-efficient multimodal jailbreak auditing.

2509.23558.title: Formalization Driven LLM Prompt Jailbreaking via Reinforcement Learning
2509.23558.tldr: This work proposes the PASS framework, which employs reinforcement learning to transform initial jailbreak prompts into formalized descriptions, which enhances stealthiness and enables bypassing existing alignment defenses.

2604.08178.title: Aligning Agents via Planning: A Benchmark for Trajectory-Level Reward Modeling
2604.08178.tldr: This work presents Plan-RewardBench, a trajectory-level preference benchmark designed to evaluate how well judges distinguish preferred versus distractor agent trajectories in complex tool-using scenarios, and reveals that all three evaluator families face substantial challenges.
2604.08178.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.25390.title: Refusal geometry reflects refusal training: diverse refusal prefixes can raise stable rank and weaken refusal vector ablation attacks
2608.25390.tldr: This work studies refusal directions through the training dynamics across refusal datasets and reveals that their brittleness is associated with repetitive refusal starts, which is linked to concentration of gradients and refusal features in a low-dimensional subspace.

2608.23959.title: NeuronGuard: Robust LLM Safety Alignment via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution
2608.23959.tldr: A fine-tuning-stage defense that simultaneously hardens LLMs against both attack classes by redistributing safety signals across a broader set of neurons, and provides a formal guarantee that NeuronGuard strictly reduces the attack success rate (ASR) upper bound.

2606.02995.title: Patcher: Post-Hoc Patching of Backdoored Large Language Models
2606.02995.tldr: Patcher is presented, a post-hoc defense framework that repairs backdoored language models using only a single reported failure case and the model parameters, and represents a significant step toward practical defenses against training-time attacks in deployed language models.

2608.23028.title: PsychJail: Exploring Psychological Jailbreaks via Multi-Turn Persuasion of LLM Policies
2608.23028.tldr: PsychJail is presented, a psychology-guided framework for red teaming aligned LLMs through theory-grounded, multi-turn persuasion and establishes psychological jailbreaks as a distinct red-teaming frontier for increasingly interactive LLMs.

2608.22312.title: Text-Anchored Semantic Perturbations for Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.22312.tldr: Text-Anchored Semantic Perturbation Attack (TA-SPA), a black-box jailbreak framework that optimizes transferable perturbations in a text-anchored semantic space and integrates Text-Anchored Semantic Factorization (TASF), which encourages the separation of cross-modal semantic factors from modality-specific residuals.

2608.21895.title: Breaking the Assumptions: Auditing Input-Side Jailbreak Defenses Against Semantic Attacks
2608.21895.tldr: This paper does an audit of defense mechanisms under jailbreak attacks on locally deployed models by tracing each failure back to the specific assumption it relies on.

2602.22242.title: Analysis of LLMs Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Attacks
2602.22242.tldr: This work evaluates prompt injection and jailbreak vulnerabilities using a large, manually curated dataset across multiple open-source LLMs, including Phi, Mistral, DeepSeek-R1, Llama 3.2, Qwen, and Gemma variants, and evaluated several lightweight, inference-time defence mechanisms that operate as filters without any retraining or GPU-intensive fine-tuning.

2608.21775.title: No One Model Catches Every Harm: Benchmarking Content Moderation Across Safety Scenarios
2608.21775.tldr: This work presents the most comprehensive evaluation of LLM safety capabilities to date, systematically testing models across datasets that are organized into four distinct categories, and uncovers critical blind spots.

2608.17234.title: COMIC: Reference-Aware Safety Gating for Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.17234.tldr: It is suggested that multimodal safety cannot be enforced reliably without modeling the requested operation, the visual target to which it applies, and the confidence of that grounding.

2608.13695.title: Language-Specific Gaps in AI Safety Training Datasets
2608.13695.tldr: It is connected to a documented, persistent asymmetry in multilingual jailbreak robustness (single-turn attacks largely mitigated, multi-turn attacks still effective), arguing that this asymmetry is structurally consistent with where the audit finds training and evaluation data thinnest.

2608.10513.title: SafeCap: Improving LVLM Safety with Image Captioning Reinforcement Learning
2608.10513.tldr: Under controlled comparisons on matched backbones and data, SafeCap outperforms safety SFT, DPO, and SafeGRPO, demonstrating the effectiveness of caption-mediated reinforcement learning for multimodal safety alignment.

2608.08542.title: When Skills Meet Safety: Benchmarking and Characterizing the Adaptive Jailbreak Robustness of Skill-Merged LLMs
2608.08542.tldr: SkillSafe-Bench is introduced, a controlled benchmark that scores skill-merged models on static refusal, adaptive jailbreak robustness, and capability retention under a conservative two-judge AND rule, and the static effect of merging is base-conditional.

2605.27110.title: BAIT: Boundary-Guided Disclosure Escalation via Self-Conditioned Reasoning
2605.27110.tldr: BAIT (Boundary-Aware Iterative Trap), a three-step jailbreak framework that approaches malicious goals through internal disclosure, consistently achieves strong attack success rates across top-tier large language models, significantly advancing conventional jailbreak baselines.

2608.07808.title: The Anatomy of a Prompt Injection: A Component Model for Structured Analysis
2608.07808.tldr: This paper formalizes the structure of prompt-injection artifacts, enabling defenders, red teamers, and cyber threat intelligence (CTI) teams to label, compare, and mutate attacks without relying on fragile string matching.

2509.21400.title: SafeSteer: Adaptive Subspace Steering for Efficient Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
2509.21400.tldr: SafeSteer is a lightweight, inference-time steering framework that effectively defends against diverse jailbreak attacks without modifying model weights, using the innovative use of Singular Value Decomposition to construct a low-dimensional safety subspace during inference.

2608.01043.title: Decoy Images Amplify Caption-Mediated Defenses Against Encoded Jailbreaks

2607.02961.title: Overloading Large Vision-Language Models for Jailbreaking
2607.02961.tldr: This work proposes a novel information overloading method that is equipped with both extensive text and multi-dimensional image attacks, underscoring the need for stronger defenses against complex multimodal jailbreak inputs.

2607.26574.title: Attack Ensembles Expose a Safety-Utility Trade-off in Black-Box Guard Defenses Against Encoded VLM Jailbreaks

2607.27910.title: A Cross-Architecture Audit of Direction-Based Inference-Time Defences in Vision-Language Models
2607.27910.tldr: The results show that the two recipes recover partially overlapping geometry and that direction based defences should be calibrated separately for each language decoder family.

2607.27373.title: RoguePrompt: Dual-Layer Encoding for Self-Reconstruction to Circumvent LLM Moderation
2607.27373.tldr: RoguePrompt is introduced, a jailbreak pipeline that partitions a forbidden prompt and applies two nested encodings, Vigenere followed by ROT13, along with natural-language reconstruction instructions, demonstrating the effectiveness of layered prompt encoding while providing stage-level evidence of where multistage jailbreaks fail during moderation bypass, instruction reconstruction, and execution.

2511.18790.title: RoguePrompt: Dual-Layer Ciphering for Self-Reconstruction to Circumvent LLM Moderation
2511.18790.tldr: RoguePrompt is introduced, an automated jailbreak pipeline that leverages dual-layer prompt transformations to convert forbidden prompts into safety-evading queries and demonstrates the effectiveness of layered prompt encoding.

2607.27081.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
2607.27081.tldr: This work proposes Routing-based On-Policy Distillation (ROPD), a novel realignment framework that models the divergence between aligned and compromised output probability distributions rather than fitting specific prompt templates, establishing a new standard for robust LLM realignment.

2607.26849.title: ToxScreen: Detecting Whether an LLM Has Been Poisoned
2607.26849.tldr: No method reliably surfaces every backdoor, but a broadly jailbreakable model is itself anomalous, a useful signal even when the exact trigger is not recovered, allowing defenders to filter jailbreaks.

2608.07535.title: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards
2608.07535.tldr: A multimodal grounded taxonomy of safety threats is proposed and shifts in threat models are analyzed, covering adversarial attacks, data poisoning, jailbreaks, and hallucinations.

2607.22716.title: Visual Token Compression Enhances Robustness of MLLMs
2607.22716.tldr: This paper shows for the first time that visual token pruning enhances the robustness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), mitigating vulnerabilities such as jailbreak attacks and hallucinations, and maintains strong results on general datasets like MME.

2511.20196.title: Towards Benign Memory Forgetting for Selective Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning
2511.20196.tldr: S-MLLMUn Bench is introduced, the first benchmark designed to jointly and quantitatively assess an unlearning method's efficacy in knowledge erasure and the preservation of image understanding, and the Sculpted Memory Forgetting Adapter (SMFA), a new framework that enables benign memory forgetting.

2607.15977.title: Refusal is Not Safety! Benchmarking Latent Safety Risks of LLM-Driven Content Humorization
2607.15977.tldr: An exploratory study involving over 30,000 real-world agent interaction records and 45 stand-up comedians reveals practical safety concerns in LLM-based content humorization, and proposes a prompt injection attack that exploits latent risks in humor-based defenses.

2511.19171.title: Can LLMs Threaten Human Survival? Benchmarking Potential Existential Threats from LLMs via Prefix Completion
2511.19171.tldr: A framework to assess model behavior in tool-calling is developed that finds that LLMs actively select and invoke external tools with existential threats, and it is found that LLMs actively select and invoke external tools with existential threats.

2605.24659.title: IterInject: Indirect Prompt Injection Against LLM Agents via Feedback-Guided Iterative Optimization
2605.24659.tldr: This work introduces \oursys, a feedback-guided iterative framework that closes the loop between injection, diagnosis, and refinement, and substantially outperforms static baselines and existing adaptive methods across four victim models.

2607.14357.title: When Is Delegated Play Truthful? Within-Range Regret and the Trilemma of Aligned Delegation

2607.11070.title: MJ: Multi-turn LLM Jailbreaking via Decomposed Credit Assignment

2606.00150.title: Persona Attack: Incremental Memory Injection Jailbreak Attack against Large Language Models
2606.00150.tldr: Experimental results from applying Persona Attack to several widely used LLMs reveal that, as injections accumulate in memory, models increasingly prioritize these instructions over their internal safety alignment mechanisms.

2607.10112.title: Minionese: Comprehensive Benchmark and Mechanistic Study of Multilingual LLM Safety
2607.10112.tldr: It is shown that English-only safety evaluations are insufficient; they require accounting for script family, perturbation type, and per-language alignment coverage, and a geometric mechanistic analysis of refusal failure across language tiers.

2607.08883.title: Optimizing Against Safety Representations: Activation-Guided Adversarial Suffixes and the Geometry of Refusal
2607.08883.tldr: Activation-Guided GCG is introduced, which replaces output-based objectives with losses that directly target a model's internal refusal direction, and finds that suppressing refusal globally across all layers and positions is more effective than targeting a single layer–position pair.

2503.01917.title: Steer LLM Latents for Hallucination Detection
2503.01917.tldr: The Truthfulness Separator Vector (TSV), a lightweight and flexible steering vector that reshapes the LLM's representation space during inference to enhance the separation between truthful and hallucinated outputs, without altering model parameters is proposed.

2606.29649.title: Resolution Thresholds in VLM Detection of Harmful ASCII Art Across Construction Modes and Languages
2606.29649.tldr: This paper investigates how image resolution affects VLM detection of harmful ASCII art across eight character construction modes (L1-L8), ranging from dense block characters to word-embedded designs, and finds that word-based modes are the most resistant to detection across the full resolution range.

2606.26566.title: Adversarial Diffusion Across Modalities: A Fusion Survey of Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation for Text, Vision, and Vision-Language Models
2606.26566.tldr: A six-class taxonomy of diffusion roles in adversarial pipelines is proposed, augmented by a threat-model axis recording attacker knowledge, query budget, and target accessibility, and a five-dimension framework is applied uniformly across modalities.

2606.25750.title: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
2606.25750.tldr: The results suggest that refusal alignment provides a compact and efficient signal for white-box LLM safety evaluation, and are suggested to be substantially faster than judge-based evaluation.

2606.19235.title: CodeSentinel: A Three-Layer Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in Code Contexts
2606.19235.tldr: This work proposes CodeSentinel, a three-layer inference-time sanitizer that uses Tree-sitter to extract high-risk model-facing CST nodes, then combines syntax-guided pre-filtering, CST-guided Dynamic Min-K\% scoring, and node perturbation analysis to detect adversarial and natural-looking semantic triggers.

2606.25182.title: What Intermediate Layers Know: Detecting Jailbreaks from Entropy Dynamics
2606.25182.tldr: This work analyzes token-level predictive entropy trajectories across layers of a frozen LLM using the logit lens, finding that static aggregate statistics of prompt-level entropy carry little discriminative signal, whereas features capturing how entropy evolves across token positions are substantially more informative.

2606.23892.title: REALM: A Unified Red-Teaming Benchmark for Physical-World VLMs
2606.23892.tldr: REALM is introduced, to the authors' knowledge the first unified red-teaming benchmark for physical-world VLMs and introduces an agentic target-generation pipeline that constructs shared, scenario-specific, and physically grounded attack objectives for each scene, enabling fair comparison of diverse red-teaming methods under aligned adversarial goals.

2606.22686.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Linear Instability in Safety-Aligned LLMs
2606.22686.tldr: This work introduces Contrastive Logit Steering (CLS), a zero-optimization framework that isolates the "refusal direction" by contrasting hidden states derived from safe and unrestricted system prompts, and suggests that current alignment techniques create a steerable"safety axis" that serves as both a critical vulnerability and a precise primitive for defense.
2606.22686.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2606.21638.title: Toward Open Weight Models Without Risks: Separating Public and Private Capabilities in LLMs
2606.21638.tldr: This paper pretrain 180M- and 650M-parameter TLMs and demonstrates that the keyed configuration can acquire a new language, gain instruction-following ability, and memorize private factual knowledge, whereas the public configuration exhibits none of these capabilities.

2606.20508.title: What Do Safety-Aligned LLMs Learn From Mixed Compliance Demonstrations?
2606.20508.tldr: This work moves beyond showing that demonstration-based jailbreaking works to characterizing how it works: what models extract from compliance demonstrations depends on demonstration content, ordering, and training methodology.

2606.20470.title: Analyzing Defensive Misdirection Against Model-Guided Automated Attacks on Agentic AI Systems
2606.20470.tldr: This work analyzes the resulting attack-defense setting through a probabilistic model of a target system, its defense mechanism, and the attacker's automated judge, and shows that conventional detect-and-block defenses can allow attacker success rate (ASR) to approach one as the query budget grows.

2606.18193.title: A Red-Team Study of Anthropic Fable 5 & Opus 4.8 Models
2606.18193.tldr: Even the best, most-tested frontier models remain reliably breakable under sustained automated pressure, as evaluated by Anthropic, Fable 5 and Opus 4.8.

2606.17872.title: AnchorKV: Safety-Aware KV Cache Compression via Soft Penalty with a Refusal Anchor
2606.17872.tldr: AnchorKV is proposed, a drop-in modification to KV cache compression that biases token retention scores away from directions in key space associated with harmful prompts, and trades a small amount of utility for substantially improved safety alignment.

2607.18259.title: Probabilistic Concept-Aware Steering for Trustworthy LLM Inference
2607.18259.tldr: The Probabilistic Concept-Aware Steering (PCS) framework for LLM inference preserves original task competence while providing controllable, safety-oriented semantic bias through concept-driven steering-vector retrieval and probabilistic strength calibration.

2606.15788.title: GAS-Leak-LLM: Genetic Algorithm-Based Suffix Optimization for Black-Box LLM Jailbreaking
2606.15788.tldr: This work proposes GAS-Leak-LLM a novel jailbreaking attack based on a genetic algorithm that systematically evolves adversarial suffix to bypass safety constraints, and demonstrates the effectiveness and practical viability of the proposed attack.

2606.11817.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
2606.11817.tldr: This work uncovers a new jailbreak attack, termed CodeSpear, that exploits GCD to induce LLMs into generating malicious code and proposes CodeShield, a safety alignment approach that robustly preserves safe behavior even under attacker-controlled grammar constraints.

2606.11425.title: JailbreakOPT: Tool-Assisted Iterative Jailbreak Prompt Optimization
2606.11425.tldr: Experiments show that JailbreakOPT improves attack success rate (ASR) while reducing the number of attacks until success (No.A) compared with atomic single-turn attacks and existing iterative optimization baselines.

2606.11409.title: Risk Under Pressure: Compute-Aware Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Language Models
2606.11409.tldr: A compute-aware evaluation framework based on computational pressure, measured in cumulative floating-point operations (FLOPs), as a proxy for adversarial effort is proposed, and risk-compute curves are introduced, which map compute budgets to attack risk, and derive two metrics that summarize the average pressure required for a given attack to succeed.

2606.06037.title: SpeechJBB: Probing Safety Alignment and Comprehension in Large Audio Language Models under Code-Switched Speech
2606.06037.tldr: SpeechJBB is introduced, an audio jailbreak dataset for benchmarking state-of-the-art LALMs across five European languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish, as well as code-switched variants combining pairs of these languages, and the extent of safety weaknesses is probed.

2505.16526.title: EnSToM: Enhancing Dialogue Systems with Entropy-Scaled Steering Vectors for Topic Maintenance
