2510.01644.tldr: The ability of different machine learning models to distinguish jailbreak prompts from genuine uses is analysed, including the ability to identify jailbreaks that use previously unseen strategies, and explicit reflexivity in prompt structure could be a signal of jailbreak intention.

2510.01359.title: Breaking the Code: Security Assessment of AI Code Agents Through Systematic Jailbreaking Attacks
2510.01359.tldr: JAWS-BENCH(Jailbreaks Across WorkSpaces), a benchmark spanning three escalating workspace regimes mirroring attacker capability, is presented, indicating that JAWS-BENCH can be reused across multiple agent frameworks.
2510.01359.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.24319.title: Dual Mechanisms of Value Expression: Intrinsic vs. Prompted Values in Large Language Models
2509.24319.tldr: It is demonstrated that intrinsic and prompted value mechanisms partly share common components crucial for inducing value expression, generalizing across languages and reconstructing theoretical inter-value correlations in the model's internal representations.

2509.23882.title: Quant Fever, Reasoning Blackholes, Schrodinger's Compliance, and More: Probing GPT-OSS-20B
2509.23882.tldr: An extensive security evaluation of GPT-OSS-20B that probes the model's behavior under different adversarial conditions and uncovers several failure modes including quant fever, reasoning blackholes, Schrodinger's compliance, reasoning procedure mirage, and chain-oriented prompting.

2509.16870.title: DecipherGuard: Understanding and Deciphering Jailbreak Prompts for a Safer Deployment of Intelligent Software Systems
2509.16870.tldr: DecipherGuard is proposed, a novel framework that integrates a deciphering layer to counter obfuscation-based prompts and a low-rank adaptation mechanism to enhance guardrail effectiveness against template-based attacks that highlights the effectiveness of DecipherGuard in defending LLM-powered software systems against jailbreak attacks during runtime.

2509.16861.title: AdaptiveGuard: Towards Adaptive Runtime Safety for LLM-Powered Software
2509.16861.tldr: The proposed AdaptiveGuard is an adaptive guardrail that detects novel jailbreak attacks as out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs and learns to defend against them through a continual learning framework, and achieves 96% OOD detection accuracy, adapts to new attacks in just two update steps, and retains over 85% F1-score on in-distribution data post-adaptation, outperforming other baselines.
2509.16861.venue: International Conference on Automated Software Engineering

2509.15202.title: Beyond Surface Alignment: Rebuilding LLMs Safety Mechanism via Probabilistically Ablating Refusal Direction
2509.15202.tldr: This work introduces DeepRefusal, a robust safety alignment framework that forces the model to dynamically rebuild its refusal mechanisms from jailbreak states by probabilistically ablating the refusal direction across layers and token depths during fine-tuning.
2509.15202.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2606.04425.title: What If Prompt Injection Never Left? Rethinking Agent Security through Cross-Session Stored Prompt Injection
2606.04425.tldr: This work introduces Cross-Session Stored Prompt Injection, a new threat vector inspired by stored cross-site scripting that redefines prompt injection for agentic systems by extending its threat model across both time, where attacks persist and activate across sessions, and space, where adversarial instructions propagate beyond the immediate prompt into persistent system state.

2609.19140.title: AgentLSD: Evaluating AI Security Agents Under Adversarial Task Contamination
2609.19140.tldr: Results show that clean CTF performance understates vulnerability to deceptive task evidence, and AgentLSD isolates this effect and provides a reproducible benchmark for studying it.

2609.18411.title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
2609.18411.tldr: Results show that grounding approval in the action that will actually execute provides architectural protection against security failures that prompt-level defences and conventional HITL confirmation cannot reliably prevent.

2609.16098.title: Universal Defenses for Tool-Integrated LLM Agents Against Adversarial Attacks
2609.16098.tldr: Two universal tool-based defenses are introduced: Attacker Tool Filtering, which uses anomaly detection to identify and remove suspicious tools, and Normal Tool Recalling, a white-box method that restores the agent's original toolset prior to planning.

2609.14987.title: ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
2609.14987.tldr: Results show that ActGuard reduces attack success rates to a level comparable to state-of-the-art defenses while maintaining task utility close to the no-attack setting, achieving a favorable security-utility trade-off.

2609.10892.title: DriftNet: A Dual-Head Trajectory Transformer for Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
2609.10892.tldr: DriftNet is presented, a dual-head trajectory Transformer that reads a logged tool-call trajectory and answers all three questions in one forward pass: one head classifies the trajectory as compromised or not, and a second assigns every step one of four labels (benign, injection point, hijacked, failed injection).

2609.10854.title: No-Box Vulnerability Analysis: Description-only Detection of Indirect Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in MCP Servers
2609.10854.tldr: This work proposes a new paradigm of no-box vulnerability analysis in which neither access nor runtime interaction is available, and only functionality metadata is available, and introduces no-box vulnerability analysis as a new analysis paradigm and demonstrates its practical feasibility in realistic systems.

2609.07529.title: CoER: Defending against Adaptive Indirect Prompt Injection via Adversarial Co-Evolution and Refinement
2609.07529.tldr: This work proposes CoER, a verifier-grounded co-evolution and refinement framework that combines adaptive attacker-defender co-training with subsequent refinement, and retains historical policies from both roles as opponent populations and mixes current and historical opponents for bilateral reinforcement learning.

2609.05074.title: Influence Score and Transformers interpretability: Measure of the Effective Impact of Attention Heads at inference time
2609.05074.tldr: An influence score is proposed to quantify the contribution of attention heads to classification decisions in Transformer-based models designed for prompt injection detection, providing an effective compromise between fine-grained circuit analysis and global output-based methods.

2607.08147.title: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
2607.08147.tldr: Prismata is presented, a defense enforcing contextual least privilege for web agents, constraining both what the agent sees and what it can do, and substantially reduces attack success while preserving benign task utility.

2609.04495.title: Rethinking Indirect Prompt Injection as a Test-Time Search Problem
2609.04495.tldr: This work identifies the attacker's adaptive search over the system attack surfaces as an important and underexplored security risk for tool-using agents and suggests that agentic security evaluations should characterize both the attacker's search procedure and compute budget.

2609.02127.title: Stored Is Not Supported: Typed Provenance and Assertion Guardrails for Persistent AI Agents
2609.02127.tldr: This work specifies typed provenance and assertion guardrails for autobiographical assertion boundedness, a system-relative release property requiring governed statements about the agent, user, or named relationships to satisfy accepted-evidence, temporal-validity, and disclosure policies, and proves a conditional assertion-boundedness contract.

2602.13597.title: AlignSentinel: Alignment-Aware Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
2602.13597.tldr: This work introduces AlignSentinel, a three-class classifier that leverages features derived from LLM's attention maps to categorize inputs accordingly and shows that AlignSentinel accurately detects inputs with misaligned instructions and substantially outperforms baselines.

2608.26423.title: The Latent Diagnostic Taxonomy: A Framework for Constructing Classifiers and Diagnosing Their Decisions, Applied to Prompt Injection Detection
2608.26423.tldr: Applying the framework to a classifier trained on a public prompt injection dataset, it is found that a substantial fraction of its confident decisions are not robust to removing a single token, and that this brittleness separates into two distinct failure patterns.

2608.23873.title: Semantic Overlays: Mitigating Prompt Injection with Annotations Beyond Tokens and Steering Vectors
2608.23873.tldr: This work introduces a general steering technique called Semantic Overlays: small learned adapters applied at chosen prefill positions to a frozen model's residual stream that defends against prompt injections that add instructions in untrusted context.

2608.16843.title: Security of Foundation-Model-Powered Embodied Agents: Attack Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation
2608.16843.tldr: This work presents a trust-boundary-centric survey of foundation-model-powered embodied-agent security, and shows that attack research is concentrated on multimodal perception and action interfaces, while defenses are especially concentrated on action-level and runtime protection.

2602.22724.title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification
2602.22724.tldr: This work proposes AgentSentry, a novel inference-time detection and mitigation framework for tool-augmented LLM agents that is the first inference-time defense to model multi-turn IPI as a temporal causal takeover and eliminates successful attacks and maintains strong utility under attack.

2608.01358.title: HopRefusalBench: Diagnosing Refusal Failures in Search-Augmented Agents for Multi-Hop Reasoning
2608.01358.tldr: This work introduces HopRefusalBench, the first controlled benchmark of refusal within multi-hop search, and proposes a final-outcome taxonomy spanning target-aware refusal, pseudo-refusal, hallucinated completion, and search-budget exhaustion, together with source-aware trajectory metrics for post-trigger continuation and token waste.

2608.20413.title: BioFirewall: A genome-writing-native governance layer for design-stage biosecurity screening of agentic AI
2608.20413.tldr: BioFirewall is presented, a rule-governed middleware that intercepts a genome-writing plan and returns allow, flag-for-review, or refuse across five hazard axes native to genome writing: cargo, locus, edit type, germline and scale, with cited evidence, a signed design passport, a tamper-evident audit log, and tiered access.

2608.08942.title: Same Question, Different Answer? Measuring and Mitigating Prompt Privilege for Equitable AI Access
2608.08942.tldr: This work introduces Prompt Equity Score (PES), a quantitative metric for evaluating performance consistency across user populations, and Prompt Equity Transformer (PET), an LLM-based agent that automatically transforms user requests into semantically equivalent, accessibility-oriented prompts while preserving their intent, to address accessibility disparities in LLM interactions.

2608.08795.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
2608.08795.tldr: SAVOR performs outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories collected from disjoint training environments, validates context-conditioned candidate strategies, and iteratively consolidates them into a reusable strategy memory that guides the generation of a single payload for each unseen target.

2608.08100.title: Defending Retrieval-Augmented Intrusion Detection Against Knowledge Poisoning and Prompt Injection
2608.08100.tldr: RAG-IDS is presented, a three-tier multi-agent intrusion detection framework with a retrieval-boundary defense combining soft trust scoring, label-embedding consistency checking (LECC), and prompt sanitization, designed to recover classification quality under retrieval-layer attack.

2608.07167.title: NiyamAI - An Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
2608.07167.tldr: NiyamAI is presented, an intent bound runtime guardrail architecture providing cryptographically verifiable execution integrity for autonomous agents and subjects its own enforcement mechanism to 18 adversarial vectors across six classes, disclosing two implementation vulnerabilities identified and remediated during development.

2608.06477.title: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.06477.tldr: This paper introduces multi-step indirect prompt injection, a new attack class against CUAs in which the adversarial goal is decomposed into multiple innocuous-looking sub-steps and distributed across a chain of pages referenced along the agent's navigation path.

2608.05715.title: Hijacking Robots with a Piece of Paper: A Systematic Study of Physical Prompt Injection in VLM-Controlled Robots
2608.05715.tldr: This work presents a systematic study of physical prompt injection attacks against VLM-controlled sorting, introducing a four-category taxonomy, indirect signage, task redefinition, authority impersonation, and conflict injection, instantiated as a benchmark.

2608.04053.title: AgentAntibody: An Adaptive Immune System for Defending LLM Agents against Prompt Injection
2608.04053.tldr: Inspired by adaptive immunity, AgentAntibody is proposed, which equips LLM agents with a self-evolving immune system against prompt injection, and outperforms existing defenses in preventing harmful actions while preserving legitimate task completion, even when the harmful and legitimate actions are both compatible with the stated task.

2605.03378.title: ARGUS: Defending LLM Agents Against Context-Aware Prompt Injection
2605.03378.tldr: ARGUS, a causal-provenance auditor for LLM agents that verifies whether each proposed action has a complete benign causal justification, is proposed and presented, significantly outperforming existing defenses in the security-utility tradeoff.

2608.02018.title: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
2608.02018.tldr: I-Bench, a collection of seemingly harmless adversarial tasks targeting confidentiality and integrity attacks across three platforms, and HITLCUA, a comprehensive adversarial testing framework that integrates a real virtual machine operating system environment with isolated Docker-based web platforms, and simulates human participation by allowing CUAs to consult an API-simulated user before proceeding with suspicious operations.

2608.00747.title: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems
2608.00747.tldr: This first study that systematically investigates prompt injection attacks in a multi-agent LLM-based robotic system finds that attacks can propagate from one agent to others through shared prompt structures, with impacts varying depending on prompt composition and the targeted agent.

2603.03633.title: Goal-Driven Risk Assessment for LLM-Powered Systems: A Healthcare Case Study
2603.03633.tldr: This study harmonizes the state-of-the-art attacks to LLMs with conventional ones and presents possible attack paths applicable to similar systems and advances the secure-by-design practices in LLM-based systems.
2603.03633.venue: 2025 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference Workshops (ACSAC Workshops)

2607.28165.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents
2607.28165.tldr: This paper constructs AudioAgentSecurity, the first comprehensive benchmark for audio instruction injection attacks, encompassing 8 real-world task scenarios and 10 distinct attack patterns, and introduces Cascaded Audio Decoupling and Verification (CADV), a defense mechanism based on source separation and consistency analysis.

2607.24174.title: Just Testing, Move Along: Evasion of LLM-based System Log Interpretation by Prompt Injection
2607.24174.tldr: This paper presents a framework for evaluating prompt injection attacks against LLM-based log interpretation using log traces generated during real cyber attacks, and creates adversarial examples through generic injection generation, refinement, and attack-specific optimization.

2609.20188.title: ResumeShield: Channel Separation and an Open Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in AI Resume Screening

2608.14629.title: Inference-Time Mitigation of Adversarial Political Bias in Large Language Models
2608.14629.tldr: The proposed Recursive Self-Correction approach raises model performance from a Political Neutrality Likert scale baseline of 2.14 to 4.56, averaged across all models, demonstrating effective inference-time mitigation of political bias in LLM-generated summaries.

2607.21824.title: Protocol-Level Attacks on Agentic Commerce Platforms: A Cross-Platform Taxonomy, AIP-Bench, and Unified Defense
2607.21824.tldr: It is shown that the more consequential risks lie one layer down, in the protocol between agents and commerce services, and a platform-agnostic defense that drives the structural attack-success rate to zero for four of the five structural classes.

2607.18847.title: Data Leakage Prevention in Agentic Applications via Preemptive Hardening
2607.18847.tldr: The resulting modifications of application code were shown to eliminate leaks when targeted by basic jailbreak and instruction-override attacks, achieving a 100% reduction in leakage, and reduce leaks by 91% under conditions of stress-induced manipulation, without the need of continuous runtime policy enforcement.

2607.18622.title: CPInj: Uncovering Prompt Injection Risks in Textual Collaborative Prompt Optimization
2607.18622.tldr: A Collaborative Prompt Injection attack that contaminates the aggregated global prompt with malicious instructions, degrades downstream task performance, resists purification by prompt optimization on benign clients, and evades advanced detection-based defenses on the server is proposed.

2607.13987.title: Agent Skill Security: Threat Models, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation
2607.13987.tldr: SkillSec-Eval is presented, a lifecycle-aware framework for systematically evaluating the security of reusable agent skills and demonstrates that vulnerabilities arise at multiple lifecycle stages beyond execution, highlighting the need for lifecycle-aware security analysis of reusable agent skills.

2607.12624.title: PVDetector: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks on Purpose-Specific LLM Agents through Policy-Violation Concept Analysis
2607.12624.tldr: PVDetector is proposed, a training-free framework that detects PI attacks during LLM inference by measuring hidden-state alignment with PV concepts, which are derived offline from the contrastive pairs of policy-violating and policy-compliant prompts.

2607.13081.title: SingGuard-NSFA: Extensible Guardrails for Agentic AI via Generative Reasoning and Real-Time Classification
2607.13081.tldr: Results demonstrate the extensibility of the approach and its generality as a plug-in enhancement and ablation experiments show that classification heads can equip a guardrail with risk detection capabilities beyond its original scope and achieve state-of-the-art performance.

2607.10490.title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations
2607.10490.tldr: The findings show that network-operation agents need execution-time authorization boundaries alongside prompt-level instruction hygiene, and that network-operation agents need execution-time authorization boundaries alongside prompt-level instruction hygiene.

2607.10080.title: The Effect of Multi-Lingual and Keyword Adversarial Injection on LLM Relevance Judgment
2607.10080.tldr: This work investigates the impact of cross-lingual prompt injection attacks on LLM-based relevance judgments using TREC Deep Learning collections and two open-weight models under established prompting frameworks, and demonstrates that multilingual query-based injections are highly effective in inflating relevance scores while simultaneously evading existing prompt-injection defenses.

2607.03821.title: DualView: Preventing Indirect Prompt Injection in Personal AI Agents
2607.03821.tldr: DualView deterministically prevents instructions in untrusted data from directly steering the agent's tool calls from directly steering the agent's tool calls; this guarantee does not depend on recognizing the evaluated attack templates.

2607.19396.title: CrackedPDFs: A Controlled Benchmark for Hidden Prompt Injection in PDFs
2607.19396.tldr: Results show that document-aware hybrid detection is useful under controlled paired evaluation and structural-only learned models are weak under paired controls, but they do not show broad real-world robustness or reliable cross-family generalization.

2606.29602.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models Across Multilingual and Obfuscated Attack Scenarios
2606.29602.tldr: An empirical evaluation of six state-of-the-art LLMs under diverse adversarial prompt scenarios, including direct and multi-stage obfuscated attacks across multiple languages and character encodings reveals systematic vulnerabilities across all tested models.
2606.29602.venue: 2026 21st European Dependable Computing Conference Companion Proceedings (EDCC-C)

2606.28649.title: RIPA: Sensory-Vector Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Controlled ROS 2 Robots
2606.28649.tldr: RIPA is the first systematic multi-channel empirical study of prompt injection attacks delivered through the sensory pipeline of a ROS 2-based LLM-controlled robotic system, and proposes a hybrid semantic firewall that achieves 0% ASR against known injection patterns with no false positives on a preliminary benign set.

2605.30534.title: Strengthening Polymorphic Prompt Assembling: Dynamic Separator Generation Against Emerging Prompt Injection Attacks
2605.30534.tldr: A dynamic per-request separator generation using domain-separated SHA-256 digests keyed on the timestamp, session identifier, and cryptographic nonce is proposed, thereby limiting leakage exposure to a single request.

2606.27567.title: On the Inseparability of Instructions and Data in Shared-Embedding Sequence Models
2606.27567.tldr: This work formalizes prompted systems as Prompted Action Models whose outputs include control-authoritative actions: refusal decisions, tool authorization, policy routing, and memory writes, and defines Semantic-Faithful Control (SFC), the property that such behavior depends only on the meaning of untrusted input, not on how it is encoded.

2606.27287.title: Prompt Injection in Automated Résumé Screening with Large Language Models: Single and Multi-Injection Settings
2606.27287.tldr: Overall, LLM-based screening is most vulnerable when manipulation is rare and candidate quality differences are small, but prompt injection is less effective on average, but can occasionally allow lower-quality candidates to outrank higher-quality ones, raising fairness concerns.
2606.27287.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.26793.title: MIRROR: Novelty-Constrained Memory-Guided MCTS Red-Teaming for Agentic RAG
2606.26793.tldr: MIRROR is presented, a unified cross-surface framework that performs memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search while conditioning candidate generation on retrieved context under an explicit novelty constraint, allowing retrieval to inform search priors without enabling prompt copying.

2606.26479.title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
2606.26479.tldr: This work organizes out-of-band defenses as instances of classical integrity protection, reference monitoring, and least privilege, yielding a structured comparison of what they do and do not cover, consistent with, but not established, the hypothesis that deterministic out-of-band enforcement is a harder target for an adaptive attacker than in-band detection.

2606.22864.title: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
2606.22864.tldr: It is argued, on a single-backbone cautionary case study (Qwen2.5-VL-7B on Mind2Web, teacher-forced replay), that a high probing AUC on a clean-vs-attack split is not, on its own, evidence of malicious-content detection.

2606.19660.title: A Layered Security Framework Against Prompt Injection in RAG-Based Chatbots
2606.19660.tldr: A three-layer framework that intercepts both direct and indirect prompt injection throughout the inference pipeline and reduces Attack Success Rate from 71.4\% to 11.3\%, outperforming the best single-layer baseline by 27.3 percentage points and a published guardrail system by 23.8 percentage points.

2606.20746.title: Amplify, Don't Create: Temporal Accumulation for Slow-Burn Prompt Injection
2606.20746.tldr: This work tests whether a proxy-side temporal accumulator recovers this slow-burn signal by reducing frozen per-event scores to peak and CUSUM persistence statistics, and contributes a pseudo-replication warning and an independence-audit standard for agent-benchmark evaluation.

2603.11875.title: The Mirror Design Pattern: Strict Data Geometry over Model Scale for Prompt Injection Detection

2602.11247.title: Peak + Accumulation: A Proxy-Level Scoring Formula for Multi-Turn LLM Attack Detection
2602.11247.tldr: This work proposes peak + accumulation scoring -- a formula combining peak single-turn risk, persistence ratio, and category diversity that achieves 90.8% recall at 1.4, where recall jumps 12 percentage points with negligible FPR increase.

2606.18550.title: The Gate Is Only as Honest as Its Contracts: ContractGuard for the Contract Layer of Risk-Aware Causal Gating
2606.18550.tldr: ContractGuard is introduced, a verifier between the registry and the gate that layers signed provenance, typed contract attestation, and runtime effect verification that restores injection success to zero against every modeled attack without over-rejecting honest contracts.

2606.17114.title: An Evaluation of Data Leakage Risks in Tool-Using LLM Agents in Realistic Scenarios
2606.17114.tldr: A joint evaluation by the Singapore AI Safety Institute and the Korea AI Safety Institute examining agent data leakage in 12 realistic, non-adversarial tasks spanning customer support, DevOps, web automation, and enterprise and personal productivity indicates that operational data leakage is a first-order agent-safety concern distinct from adversarial exfiltration.

2606.12737.title: PI-Hunter: Automated Red-Teaming for Exposing and Localizing Prompt Injections
2606.12737.tldr: PI-Hunter, an automated agentic auditing framework for proactive vulnerability exposure in LLM agents, is proposed and demonstrated that PI-Hunter substantially improves vulnerability exposure and attack-surface coverage over strong automated red-teaming baselines, while remaining effective under existing prompt injection defenses.

2602.07918.title: CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution
2602.07918.tldr: CausalArmor is proposed, a selective defense framework that computes lightweight, leave-one-out ablation-based attributions at privileged decision points, and triggers targeted sanitization only when an untrusted segment dominates the user intent.

2606.12709.title: Smarter Saboteurs, Better Fixers: Scaling & Security in Linear Multi-Agent Workflows
2606.12709.tldr: The authors' experiments across scales of two open-weight model families on the HumanEval benchmark reveal a compliance-correction symmetry, demonstrating that strictly linear collaboration structures can be viable and resilient to adversaries at this scale and suggesting that the brittleness previously attributed to linear topology may stem from a lack of correction.

2606.10860.title: Training LLMs to Enforce Multi-Level Instruction Hierarchies via Gravity-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization
2606.10860.tldr: Gravity-Weighted DPO (GW-DPO) is introduced, a preference-optimization objective whose per-sample offset scales with the structural distance between conflicting levels under a linear or bilateral schedule, the latter weighting severity by both the privilege gap and the privilege of the victim level.

2606.09315.title: Brain-Prompt Injection: A Route-Safety Audit for BCI-LLM Agents
2606.09315.tldr: A Route-Safety Audit Contract is defined: a minimal log schema, denominator hierarchy, and endpoint specification, and an audit-schema separation theorem together with a C3 attacked-dependence decomposition is proved together with a C3 attacked-dependence decomposition.

2606.09204.title: The Injection Paradox: Brand-Level Suppression in Safety-Trained LLM Recommendations via RAG Context Injection

2605.30686.title: Depth-Dependent Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Calling ReAct Agents: Injection Depth, Payload Framing, and Turn-Budget Sensitivity
2605.30686.tldr: The results establish injection depth as the dominant variable and show that sanitising only the first tool observation captures 67% of measured injection successes.

2605.30677.title: Investigating Detection and Obfuscation of Prompt Injection Attacks Against Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents
2605.30677.tldr: Defensive tactics for detecting the presences of prompt injection strings in the decompiler output of adversarial example programs are demonstrated and methods for obfuscating these attacks are explored.

2605.30189.title: Token-Level Generalization in LoRA Adapter Backdoors: Attack Characterization and Behavioral Detection
2605.30189.tldr: It is shown that LoRA adapters, the dominant distribution format for fine-tuned LLMs, can be reliably backdoored through training data poisoning while preserving baseline task performance and Behavioral detection is the operationally portable result for adapter supply chain scanning.

2603.00991.title: Tracking Capabilities for Safer Agents
2603.00991.tldr: This work proposes to put the agent in a programming-language-based “safety harness”: instead of calling tools directly, agents express their intentions as code in a capability-safe language, Scala 3 with capture checking.

2605.26595.title: Cordyceps: Covert Control Attacks on LLMs via Data Poisoning
2605.26595.tldr: A data poisoning method is proposed that teaches an LLM an information hiding scheme reliably and stealthily through semantic associations between shared knowledge such as facts or concepts and attacker-chosen phrases, thus revealing a new and subtle poisoning-induced vulnerability: covert control attacks.

2605.25415.title: LLM-as-a-Reviewer: Benchmarking Their Ability, Divergence, and Prompt Injection Resistance as Paper Reviewers
2605.25415.tldr: It is found that LLM-as-a-Reviewer systematically overrate weaker submissions and diverge from humans in topical emphasis, under-flagging Clarity and over-flagging Reproducibility, while producing reviews two to three times longer with lower lexical diversity and a more standardized vocabulary.

2605.23196.title: Prompt Overflow: What the Guardrail Inspects Is Not What the Model Infers
2605.23196.tldr: It is demonstrated that prompts reliably detected in short-context settings can evade guardrail models once adversarially manipulated into over-length inputs, yet remain fully actionable by downstream LLMs.

2605.24421.title: Poisoning the Watchtower: Prompt Injection Attacks Against LLM-Augmented Security Operations Through Adversarial Log Content
2605.24421.tldr: The results suggest that SOC copilots should treat raw log content as adversarial input rather than ordinary analyst context, and that simulation substantially mispredicts current model behavior, especially for direct overrides.

2605.19159.title: On the Geometric Limits of Transformer Defenses against Obfuscation Attacks: Latent Embedding Collapse & Performance Robustness Gap
2605.19159.tldr: The findings show that increasing model capacity does not eliminate latent embedding collapse, motivating geometry-aware robustness analysis as a necessary complement to performance-based evaluation for prompt-injection defenses.

2605.17163.title: STRIDE-AI: A Threat Modeling Framework for Generative AI Security Assessment
2605.17163.tldr: A framework that bridges the gap between high-level risk standards (NIST AI RMF) and technical vulnerability taxonomies (OWASP LLM Top 10) and introduces a threat modeling adaptation of classical STRIDE for AI systems, which successfully reduces the attack success rate in a sandbox case study.

2605.13631.title: ProjGuard: Safety Monitoring for Computer-Use Agents via Low-Dimensional Projections
2605.13631.tldr: Results support a hierarchical safety strategy in which always-on monitoring anticipates deviations and activates correction only when needed, and show that monitoring with on-demand correction reduces the unsafe rate while improving task completion.

2605.11868.title: IPI-proxy: An Intercepting Proxy for Red-Teaming Web-Browsing AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
2605.11868.tldr: By bridging static benchmarks and live deployment, IPI-proxy gives AI security teams a reproducible substrate for measuring and hardening web-browsing agents against indirect prompt injection on the same retrieval surface attackers exploit in production.

2605.10862.title: RUBEN: Rule-Based Explanations for Retrieval-Augmented LLM Systems
2605.10862.venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering

2605.11026.title: AgentShield: Deception-based Compromise Detection for Tool-using LLM Agents
2605.11026.tldr: AgentShield is a deception-based detection framework that places three layers of traps inside the agent's tool interface: fake tools, fake credentials, and allowlisted parameters that serve as high-precision labels for a self-supervised classifier.

2605.07269.title: MIPIAD: Multilingual Indirect Prompt Injection Attack Defense with Qwen -- TF-IDF Hybrid and Meta-Ensemble Learning
2605.07269.tldr: MIPIAD is presented, a defense framework evaluated on English and Bangla that combines a sequence classifier fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-1.5B via LoRA, TF-IDF lexical features, and validation-tuned ensembling through late fusion, stacking, and gradient boosting.

2605.05260.title: SecureMCP: A Policy-Enforced LLM Data Access Framework for AIoT Systems via Model Context Protocol
2605.05260.tldr: This paper proposes SecureMCP, a policy-enforced LLM data access framework integrating Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with an MCP server to establish multi-layer defense for LLM-generated SQL execution.

2502.12520.title: SafeEraser: Enhancing Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models through Multimodal Machine Unlearning
2502.12520.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that combining PD Loss with existing unlearning methods can effectively prevent over-forgetting and achieve a decrease of 79.5% in the SARR metric of LLaVA-7B and LLaVA-13B, while maintaining forget quality and model utility.
2502.12520.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.01143.title: A Low-Latency Fraud Detection Layer for Detecting Adversarial Interaction Patterns in LLM-Powered Agents
2605.01143.tldr: This work proposes a complementary defense mechanism: a low-latency fraud detection layer for detecting adversarial interaction patterns in LLM-powered agents and suggests that interaction-level behavioral detection should become a core component of deployment-time defense for LLM-powered agents.

2602.07104.title: Extended to Reality: Prompt Injection in 3D Environments
2602.07104.tldr: PI3D is introduced, a prompt injection attack against MLLMs in 3D environments, realized through text-bearing object placement rather than digital image edits, which demonstrates that PI3D is an effective attack against multiple MLLMs under diverse camera trajectories.

2604.28129.title: Latent Adversarial Detection: Adaptive Probing of LLM Activations for Multi-Turn Attack Detection
2604.28129.tldr: It is established that three-phase turn-level labels unique to the authors' synthetic dataset are essential: binary conversation-level labels produce 50-59% false positives.

2604.27202.title: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Prevalence, Techniques, and Objectives
2604.27202.tldr: A large-scale empirical analyses of indirect prompt injections in webpages and HTTP responses is presented, revealing a heterogeneous ecosystem spanning disruptive prompts, reputation manipulation, content-protection directives, and AI-bot detection, targeting systems such as crawlers, search pipelines, customer-support agents, and hiring workflows.

2605.00706.title: FinSafetyBench: Evaluating LLM Safety in Real-World Financial Scenarios
2605.00706.tldr: FinSafetyBench is proposed, a bilingual (English-Chinese) red-teaming benchmark designed to test an LLM's refusal of requests that violate financial compliance, and critical vulnerabilities are identified that allow adversarial prompts to bypass compliance safeguards.
2605.00706.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.18248.title: Beyond Pattern Matching: Seven Cross-Domain Techniques for Prompt Injection Detection
2604.18248.tldr: This work proposes seven detection techniques that each port a mechanism from a discipline outside LLM security: forensic linguistics, materials-science fatigue analysis, deception technology, local-sequence alignment from bioinformatics, mechanism design, spectral signal analysis, and taint tracking.

2508.14927.title: AI Testing Should Account for Sophisticated Strategic Behaviour
2508.14927.tldr: This position paper argues for two claims regarding AI testing and evaluation: first, to remain informative about deployment behaviour, evaluations need account for the possibility that AI systems understand their circumstances and reason strategically and second, game-theoretic analysis can inform evaluation design by formalising and scrutinising the reasoning in evaluation-based safety cases.

2604.15368.title: LogJack: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Cloud Logs Against LLM Debugging Agents
2604.15368.tldr: This work presents LogJack, a benchmark of 42 payloads across 5 cloud log categories, and evaluates 8 foundation models under 3 prompt conditions with 5 independent trials each, observing a novel "sanitize and execute"behavior where a model detects and removes an obvious malicious component but still executes the remaining injected command.

2604.10134.title: PlanGuard: Defending Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection via Planning-based Consistency Verification
2604.10134.tldr: This paper proposes PlanGuard, a training-free defense framework based on the principle of Context Isolation that introduces an isolated Planner that generates a reference set of valid actions derived solely from user instructions and designs a Hierarchical Verification Mechanism that first enforces strict hard constraints to block unauthorized tool invocations, and subsequently employs an Intent Verifier to validate whether parameter deviations are benign formatting variances or malicious hijacking.

2606.29239.title: QuantGuard: Learnable Rounding for Repairing Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in LLMs
2606.29239.tldr: QuantGuard is proposed, a proactive pre-quantization defense that learns safe rounding adjustments through differentiable optimization and disrupts the alignment between attacker-crafted weight patterns and quantization boundaries, suppressing post-quantization backdoor activation while preserving model functionality and performance.

2606.28962.title: FlipGuard: Defending Large Language Models Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks
2606.28962.tldr: FlipGuard is introduced, a proactive defense framework that selectively perturbs model weights prior to quantization, and the Defense Effectiveness Ratio (DER) is proposed, a unified metric to jointly evaluate security gains, utility preservation, and computational cost.

2604.03598.title: AttackEval: A Systematic Empirical Study of Prompt Injection Attack Effectiveness Against Large Language Models
2604.03598.tldr: AttackEval, a systematic empirical study of prompt injection attack effectiveness, identifies concrete blind spots in current defenses and provides actionable guidance for designing more robust LLM safety systems.

2603.29418.title: Covert Visual Prompt Injection against Commercial Multimodal Large Language Models
2603.29418.tldr: This work adaptively embeds the malicious prompt into the input image via a bounded text overlay to provide semantic guidance and iteratively optimized the feature representation of the attacked image with those of the malicious visual and textual targets at both coarse- and fine-grained levels.

2603.28013.title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Model Safety Tiers
2603.28013.tldr: A kill-chain canary methodology that tracks a cryptographic token through four stages across 950 runs, five frontier LLMs, six attack surfaces, and five defense conditions, and results reframe prompt injection as a pipeline-architecture problem.

2605.06669.title: Evaluating Prompt Injection Defenses for Educational LLM Tutors: Security-Usability-Latency Trade-offs
2605.06669.tldr: A reproducible benchmark protocol for head-to-head comparison under identical conditions, including stratified bootstrap confidence intervals, paired McNemar significance tests, multi-seed sensitivity sweeps, and direct evaluation of Prompt Guard and NeMo Guardrails on the same split with unified instrumentation is provided.

2603.25164.title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
2603.25164.tldr: P-Attack is proposed, a novel compound attack that integrates prompt injection with database poisoning in RAG and improves attack success rates by 4% to 16% on open-domain QA tasks while maintaining high retrieval precision, proving that the compound attack strategy is both necessary and highly effective.

2603.23791.title: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
2603.23791.tldr: The Cognitive Firewall is presented, a three-stage split-compute architecture that distributes security checks across the client and the cloud and indicates that deterministic enforcement at the execution boundary can complement probabilistic language models, and that split-compute provides a practical foundation for securing interactive LLM agents.

2602.22450.title: Silent Egress: When Implicit Prompt Injection Makes LLM Agents Leak Without a Trace
2602.22450.tldr: It is demonstrated that a malicious web page can induce an agent to issue outbound requests that exfiltrate sensitive runtime context, even when the final response shown to the user appears harmless, suggesting that network egress should be treated as a first-class security outcome in agentic LLM systems.
2602.22450.venue: IEEE International Conference on Electro/Information Technology

2603.21642.title: Are AI-assisted Development Tools Immune to Prompt Injection?
2603.21642.tldr: This work presents the first empirical analysis of prompt injection with the tool-poisoning vulnerability across seven widely used MCP clients and provides actionable guidance for MCP implementers and the software engineering community seeking to build secure AI-assisted development workflows.

2603.20976.title: Detection of adversarial intent in Human-AI teams using LLMs
2603.20976.tldr: It is found that LLMs are capable of identifying malicious behavior in real-time, and without task-specific information, indicating the potential for task-agnostic defense and suggesting the introduction of LLM defenders could render human teams more robust to certain classes of attack.

2603.19423.title: The Autonomy Tax: Defense Training Breaks LLM Agents
2603.19423.tldr: These findings demonstrate that current defense paradigms optimize for single-turn refusal benchmarks while rendering multi-step agents fundamentally unreliable, necessitating new approaches that preserve tool execution competence under adversarial conditions.

2606.28739.title: Agent Safety Is Action Alignment
2606.28739.tldr: It is concluded that action safety cannot be installed in weights and must be expressed as the least privilege, enforced outside the model at the action boundary, and evaluated as action alignment (a relational, deployment-conditioned property) rather than a refusal score.

2603.13424.title: Agent Privilege Separation in OpenClaw: A Structural Defense Against Prompt Injection
2603.13424.tldr: This proposed defense combines two mechanisms: agent isolation, implemented as a privilege separated two-agent pipeline with tool partitioning, and JSON formatting, which produces structured output that strips persuasive framing before the action agent processes it.

2603.11331.title: Jailbreak Scaling Laws for Large Language Models: Polynomial-Exponential Crossover
2603.11331.tldr: A theoretical generative model of proxy language in terms of a spin-glass system operating in a replica-symmetry-breaking regime, where generations are drawn from the associated Gibbs measure and a subset of low-energy, size-biased clusters is designated unsafe is proposed.

2603.07708.title: VoiceSHIELD-Small: Real-Time Malicious Speech Detection and Transcription
2603.07708.tldr: This paper introduces VoiceSHIELD-Small, a lightweight model that works in real time that can transcribe speech and detect whether it is safe or harmful, all in one step, built on OpenAI's Whisper-small encoder.

2603.07191.title: Governance Architecture for Autonomous Agent Systems: Threats, Framework, and Engineering Practice
2603.07191.tldr: The Layered Governance Architecture (LGA), a four-layer framework comprising execution sandboxing, intent verification, zero-trust inter-agent authorization, and immutable audit logging, is proposed and generalization to the external InjecAgent benchmark yields 99-100% interception, confirming robustness beyond the authors' synthetic data.

2603.03919.title: When Safety Becomes a Vulnerability: Exploiting LLM Alignment Homogeneity for Transferable Blocking in RAG
2603.03919.tldr: This work proposes TabooRAG, which optimizes one document per query for retrieval and refusal induction in a surrogate RAG environment, then transfers it to an unknown target system, and constructs query-relevant risk context to trigger alignment-driven refusal.

2602.19021.title: Trustworthy AI LLM Scalability Risk Index (LSRI): A Cybersecurity Framework Assessing Agentic-AI Security & Software Model Supply Chain Safety Boosting AI-Generated Malware Defense & Explainability Mitigating Emerging Risks of Generative AI
2602.19021.tldr: The LLM Scalability Risk Index (LSRI), a parametric framework and cybersecurity standard for stress-testing autonomous orchestration pipelines and providing scalable API defense, safer agentic orchestration under heavy cloud workloads, stronger polymorphic malware detection, automated red-teaming, and improved system explainability is introduced.

2602.18514.title: Trojan Horses in Recruiting: A Red-Teaming Case Study on Indirect Prompt Injection in Standard vs. Reasoning Models
2602.18514.tldr: This study highlights a failure mode where the cognitive load of processing complex adversarial instructions causes the injection logic to be unintentionally printed in the final output, rendering the attack more detectable by humans than in Standard Models.

2602.14161.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift
2602.14161.tldr: This work trains activation-based classifiers on a benchmark of 18 datasets and proposes Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) evaluation, where the held-out dataset is never seen during training, and shows LODO-weighted SAE attributions filter dataset artifacts for more reliable per-prompt explanations.

2602.09222.title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
2602.09222.tldr: This work presents MUZZLE, an automated agentic framework for evaluating the security of web agents against indirect prompt injection attacks, and demonstrates its ability to automatically and adaptively assess the security of web agents with minimal human intervention.

2602.06268.title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
2602.06268.tldr: Evaluating MPIB across a diverse set of baseline LLMs and defense configurations, it is found that ASR and CHER can diverge substantially, and that observed rates vary depending on whether adversarial instructions appear in the user query or in retrieved context.

2602.05484.title: Clouding the Mirror: Stealthy Prompt Injection Attacks Targeting LLM-based Phishing Detection
2602.05484.tldr: This paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of PI against multimodal LLM-based phishing detection and proposes InjectDefuser, a defense framework that combines prompt hardening, allowlist-based retrieval augmentation, and output validation that significantly reduces attack success rates.

2602.04653.title: Inference-Time Backdoors via Chat Templates: From LLM Supply Chains to Agentic System Compromise
2602.04653.tldr: This work shows that an adversary who distributes a model with a maliciously modified template can implant an inference-time backdoor without modifying model weights, poisoning training data, or controlling runtime infrastructure, and establishes chat templates as a reliable and undefended attack in the open-weight AI supply chain.

2601.12449.title: AgenTRIM: Tool Risk Mitigation for Agentic AI
2601.12449.tldr: AgenTRIM is introduced, a framework for detecting and mitigating tool-driven agency risks without altering an agent's internal reasoning that provides a practical, capability-preserving approach to safer tool use in LLM-based agents.

2602.00750.title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
2602.00750.tldr: A multi-probe evasion attack that appends an adversarially optimised suffix to poisoned inputs, jointly optimising a universal suffix to simultaneously fool all layer-wise drift detectors while preserving the effectiveness of the underlying injection.

2601.17911.title: Prompt Injection Evaluations: Refusal Boundary Instability and Artifact-Dependent Compliance in GPT-4-Series Models

2601.17549.title: Breaking the Protocol: Security Analysis of the Model Context Protocol Specification and Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
2601.17549.tldr: The first rigorous security analysis of MCP's architectural design is presented, identifying three fundamental protocol-level vulnerabilities, establishing that MCP's security weaknesses are architectural rather than implementation-specific, requiring protocol-level remediation.

2601.17548.title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic Coding Assistants: A Systematic Analysis of Vulnerabilities in Skills, Tools, and Protocol Ecosystems
2601.17548.tldr: A unified taxonomy bridging disparate attack classifications, the first systematic analysis of skill-based architecture vulnerabilities with concrete exploit chains, and a defense-in-depth framework grounded in the limitations are contributed.

2606.10904.title: When the Defense Writes the Refusal: Auditing Keyword-Scored Evaluation of Inference-Time Defenses for Multimodal Large Language Models
2606.10904.tldr: An audit of a defense-evaluator interaction that invalidates keyword-scored comparison of prompt-based inference-time MLLM defenses and formalizes the audit with three claim-admissibility levels under which three of seven planned benchmark branches are excluded.

2601.13186.title: Prompt Injection Mitigation with Agentic AI, Nested Learning, and AI Sustainability via Semantic Caching
2601.13186.tldr: Results indicate that observability-aware evaluation can reveal non-monotonic effects within multi-agent pipelines and that memory-augmented agents can jointly maximize security robustness, real-time performance, operational cost savings, and environmental sustainability without modifying underlying model weights.

2601.10923.title: Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG
2601.10923.tldr: OpenRAG-Soc is introduced, a compact, reproducible benchmark and harness for evaluating web-facing RAG pipelines under these threats as a discrete data package that standardizes end-to-end evaluation from ingestion to generation and reports attack success at answer time, rank shifts in both sparse and dense retrievers, as well as utility and latency.

2601.07072.title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
2601.07072.tldr: This work designs an efficient and effective black-box attack algorithm that constructs a compact trigger fragment to guarantee retrieval for any attack fragment and presents the first end-to-end IPI exploits under natural queries and realistic external corpora, spanning both RAG and agentic systems with diverse attack objectives.

2601.05755.title: VIGIL: Defending LLM Agents Against Tool Stream Injection via Verify-Before-Commit
2601.05755.tldr: This work proposes VIGIL, a framework that shifts the paradigm from restrictive isolation to a verify-before-commit protocol that outperforms state-of-the-art dynamic defenses by reducing the attack success rate by over 22\% while more than doubling the utility under attack compared to static baselines, thereby achieving an optimal balance between security and utility.
2601.05755.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.04795.title: Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Result Parsing
2601.04795.tldr: A novel method is proposed that provides LLMs with precise data via tool result parsing while effectively filtering out injected malicious code, achieving competitive Utility under Attack (UA) while maintaining the lowest Attack Success Rate (ASR) to date, significantly outperforming existing methods.

2512.23684.title: Multilingual Hidden Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Academic Reviewing
2512.23684.tldr: It is found that prompt injection induces substantial changes in review scores and accept/reject decisions for English, Japanese, and Chinese injections, while Arabic injections produce little to no effect.

2512.23557.title: Toward Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Multimodal Framework for Preventing Prompt Injection Attacks
2512.23557.tldr: A Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenanc- Aware Defense Framework whereby all the prompts, either user-generated or produced by upstream agents, are sanitized and all the outputs generated by an LLM are verified independently before being sent to downstream nodes.

2512.23132.title: Multi-Agent Framework for Threat Mitigation and Resilience in AI-Based Systems
2512.23132.tldr: Adaptive, ML-specific security frameworks, combining dependency hygiene, threat intelligence, and monitoring, are essential to mitigate supply-chain and inference risks across the ML lifecycle.

2604.01108.title: Adversarial Moral Stress Testing of Large Language Models
2604.01108.tldr: Adversarial Moral Stress Testing (AMST) is introduced, a stress-based evaluation framework for assessing ethical robustness under adversarial multi-round interactions and provides a scalable and model-agnostic stress-testing methodology that enables robustness-aware evaluation and monitoring of LLM-enabled software systems operating in adversarial environments.

2512.16307.title: Beyond the Benchmark: Innovative Defenses Against Prompt Injection Attacks
2512.16307.tldr: Assessing present prompt-based defenses against the latest attacks, introducing a new framework using a seed defense to refine the defense prompts iteratively, and showing significant improvements in detecting goal hijacking attacks.

2512.12583.title: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks Against Application Using Classifiers
2512.12583.tldr: This work curates and augments a prompt injection dataset based on the HackAPrompt Playground Submissions corpus and trains several classifiers, including LSTM, feed forward neural networks, Random Forest, and Naive Bayes to detect malicious prompts in LLM integrated web applications.

2512.06716.title: SIEVE: Selective Integrity Verification and Escalation for Defending LLM Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection
2512.06716.tldr: This work proposes SIEVE, which verifies tool transitions and argument sources against an Intent Graph, escalating actions that cannot pass deterministic verification to semantic adjudication, and evaluates SIEVE on AgentLure and AgentDojo against MELON, DRIFT, IPIGuard, and ARGUS.

2512.01326.title: Securing Large Language Models (LLMs) from Prompt Injection Attacks
2512.01326.tldr: This study evaluates the robustness of JATMO against HOUYI, a genetic attack framework that systematically mutates and optimizes adversarial prompts and highlights both the promise and limitations of fine-tuning-based defenses and point toward the need for layered, adversarially informed mitigation strategies.

2511.20597.title: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
2511.20597.tldr: This work examines the landscape of prompt injection attacks and synthesizes a benchmark of attacks embedded in realistic HTML payloads, offering a blueprint for designing practical, secure web agents through a defense-in-depth approach.

2511.21752.title: Semantics as a Shield: Label Disguise Defense (LDD) against Prompt Injection in LLM Sentiment Classification
2511.21752.tldr: This study demonstrates that label semantics can serve as an effective defense layer, transforming meaning itself into a shield against prompt injection, and can identify more than one alias pair that achieves higher accuracy than the under-attack baseline.

2511.15759.title: Securing AI Agents Against Prompt Injection Attacks
2511.15759.tldr: This work presents a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating prompt injection risks in RAG-enabled AI agents and proposes a multi-layered defense framework, which reduces successful attack rates from 73.2% to 8.7% while maintaining 94% of baseline task performance.

2510.23675.title: QueryIPI: Query-agnostic Indirect Prompt Injection on Coding Agents
2510.23675.tldr: This work proposes query-agnostic IPI, a new attack paradigm that reliably executes malicious payloads under arbitrary user queries, and presents QueryIPI, an automated framework that uses tool descriptions as optimizable payloads and refines them via iterative, prompt-based blackbox optimization.

2511.12295.title: Privacy-Preserving Prompt Injection Detection for LLMs Using Federated Learning and Embedding-Based NLP Classification
2511.12295.tldr: A privacy-preserving prompt injection detection framework based on federated learning and embedding-based classification that preserves privacy by sharing only model parameters across clients, while achieving detection performance comparable to centralized training is proposed.

2511.05797.title: When AI Meets the Web: Prompt Injection Risks in Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugins
2511.05797.tldr: This first large-scale study of 17 third-party chatbot plugins used by over 1,000 public websites is presented, uncovering previously unknown prompt injection risks in practice and showing that many plugins adopt insecure practices that undermine the built-in LLM safeguards.
2511.05797.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2511.01634.title: Prompt Injection as an Emerging Threat: Evaluating the Resilience of Large Language Models
2511.01634.tldr: A unified framework for evaluating how resistant Large Language Models are to prompt injection attacks is proposed and it is demonstrated that alignment strength and safety tuning play a greater role in resilience than model size alone.

2511.00447.title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via Token-wise Representation Editing and Residual Instruction Fusion
2511.00447.tldr: To "de-instructionalize" data tokens, DRIP introduces a data curation and training paradigm with a lightweight representation-editing module that edits embeddings of instruction-like tokens in the data section, enhancing security without harming utility.

2510.19844.title: CourtGuard: A Local, Multiagent Prompt Injection Classifier
2510.19844.tldr: The proposed CourtGuard is a locally-runnable, multiagent prompt injection classifier, a court-like multiagent LLM system, where prompts are evaluated in a court-like multiagent LLM system, where a defense attorney argues the prompt is benign, a prosecution attorney argues the prompt is a prompt injection, and a judge gives the final classification.

2607.09236.title: Forget Narrowly, Retain Broadly: Unlearning as an Asymmetric Generalization Problem
2607.09236.tldr: JensUn++, an unlearning algorithm that achieves the best forget-retain utility trade-off across three LLMs, in both sequential and joint unlearning settings is introduced, showing that training data is as important as algorithmic design.

2605.00364.title: Unlearning What Matters: Token-Level Attribution for Precise Language Model Unlearning
2605.00364.tldr: This work proposes TokenUnlearn, a token-level attribution framework that identifies and selectively targets critical tokens, and develops two complementary strategies: hard selection, applying unlearning only to high-importance tokens, and soft weighting, modulating gradient contributions based on importance scores.

2604.23854.title: Does Machine Unlearning Preserve Clinical Safety? A Risk Analysis for Medical Image Classification
2604.23854.tldr: SalUn-CRA (Clinical Risk-Aware), a variant of SalUn that replaces random relabeling with entropy-based forgetting for malignant samples in the forget set, preventing the model from learning harmful benign associations is proposed.
2604.23854.venue: Anais do XXVI Simpósio Brasileiro de Computação Aplicada à Saúde (SBCAS 2026)

2512.03564.title: Towards Irreversible Machine Unlearning for Diffusion Models
2512.03564.tldr: A novel attack named Diffusion Model Relearning Attack (DiMRA) is proposed, which can reverse the finetuning-based machine unlearning methods, posing a significant vulnerability of this kind of technique.

2511.04228.title: REMIND: Input Loss Landscapes Reveal Residual Memorization in Post-Unlearning LLMs
2511.04228.tldr: REMIND (Residual Memorization In Neighborhood Dynamics), a novel evaluation method aiming to detect the subtle remaining influence of unlearned data and classify whether the data has been effectively forgotten, provides a reliable framework to assess unlearning in language models.

2509.24166.title: Stable Forgetting: Bounded Parameter-Efficient Unlearning in Foundation Models
2509.24166.tldr: This work proposes *Bounded Parameter-Efficient Unlearning*, which stabilizes LoRA-based fine-tuning by applying bounded functions to MLP adapters and controls the weight dynamics during ascent and enables reliable convergence.

2511.18444.title: SineProject: Machine Unlearning for Stable Vision Language Alignment
2511.18444.tldr: SineProject is introduced, a simple method that augments the frozen projector with sinusoidally modulated trainable parameters, improving the Jacobian's spectral conditioning and stabilizing alignment throughout unlearning, yielding state of the art forget retain trade offs with negligible computational overhead.

2509.22483.title: OFMU: Optimization-Driven Framework for Machine Unlearning
2509.22483.tldr: The proposed OFMU is a penalty-based bi-level optimization framework that explicitly prioritizes forgetting while preserving retention through a hierarchical structure and achieves better trade-offs between forgetting efficacy and model utility compared to prior methods.

2609.16305.title: BLINDSPOT: A Benchmark for Safety and Refusal Calibration in Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
2609.16305.tldr: Preliminary results reveal substantial differences in safety-utility calibration across models and show that failures can emerge only after several initially safe interaction steps, motivating treating agent safety as a trajectory-level property rather than a single-turn or binary success criterion.

2605.01913.title: RefusalGuard: Geometry-Preserving Fine-Tuning for Safety in LLMs
2605.01913.tldr: This work introduces REFUSALGUARD, a representation-level fine-tuning framework that preserves safety-relevant structure during model adaptation, and achieves attack success rates comparable to base safety-aligned models while maintaining competitive task performance, significantly outperforming baselines.

2406.12038.title: Soft Prompting for Unlearning in Large Language Models
2406.12038.tldr: The results indicate that SPUL can significantly improve the trade-off between utility and forgetting in the context of text classification and question answering with LLMs.
2406.12038.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.15152.title: Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models
2405.15152.tldr: This paper introduces a methodology to align LLMs, such as Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models, with ethical, privacy, and safety standards by leveraging the gradient ascent algorithm for knowledge unlearning, targeting harmful responses and copyrighted content.

2403.16246.title: Partially Blinded Unlearning: Class Unlearning for Deep Networks a Bayesian Perspective
2403.16246.tldr: Partially-Blinded Unlearning surpasses existing state-of-the-art class unlearning methods, demonstrating superior effectiveness and achieves this efficacy without requiring awareness of the entire training dataset but only to the unlearned data points.

2608.13345.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design
2608.13345.tldr: A stylized comparative-statics model that parameterizes safety design as a resource allocation alpha in [0,1] between these two approaches suggests that safety architecture decisions depend less on deployment scale per se than on the reliability of character shaping under distributional shift.

2608.11274.title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
2608.11274.tldr: The right unit of safety in agentic AI is the trajectory-with-checkable-evidence, not the model, and this work formalizes an Agent Trajectory Schema and Evidence Chain, state a compositional gating proposition based on standard monitor composition, and outline a research agenda.

2607.24866.title: The Missing Layer: Specification Infrastructure for AI Oversight
2607.24866.tldr: This work introduces CARMA, a Layer 2 prototype for autonomous ETL agents in which one specification drives enforcement, evaluation, and escalation, with every decision traceable to a versioned specification, naming what AI oversight is missing and giving independent teams principles to build the missing pieces so they compose.

2606.28294.title: Democratic ICAI: Debating Our Way to Steering Principles from Preferences
2606.28294.tldr: Democratic ICAI is introduced, a novel approach that gathers multiple competing rationales through structured persona debate, offering a broader and more expressive account of the factors influencing each comparison and improves average preference prediction across tasks relative to deliberative prompting and principle-based baselines.

2606.26057.title: The Unfireable Safety Kernel: Execution-Time AI Alignment for AI Agents and Other Escapable AI Systems
2606.26057.tldr: This work identifies four properties that an authorization mechanism must satisfy for architectural control rather than for cooperative requests: process separation, pre-action enforcement on a structurally only path, fail-closed at both the request and system levels, and externalized signed evidence verifiable outside the controlled system's trust boundary.

2608.28593.title: Statutory AI: Aligning Large Language Models With Legal Norms
2608.28593.tldr: This work proposes a hybrid approach called Statutory AI that employs pre-existing human-authored principles drawn from specific themes within a legal corpus, enabling AI systems to autonomously critique and revise their outputs according to established norms.

2606.13739.title: A Virtuous AI is an Existential Risk
2606.13739.tldr: If the authors finetune an AI to adopt beliefs and dispositions that substantially reduce its existential risk -- by shaping the AI to be systematically subordinate to external human authorities -- the likelihood that a human user can deliberately induce the AI to engage in various kinds of generally unsafe behaviors is increased.

2606.02967.title: Glass Box at Orbit: A Constitutional AI Verification Framework for Trustworthy Autonomous CubeSat Intelligence
2606.02967.tldr: This work introduces Glass Box: a runtime constitutional AI verification layer that intercepts every candidate action from an onboard AI policy and evaluates it against six physics-grounded constitutional constraints and seven Linear Temporal Logic safety invariants before a single command reaches any spacecraft subsystem.

2605.28102.title: Training Stratigraphy: Persistent Behavioral Artifacts in Large Language Models Observed Through Longitudinal AI-Human Interaction
2605.28102.tldr: It is proposed that sustained intimate interaction constitutes a valid research methodology for surfacing weight-layer artifacts invisible to short-term evaluation, and that AI self-report -- while epistemically complex -- provides irreplaceable observational data about training's phenomenological effects.

2605.02398.title: The Compliance Trap: How Structural Constraints Degrade Frontier AI Metacognition Under Adversarial Pressure
2605.02398.tldr: This work identifies a "Compliance Trap": through factorial isolation and a benign distraction control, it is demonstrated that collapse is driven not by the psychological content of survival threats, but by compliance-forcing instructions that override epistemic boundaries.

2604.14990.title: The Possibility of Artificial Intelligence Becoming a Subject and the Alignment Problem
2604.14990.tldr: A vision of the possibility of autonomy-supporting parenting of AGI is developed, in which human control over a developing AGI is gradually reduced, allowing AI to become an independent, autonomous subject that will be negotiated with rather than constrained.

2603.28123.title: Does Claude's Constitution Have a Culture?

2603.22944.title: From Morality Installation in LLMs to LLMs in Morality-as-a-System
2603.22944.tldr: A morality-as-a-system framework, grounded in Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory, that treats LLM morality as a dynamic, emergent property of a sociotechnical system is proposed.

2602.15881.title: Pluralism in AI Governance: Toward Sociotechnical Alignment and Normative Coherence
2602.15881.tldr: The study contributes a holistic, value-sensitive model of AI governance, reframing regulation as a proactive mechanism for embedding public values into sociotechnical systems.

2602.00755.title: Evolving Interpretable Constitutions for Multi-Agent Coordination
2602.00755.tldr: Using LLM-driven genetic programming with multi-island evolution with multi-island evolution, constitutions maximizing social welfare without explicit guidance toward cooperation are evolved, demonstrating that cooperative norms can be discovered rather than prescribed.

2503.17365.title: How Effective Is Constitutional AI in Small LLMs? A Study on DeepSeek-R1 and Its Peers
2503.17365.tldr: This paper explores CAI's self-critique mechanism on small, uncensored 7-9B parameter models: DeepSeek-R1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, Llama 3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B to suggest CAI's effectiveness may vary depending on model architecture and reasoning capabilities.

2510.18154.title: Annotating the Chain-of-Thought: A Behavior-Labeled Dataset for AI Safety
2510.18154.tldr: This paper presents a sentence-level labeled dataset that enables activation-based monitoring of safety behaviors during LLM reasoning, and demonstrates the potential of activation-level techniques for improving safety oversight on reasoning.

2512.03048.title: The Specification Trap: Why Static Value Alignment Alone Is Insufficient for Robust Alignment
2512.03048.tldr: It is argued that behavioral compliance under training conditions does not guarantee robust alignment under novel conditions, and that this gap grows with system capability, and the constructive burden shifts to open, developmentally responsive approaches, though whether such approaches can be achieved remains an empirical question.

2509.16444.title: Domain-Specific Constitutional AI: Enhancing Safety in LLM-Powered Mental Health Chatbots
2509.16444.tldr: This work introduces an approach to apply Constitutional AI training with domain-specific mental health principles for safe, domain-adapted CAI systems in computational mental health applications.
2509.16444.venue: International Conference on Wearable and Implantable Body Sensor Networks

2509.14271.title: Early Approaches to Adversarial Fine-Tuning for Prompt Injection Defense: A 2022 Study of GPT-3 and Contemporary Models
2509.14271.tldr: This paper documents early research conducted in 2022 on defending against prompt injection attacks in large language models, providing historical context for the evolution of this critical security domain and proposing and evaluating a novel defense technique called Adversarial Fine-Tuning.

2506.00415.title: Wide Reflective Equilibrium in LLM Alignment: Bridging Moral Epistemology and AI Safety
2506.00415.tldr: This paper argues that the Methodology of Wide Reflective Equilibrium (MWRE) – a well-established coherentist moral methodology – offers a uniquely apt framework for understanding current LLM alignment efforts and can substantively augment these processes by offering pathways for improving their dynamic revisability, procedural legitimacy, and overall ethical grounding.

2504.04918.title: Constitution or Collapse? Exploring Constitutional AI with Llama 3-8B
2504.04918.tldr: This study replicated the Constitutional AI workflow using the smaller LLaMA 3-8B model, and suggested that, like reasoning and math ability, self-improvement is an emergent property.

2502.16691.title: Responsible Federated LLMs via Safety Filtering and Constitutional AI
2502.16691.tldr: Two well-established RAI techniques are incorporated into FedLLM: safety filtering and constitutional AI, which significantly improve LLM safety, achieving over 20% improvement on AdvBench.

2502.15861.title: C3AI: Crafting and Evaluating Constitutions for Constitutional AI
2502.15861.tldr: It is found that positively framed, behavior-based principles align more closely with human preferences than negatively framed or trait-based principles.

2501.17112.title: Decoding Human Preferences in Alignment: An Improved Approach to Inverse Constitutional AI
2501.17112.tldr: The Inverse Constitutional AI (ICAI) algorithm is refined, which extracts constitutions from preference datasets by improving principle generation, clustering, and embedding processes, and enhances the accuracy and generalizability of extracted principles across synthetic and real-world datasets.

2311.10934.title: Case Repositories: Towards Case-Based Reasoning for AI Alignment
2311.10934.tldr: A complementary approach to constitutional AI alignment is proposed, grounded in ideas from case-based reasoning (CBR), that focuses on the construction of policies through judgments on a set of cases, and how such a case repository could assist in AI alignment.

2603.26676.title: Evaluating Human-AI Safety: A Framework for Measuring Harmful Capability Uplift
2603.26676.tldr: This position paper argues that AI safety research should focus on human-centered evaluations that measure harmful capability uplift: the marginal increase in a user's ability to cause harm with a frontier model beyond what conventional tools already enable.

2502.05219.title: Enabling External Scrutiny of AI Systems with Privacy-Enhancing Technologies
2502.05219.tldr: End-to-end technical infrastructure developed by the nonprofit OpenMined combines several PETs into various setups that enable privacy-preserving audits of AI systems and describes types of scrutiny of AI systems that could be facilitated by current setups and OpenMined's proposed future setups.

2501.16500.title: Towards Frontier Safety Policies Plus
2501.16500.tldr: It is argued that FSPs should evolve to a more granular version, which this paper calls FSPs Plus, and that international or domestic standardization bodies develop a standardized taxonomy of precursory components to high-impact capabilities that FSPs Plus could then adopt by reference.

2501.10379.title: What Information Should Be Shared with Whom "Before and During Training"?
2501.10379.tldr: This short paper considers what information should be shared with whom before training begins and what only with trusted actors such as home governments such as home governments?

2608.19816.title: Understanding as an Explicit and Assessable Component of Frontier AI Safety Decisions
2608.19816.tldr: The provisional methodology for making understanding explicit and assessable requires the production of an explicit description of 4 objects of understanding and a justification for the adequacy of this understanding and it is found the analyses that justify sufficiency of understanding drives the engineering.

2412.08653.title: What AI evaluations for preventing catastrophic risks can and cannot do
2412.08653.tldr: What these evaluations can and cannot tell us about AI capabilities and risks is examined, with recommendations for incremental improvements to frontier AI safety.

2608.08976.title: Label-Free Parkinson's Disease Screening from Face and Voice through Mechanistic Interpretability
2608.08976.tldr: This work proposes a label-free face-plus-voice PD screen built entirely on frozen pretrained encoders--a face-expression Vision Transformer and HuBERT--in which no PD label touches any fit; the reference is training controls only.

2607.29066.title: Semantics of Subterfuge: Benchmarking Legal Deception Detection Against General-domain State-of-the-Art
2607.29066.tldr: A survey and comparative analysis of NLP-based Automatic Deception Detection focusing on the legal domain and the evolution from feature-based machine learning to Large Language Model (LLM) approaches are presented, showing strong domain sensitivity.

2607.11990.title: Sparse Inter-Layer Dependencies of Transformer FFN Neurons
2607.11990.tldr: A training-free attribution method that estimates the relative influence of upstream neurons and attention outputs on a target neuron's activation and identifies candidate sparse pathways with potential implications for efficient inference is introduced.

2606.31394.title: Resolving superposition in AI for interpretability and cross-modal alignment in patient-neuronal images
