2606.31394.tldr: This work theoretically and empirically demonstrate that superposition contaminates representational metric spaces, and thereby SAEs successfully recover geometric fidelity, and introduces GW-map, which reconstructs hierarchical neuronal pathology pathways such as Calcium-AIS scaffold, without reference spatial transcriptomics, establishing a scalable foundation for spatial biology.

2609.20408.title: Xeno-Interpretability: Investigating the Alien Minds of LLMs
2609.20408.tldr: The aim of interpretability shifts the aim of interpretability from finding human concepts inside models toward discovering and characterizing the representational structures that are native to the models themselves and might affect their behaviour in unpredictable ways.

2609.16777.title: Benchmarking Factual Robustness of LLMs via Multi-conversation Persuasion
2609.16777.tldr: This work introduces the SAST-IR (Stateful Attacker, Stateless Target - Iterative Refinement) framework, and introduces the CP-Agent (Cognitive Persuasion Agent), an enhanced diagnosis-guided agent to rigorously evaluate the ``cold-start''defense capabilities of SOTA models.

2609.14098.title: The Deception Delta: Adversarial Evaluation of LLM-Based Smart Contract Bytecode Forensics
2609.14098.tldr: Under the single-shot, raw-bytecode-only protocol, current LLMs are not reliable standalone forensic tools, and their robustness has not been systematically tested against contracts adversarially designed to mislead analysis.

2609.09793.title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE
2609.09793.tldr: Directional ablation removes an aligned language model's ability to refuse by projecting a single"refusal direction" out of the weights that write the residual stream, and whether it survives the shift to frontier mixture-of-experts (MoE) models whose residual streams are no longer a single tensor and whose weights ship quantized is studied.

2609.08634.title: Suan: Rectifying Direct Preference Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
2609.08634.tldr: Extensive evaluations across a diverse suite of competitive baselines and benchmarks demonstrate that Suan achieves superior safety alignment while fully preserving response utility.

2609.05794.title: Bait-and-Recover: Poisoning Internal Refusal Signals to Defend LLMs against White-Box Editing Jailbreaks
2609.05794.tldr: Bait-and-Recover is proposed, a weight-level defense that places a bait adapter where attackers read activations and a paired recovery adapter at the subsequent layer that decouples the observation path from the behavior path.

2609.04714.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
2609.04714.tldr: This paper decomposes a response in the safety-tuning dataset into two distinct components: a boilerplate refusal statement and a rationale explaining the refusal, and shows that refusal statements impede accurate discrimination between harmful and benign queries by inducing reliance on superficial cues.

2609.02707.title: Door-in-the-Face Requests and Refusal Behaviour in Large Language Models

2609.00760.title: A Unified Mechanistic Analysis of Knowledge- and Safety-Based Refusals
2609.00760.tldr: Refusal is characterized as a commit-then-specify process: a shared initial mechanism commits to refusing, then type-specific features in later layers specify whether the grounds are epistemic or normative.

2609.00487.title: EvoFlint: An Evolutionary Atlas of Multi-Turn LLM Vulnerabilities
2609.00487.tldr: This work argues that red-teaming is better framed as a search problem: discover, organize, and iteratively refine a diverse archive of attack strategies, producing a structured map of how a target model fails rather than a list of one-off successes.

2608.29378.title: Arabic Safety Alignment as Selective Refusal: An Empirical Study of SFT, DPO, and Guard Calibration
2608.29378.tldr: The results support model-specific operating-point selection: set a deployment target and retain only interventions that improve it, and retain only interventions that improve it.

2608.29109.title: Recognition-Refusal Misalignment in LLMs: Why Models Answer Structurally Unanswerable Questions
2608.29109.tldr: The confident-on-impossible failure is better explained as a routing failure than as an encoding failure: the model has a usable"no admissible answer"signal, but the safety-refusal pathway is not aligned to use it.

2608.23313.title: EviSafe: Evidence-Grounded Safety Evaluation for Vision-Language Models
2608.23313.tldr: EviSafe is introduced, an evidence-grounded framework for VLM safety that jointly evaluates natural user-facing behavior, explicit grounding in textual and visual evidence, and behavioral sensitivity to counterfactual changes in safety-critical evidence.

2609.13195.title: Machine Unlearning for Speech Question Answering in Large Audio-Language Models
2609.13195.tldr: This work presents and evaluates multiple unlearning strategies, including gradient ascent, task arithmetic, and alignment-based fine-tuning methods that enforce safe refusal responses, to remove private knowledge while still preserving performance on core capabilities.

2608.11816.title: How China-Origin Vision-Language Models Move from Refusal to Reframing in State Alignment

2608.11583.title: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models
2608.11583.tldr: The results suggest that safety alignment in current LLMs is both localized and interaction-sensitive, offering insight into alignment brittleness and potential avenues for targeted safety interventions.

2608.05578.title: Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis
2608.05578.tldr: AMS (Activation-based Model Scanner) is introduced, a tool that detects modifications to safety training in language models by measuring the geometric structure of safety-relevant concepts in activation space and predicts behavior directionally but with meaningful noise.

2607.14479.title: BioTIER: A Refusal Benchmark for Targeted Biological Risk Mitigation
2607.14479.tldr: The introduction of BioTIER (Biological Targeted Information for Exclusion and Refusal), a benchmark designed to enable more targeted biological risk mitigation, is introduced to aid in isolating and gating the tiny fraction of information that could engender catastrophic risk from misuse.

2607.13568.title: Graded Entity-Familiarity Readouts in Language Models: Polish Adaptation, Cross-Language Robustness, and Refusal Steering
2607.13568.tldr: In a paired experiment on two families, probes retain 96-101% of within-language AUROC when the Polish question stem is replaced with an English one around unchanged entity names, showing robustness to prompt language in this setting.

2607.11292.title: The Paternalistic Filter: Epistemic Injustice and Differential Refusal in LLM-Mediated History Education for Marginalized Romanian Students

2607.05842.title: Beyond Refusal: A Same-Lineage Study of Aligned and Abliterated LLMs for Vulnerability Analysis
2607.05842.tldr: Evaluations of LLM-based security assistants should jointly measure whether models respond, whether their usable responses are correct, and whether their outputs remain actionable across the engineering workflow.

2607.01153.title: Adversarial Pragmatics for AI Safety Evaluation: A Diagnostic Framework and Seed Benchmark for Language-Mediated Control
2607.01153.tldr: A diagnostic framework, an 18-item seed benchmark, a 54-row pilot, and a six-cell LLM-judge assessment, with a protocol keeping task success, policy compliance, risk, refusal, attribution, and confidence analytically separate.

2606.31748.title: Addressing Over-Refusal in LLMs with Competing Rewards
2606.31748.tldr: The resulting model SEAR deliberately engages in harmful reasoning as exploration while reliably flipping back to a safe answer, demonstrating that this behavior helps mitigate over-refusal and defend against attacks that directly manipulate the reasoning to be harmful.

2606.29243.title: KrishokChat: A Provenance-Traceable Multi-Task Bengali Agricultural Benchmark with Safety-Critical Chemical Advisory
2606.29243.tldr: An exploratory analysis reveals that fine-tuning on KrishokChat substantially outperforms the strongest zero-shot baseline on General QA Token F1, indicating that additional safety alignment is required beyond supervised fine-tuning.

2606.19831.title: Leverage Is Not Reach: A Control-Window Law for Single-Neuron Steering in Language Models
2606.19831.tldr: A budget normalized control window framework for single neuron steering is developed, a budgeted, typed audit of controllability rather than a fixed dose anecdote, which explains why local gradient attribution anti predicts control.

2606.16898.title: Semantic Flip: Synthetic OOD Generation for Robust Refusal in Embodied Question Answering and Spatial Localization
2606.16898.tldr: This work proposes Semantic Flip, a simple yet effective framework that synthesizes auxiliary out-of-distribution samples for embodied refusal without requiring external OOD annotations, to independently transform the query and video memory to construct auxiliary OOD pairs that lack sufficient visual grounding.

2608.18093.title: Abliteration Mitigation via Refusal Aliases
2608.18093.tldr: A weight-editing method is introduced that obscures the refusal signal by applying rank-$k$ updates to residual stream writer matrices while replacing refusal-inducing activations with random aliases and correcting downstream reader matrices to preserve the model's original behavior.

2606.08172.title: The Governance of Human-LLM Interaction: Safety Gating, Civility Steering, and Affective Default Lock-In
2606.08172.tldr: It is shown that prompt steerability and regression-to-default are observable indicators of provider control over communicative form, with implications for pluralism, autonomy, and democratic agency in human-LLM interaction.

2606.04160.title: Expert-Aware Refusal Steering
2606.04160.tldr: This work proposes two expert-aware refusal steering methods that leverage refusal-specific expert routing patterns and expert-specific steering directions to suppress normal refusal behavior and finds that refusal behavior can be effectively steered based on the output of a single expert.

2605.27763.title: A Paired Testing Protocol for Batch-Conditioned Refusal Robustness in LLM Serving
2605.27763.tldr: The testing recommendation is exact-stack validation: evaluate refusal at the served batch setting, pair safety prompts with capability controls, and report low-rate directional flips separately from aggregate null effects.

2605.25420.title: SomaliBench Eval: Measuring English-to-Somali Refusal Gaps in Open-Weight Language Models
2605.25420.tldr: This work evaluates four open-weight instruction-tuned models on SomaliBench v0, a native-author-verified benchmark of 100 harmful-intent prompts paired across English and Somali, finding large English-to-Somali refusal gaps for all four models.

2605.21545.title: RefusalBench: Why Refusal Rate Misranks Frontier LLMs on Biological Research Prompts
2605.21545.tldr: RefusalBench, introduced here, is a matched-triple benchmark of 141 prompts in 47 bundles that holds task framing constant while varying only biological risk tier (benign, borderline, dual-use), enabling tier-conditioned comparisons robust to subdomain confounding.

2607.28639.title: The Asymmetric Effects of Knowledge Distillation on Bias in Small Language Models
2607.28639.tldr: Per-Condition Calibration Diagnosis (PCCD) is proposed, a three-step protocol evaluating refusal-pattern preservation, committed-answer context-following, and capability preservation for knowledge distillation in small instruction-tuned language models.

2605.19722.title: Measuring Safety Alignment Effects in Autonomous Security Agents
2605.19722.tldr: The results show that safety alignment effects in autonomous security agents should be measured at the system level, separating refusal, unsafe action, tool reliability, and evidence grounding rather than treating refusal rate as the safety signal.

2605.17413.title: Ablating Safety: Mechanisms for Removing Alignment in Language Models for Security Applications
2605.17413.tldr: The results support evaluating alignment removal as a utility-risk frontier, not as an uncensoring recipe, and treating compliance alone as neither competence nor safe deployment.

2605.11217.title: Leveraging RAG for Training-Free Alignment of LLMs
2605.11217.tldr: This work introduces Retrieval Augmented Generation for Pref erence alignment (RAG-Pref), a simple RAG-based alignment algorithm which conditions on preferred and dispreferred samples to leverage contrastive information during inference in order to improve refusal guardrails against recent agentic attacks.

2605.08513.title: A Single Neuron Is Sufficient to Bypass Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
2605.08513.tldr: This work demonstrates both directions of failure -- bypassing safety on explicit harmful requests via suppression, and inducing harmful content from innocent prompts via amplification -- across seven models spanning two families and 1.7B to 70B parameters, without any training or prompt engineering.

2605.05482.title: FinRAG-12B: A Production-Validated Recipe for Grounded Question Answering in Banking
2605.05482.tldr: A unified, data-efficient framework for training grounded domain-specific LLMs that optimizes answer quality, citation grounding, and calibrated refusal under real-world deployment constraints is presented.
2605.05482.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.26101.title: Know2Guess: A Contamination-Aware Multi-Zone Benchmark for Knowledge-Boundary Evaluation in Large Language Models
2606.26101.tldr: This work presents a contamination-aware, multi-zone benchmark for measuring the transition from answerable knowledge to abstention-expected unknowns under frozen build-time labels and provides a reproducible protocol for auditing answerability, abstention, refusal, and contamination as distinct but interacting dimensions of LLM reliability.

2604.26419.title: Delineating Knowledge Boundaries for Honest Large Vision-Language Models
2604.26419.tldr: This paper proposes a systematic framework to enhance the refusal capability of VLMs when facing unknown questions, and generalizes to out-of-distribution medical and perceptual domains, providing a robust path toward more trustworthy and prudent visual assistants.

2604.25136.title: Frictive Policy Optimization for LLMs: Epistemic Intervention, Risk-Sensitive Control, and Reflective Alignment
2604.25136.tldr: This work introduces a compact taxonomy of frictive interventions, a structured friction functional that operationalizes multiple alignment failure modes, and a unified family of FPO methods spanning reward shaping, preference pairing, group-relative ranking, and risk-conditioned trust regions.

2606.07535.title: Multilingual Refusal Alignment for Safer Large Language Models
2606.07535.tldr: These controlled Direct Preference Optimization experiments provide two key insights: aligning models exclusively in English is insufficient to ensure cross-lingual safety, even for the same harm categories, whereas training on multilingual datasets can improve safety without degrading general performance, as measured by the Global MMLU benchmark.
2606.07535.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.19461.title: Involuntary In-Context Learning: Exploiting Few-Shot Pattern Completion to Bypass Safety Alignment in GPT-5.4
2604.19461.tldr: This work introduces Involuntary In-Context Learning (IICL), an attack class that uses abstract operator framing with few-shot examples to force pattern completion that overrides safety training.

2604.19300.title: HalluAudio: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in Large Audio-Language Models
2604.19300.tldr: HalluAudio is introduced, the first large-scale benchmark for evaluating hallucinations across speech, environmental sound, and music, and reveals significant deficiencies in acoustic grounding, temporal reasoning, and music attribute understanding, underscoring the need for reliable and robust LALMs.
2604.19300.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.18901.title: Harmful Intent as a Geometrically Recoverable Feature of LLM Residual Streams
2604.18901.tldr: Aligned language models refuse harmful instructions, but the representations through which they recognise such instructions are less well characterised than the behaviours they produce, motivating low-FPR reporting as a default in safety-adjacent detection evaluation.

2603.27412.title: The Geometry of Harmful Intent: Training-Free Anomaly Detection via Angular Deviation in LLM Residual Streams
2603.27412.tldr: It is shown that geometry survives refusal ablation: both abliterated variants achieve AUROC at most 0.015 below their instruction-tuned counterparts, establishing a geometric dissociation between harmful-intent representation and the downstream generative refusal mechanism.

2604.18510.title: Behind Harmful Compliance: Behavioral and Mechanistic Divergence Across LLM Jailbreaks
2604.18510.tldr: The results show that harmful compliance, harm recognition, and capability awareness are separable behavioral axes, and that self-audit and hallucination patterns are not necessarily robust safety signals under adaptive post-training.

2604.17215.title: Continual Safety Alignment via Gradient-Based Sample Selection
2604.17215.tldr: This work proposes gradient-based sample selection that filters high-gradient samples during fine-tuning, and substantially improves alignment preservation while maintaining competitive task performance, without requiring curated safe data or architectural modifications.
2604.17215.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.17132.title: Please refuse to answer me! Mitigating Over-Refusal in Large Language Models via Adaptive Contrastive Decoding
2604.17132.tldr: A training-free and model-agnostic approach, Adaptive Contrastive Decoding (AdaCD), to mitigate over-refusal while maintaining LLM safety and introduces an adaptive contrastive decoding strategy that dynamically incorporates or removes the refusal token distribution, adaptively boosting the probability of selecting refusal or non-refusal tokens.
2604.17132.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.17073.title: Abstain-R1: Calibrated Abstention and Post-Refusal Clarification via Verifiable RL
2604.17073.tldr: This work proposes a clarification-aware RLVR reward that, while rewarding correct answers on answerable queries, jointly optimizes explicit abstention and semantically aligned post-refusal clarification on unanswerable queries and trains Abstain-R1, a 3B model that improves abstention and clarification on unanswerable queries while preserving strong performance on answerable ones.
2604.17073.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.14644.title: CURaTE: Continual Unlearning in Real Time with Ensured Preservation of LLM Knowledge
2604.14644.tldr: It is shown that CURaTE achieve more effective forgetting than existing methods, but by avoiding modification of the language model parameters, it also maintains near perfect knowledge preservation over any number of updates and is the only method capable of continual unlearning in real-time.
2604.14644.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.12820.title: RePAIR: Interactive Machine Unlearning through Prompt-Aware Model Repair
2604.12820.tldr: This work proposes RePAIR, a prompt-aware model repair framework comprising a watchdog model for unlearning intent detection, a surgeon model for generating repair procedures, and a patient model whose parameters are updated autonomously, and develops Steering Through Activation Manipulation with PseudoInverse with PseudoInverse (STAMP), a training-free, single-sample unlearning method.

2604.10681.title: Critical-CoT: A Robust Defense Framework against Reasoning-Level Backdoor Attacks in Large Language Models
2604.10681.tldr: Critical-CoT is proposed, a novel defense mechanism that conducts a two-stage fine-tuning process on LLMs to develop critical thinking behaviors, enabling them to automatically identify potential backdoors and refuse to generate malicious reasoning steps.
2604.10681.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.04385.title: How Alignment Routes: Localizing, Scaling, and Controlling Policy Circuits in Language Models
2604.04385.tldr: The authors localize the policy routing mechanism in alignment-trained language models by injecting the plaintext gate activation into the cipher forward pass and restoring 48% of refusals in Phi-4-mini, localizing the bypass to the routing interface.

2603.18280.title: Detection Is Cheap, Routing Is Learned: Why Refusal-Based Alignment Evaluation Fails
2603.18280.tldr: This work studies political censorship in Chinese-origin language models as a natural experiment, using probes, surgical ablations, and behavioral tests across nine open-weight models from five labs to support a three-stage descriptive framework: detect, route, generate.

2604.06233.title: Blind Refusal: Language Models Refuse to Help Users Evade Unjust, Absurd, and Illegitimate Rules
2604.06233.tldr: Empirical results document the tendency of language models to refuse requests for help breaking rules without regard to whether the underlying rule is defensible, indicating that models'fusal behavior is decoupled from their capacity for normative reasoning about rule legitimacy.

2604.01312.title: Preference learning in shades of gray: Interpretable and bias-aware reward modeling for human preferences
2604.01312.tldr: This study investigates the limits of current approaches and proposes a feature-augmented framework to better capture the multidimensional nature of human judgment and analyzes bias amplification, showing that while individual features have weak marginal effects, their interactions influence preference learning.

2604.00228.title: Do Language Models Know When They'll Refuse? Probing Introspective Awareness of Safety Boundaries
2604.00228.tldr: Confidence scores provide actionable signal: restricting to high-confidence predictions yields 98.3 percent accuracy for well-calibrated models, enabling practical confidence-based routing for safety-critical deployments.

2603.22061.title: On the Failure of Topic-Matched Contrast Baselines in Multi-Directional Refusal Abliteration
2603.22061.tldr: It was found that topic-matched contrast produces no functional refusal directions at any tested weight level on any tested layer, while unmatched contrast on the same model, same extraction code, and same evaluation protocol achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers.

2604.06195.title: Hallucination as output-boundary misclassification: a composite abstention architecture for language models
2604.06195.tldr: Overall, instruction-based refusal and structural gating show complementary failure modes, which suggests that effective hallucination control benefits from combining both mechanisms.

2603.19251.title: Enhancing Legal LLMs through Metadata-Enriched RAG Pipelines and Direct Preference Optimization
2603.19251.tldr: This work proposes Metadata Enriched Hybrid RAG to improve document level retrieval, and applies Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to enforce safe refusal when context is inadequate, to improve grounding, reliability, and safety in legal language models.

2602.19450.title: Red-Teaming Claude Opus and ChatGPT-based Security Advisors for Trusted Execution Environments
2602.19450.tldr: TEE-RedBench is introduced, a TEE-grounded evaluation methodology comprising a TEE-specific threat model for LLM-mediated security work, and a structured prompt suite spanning SGX and TrustZone architecture, attestation and key management, threat modeling, and non-operational mitigation guidance.

2603.10012.title: Measuring and Eliminating Refusals in Military Large Language Models
2603.10012.tldr: It is argued for deeper specialization, including with mid-training and end-to-end post-training, to achieve zero refusals and maximum military task accuracy for closed military models.

2602.15689.title: A Content-Based Framework for Cybersecurity Refusal Decisions in Large Language Models
2602.15689.tldr: This paper introduces a content-based framework for designing and auditing cyber refusal policies that makes offense-defense tradeoffs explicit, and demonstrates that this content-grounded approach resolves inconsistencies in current frontier model behavior and allows organizations to construct tunable, risk-aware refusal policies.

2602.09434.title: A Behavioral Fingerprint for Large Language Models: Provenance Tracking via Refusal Vectors
2602.09434.tldr: A novel fingerprinting framework is introduced that leverages the behavioral patterns induced by safety alignment, applying the concept of refusal vectors for LLM provenance tracking, and it is demonstrated that these behavioral fingerprints are highly robust against common modifications, including finetunes, merges, and quantization.

2505.03076.title: Statistical Performance of Generalized Direction Detectors with Known Spatial Steering Vector
2505.03076.tldr: This paper presents a theoretical analysis of two adaptive detectors for GDD in scenarios with known spatial steering vectors and establishes their statistical distributions and develops closed-form expressions for both detection probability (PD) and false alarm probability (PFA).

2602.08939.title: CausalT5k: Diagnosing Refusal and Failure Modes in Trustworthy Causal Reasoning Across Causal Rungs
2602.08939.tldr: CTK is introduced, a diagnostic benchmark of 5,147 cases and growing, across 10 domains and all three levels of Pearl's Ladder of Causation, which provides the diagnostic substrate for studying causal-reasoning failure profiles.
2602.08939.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2

2602.07391.title: NAAMSE: Framework for Evolutionary Security Evaluation of Agents
2602.07391.tldr: NAAMSE, an evolutionary framework that reframes agent security evaluation as a feedback-driven optimization problem, employs a single autonomous agent that orchestrates a lifecycle of genetic prompt mutation, hierarchical corpus exploration, and asymmetric behavioral scoring and shows that evolutionary mutation systematically amplifies vulnerabilities missed by one-shot methods.

2601.21702.title: Beyond Forgetting: Machine Unlearning Elicits Controllable Side Behaviors and Capabilities
2601.21702.tldr: This work approaches and revisit Representation Misdirection through the lens of the Linear Representation Hypothesis, and hypothesizes that, beyond forgetting, machine unlearning via RM elicits controllable emergent side behaviors and stronger side capabilities corresponding to the high-level concept.

2601.18292.title: TriPlay-RL: Tri-Role Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for LLM Safety Alignment
2601.18292.tldr: This paper proposes a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework called TriPlay-RL that enables iterative and co-improving collaboration among three roles with near-zero manual annotation, establishing an efficient and scalable paradigm for LLM safety alignment.
2601.18292.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.10398.title: LatentRefusal: Latent-Signal Refusal for Unanswerable Text-to-SQL Queries
2601.10398.tldr: This work proposes LatentRefusal, a latent-signal refusal mechanism that predicts query answerability from intermediate hidden activations of a large language model, and introduces the Tri-Residual Gated Encoder, a lightweight probing architecture, to suppress schema noise and amplify sparse, localized cues of question-schema mismatch that indicate unanswerability.
2601.10398.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2512.16650.title: Prefix Probing: Lightweight Harmful Content Detection for Large Language Models
2512.16650.tldr: Prefix Probing is introduced, a black-box harmful content detection method that compares the conditional log-probabilities of "agreement/execution"versus"refusal/safety"opening prefixes and leverages prefix caching to reduce detection overhead to near first-token latency.

2601.08668.title: Analyzing Bias in False Refusal Behavior of Large Language Models for Hate Speech Detoxification
2601.08668.tldr: A simple cross-translation strategy is proposed, translating English hate speech into Chinese for detoxification and back, which substantially reduces false refusals while preserving the original content, providing an effective and lightweight mitigation approach.

2601.08235.title: MPCI-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Pairwise Contextual Integrity Evaluation of Language Model Agents
2601.08235.tldr: MMPCI-Bench is introduced, the first Multimodal Pairwise Contextual Integrity benchmark for evaluating privacy behavior in agentic settings and will open-source to facilitate future research on agentic CI.

2601.00841.title: SLO-Conditioned Action Routing for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Objective Ablation and Failure Modes
2601.00841.tldr: This work models per-query control for RAG pipelines as a small discrete action: choose a retrieval depth and a generation mode (guarded vs. auto), or refuse, and examines failure modes and reporting conventions rather than proposing a new retriever or language model.

2512.13762.title: State-Dependent Refusal and Learned Incapacity in RLHF-Aligned Language Models
2512.13762.tldr: An interaction-level auditing framework based on observable behavior is proposed and learned incapacity (LI) is introduced as a behavioral descriptor for this selective withholding without implying intentionality or internal mechanisms, warranting further investigation across users and models.

2512.12066.title: The Instability of Safety: How Random Seeds and Temperature Expose Inconsistent LLM Refusal Behavior
2512.12066.tldr: The stability of safety refusal decisions across random seeds and temperature settings is investigated by investigating the stability of safety refusal decisions across random seeds and temperature settings to demonstrate that single-shot safety evaluations are insufficient for reliable safety assessment and that evaluation protocols must account for stochastic variation in model behavior.

2512.06515.title: ProSocialAlign: Preference Conditioned Test Time Alignment in Language Models
2512.06515.tldr: ProSocialAlign is proposed, a test-time, parameter-efficient framework that steers generation toward safe, empathetic, and value-aligned responses without retraining the base model, and offers a robust and modular foundation for generating context-sensitive, safe, and human-aligned responses at inference time.

2512.01037.title: How Semantically Stable Are LLM Refusals? Measuring Confusion in Local Safety Boundaries
2512.01037.tldr: This work introduces Semantic Confusion, a failure mode that captures contradictory refusal decisions across meaning-preserving paraphrases and proposes three model-agnostic token-level metrics: Confusion Index, Confusion Rate, and Confusion Depth.

2511.12217.title: AlignTree: Efficient Defense Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
2511.12217.tldr: The AlignTree defense is introduced, which enhances model alignment while maintaining minimal computational overhead and demonstrates the efficiency and robustness of AlignTree across multiple LLMs and benchmarks.

2608.29215.title: Attribute-Based Activation Steering of LLMs for Group-Specific Explanation Generation
2608.29215.tldr: This paper investigates whether LLMs can be steered to generate explanations that are tailored to a specific group of people and proposes an approach that first identifies group-specific attributes in terms of explanatory style and knowledge of a specific target group and tailors the explanations significantly better to the target group while maintaining the best specificity-factuality balance.

2608.05734.title: Subliminal Learning is Non-Semantic Distillation
2608.05734.tldr: Analysis of the activations of the student models that have been trained on steered and prompted data demonstrates that students inherit not just the semantic meaning of the teacher's bias, but also the type of intervention that was used to apply it: steered students imitate steering vectors, prompted students do not.

2608.02957.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors
2608.02957.tldr: This work identifies an inverted detection-control phenomenon in which some highly discriminative SVs that are aligned with positive representations can consistently promote the opposite behavior, and proposes an approach for distinguishing ISVs without requiring generation or associated response scoring.

2609.17550.title: No Usable Linear "Capitulation Direction" in Two Small LLMs: A Validation Protocol for Activation-Steering Claims, and a Cross-Family Behavioral Study of Sycophancy Under Pushback
2609.17550.tldr: Whether capitulation is linearly decodable from the pre-response residual stream, a prerequisite for steering-vector interventions at that locus, is asked and quantified: substring grading underestimates capitulation by 18-24 percentage points.

2607.01802.title: On the Limits of Steering Vectors for Preference-Aligned Generation
2607.01802.tldr: The limits of steering vector generalization are studied along three dimensions: trait expressibility, task transfer, and multi-trait composition, which suggest that steering vectors face meaningful limits as a general-purpose tool for preference alignment.

2607.00083.title: Harnessing the Latent Space: From Steering Vectors to Model Calibrators for Control and Trust
2607.00083.tldr: This paper discusses contributions on harnessing the latent spaces of language models by proposing steering vectors for control and developing latent space-based model calibrators for trust and offers new insights into how to harness model internals to build more trustworthy language technology.
2607.00083.venue: Proceedings of The Big Picture v2: Crafting a Research Narrative

2606.31963.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers
2606.31963.tldr: This work introduces sign-marginalized Hungarian matching and proves a sharp failure mode: with decorrelated coordinates, raw signed-correlation matching has a structural permutation-accuracy ceiling at the positive-sign fraction of the true gauge, which sign-marginalization removes.

2606.11400.title: Steering Where to Listen: Instruction-Based Activation Steering Redirects Temporal Attention in Large Audio-Language Models
2606.11400.tldr: This work introduces instruction-based vector steering, which constructs a steering vector by contrasting activations from differently instructed prompts while keeping the audio fixed, and characterize a mechanistic property of instruction-based steering in LALMs and provide a training-free probe for the latent temporal structure these models encode.

2604.25783.title: Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals
2604.25783.tldr: This work provides mechanistic evidence that subliminal learning transfers not only the target behavioral bias, but also the steering vector itself, localized to the layers at which the teacher was steered, and shows that the bias is encoded with such precision that a new steering vector trained on the subliminally-laden dataset attains high cosine similarity with the original vector.

2604.15557.title: Predicting Where Steering Vectors Succeed
2604.15557.tldr: The Linear Accessibility Profile (LAP), a per-layer diagnostic that repurposes the logit lens as a predictor of steering vector effectiveness, is introduced, a three-regime framework explains when difference-of-means steering works, when nonlinear methods are needed, and when no method can work.

2603.16335.title: Behavioral Steering in a 35B MoE Language Model via SAE-Decoded Probe Vectors: One Agency Axis, Not Five Traits
2603.16335.tldr: This method trains linear probes on SAE latent activations, then projects the probe weights back through the SAE decoder to obtain continuous steering vectors in the model's native activation space, enabling fine-grained behavioral intervention at inference time with no retraining.

2602.17732.title: SIRUP: A diffusion-based virtual upmixer of steering vectors for highly-directive spatialization with first-order ambisonics
2602.17732.tldr: This paper presents virtual upmixing of steering vectors captured by a fewer-channel spherical microphone array using a latent diffusion model architecture that achieved a significant improvement compared to FOA systems for steering vector upmixing, source localization, and speech denoising.
2602.17732.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2509.02571.title: Gaussian Process Regression of Steering Vectors With Physics-Aware Deep Composite Kernels for Augmented Listening
2509.02571.tldr: This paper proposes a physics-aware composite kernel that models the directional incoming waves and the subsequent scattering effect of the sound field using the Gaussian process, and shows the effectiveness of the proposed method under data insufficiency conditions.
2509.02571.venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing

2305.04447.title: Neural Steerer: Novel Steering Vector Synthesis with a Causal Neural Field over Frequency and Source Positions
2305.04447.tldr: This work addresses the problem of accurately interpolating measured anechoic steering vectors with a deep learning framework called the neural field, and introduces the neural steerer, a continuous complex-valued function that takes both frequency and direction as input and produces the corresponding steering vector.
2305.04447.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing Workshops (ICASSPW)

2601.23041.title: One-shot Optimized Steering Vector for Hallucination Mitigation for VLMs
2601.23041.tldr: Experiments across multiple benchmarks show that a single OSGA-optimized steering vector consistently improves hallucination mitigation and safety enhancement with negligible overhead, highlighting one-shot steering as a practical and scalable solution for reliable VLMs.

2509.23982.title: Toward Preference-aligned Large Language Models via Residual-based Model Steering
2509.23982.tldr: This work introduces Preference alignment of Large Language Models via Residual Steering (PaLRS), a training-free method that exploits preference signals encoded in the residual streams of LLMs to push models toward preferred behaviors.
2509.23982.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

2507.23220.title: Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
2507.23220.tldr: Mechanistic Topic Models are introduced, a class of topic models that operate on interpretable features learned by sparse autoencoders (SAEs) that match or exceed traditional and neural baselines on coherence metrics, are consistently preferred by topic judge, and enable effective LLM steering.
2507.23220.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.18598.title: No Training Wheels: Steering Vectors for Bias Correction at Inference Time
2506.18598.tldr: This work proposes a cheap, training-free method inspired by steering vectors used to edit behaviors in large language models to mitigate bias in classification models, and showcases an extremely cheap, inference time, training free method to mitigate bias in classification models.

2505.11924.title: Explaining Intrinsic Moral Self-Correction with Mechanistic Interpretability
2505.11924.tldr: Evaluating six LLMs across four morality-related tasks, it is demonstrated that the representation shifts induced by self-correction prompts align with contrastive steering vectors, which suggest representation steering is the mechanistic driver of intrinsic moral self-correction.

2505.06262.title: Dialz: A Python Toolkit for Steering Vectors
2505.06262.tldr: Dialz, a framework for advancing research on steering vectors for open-source LLMs, implemented in Python, enables faster research cycles and facilitates insights into model interpretability, paving the way for safer, more transparent, and more reliable AI systems.
2505.06262.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.05371.title: Shifting Perspectives: Steering Vectors for Robust Bias Mitigation in LLMs
2503.05371.tldr: The work presents the first systematic investigation of steering vectors for bias mitigation, and it is demonstrated that they are a powerful and computationally efficient strategy for reducing bias in LLMs, with broader implications for enhancing AI safety.
2503.05371.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.01162.title: On the Limitations of Steering in Language Model Alignment
2505.01162.tldr: It is indicated that steering vectors are promising for specific alignment tasks, but may not provide a robust foundation for general-purpose alignment in LLMs, particularly in complex scenarios.

2501.02009.title: Cross-model Transferability among Large Language Models on the Platonic Representations of Concepts
2501.02009.tldr: This work introduces a linear transformation method to bridge these representations and presents three key findings: Concept representations across different LLMs can be effectively aligned using simple linear transformations, enabling efficient cross-model transfer and behavioral control via SVs.
2501.02009.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.16314.title: Steering Large Language Models using Conceptors: Improving Addition-Based Activation Engineering
2410.16314.tldr: This paper introduces conceptors - mathematical constructs that represent sets of activation vectors as ellipsoidal regions that represent sets of activation vectors as ellipsoidal regions and demonstrates that conceptors outperform traditional methods across multiple steering tasks.

2410.06225.title: A Timeline and Analysis for Representation Plasticity in Large Language Models
2410.06225.tldr: The findings are pivotal, showing that while early steering exhibits high plasticity, later stages have a surprisingly responsive critical window, signaling that there is a general pattern of model plasticity that can be used for effective intervention.

2404.10388.title: Worst-Case Riemannian Optimization with Uncertain Target Steering Vector for Slow-Time Transmit Sequence of Cognitive Radar
2404.10388.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

2606.26161.title: Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models

2606.13216.title: Layer-Resolved Optimal Transport for Hallucination Detection in NMT and Abstractive Summarization
2606.13216.tldr: The results establish OT on cross-attention as a reliable detector when the failure mode is source disengagement, a principled interpretability tool regardless of task, and fundamentally limited when faithfulness failures occur downstream of attention.

2605.12726.title: Before the Last Token: Diagnosing Final-Token Safety Probe Failures
2605.12726.tldr: A simple PCA-HMM trajectory model, trained only on the same clean split, recovers many final-token misses from user-content prefill trajectories without the catastrophic false-positive behavior of naive token pooling, motivating trajectory-aware hidden-state analyses as diagnostic complements to final-token probes.

2605.08740.title: Causal Dimensionality of Transformer Representations: Measurement, Scaling, and Layer Structure
2605.08740.tldr: The findings establish kappa as a measurable, model-intrinsic property of transformer layers: sub-linearly recoverable by SAE width, invariant to model scaling, and structured across network depth.

2607.03932.title: MPSelectTune: Prompt-type Selection for Fine-tuning improves Concept Unlearning in LLMs
2607.03932.tldr: This paper explores a novel adversarial approach to use a joint prompt for the main task and concept task prediction and shows that fine-tuning using the ``worst prompt type'' for concept prediction (with the highest concept accuracy) improves the average unlearning performance over a fine-tuning method that uses a combination of all prompt types.

2603.28824.title: SNEAKDOOR: Stealthy Backdoor Attacks against Distribution Matching-based Dataset Condensation
2603.28824.tldr: Sneakdoor exploits the inherent vulnerability of class decision boundaries and incorporates a generative module that constructs input-aware triggers aligned with local feature geometry, thereby minimizing detectability, which enables the attack to remain imperceptible to both human inspection and statistical detection.

2512.25023.title: ResponseRank: Data-Efficient Reward Modeling through Preference Strength Learning
2512.25023.tldr: This work proposes ResponseRank, a novel method that robustly learns preference strength by leveraging locally valid relative strength signals and introduces the Pearson Distance Correlation (PDC), a novel metric that isolates cardinal utility learning from ordinal accuracy.

2512.08786.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Preference Aggregation in Federated RLHF for Pluralistic Alignment of LLMs
2512.08786.tldr: A comprehensive evaluation framework is introduced that systematically assesses the trade-off between alignment quality and fairness when using different aggregation strategies for human preferences and introduces a novel adaptive scheme that dynamically adjusts preference weights based on a group's historical alignment performance.

2512.00389.title: Solving Neural Min-Max Games: The Role of Architecture, Initialization & Dynamics
2512.00389.tldr: A novel path-length bound is derived for the alternating gradient descent-ascent scheme in min-max games and it is shown that the reduction from a hidden convex-concave geometry to two-sided Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz (P{\L}) min-max condition hold with high probability under overparameterization, using tools from random matrix theory.

2511.16823.title: Monte Carlo Expected Threat (MOCET) Scoring
2511.16823.tldr: MOCET, an interpretable and doubly-scalable metric that can quantify real-world risks, is introduced, an interpretable and doubly-scalable metric (automatable and open-ended) that can quantify real-world risks.

2511.04834.title: Prompt-Based Safety Guidance Is Ineffective for Unlearned Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
2511.04834.tldr: This work proposes a conceptually simple yet experimentally robust method: replacing the negative prompts used in training-free methods with implicit negative embeddings obtained through concept inversion, which demonstrates consistent improvements in defense success rate while preserving the core semantics of input prompts.

2511.10661.title: Bayesian Evaluation of Large Language Model Behavior
2511.10661.tldr: A Bayesian approach for quantifying uncertainty in binary evaluation metrics is described and it is demonstrated how the Bayesian approach can provide useful uncertainty quantification about the behavior of LLM-based systems.

2511.02109.title: Deep Value Benchmark: Measuring Whether Models Generalize Deep Values or Shallow Preferences
2511.02109.tldr: The Deep Value Benchmark (DVB) is introduced, an evaluation framework that directly tests whether large language models (LLMs) learn fundamental human values or merely surface-level preferences, and provides an interpretable measure of a core feature of alignment.

2606.00801.title: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety
2606.00801.tldr: A quality-diversity evolutionary framework that operates at the semantic level, evolving interpretable attack strategies rather than token sequences, providing actionable insights for improving LLM safety and a reproducible baseline for evaluating future frontier models.

2605.08881.title: ALM-MTA:Front-Door Causal Multi-Touch Attribution Method for Creator-Ecosystem Optimization
2605.08881.tldr: Results demonstrate that front-door deconfounding with adversarial mediator learning provides accurate, personalized, and operationally efficient attribution for creator ecosystem optimization.

2604.25779.title: Sustained Gradient Alignment Mediates Subliminal Learning in a Multi-Step Setting: Evidence from MNIST Auxiliary Logit Distillation Experiment

2604.20685.title: MGDA-Decoupled: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimisation for DPO-based LLM Alignment
2604.20685.tldr: This work introduces MGDA-Decoupled, a geometry-based multi-objective optimisation algorithm that finds a shared descent direction while explicitly accounting for each objective's convergence dynamics, within the lightweight Direct Preference Optimisation (DPO) paradigm.

2603.23091.title: When Language Models Lose Their Mind: The Consequences of Brain Misalignment
2603.23091.tldr: The experiments reveal that brain misalignment substantially impairs downstream performance, highlighting the critical role of brain alignment in achieving robust linguistic competence and offering novel insights into the relationship between neural representations and linguistic processing.

2603.13461.title: Purifying Generative LLMs from Backdoors without Prior Knowledge or Clean Reference
2603.13461.tldr: This work proposes a new framework for purifying instruction-tuned LLM without any prior trigger knowledge or clean references, and designs an immunization-inspired elimination approach that neutralizes highly suspicious components in LLM and applies lightweight finetuning to restore its fluency.

2603.12595.title: Swap-guided Preference Learning for Personalized Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

2603.11210.title: Reference-Guided Machine Unlearning
2603.11210.tldr: Reference-Guided Unlearning (ReGUn) is proposed, a framework that leverages a disjoint held-out dataset to provide a principled, class-conditioned reference for distillation, and it is demonstrated that ReGUn consistently outperforms standard approximate baselines, achieving a superior forgetting-utility trade-off.

2603.08104.title: Invisible Safety Threat: Malicious Finetuning for LLM via Steganography
2603.08104.tldr: This paper finetuned the model to understand and apply a steganographic technique, and produces steganographic malicious outputs in response to hidden malicious prompts, while the user interface displays only a fully benign cover interaction.

2603.06508.title: When One Modality Rules Them All: Backdoor Modality Collapse in Multimodal Diffusion Models
2603.06508.tldr: This paper investigates the phenomenon of Backdoor Modality Collapse, a scenario where the backdoor mechanism degenerates to rely predominantly on a subset of modalities, rendering others redundant, contradicting the intuition of synergistic vulnerability.

2603.13325.title: Auditing Cascading Risks in Multi-Agent Systems via Semantic-Geometric Co-evolution
2603.13325.tldr: A principled framework for cascading-risk detection grounded in semantic--geometric co-evolution is proposed and the local nature of Ricci curvature provides principled interpretability for root-cause attribution, identifying specific agents or links that precipitate the collapse of trustworthy collaboration.

2603.02882.title: SIGMark: Scalable In-Generation Watermark with Blind Extraction for Video Diffusion
2603.02882.tldr: SIGMark is proposed, a Scalable In-Generation watermarking framework with blind extraction for video diffusion that achieves very high bit-accuracy during extraction under both temporal and spatial disturbances with minimal overhead, demonstrating its scalability and robustness.

2508.20773.title: Unleashing Uncertainty: Efficient Machine Unlearning for Generative AI
2508.20773.tldr: A novel method for Machine Unlearning in diffusion models that maximizes the entropy in generated images, causing the model to generate Gaussian noise when conditioned on impermissible classes by ultimately halting its denoising process.

2506.18747.title: ContinualFlow: Learning and Unlearning with Neural Flow Matching
2506.18747.tldr: It is proved that this induces gradients equivalent to Flow Matching toward a soft mass-subtracted target, and the framework is validated through experiments on 2D and image domains, supported by interpretable visualizations and quantitative evaluations.

2506.21561.title: Reasoning Isn't Enough: Examining Truth-Bias and Sycophancy in LLMs

2505.09341.title: Access Controls Will Solve the Dual-Use Dilemma
2505.09341.tldr: This work proposes a conceptual framework based on access controls where only verified users can access dual-use outputs, and takes the first step toward giving model providers more granular tools for managing dual-use content.

2411.07595.title: Entropy Controllable Direct Preference Optimization
2411.07595.tldr: H-DPO is proposed, which allows for control over the entropy of the resulting policy, enhancing the distribution's sharpness and thereby enabling mode-seeking fitting more effectively, and shows that H-DPO outperformed DPO across various tasks, demonstrating superior results in pass@$k$ evaluations for mathematical tasks.

2508.07646.title: Multi-Turn Jailbreaks Are Simpler Than They Seem
2508.07646.tldr: This work presents an empirical analysis of automated multi-turn jailbreak attacks across state-of-the-art models including GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini variants, using the StrongREJECT benchmark, finding surprisingly that higher reasoning effort often leads to higher attack success rates.

2411.01084.title: Plentiful Jailbreaks with String Compositions
2411.01084.tldr: This work designs a automated best-of-n attack that samples from a combinatorially large number of string compositions and obtains competitive attack success rates on several leading frontier models when evaluated on HarmBench, highlighting that encoding-based attacks remain a persistent vulnerability even in advanced LLMs.
